author: dhess
body:
Hi,

We ran into a very tricky networking issue with Cilium, Multus, and Kata containers on Talos. It came and went over the past week or two. I finally resorted to using Claude (Fable) to help me diagnose it, and after a bit of back and forth, it nailed the fix. After spending some time trying to understand the cause, I have the gist of it, but as I'm not a kernel dev, I asked Claude to prepare the bug report. 

I've vetted this report to the best of my ability and I believe it's sound. (However, I have not audited Talos's kernel build to see whether any patches are applied that would change the behavior cited in the upstream kernel.) I have personally verified the workaround and production logs, in any case.

Though I'm a bit reluctant to submit an LLM-generated bug report, I think that in this case, due to the very tricky nature of the issue, it's on balance the right thing to do.

## Bug Report

### Description

Kata Containers pods on Talos silently lose effectively all inbound traffic when two common conditions combine: (a) `net.core.default_qdisc=fq` — in our case set node-wide by Cilium's bandwidth manager ([`pkg/datapath/linux/bandwidth/bandwidth.go`, `{Name: ...default_qdisc, Val: "fq"}`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/pkg/datapath/linux/bandwidth/bandwidth.go#L292), `enable-bandwidth-manager` + `enable-bbr`); the Talos kernel's own built-in default is `pfifo_fast` (`CONFIG_DEFAULT_NET_SCH` in `siderolabs/pkgs`) — and (b) any process on the node enabling software RX packet timestamping: one socket with `SO_TIMESTAMP`/`SO_TIMESTAMPNS`/`SOF_TIMESTAMPING_RX_SOFTWARE`, or a single legacy `SIOCGSTAMP` ioctl ([`net/core/sock.c:3786`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/net/core/sock.c#L3786)), flips the global `netstamp_needed_key`. When both hold, the per-pod `tap0_kata` (Kata tcfilter network model) gets `sch_fq`, and every timestamped inbound frame is dropped before it reaches the VM. Pods get an IP but ARP/ND for their gateway never resolves; the only counter anywhere that shows the loss is `fq`'s `horizon_drops`.

Causal chain (all references are to the v6.18 tree Talos 1.13.5 ships):

1. With `netstamp_needed_key` enabled, every received skb gets `skb->tstamp = ktime_get_real()` with `tstamp_type = SKB_CLOCK_REALTIME` ([`net/core/dev.c:2397`, `net_timestamp_set()`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/net/core/dev.c#L2397)).
2. Kata's tcfilter model moves frames pod-iface → tap with a tc u32 filter + `act_mirred` ingress redirect. `tcf_mirred_to_dev()` calls `skb_set_redirected(skb, tc_at_ingress)` ([`net/sched/act_mirred.c:335`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/net/sched/act_mirred.c#L335)).
3. `skb_set_redirected()` is supposed to clear the realtime RX timestamp (via [`skb_clear_tstamp()`, `include/linux/skbuff.h:4468`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/include/linux/skbuff.h#L4468)) before the skb is enqueued on the target device — protection added in 2018 by commit [`7236ead1b149`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/7236ead1b149) ("act_mirred: clear skb->tstamp on redirect", Eric Dumazet) for exactly this scenario: "If sch_fq is used at ingress, skbs that might have been timestamped by net_timestamp_set() if a packet capture is requesting timestamps could be delayed by arbitrary amount of time, since sch_fq time base is MONOTONIC."
4. But the entire clear sits inside `#ifdef CONFIG_NET_REDIRECT` ([`include/linux/skbuff.h:5280-5288`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/include/linux/skbuff.h#L5280-L5288)), and `NET_REDIRECT` is a promptless Kconfig symbol whose only selector in-tree is `CONFIG_IFB` ([`drivers/net/Kconfig:152-155`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/drivers/net/Kconfig#L152-L155)). The Talos kernel builds `NET_ACT_MIRRED=y` but not `IFB`, so `NET_REDIRECT` is off and `skb_set_redirected()` compiles down to `skb->redirected = 1;` — the protection is silently absent.

   This is confirmed in the shipped kernel configs in `siderolabs/pkgs` — both architectures, both `release-1.13` and current `main`: `CONFIG_NET_ACT_MIRRED=y` with `# CONFIG_IFB is not set` and no `CONFIG_NET_REDIRECT` line (promptless symbol, so absence == disabled). At time of writing: [`release-1.13`/`config-amd64`](https://github.com/siderolabs/pkgs/blob/release-1.13/kernel/build/config-amd64) (L1874, L2628), [`main`/`config-amd64`](https://github.com/siderolabs/pkgs/blob/main/kernel/build/config-amd64) (L1831, L2572), and the corresponding [`release-1.13`/`config-arm64`](https://github.com/siderolabs/pkgs/blob/release-1.13/kernel/build/config-arm64) (L1862, L2874) / [`main`/`config-arm64`](https://github.com/siderolabs/pkgs/blob/main/kernel/build/config-arm64) (L1818, L2817) lines — so the gap is still present in `main`.
5. `sch_fq` then reads the CLOCK_REALTIME stamp (~1.78e18 ns) as a CLOCK_MONOTONIC earliest-departure time decades in the future, i.e. beyond its 10 s horizon, and drops (`horizon_drop` is the default; [`net/sched/sch_fq.c:534`, `fq_packet_beyond_horizon()`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/net/sched/sch_fq.c#L534)). Untimestamped packets take fq's fastpath and survive — matching our field data exactly.

Mainstream distro kernels ship `CONFIG_IFB=m` — verified in the current configs of [Debian](https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.38-1/debian/config/config) (6.12.38-1), [Ubuntu](https://git.launchpad.net/~ubuntu-kernel/ubuntu/+source/linux/+git/noble/plain/debian.master/config/annotations) (noble, all architectures), [Fedora](https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/kernel/raw/rawhide/f/kernel-x86_64-fedora.config) (rawhide), [openSUSE](https://github.com/openSUSE/kernel-source/blob/master/config/x86_64/default), [Alpine](https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/master/main/linux-lts/lts.x86_64.config) (`linux-lts`), and the container-optimized [Flatcar](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/blob/main/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-modules/files/commonconfig-6.12) — and selecting `NET_REDIRECT` from a `=m` tristate still forces it `=y`, so those kernels all get the tstamp clearing.

We root-caused it in production after several weeks of intermittent "Kata pod gets an IP but has no egress; a node reboot fixes it" — behavior consistent with a reboot clearing the node's timestamping state (we have not yet identified which process enables it on affected nodes). An independent public report with the same drop point (Kata tap + fq `horizon_drops`, also on Talos) is anthony-spruyt/spruyt-labs#951; their `default_qdisc=fq` was set directly in their machine config for BBR, and their timestamp source (Cilium datapath) differs from ours, but the result and mitigation are the same.

#### Reproduction (self-contained, no Kata needed)

Run on a Talos node (e.g. via a privileged `kubectl debug node/...` netshoot pod; needs iproute2 + a tcpdump with `--time-stamp-precision`):

```bash
set -eu
ip netns add fqrepro
NS="ip netns exec fqrepro"
$NS ip link set lo up
$NS ip link add va type veth peer name vb
$NS ip tuntap add tapx mode tap
$NS tc qdisc replace dev tapx root fq        # what default_qdisc=fq gives Kata taps
$NS ip link set va up; $NS ip link set vb up; $NS ip link set tapx up
$NS ip addr add 10.99.0.1/24 dev va
$NS tc qdisc add dev vb handle ffff: ingress
$NS tc filter add dev vb parent ffff: u32 match u32 0 0 \
    action mirred egress redirect dev tapx   # Kata's tcfilter plumbing
# flip the global RX-timestamping static key (SO_TIMESTAMPNS):
$NS tcpdump --time-stamp-precision=nano -i lo -w /dev/null 2>/dev/null & TP=$!
sleep 1
$NS ping -c 20 -i 0.05 -W 1 10.99.0.99 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true  # 20 ARP frames va->vb
kill $TP 2>/dev/null
$NS tc -s qdisc show dev tapx | grep -E 'Sent|horizon'
ip netns del fqrepro
```

Expected on Talos (`NET_REDIRECT` absent): `horizon_drops` ≈ 20 (every frame). Expected on a distro kernel with `CONFIG_NET_REDIRECT=y`: `horizon_drops 0`. Without the `tcpdump` line (timestamping off): `horizon_drops 0` on both — isolating the two variables.

#### Workaround

The workaround we validated in production is `tc qdisc replace dev tap0_kata root pfifo_fast` inside the affected pod's network namespace — restores the pod instantly. Note that changing `net.core.default_qdisc` away from `fq` is not viable when Cilium's bandwidth manager is enabled, since the agent re-asserts `fq`.

### Logs

All nodes running with `fq` via Cilium bandwidth manager:

```
# talosctl -n <node> read /proc/sys/net/core/default_qdisc
fq
```

Production capture from an affected pod's netns; all inbound frames dropped — only 16 untimestamped frames were ever delivered, via fq's fastpath:

```
# tc -s filter show dev eth0 ingress
  action order 1: mirred (Egress Redirect to device tap0_kata) stolen
  Action statistics:
  Sent 736468 bytes 11657 pkt (dropped 0, overlimits 11657 requeues 0)

# tc -s qdisc show dev tap0_kata
qdisc fq 0: root refcnt 2 limit 10000p flow_limit 100p buckets 1024 [...] horizon 10s horizon_drop offload_horizon 0us
 Sent 1216 bytes 16 pkt (dropped 11657, overlimits 0 requeues 0)
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
  [...]
  gc 0 highprio 0 fastpath 16 throttled 0
 horizon_drops 11657
```

Kernel config on the affected node:

```
# talosctl -n <node> read /proc/config.gz | zcat | grep -E 'NET_REDIRECT|NET_ACT_MIRRED|IFB'
CONFIG_NET_ACT_MIRRED=y
# CONFIG_IFB is not set
```

Replacing the tap's qdisc restored the pod instantly:

```
# nsenter -t <kata-vmm-pid> -n tc qdisc replace dev tap0_kata root pfifo_fast
# → pod gateway ARP resolves within seconds, egress fully restored
```

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.13.5 (kernel 6.18.36-talos)
- Kubernetes version: v1.36.2
- Platform: metal (amd64); Kata Containers system extension 3.31.0 (kata-hardened runtime class); affected pods attached via Multus macvlan; Cilium with `enable-bandwidth-manager: true` / `enable-bbr: true` (source of `net.core.default_qdisc=fq`; the Multus macvlan datapath itself does not traverse Cilium)
title: Kata pods silently lose all ingress (sch_fq horizon_drop) when packet timestamping is active

author: lukepostulka
body:
## Feature Request

### Description

Please consider compiling the in-tree containerd devmapper snapshotter
(`plugins/snapshots/devmapper`) into the CRI containerd shipped with Talos, or
exposing it as a system extension.

**Use case:** Kata Containers with a block-device-backed container rootfs. With
the devmapper snapshotter, kata (via `snapshotter = "devmapper"` on the runtime
handler) consumes the container rootfs as a virtio-blk device instead of
virtiofs. That gives each VM an honestly sized root filesystem: writes past the
size hit a clean in-guest ENOSPC, instead of landing on the node filesystem where
the only enforcement is kubelet ephemeral-storage eviction (which kills the whole
VM). For multi-tenant Kata workloads this is the difference between "tenant
fills their disk and gets a write error" and "tenant fills their disk and their
sandbox is SIGKILLed".

**Current state on Talos 1.13 (containerd 2.2.5):** the bundled containerd
registers only the `native` and `overlayfs` snapshotters, so a
`[plugins."io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.devmapper"]` config section is inert.
Everything else needed is already on the host: `dm-thin-pool` loads via
`machine.kernel.modules`, an LVM thin-pool activates fine at boot, and
`dmsetup` is present.

**Workaround we run today:** an external proxy snapshotter — ~60 lines of Go
around the upstream `plugins/snapshots/devmapper` package, served over a
`[proxy_plugins]` socket from a privileged DaemonSet (the same pattern as the
stargz/nydus/soci snapshotters). It works, but it means shipping a second copy
of containerd's snapshotter code that must be version-pinned to the node's
containerd, for a plugin that is already in the containerd source tree Talos
builds from.

Happy to provide the full working configuration (machine config + DaemonSet) or
test a build.
title: Include the devmapper snapshotter in the bundled containerd

author: Gottox
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

With Talos 1.14, simpledrm is compiled into the Kernel and binds the GPU to the host.

`sysfb` now registers a `simple-framebuffer` device of the boot GPU and `simpledrm` binds to it. `vfio-pci` can then no longer reserve the GPU, so a KubeVirt guest gets the device but cannot use it.

I haven't found a way to disable simpledrm on the boot GPU. Downgrading the node to 1.13.10 with the same schematic fixes it.

### Logs

`/proc/iomem`:

```
2800000000-2fffffffff : 0000:c3:00.0
  2800000000-2801fa3fff : BOOTFB
    2800000000-2801fa3fff : simpledrm
```

dmesg while the guest runs:

```
vfio-pci 0000:c3:00.0: BAR 0: can't reserve [mem 0x2800000000-0x2fffffffff 64bit pref]
```

Guest amdgpu:

```
amdgpu 0000:07:00.0: PSP tmr init failed!
amdgpu 0000:07:00.0: PSP firmware loading failed
amdgpu 0000:07:00.0: probe with driver amdgpu failed with error -22
```

With `initcall_blacklist=sysfb_init` in the cmdline:

```
blacklisting initcall sysfb_init
[drm] Initialized simpledrm 1.0.0 for simple-framebuffer.0 on minor 0
```

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.14.0 (kernel 6.18.48-talos); works on v1.13.10 with the same schematic
- Kubernetes version: v1.35.0
- Platform: bare metal, Framework Desktop, UEFI/sd-boot, Image Factory `metal-installer`, kernel args `amd_iommu=on iommu=pt video=efifb:off video=simplefb:off`, `PCIDriverRebindConfig` to `vfio-pci`, KubeVirt v1.9.0
title: 1.14 kernel enables CONFIG_DRM_SIMPLEDRM, breaking VFIO passthrough of the boot GPU

author: muhlba91
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

Following the documented Talos 1.14 migration path — moving `.cluster.controlPlane.endpoint` and `.cluster.clusterName` into a `KubeClusterConfig` document, as deprecated by #13771 — causes `machined` (PID 1) to panic and crash-loop indefinitely on any cluster that also has `.cluster.serviceAccount.key` set (i.e. essentially any real, bootstrapped cluster).

**Root cause:**

`internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/secrets/root.go` (`RootKubernetesController`) was correctly updated in #13771 to guard on `cfg.Config().K8sClusterConfig() != nil` and to read cluster name/endpoint from the new document. However, it also calls `cfgProvider.K8sServiceAccountConfig()`, whose implementation in `pkg/machinery/config/types/v1alpha1/v1alpha1_k8s_bridge.go` was not updated to match:

```go
func (c *Config) K8sServiceAccountConfig() config.K8sServiceAccountConfig {
	if c.ClusterConfig == nil || c.ClusterConfig.ClusterServiceAccount == nil {
		return nil
	}

	return serviceAccountShim{
		endpoint: c.ClusterConfig.Endpoint(), // panics if ControlPlane is nil
		key:      c.ClusterConfig.ClusterServiceAccount,
	}
}
```

This guards on `ClusterServiceAccount == nil`, but not on `ClusterConfig.ControlPlane` being nil, before calling `.Endpoint()`. And `Endpoint()` itself, in `v1alpha1_clusterconfig.go`, has no defensive nil check:

```go
func (c *ClusterConfig) Endpoint() *url.URL {
	return c.ControlPlane.Endpoint.URL // nil pointer dereference
}
```

Once `.cluster.controlPlane` is removed from the v1alpha1 document (per the documented migration to `KubeClusterConfig`), `c.ControlPlane` is nil, and this is an immediate dereference on it.

**Impact:** because this runs inside `controller-runtime`, which is part of `machined` itself, the panic crashes PID 1. `machined` respawns, immediately hits the same nil field on its next reconcile pass, and panics again — an indefinite crash loop with no automatic recovery. The node remains `Ready: false` throughout. `talosctl apply-config` itself reports success ("Applied configuration without a reboot") with no indication the change is unsafe. Only remediation found was reverting the machine config to restore `.cluster.controlPlane.endpoint`.

**Reproduction:**

1. Start from a working Talos 1.14.0 machine config with `.cluster.serviceAccount.key` set (standard/required for any bootstrapped cluster) and legacy `.cluster.controlPlane.endpoint` / `.cluster.clusterName`.
2. Add a `KubeClusterConfig` document with equivalent `clusterName`/`endpoint`.
3. Remove `.cluster.controlPlane` and `.cluster.clusterName` from the v1alpha1 document (per the documented deprecation).
4. `talosctl apply-config --mode no-reboot -f <config>`.

**Expected behavior:** `K8sServiceAccountConfig()` should check whether `ClusterConfig.ControlPlane` (and/or `ControlPlane.Endpoint`) is nil before calling `.Endpoint()`, and/or `ClusterConfig.Endpoint()` itself should guard against a nil `ControlPlane` — consistent with how `RootKubernetesController` already guards on `K8sClusterConfig() != nil` for the rest of its logic.

### Logs

```
kern:     info: init[136]: segfault at 0 ip 00000000011fb7b4 sp 0000206d55a03258 error 4 in init[dfb7b4,400000+27f8000] likely on CPU 4 (core 0, socket 1)
kern:     info: Code: 00 00 48 85 f6 0f 85 89 00 00 00 48 8b 08 48 85 c9 74 74 48 8b 51 28 48 85 d2 74 58 48 83 ba 98 00 00 00 00 74 4e 48 8b 52 20 <48> 8b 12 48 8b 12 48 c7 84 24 b0 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 48 89 94 24
user: warning: [talos] controller failed {"component": "controller-runtime", "controller": "secrets.RootKubernetesController", "error": "controller \"secrets.RootKubernetesController\" panicked: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference\ngoroutine 546 [running]:\nruntime/debug.Stack()\n\t/go/src/runtime/debug/stack.go:26 +0x5e\ngithub.com/cosi-project/runtime/pkg/controller/runtime/internal/rruntime.(*Adapter).runOnce.func2()\n\t/.cache/mod/github.com/cosi-project/runtime@v1.16.3/pkg/controller/runtime/internal/rruntime/run.go:67 +0x4c\npanic({0x3069ca0?, 0x5dde3e0?})\n\t/go/src/runtime/panic.go:860 +0x13a\ngithub.com/siderolabs/talos/pkg/machinery/config/types/v1alpha1.(*ClusterConfig).Endpoint(...)\n\t/src/pkg/machinery/config/types/v1alpha1/v1alpha1_clusterconfig.go:66\ngithub.com/siderolabs/talos/pkg/machinery/config/types/v1alpha1.(*Config).K8sServiceAccountConfig(...)\n\t/src/pkg/machinery/config/types/v1alpha1/v1alpha1_k8s_bridge.go:331\ngit..."}
```

This repeats indefinitely (roughly every few seconds, PID changing on each respawn — observed 136 → 3333 → 325) until the machine config is reverted to restore `.cluster.controlPlane.endpoint`.

Once reverted, the node also showed transient `Authorization error (user=apiserver-kubelet-client, verb=get, resource=nodes, subresource=pods)` errors and a brief `connection refused` on `:6443`, which self-resolved after a couple of minutes — likely PKI/static-pod churn from the crash/revert window rather than a separate root cause, but noting it in case it's relevant.

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.14.0
- Kubernetes version: v1.37.0
- Platform: bare metal
title: KubeClusterConfig migration panics machined via unguarded ClusterConfig.Endpoint() in K8sServiceAccountConfig()

author: rouke-broersma
body:
## Bug Report

`talosctl gen config <name> <cluster endpoint>` is authoritive for the default `KubeServiceAccountConfig.issuer.issuerURL` even when an explicit `KubeClusterConfig` is passed which can cause a mismatch between expected issuer and actual issuer.

### Description

I had a mistake in my gen config scripts where I used the node ip as the cluster endpoint. Pre 1.14 this didn't matter because I had `cluster.controlPlane.endpoint` set explicitly in config so cluster endpoint was unused. After migrating to the new config documents for 1.14 I started having authentication failures from service accounts in the cluster to controlplane. I eventually discovered that the KubeServiceAccountConfig issuerUrl was a node IP instead of the cluster endpoint.

A difference between cluster endpoint and isssuer URL is probably not neccesarily wrong so I don't think there should be validation on this mismatch on config apply, however I don't think gen config without an explicit KubeServiceAccountConfig should be able to result in this disjoint configuration. 

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.14.0
- Kubernetes version: v1.37.0
- Platform: metal
title: talosctl gen config cluster endpoint is used for KubeServiceAccountConfig issuerUrl when KubeClusterConfig is set

body:
## Bug Report

### Description

The schema for 1.14 incorrectly lists `UnattendedInstallConfig` as `UnattendedInstall`.

author: lexfrei
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

`--insecure` no longer reaches `talosctl meta write` or `talosctl meta delete`.

v1.13.7 registered it on the parent as a persistent flag:

```go
metaCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVarP(&metaCmdFlags.insecure, "insecure", "i", false, ...)
```

v1.14.0 registers it through the new `InsecureFlags` mix-in, which uses the local flag set:

```go
// cmd/talosctl/pkg/talos/global/insecure.go
func (a *InsecureFlags) AddFlags(cmd *cobra.Command) {
	cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&a.Insecure, "insecure", "i", false, "use the insecure (encrypted with no auth) maintenance service")
	...
}

// cmd/talosctl/cmd/talos/meta.go
metaCmdFlags.InsecureFlags.AddFlags(metaCmd)
```

cobra merges a parent's persistent flags into a child at parse time, but not its local ones, so `meta write` never sees it. The parent cannot carry it either: `metaCmd` is `Args: cobra.NoArgs` with no `RunE`.

`talosctl meta --help` still lists `-i, --insecure`, while `talosctl meta write --help` does not, which is what makes this easy to miss.

`wipe` does it the other way and works: `wipeDiskCmdFlags.InsecureFlags.AddFlags(wipeDiskCmd)` registers on the subcommand that runs.

Writing a META key over the maintenance service happens before a machine config exists, so I don't see another way to reach it from the CLI. Registering on `metaWriteCmd` and `metaDeleteCmd` would fix it, or `InsecureFlags` could grow a persistent variant.

### Logs

```
$ talosctl version --client
Client:
	Tag:         v1.14.0

$ talosctl meta write --insecure 0x0a value --nodes 192.0.2.1
unknown flag: --insecure

$ talosctl meta --insecure write 0x0a value --nodes 192.0.2.1
unknown flag: --insecure
```

### Environment

- Talos version: client v1.14.0, built from the v1.14.0 module; v1.13.7 works
- Kubernetes version: n/a, parsing fails before any connection
- Platform: n/a
title: talosctl meta: --insecure is unreachable since v1.14.0

author: doublek
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

`ApplyConfiguration` cancels a pending `--mode=try` rollback timer even when `dry_run: true`, because the cancel runs before the dry-run early return. The config applied under `try` then becomes permanent.

- The cancel also runs before `configloader.NewFromBytes` (line 207) and before `Validate` (line 224), so a request carrying a config Talos would reject still cancels the timer.
- `mode=TRY` is the one exempt mode, so a dry run in TRY mode is unaffected.

**Expected behaviour.** The documentation describes try mode as "change is applied immediately (if not possible, returns an error), and reverts it automatically in 1 minute if no configuration update is applied". A dry run applies no configuration update, so it should not act as the confirming apply. `dry_run: true` should have no effect on node state.

**Impact.** An operator using try mode is deliberately holding a change in a self-reverting state while deciding whether to keep it, typically for a change that could cut off API access to the node. Running a dry run to inform that decision is the natural next step, and it silently commits the change instead. Tooling that presents a dry run as a read-only preview inherits the same footgun.

**Steps to reproduce.**

1. `talosctl apply-config --mode=try --timeout=5m ...`
2. During the window, `talosctl apply-config --dry-run ...` in any mode other than `try`.
3. Wait past the timeout. The config applied in step 1 is still active.

### Logs

No node logs captured for this one. It was first noticed across three `try` windows on 1.13.4: the two with no dry run reverted on schedule, and the one where a dry run was issued was still applied well past its timeout. 

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.13.4.
- Kubernetes version: v1.35.5
- Platform: bare metal
title: apply-config with dry_run=true cancels a pending --mode=try rollback

author: maxpain
body:
## Summary

When running talosctl upgrade-k8s, the “pre-pulling images” phase appears to run sequentially per image (i.e., it completes pulling the first image on all target nodes, then moves to the next image, etc.). This significantly increases upgrade time on clusters with multiple control-plane nodes and/or slow registry access.

## Current behavior

During talosctl upgrade-k8s, logs show the following pattern:
	•	Pull kube-apiserver on node A, node B, node C
	•	Only after that, start pulling kube-controller-manager on node A, node B, node C
	•	Then kube-scheduler, then kubelet, etc.

## Expected behavior

One of the following would be very helpful:
	1.	Parallel pre-pull across images, e.g. pull multiple images concurrently per node (bounded concurrency).
	2.	Configurable concurrency, e.g. a flag like:
	•	--pre-pull-concurrency=<N> (total tasks)
	•	and/or --pre-pull-image-concurrency=<N> / --pre-pull-node-concurrency=<N>
	3.	If parallelism is intentionally avoided, please document the rationale (resource constraints, registry throttling, etc.), and consider adding a knob to opt into concurrency.

```
 > "10.251.128.6": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.34.3
 > "10.251.128.9": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.34.3
 > "10.251.128.13": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.34.3
 > "10.251.128.6": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.34.3
 > "10.251.128.9": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.34.3

 > "10.251.128.6": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.34.3
 > "10.251.128.9": pre-pulling registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.34.3
```

author: noe-charmet
body:
## Feature Request

We would like to be able to use a wildcard when defining network interfaces configurations in Talos machine config.

### Description

Our machines have 2 interfaces (public and private), which both have DHCP and expose a default route. To avoid confusion, we define a Talos patch that assigns metrics like the following.


```yaml
# Prefer public interface routes over private interface routes
machine:
  network:
    interfaces:
      - interface: enp1s0f0np0
        dhcp: true
        dhcpOptions:
          routeMetric: 10
      - interface: enp1s0f1np1
        dhcp: true
        dhcpOptions:
          routeMetric: 1024
      - interface: enp2s0f0np0
        dhcp: true
        dhcpOptions:
          routeMetric: 10
      - interface: enp2s0f1np1
        dhcp: true
        dhcpOptions:
          routeMetric: 1024
...
      - interface: enp8s0f1np1
        dhcp: true
        dhcpOptions:
          routeMetric: 1024
```

As you can see all our public interfaces are in the format `enp*s0f0np0` and the private ones `enp*s0f1np1`.
I would like to be able to use a wild card and not have a surprise if some machine gets assigned another number for its enp interface.
title: Support wildcard in interface name in machine config

author: Sushi1324
body:
## Feature Request

### Description

Talos already parses `provider-id` out of nocloud metadata, but nothing ever hands it to the kubelet, so nodes register with an empty `spec.providerID` unless there is a CCM in the cluster to fill it in.

The parsing half is there. `platform/nocloud/metadata.go`:

```go
ProviderID   string `yaml:"provider-id,omitempty"`
```

and `nocloud.go` puts it on the resource:

```go
networkConfig.Metadata = &runtimeres.PlatformMetadataSpec{
    Platform:     n.Name(),
    Hostname:     hostname,
    InstanceID:   metadata.InstanceID,
    InstanceType: metadata.InstanceType,
    ProviderID:   metadata.ProviderID,
    ...
}
```

That is in 1.13.x, 1.14.0 and main, so this isn't a version I'm behind on. What's missing is the last hop: `KubeletSpecController` doesn't have `PlatformMetadatas.talos.dev` in its `Inputs()`, and the only cloud-related arg it builds is `--cloud-provider=external`. So the value gets parsed, shows up in `talosctl get platformmetadata`, and then goes nowhere.

Where this bites is Cluster API on Proxmox. CAPMOX already emits the value; with `providerIDInjection` enabled the generated meta-data looks like:

```
instance-id: b38cd8b3-1c70-466e-b299-b57e2530ed1b
local-hostname: <machine>
provider-id: proxmox://b38cd8b3-1c70-466e-b299-b57e2530ed1b
kubernetes-version: v1.33.4
```

Talos reads that and the node still comes up with `spec.providerID` empty. CAPI matches Machines to Nodes on provider ID, so the Machine never gets a `nodeRef` and sits at `Provisioned` / `READY Unknown` forever. `clusterctl move` then refuses with "still provisioning the node", control plane rollouts stall waiting for a machine that will never look healthy, and a MachineHealthCheck eventually hits `nodeStartupTimeout` and deletes a node that was fine all along. The usual workaround is patching `node.spec.providerID` from outside after registration, which has to keep running forever since every machine roll produces a new node.

What I'd like: add the platform metadata resource to `KubeletSpecController.Inputs()`, and set `args["provider-id"]` when `ProviderID` is non-empty and the user hasn't already set it in `machine.kubelet.extraArgs`. That's the same deference the controller already does for `node-ip` and `hostname-override`.

I'm aware the usual answer here is to run a CCM, and that's reasonable on a real cloud. nocloud is the platform where there often isn't one, and on Proxmox specifically it means putting hypervisor API credentials into every workload cluster and living with nodes tainted uninitialized until the CCM shows up. Setting the flag from metadata Talos has already read seems cheaper than that. `extraArgs` doesn't help either, since the value is per-VM and the machine config is rendered per pool.

Two things I'd want your opinion on before writing it:

Should this be automatic whenever `ProviderID` is populated, or behind a `machine.kubelet` opt-in? I don't have a preference and would rather build whichever you'd take.

More importantly, ordering. The metadata may not be there when the kubelet spec is first built, and changing kubelet args restarts the kubelet, so a naive version risks a restart during bootstrap. Is it acceptable to wait on the resource for platforms that publish it, or would you rather eat the one restart? (`spec.providerID` is immutable once set, so whatever we do it should only apply at registration.)

Happy to send the PR with tests and a docs note, DCO signed, once those are settled. Thanks!
title: Set kubelet --provider-id from PlatformMetadata.ProviderID

author: rothgar
body:
## Feature Request

Expose a `talosctl upgrade-hardware` to update firmware on supported devices.

### Description

This will introduce a new controller and API surface that will update select hardware devices supported by the [Linux Vendor Firmware Service (LVFS)](https://fwupd.org/). The user experience will be similar to `fwupdmgr` but exposed directly as part of the Talos system and hook into the lifecycle management of machines (e.g. reboot when needed).

This will only be available for `platform=metal` systems.

Explicit non-goals is to add additional binaries or packages to the system. Where possible, the LVFS components will be written in go and standard linux kernel interfaces will be used for writing hardware devices (e.g. `/dev/efi_capsule_loader`).
title: Talos firmware management

author: shanduur
body:
Talos can provision RAID1 and RAID10 LVs, but the typed reports omit `lv_health_status`, `raid_sync_action`, `raid_mismatch_count`, and `copy_percent`. Existing LV reconciliation handles size and growth, with no failed-leg repair operation.

VG and PV reports already expose partial or missing state. Operators still need to know which LV has lost redundancy and how far its repair has progressed. Scans depend on block-resource events, so adding fields alone would leave the question of how health gets refreshed when a disk develops I/O errors but stays present. The inspected controllers and package recipe had no dmeventd integration.

LVM provides dmeventd monitoring and manual `lvconvert --repair`. Its default RAID fault policy is `warn`; automatic allocation requires a separate policy. These give Talos mechanisms to build on without assuming that every failed leg should be replaced automatically.

## Requested support

- [ ] Reports expose per-LV RAID health, repair progress, mismatches, and observation freshness.
- [ ] Device-mapper events or bounded polling refresh health even when devices stay present. Monitoring failures are visible.
- [ ] An explicit repair operation checks device identity and replacement capacity. Automatic replacement requires a documented policy.
- [ ] Tests verify data after failure, replacement, and restart during repair.

## References

- [Typed LV reports](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/pkg/lvm/lv.go#L18-L64)
- [Supported layouts](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/pkg/lvm/lv.go#L93-L145)
- [Scan loop](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_scan.go#L48-L125)
- [Refresh inputs](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_refresh_trigger.go#L27-L56)
- [Existing LV reconciliation](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_logical_volume_reconcile.go#L228-L247)

- [Monitoring unit](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/scripts/lvm2_monitoring_systemd_red_hat.service.in)
- [RAID fault policy](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/conf/example.conf.in#L1681-L1702)
title: LVM RAID needs per-LV health reporting and a supported repair operation

author: shanduur
body:
A RAID1 or RAID10 LV can retain enough copies to operate after a PV goes missing, while its VG is incomplete. Talos waits for `LVM_VG_NAME_COMPLETE` before running `vgchange -aay --autoactivation event`, and this path has no explicit degraded-activation fallback.

The supported boot behavior needs to be clear. If Talos allows degraded activation, it should retain LVM's safety checks and handle mixed VGs without blanket partial activation of linear or RAID0 volumes. If activation is blocked, the operator needs a bounded outcome and a status that explains why.

## Requested behavior

- [ ] The supported policy states when activation fails closed and when degraded activation is allowed.
- [ ] Any degraded path retains LVM safety checks and does not enable blanket partial activation.
- [ ] Blocked activation has a bounded outcome and an actionable status.
- [ ] VM tests cover RAID1, RAID10, unsafe failure patterns, and mixed VGs. Successful boots verify the original data.

## References

- [Completeness gate](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_activation.go#L160-L197)
- [Activation commands](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/pkg/lvm/activate.go#L13-L48)

- [Upstream event activation](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/udev/69-dm-lvm.rules.in#L65-L89)
- [Activation modes](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/conf/example.conf.in#L1890-L1910)
title: Define degraded boot support for LVM RAID volumes

author: shanduur
body:
Talos disables automatic LVM metadata backups with `backup = 0` and `archive = 0`. The configuration explains why: the root filesystem is read-only, and EPHEMERAL is an unsafe place to keep the backup.

That leaves a recovery gap. The LVM API exposes removal operations but no export or restore, and machine configuration does not preserve the actual PV UUIDs and extent mappings. On-PV metadata copies remain enabled, and external rescue tools may still recover the storage. A supported Talos workflow would let operators save the required metadata before they need those tools.

LVM already provides `vgcfgbackup`, `vgcfgrestore`, and metadata archives. Talos needs a way to retain versioned copies off-node, validate them against the target storage, and restore in an authorized, quiescent maintenance state. The policy also needs to cover an archive-storage failure before a metadata-changing operation.

## Requested support

- [ ] Operators can export metadata and retain versioned pre-change archives off-node.
- [ ] Archive identity and version checks reject mismatched or unsuitable restores.
- [ ] The policy defines what happens if archive storage fails before a metadata change.
- [ ] Restore requires authorization and a quiescent maintenance state.
- [ ] A recovery test verifies data checksums. Documentation distinguishes metadata backup from user-data backup.

## References

- [Disabled backup/archive policy](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/hack/lvm.conf#L1-L8)
- [Public LVM API](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/api/machine/lvm.proto#L10-L28)

- [Upstream defaults](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/conf/example.conf.in#L950-L976)
- [Backup limits](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/man/vgcfgbackup.8_des)
- [Restore semantics](https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/blob/d804677c7565bff40c87ed830473674119f23f6a/man/vgcfgrestore.8_des)
title: Provide LVM metadata export, off-node archives, and restore

author: shanduur
body:
Talos reports `sync_action`, but the inspected MD API and controllers have no check schedule, check or repair requests, mismatch count, or last-successful-check result. The existing XFS scrub scheduler checks the filesystem; it does not check agreement between MD mirror members.

mdadm supplies check timers and services for systemd, with the kernel performing the check. Talos needs an equivalent way to request and schedule checks for its supported RAID1 arrays, then retain the outcome across restart. Distribution packaging determines whether the upstream timers are enabled.

There is a safety detail to preserve in the API: MD `check` leaves readable mismatches uncorrected, but normal read-error recovery can still write recovered blocks. It is not strictly read-only. Repair also cannot determine which of two divergent copies contains correct user data, so it needs explicit authorization.

## Requested support

- [ ] Operators can request checks and configure a schedule with concurrency and I/O limits.
- [ ] Status reports progress, mismatches, errors, and persistent completion results.
- [ ] Restart or interruption does not count as successful completion.
- [ ] Repair requires explicit authorization and documents how it handles inconsistent copies.
- [ ] Tests cover read errors, mismatches, interruption, and concurrent rebuild activity.

## References

- [Current status schema](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/pkg/machinery/resources/storage/md_array_status.go#L25-L47)
- [Current MD API](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/api/machine/md.proto#L10-L18)
- [Existing distinct XFS scrub](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/block/fs_scrub_schedule.go#L22-L32)

- [Check timer](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/systemd/mdcheck_start.timer)
- [Check service](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/systemd/mdcheck_start.service)
- [Check versus repair and read-error semantics](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/md.4#L736-L780)
title: Add scheduled MD consistency checks and persistent results

author: shanduur
body:
VG and LV reconciliation collect operational errors, log them, and return to an event-only loop. They neither schedule a retry nor return those errors to the runtime.

If a create or extend command fails before changing any resource, nothing from that attempt necessarily wakes the controller again. The requested volume or size can remain unapplied until an unrelated event arrives.

A regression test should fail one command before it changes storage, restore backend availability, and withhold further resource events. Reconciliation should still retry and finish. A separate case should allow partial success, so the retry must inspect current state before issuing another mutation.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Transient errors trigger bounded retries without external events.
- [ ] Permanent configuration errors do not cause repeated mutation attempts.
- [ ] Each retry checks current storage state and handles partial success safely.
- [ ] Tests cover no-event recovery, persistent failure, and cancellation.

## References

- [VG event loop](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_volume_group_reconcile.go#L82-L132)
- [LV logged errors](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/lvm_logical_volume_reconcile.go#L176-L198)
title: LVM provisioning can stop retrying after a transient failure

author: shanduur
body:
An array becomes `Ready` when it is not `Rebuilding`, even though an idle mirror may have a failed member. The current status has no degraded count, healthy-member count, or per-member fault state. Some health-read errors are ignored too.

This matters when a failed disk stays enumerated. Both disks still match the selector and `sync_action` can be idle, leaving consumers with a provisioning status that says nothing about lost redundancy. A failed health read should also make health unknown instead of leaving callers to interpret missing data.

## Requested status changes

- [ ] Status distinguishes provisioning, availability, redundancy, and rebuild progress.
- [ ] Failed health reads produce an explicit unknown or stale observation.
- [ ] Tests cover an idle degraded array and failed health reads.
- [ ] Recovery tests wait for restored redundancy and verify data. Accepting `Ready` or `Rebuilding` is not enough.

## References

- [Ready assignment](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_array_reconcile.go#L226-L230)
- [Observation](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_array_reconcile.go#L348-L367)
- [Status schema](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/pkg/machinery/resources/storage/md_array_status.go#L25-L47)
- [Existing integration completion condition](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/integration/api/storage.go#L1480-L1485)
- [Kernel MD recovery behavior](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/md.4#L709-L723)
title: MD status cannot distinguish an idle degraded array from a healthy one

author: shanduur
body:
The last-resort controller consumes its grace timer before attempting `mdadm --run`. If the command fails, the controller logs the error and waits for another block-device or udev-service event. It does not rearm the timer.

A transient failure can therefore leave an otherwise recoverable array inactive indefinitely if nothing else changes. The monitor controller's restart backoff does not cover this activation path.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Retryable failures schedule bounded backoff, without a tight loop.
- [ ] Each attempt checks current array eligibility and prerequisite health.
- [ ] Retries stop when no eligible arrays remain or the controller stops.
- [ ] Tests cover no-event recovery and persistent failure. Retries do not add blanket `--force` assembly.

## References

- [Consumed timer and logged failure](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_last_resort.go#L94-L116)
- [Actual --run command](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/pkg/md/array.go#L210-L218)
- [Upstream timer](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/systemd/mdadm-last-resort@.timer)
- [Upstream service](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/systemd/mdadm-last-resort@.service)
title: A transient MD activation failure has no scheduled retry

author: shanduur
body:
For a two-slot mirror with healthy A and failed-but-attached B, selecting replacement C can make the reconciler request three active slots. It calculates target width from all attached members plus newly selected devices, without using the member roles parsed by the backend.

That leaves replacement intent ambiguous. A replacement can fill a vacancy after B detaches, but the same operation while B remains attached can become a growth request. The controller already waits for idle sync before mutation. The public MD API exposes only `Destroy`, so it also lacks a supported operator replacement operation.

## Replacement requirements

- [ ] Replacement, adding a spare, and growing active width have separate semantics. Existing intentional growth still works.
- [ ] Replacement preserves active width and checks the failed member identity.
- [ ] The operation rejects foreign devices and requires explicit destructive removal.
- [ ] Tests verify completed rebuild and data checksums, including recovery after interruption.

## References

- [Add/grow reconciliation](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_array_reconcile.go#L269-L333)
- [Member roles](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/pkg/md/array.go#L94-L114)
- [Public API](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/api/machine/md.proto#L10-L18)
- [Spare addition behavior](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/mdadm.8.in#L1309-L1320)
title: Replacing an attached failed MD member can request array growth

author: shanduur
body:
The MD reconciler checks for two matching disks before looking for an existing array. When one member of a RAID1 mirror disappears, reconciliation returns `Waiting` without reporting the surviving array's UUID or state.

A controller test reproduced this with a fake array that had two configured slots, one surviving member, and UUID `existing-degraded-array`. The controller published an empty UUID. It should observe the existing array before deciding whether there are enough disks to create a new one.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] The controller reports the existing array identity and availability with one surviving member.
- [ ] New array creation still requires enough disks.
- [ ] Tests cover a missing disk and a failed disk that remains present.

## References

- [Member-count gate](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_array_reconcile.go#L160-L208)
- [Existing delayed activation](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/b735fd68373a8b0738f235fb06728e406879df38/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/storage/md_last_resort.go)
- [Upstream last-resort unit](https://github.com/md-raid-utilities/mdadm/blob/8b414a0d4753693d67b9a5822994e5f0c91b0b0a/systemd/mdadm-last-resort@.service)
title: An existing MD array loses its status when one disk disappears

author: shanduur
body:
mdadm 4.6 writes monitor events to stderr. Talos passes stdout to the event callback and buffers stderr until the process exits, so the callback never receives the events that should advance `MDRefreshRequest`. The buffer can also grow without a limit while the monitor runs.

The existing test hides this because its shell fixture writes events to stdout. Changing the three `printf` statements in `TestMonitorStreamsEvents` to use `>&2` reproduces the failure: three events expected, none received. The unchanged MD and LVM package tests passed in a disposable export of this commit. This reproduction used the production wrapper with a shell fixture; no disk was failed.

Other block events can still refresh status, and the monitor already has restart backoff. The fix needs to deliver stderr events while mdadm is running and keep diagnostic storage bounded.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] A stderr event advances `MDRefreshRequest` while mdadm is running, without another device event.
- [ ] Diagnostic storage stays bounded. No-array termination remains quiet.
- [ ] Tests cover malformed output, cancellation, and restart without duplicate events.

## References

author: vitaly-zverev
body:
### Description

MDArrayStatus (storage.MDArrayReconcileController) reflects the RAID array's state correctly only at the moment of its own initial reconcile after boot. If the array's kernel-level state changes afterward (e.g. a recover resync started before or during boot completes later, while machined keeps running), the resource is never updated to reflect the new state — it stays stuck at whatever it observed on first reconcile, seemingly indefinitely, until the next reboot causes a fresh reconcile with correct, current data.

## Bug Report

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the VM with all 4 disks attached (drv1-drv4, virtio-scsi), cdrom on a separate AHCI controller.
2. Apply machine config with two `RAIDArrayConfig` documents (`boot0`, `extra0`) + `UnattendedInstallConfig` installing onto `boot0`:
   ```
   talosctl apply --nodes 127.0.0.1 -e 127.0.0.1 --insecure --file controlplane_boot_md_plus_extra_md.yaml
   ```
3. Bootstrap the cluster:
   ```
   talosctl bootstrap --nodes 127.0.0.1 -e 127.0.0.1 --talosconfig talosconfig
   ```
4. Shut the node down cleanly:
   ```
   talosctl shutdown --nodes 127.0.0.1 -e 127.0.0.1 --talosconfig talosconfig
   ```
5. Restart the VM **without drv1** (i.e. `boot0` now has only one of its two members, `sdb`/drv2 — array boots degraded).
6. Re-apply the same machine config:
   ```
   talosctl apply --nodes 127.0.0.1 -e 127.0.0.1 --insecure --file controlplane_boot_md_plus_extra_md.yaml
   ```
7. Shut the node down again:
   ```
   talosctl shutdown --nodes 127.0.0.1 -e 127.0.0.1 --talosconfig talosconfig
   ```
8. Restart the VM with the original 4-disk topology (drv1 reattached).
9. `boot0`'s missing member (`sda`, formerly drv1) rejoins and mdadm performs a `recover` resync (kernel logs it with an elevated raid-disk role, e.g. `sda[2]` instead of `sda[0]`).

## Expected behavior

After the kernel-driven resync completes within a running boot, `MDArrayStatus` for `boot0` should transition to `status: ready` / `syncAction: idle` without requiring a reboot, matching the live kernel-reported state.

## Actual behavior

`/proc/mdstat` shows the resync has completed (no in-progress percentage, clean `[UU]`):
```
md127 : active raid1 sda[2] sdb[1]
      20971392 blocks super 1.0 [2/2] [UU]
```
Confirmed also via sysfs:
- `/sys/block/md127/md/sync_action` = `idle`
- `/sys/block/md127/md/sync_completed` = `none`
- `/sys/block/md127/md/degraded` = `0`

But `talosctl get mdarraystatuses boot0 -o yaml` still reports the array as rebuilding, and the resource has never been updated since creation:
```yaml
spec:
    status: rebuilding
    syncAction: recover
    arrayState: active
metadata:
    version: 1
    created: 2026-09-09T10:29:58Z
    updated: 2026-09-09T10:29:58Z   # identical to created — never refreshed
```
This persists indefinitely across repeated checks. The sibling array `extra0` (never degraded) correctly reports `status: ready` / `syncAction: idle`.

## Key observation confirming the root cause

The resource's `created` and `updated` timestamps are identical (`2026-09-09T10:29:58Z`) and `metadata.version` stays at `1` no matter how long the node runs afterward (checked repeatedly, minutes apart, kernel-confirmed `idle`/`degraded: 0` throughout). This timestamp corresponds to the moment `machined` started after the final boot (step 8) and `MDArrayReconcileController` reconciled `boot0` for the first time, correctly observing it mid-`recover` at that instant. The resource has not been updated even once since — meaning the controller performs a one-shot observation at initial reconcile and never re-observes `sync_action`/array state afterward, rather than merely "missing the completion event" as a transient race.

## Suspected cause

`MDArrayReconcileController` snapshots the array state once at initial reconcile (here, at boot in step 8, while recovery was in progress) and never re-observes it again afterward — it does not appear to re-poll `sync_action`/array state, and/or is not subscribed to the udev/netlink `change` event that fires when `sync_action` transitions to `idle`. This is not a narrow race on catching the completion event; the resource simply stops being reconciled after its first observation for the lifetime of the boot.

Confirmed this is boot-scoped, not permanent: rebooting the node again (step 10 below) causes the controller to reconcile from scratch and correctly report the now-healthy state.

## Additional step confirming the finding

10. Reboot the node again (`talosctl reboot`), without changing disk topology. `boot0` is now healthy/idle at the kernel level (unchanged from before). After this reboot, `talosctl get mdarraystatuses boot0 -o yaml` correctly reports:
    ```yaml
    spec:
        status: ready
        syncAction: idle
        arrayState: active
    metadata:
        version: 1
        created: 2026-09-09T10:58:43Z
        updated: 2026-09-09T10:58:43Z   # new reconcile, fresh timestamp, correct state
    ```
    This confirms the controller's *logic* for determining status is correct — it correctly read `ready`/`idle` when reconciling at this new boot. The bug is specifically that it does not re-observe state changes to an *already-reconciled* array within a running `machined` process; it only reflects the state truthfully at the moment of its first reconcile per boot.

## Additional data

Independently verified that RAID membership metadata is correctly persisted on the underlying qcow2 images at all times (via `qemu-nbd --read-only` + `mdadm --examine` on the host while the VM was shut down) — `Array UUID`/`Name` match what Talos exposes via `DiscoveredVolume` and `md-name-talos:boot0`/`md-uuid-*` symlinks. The issue is isolated to the `MDArrayStatus` resource not refreshing, not to the underlying RAID/mdadm behavior.

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.14.0
- Kubernetes version: v1.36.3
- Platform: QEMU (metal-installer), two RAID1 arrays via RAIDArrayConfig (boot0: /dev/sda+/dev/sdb, extra0: /dev/sdc+/dev/sdd), metadata "1.0"
title: Talos mdarraystatus stale

author: wrightpt
body:
We use Talos v1.13.4 and a read-only, same-process Linux adjtimex evidence gate
for public-data collection. Our 250 ms limit applies to the conservative UTC
error bound, not merely the last measured offset or the synchronized flag.

Native time-controller logs on September 8 recorded accepted non-spike
responses at 15:23:39.325, 15:57:47.337 and 16:31:55.349 UTC. Each selected
a 2048-second next interval; the final reported slew was 132.639 microseconds.
Later, native producer receipts during 16:43–16:48 UTC had error bounds of
332.708–482.425 ms. The kernel maximum-error estimate ages between accepted
responses. We retain those failed receipts; we do not claim the wall clock was
wrong by that amount or that NTP explains separate application request delays.

We inspected the released v1.14.0 source
`9abd05af449ebf9cb1827648298291afce18d714` and upstream main
`682a0c96d808dcb3e890fb06e8270bd4f1ce1e74`. The NTP constants, scheduler,
TimeSyncConfig and production sync controller are byte-identical at these refs.
We found the 32–2048 second default bounds and Go-level MaxPoll, but no supported
configuration field to cap the production synchronizer's maximum interval.
The spike-filter repair in PR 13908 does not expose such a field.

Is there a supported native configuration or supported patch for limiting the
maximum polling interval to 128 seconds while preserving the existing minimum,
single time-discipline owner, response validation, spike rejection and retry
behavior? If none exists, would an optional validated maximum interval be an
acceptable upstream contribution, and which release/support route is appropriate?

We have an isolated candidate that keeps the released default when absent and
accepts powers of two from 32 to 2048 seconds. Reducing the cap shortens a pending
wait; increasing it does not postpone an already due sample. Configuration
changes retain spike state and kernel error evidence. Synthetic tests and
isolated installed-OS upgrade, reboot and explicit official-image rollback
checks are available. This candidate has not been installed on a shared node
and has not been represented as upstream-supported. We would provide a focused
patch and sanitized reproduction upon request and explicit approval.

We are seeking a supported remedy, not a bypass of the measurement limit.
A shorter interval cannot guarantee valid evidence through rejected responses
or outages; those intervals must remain ineligible.

Reference sources:

- [v1.14.0 TimeSyncConfig](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/9abd05af449ebf9cb1827648298291afce18d714/pkg/machinery/config/types/network/time_sync.go)
- [v1.14.0 NTP scheduler](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/9abd05af449ebf9cb1827648298291afce18d714/internal/pkg/ntp/ntp.go)
- [v1.14.0 NTP constants](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/9abd05af449ebf9cb1827648298291afce18d714/internal/pkg/ntp/consts.go)
- [v1.14.0 production sync controller](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/9abd05af449ebf9cb1827648298291afce18d714/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/time/sync.go)
- [Spike-filter repair PR 13908](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/pull/13908)
title: Supported native NTP poll cap for bounded UTC uncertainty

author: Nosmoht
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

An extension service that *provides* a block device (ZFS, iSCSI — anything backing a CSI
driver) is stopped, and 10 seconds later killed, while the pods and kernel subsystems
consuming its devices are still running. The container runtime it needs in order to shut
down cleanly is itself only signalled 30 seconds later.

**Correction (see the comment below): the reboot was `--mode force`, not graceful.** The
log carries `reboot sequence: 1 phase(s)`, which is the `RebootRequest_FORCE` branch in
`Sequencer.Reboot` — so `StopAllPods` and the whole graceful phase list were skipped by
design. What still ran is machined's `defer system.Services(c.Runtime()).Shutdown(ctx)`
(`internal/app/machined/main.go`), i.e. the full `stopServices` teardown below. The rest of
this report describes that teardown accurately; the trigger does not.

On a `--mode force` reboot of a worker running the ZFS extension with DRBD volumes on
zvols, the ZFS provider is gone at `T+10s` and the runtime holding its zvols open is
signalled at `T+30s`. In that window DRBD logs `write: error=10` / `[local-io-error]` and
detaches its backing device; LINSTOR then sets `DrbdOptions/SkipDisk` on the real IO error,
so the replica stays detached across the boot as well. In one 9-node cluster this hit 17
volumes across 5 of 6 storage workers during a rolling reboot, each needing manual repair.

**Why the existing stop ordering does not help.** `stopServices` does implement ordering:
it builds `reverseDependencies` from each service's `DependsOn()` and makes every service
wait (max 30s) for the services that depend on it before shutting down
(`internal/app/machined/pkg/system/system.go`; identical at `v1.13.3` and `v1.13.10`).

The problem is the direction. For an extension service:

```go
// internal/app/machined/pkg/system/services/extension.go, v1.13.10
func (svc *Extension) DependsOn(r runtime.Runtime) []string {
	deps := []string{"containerd"}
	for _, dep := range svc.Spec.Depends {
		if dep.Service != "" { deps = append(deps, dep.Service) }
	}
	return deps
}
```

`spec.depends` is a **start-order** declaration — the ZFS extension names `containerd`,
`udevd` and `cri`, which is what it waits for on boot. Talos reuses those same edges as the
stop order, inverted:

- `reverseDependencies["cri" | "udevd" | "containerd"]` each contain `ext-zfs-service`,
  which is why all three wait and all three hit the 30s cap.
- `reverseDependencies["ext-zfs-service"]` is **empty**, so it waits for nothing. Nothing
  declares a dependency *on* an extension service, and no built-in service can:
  at `v1.13.10`, `Kubelet.DependsOn` returns `["cri"]` and both `CRI.DependsOn` and
  `Containerd.DependsOn` return `nil` (on `main`, `CRI` additionally names `sandboxd` when
  the sandbox is enabled) — all compiled in.

A service that both *consumes* the runtime and *provides* devices to that runtime's
workloads cannot be ordered correctly, because one declaration serves both directions.

Two things compound it:

1. `extension.go` never calls `WithGracefulShutdownTimeout`, so extension services get the
   `runner.Options` default of `10 * time.Second` before SIGKILL, with no machine-config
   knob to raise it.
2. A SIGKILLed service never reports `(Finished)` — there is no Down event for it in the
   log at all — so the three services that *were* waiting for it burn the full 30s. The
   ordering that does exist is defeated by the kill.

`PreShutdownService` / `PreShutdownFunc` in `system.go` looks like the right hook, but it
is a Go interface on compiled-in services; an extension cannot implement it.

**Not specific to ZFS or DRBD.** `ext-iscsid` is stopped in the same 5ms window (see the
log). Any extension providing block devices, with consumers living in pods or kernel
modules rather than in Talos services, has the same shape. DRBD is only what made it
visible, because a detach is durable.

**What would fix it**, in rough order of preference:

1. A stop-order declaration independent of `spec.depends` — an extension may state that it
   must stop *after* `kubelet`/`cri`, so device providers drain after the workload plane
   and before `containerd`.
2. Or: treat container-mode extension services as a shutdown phase between the workload
   plane and `containerd`, with no per-extension declaration.
3. Failing either: make `GracefulShutdownTimeout` configurable per extension service, and
   emit a Down state event when a service is SIGKILLed so waiters stop burning the cap.

Independent of the above, the timeout diagnostic is unusable:
`log.Printf("gave up on %s while stopping %q", allDeps, ...)` always prints an empty list,
because `all.Wait` sets each condition slot to `nil` as its goroutine returns and
`all.String` skips `nil`. By the time the timeout is logged there is nothing left to name,
so the message cannot tell an operator which dependency was slow.

Adjacent but distinct: #13354 and #14105 concern teardown of *Talos-managed* volumes at
shutdown; this is about the ordering of extension **services** against their consumers.

### Logs

From the node's own persisted `/var/log/kernel.log`, one `--mode force` reboot:

```
14:41:26.094  [talos] starting upgrade: installer_image=...
14:41:26.992  [talos] upgrade completed successfully: exit_code=0
14:42:02.292  [talos] reboot via API received
14:42:02.302  [talos] reboot sequence: 1 phase(s)          <- FORCE: no cleanup/stopAll phases
14:42:02.302  [talos] phase reboot (1/1): 1 tasks(s)
14:42:02.332  service[kubelet](Stopping): Sending SIGTERM to task kubelet
14:42:02.332  service[ext-iscsid](Stopping): Sending SIGTERM to task ext-iscsid
14:42:02.333  service[ext-zfs-service](Stopping): Sending SIGTERM to task ext-zfs-service
14:42:02.455  service[ext-iscsid](Finished): Service finished successfully
14:42:12.359  service[ext-zfs-service](Stopping): Sending SIGKILL to task ext-zfs-service
14:42:32.326  gave up on  while stopping "cri"
14:42:32.326  gave up on  while stopping "udevd"
14:42:32.326  gave up on  while stopping "containerd"
14:42:32.326  service[cri](Stopping): Sending SIGTERM
14:42:32.370  service[cri](Finished): Service finished successfully
```

`ext-zfs-service` has no `(Finished)` line between the SIGKILL and its restart after the
boot — it never reaches a Down state.

Its start-order declaration, from the boot afterwards:

```
service[ext-zfs-service](Waiting): Waiting for service "containerd" to be "up", service "udevd" to be "up", ...
service[ext-zfs-service](Waiting): Waiting for service "cri" to be registered
```

### Environment

- Talos version: `v1.13.3`, rebooting into `v1.13.10`. The code paths quoted above are
  identical at both tags.
- Kubernetes version: `v1.36.0`
- Platform: bare-metal (`metal`), ZFS + DRBD system extensions, LINSTOR/Piraeus CSI.
- Reboot: `talosctl reboot --mode force`, issued separately after `talosctl upgrade`
  reported `exit_code=0`.
title: Extension services that provide block devices are stopped and killed before their consumers

```sh
$ _out/talosctl-linux-amd64 --nodes 172.20.0.5 get containerstatus               55s 15:42:53
NODE         NAMESPACE    TYPE              ID      VERSION   STATE     HEALTH    RESTARTS   IMAGE
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   app     524       running   healthy   51         sha256:65645c7bb6a0661892a8b03b89d0743208a18dd2f3f17a54ef4b76fb8e2f2a10
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   redis   311       running   healthy   55         sha256:ff02b58f971e7d7d156a1267e283fcbbeee91773b6aa36c49dac28ecfe28eadf
```

If the dependency container (redis) is broken (transitions to non-healthy state), the dependent (nginx app) is not stopped if it was already started at some point (when redis was healthy).

However, if you remove both `ContainerConfigs`, and then re-add only `app` (nginx):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1alpha1
kind: ContainerConfig
name: app
image: docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-alpine
dependsOn:
  containers:
    - redis
mounts:
  - tmpfs:
      size: 128MiB
      destination: /var/cache/nginx
network:
  mode: host
security:
  capabilities:
    add: [CHOWN, SETUID, SETGID, NET_BIND_SERVICE]
```

Machine config validation fails (as expected):
```yaml
# Editing MachineConfigs.config.talos.dev/v1alpha1 at node 172.20.0.5
# 
# rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = 1 error occurred:
#       * container "app" depends on container "redis", which is not configured
```

If you also add the `redis` `ContainerConfig`, but ensure it never comes up as healthy:
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1alpha1
kind: ContainerConfig
name: app
image: docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-alpine
dependsOn:
  containers:
    - redis
mounts:
  - tmpfs:
      size: 128MiB
      destination: /var/cache/nginx
network:
  mode: host
security:
  capabilities:
    add: [CHOWN, SETUID, SETGID, NET_BIND_SERVICE]
---
apiVersion: v1alpha1
kind: ContainerConfig
name: redis
image: docker.io/library/redis:7-alpine
security:
  capabilities:
    add: [SETUID, SETGID]
args: ["--BOOM"]
```

Then `app` (nginx) should be stuck with health `pending`, until `redis` comes achieves a healthy state with an age of >= 5sec (not crashlooping).
```sh
_out/talosctl-linux-amd64 --nodes 172.20.0.5 get containerstatus                7s 17:50:09
NODE         NAMESPACE    TYPE              ID      VERSION   STATE     HEALTH     RESTARTS   IMAGE
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   app     3         pending   pending    0          sha256:65645c7bb6a0661892a8b03b89d0743208a18dd2f3f17a54ef4b76fb8e2f2a10
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   redis   15        exited    degraded   3          sha256:ff02b58f971e7d7d156a1267e283fcbbeee91773b6aa36c49dac28ecfe28eadf
```

Once `redis` is fixed (remove the bad args), both containers should come up as healthy:
```sh
_out/talosctl-linux-amd64 --nodes 172.20.0.5 get containerstatus                   17:53:10
NODE         NAMESPACE    TYPE              ID      VERSION   STATE     HEALTH    RESTARTS   IMAGE
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   app     5         running   healthy   0          sha256:65645c7bb6a0661892a8b03b89d0743208a18dd2f3f17a54ef4b76fb8e2f2a10
172.20.0.5   containers   ContainerStatus   redis   216       running   healthy   39         sha256:ff02b58f971e7d7d156a1267e283fcbbeee91773b6aa36c49dac28ecfe28eadf
```

author: lucndm
body:
## Description

When `StartAllServices` gives up after `BootTimeout`, the failure is
reported as a bare `context deadline exceeded`:

```
boot error: sequence failed: error running phase 9 in boot sequence:
task 1/1: failed, 1 error occurred: * context deadline exceeded
```

On a node where a service is stuck in `Waiting` (e.g. an extension
service whose condition can never be satisfied — a qemu-guest-agent
extension on a VM without the guest-agent channel, in our case), this
ends in a FATAL reboot loop which is nearly impossible to diagnose: no
log, event, or error names the offending service.

Service conditions now carry their description in the context error for
deadline errors, so the same failure reads:

```
* service "ext-qemu-guest-agent" to be up/finished: context deadline exceeded
```

Canceled waits still return the bare `context.Canceled`, so the collapse
behavior in `conditions.WaitForAll` is unchanged; only deadline errors
carry the description (deadline errors were already returned as a
multierror and never hit the collapsed path).

Fixes #14373

## Testing

- New `TestServiceConditionDeadlineErrorMessage`: covers both the
  wait-event and wait-register paths, asserting the description and
  `context.DeadlineExceeded` are present, and that cancellation keeps
  returning the bare `context.Canceled`.
- Existing condition/system tests pass (including the exact-sentinel
  assertion in `conditions`).
- `make initramfs kernel` builds cleanly.
title: fix: name unmet services when the boot services phase times out

author: lucndm
body:
## Description

When a service is configured to run inside the shared sandbox namespace,
the sandbox launcher is published asynchronously by the sandboxd service
runner. A service can reach its first launch before the launcher exists
(CRI is started by the early services phase, sandboxd only starts later
in startEverything), which today fails the launch with:

```
sandbox namespace not available yet
```

and puts the service into a fail/restart loop (5s interval) until the
namespace appears — visible as a minutes-long DEGRADED window on every
boot with workload isolation enabled.

Instead of failing, resolve the getter in a loop and launch once the
launcher is published, aborting on context cancellation. The getter is
still resolved per launch, so a recreated namespace is picked up exactly
as before.

Fixes #14374

## Testing

- `TestSandboxUnavailable` updated: Run now waits and returns the
  context error when the launcher never appears.
- New `TestSandboxWaitForLauncher`: getter flips from nil to a mock
  launcher; Run succeeds and records a Waiting state while waiting.
- All existing process runner / restart / system service tests pass.
- `make initramfs kernel` builds cleanly.
title: fix: wait for the sandbox launcher instead of failing the first launch

author: utkuozdemir
body:
When the tunnel connection fails, the retry that should bring it back never runs:

1. Before starting the tunnel relay, the controller cancels the retry with `relayRetryTimer.Reset(0)`, which discards the timer so `relayRetryTimer.C()` becomes a nil channel.
2. The controller then waits on that nil `relayRetryTimer.C()`, which never fires.
3. When the relay fails, it reschedules with `relayRetryTimer.Reset(retryIn)`, which builds a new timer, but the select is still parked on the old nil channel and never sees it.
4. The relay is never restarted, so the tunnel stays down until the node reboots.

Keep a single `time.Timer` inside `ResettableTimer` for the life of the controller and only stop or re-arm it, so `relayRetryTimer.C()` is always the same non-nil channel and the rescheduled retry reaches the select.
title: fix: reconnect the WireGuard over gRPC tunnel after a failure

author: lexfrei
body:
# Pull Request

## What? (description)

`InsecureFlags` gets an `AddPersistentFlags`, and `talosctl meta` switches to it, so `meta write` and `meta delete` see `--insecure` and `--cert-fingerprint` again. Tests cover parsing both flags on the two subcommands, plus a walk over the command tree that fails if a command which runs nothing carries `--insecure` as a local flag.

## Why? (reasoning)

Fixes #14346

Since v1.14.0 `talosctl meta write --insecure` fails with `unknown flag: --insecure`. #13500 replaced `metaCmd.PersistentFlags()` with `InsecureFlags.AddFlags(metaCmd)`, and that one registers in the local flag set. Cobra merges a parent's persistent flags into a child, not its local ones, and `metaCmd` is `Args: cobra.NoArgs` with no `RunE`, so the flag had nowhere to land. `talosctl meta --help` still listed it.

Writing a META key goes over the maintenance service, before a machine config exists, so there is no other route to that operation.

`wipe` registers the mix-in on the subcommands that run and works. Persistent flags on the parent keep both `meta write --insecure` and `meta --insecure write` working, the same as v1.13.7.

## Acceptance

Please use the following checklist:

- [x] you linked an issue (if applicable)
- [x] you included tests (if applicable)
- [x] you ran conformance (`make conformance`)
- [x] you formatted your code (`make fmt`)
- [x] you linted your code (`make lint`)
- [x] you generated documentation (`make docs`)
- [x] you ran unit-tests (`make unit-tests`)

Conform passes everything except the GPG identity check, which wants the signing key to belong to a siderolabs org member. The CLI reference was regenerated with the same generator the docs target runs, and it reproduces the committed file byte for byte on a clean tree.

author: tbavelier
body:
## What?

Add an opt-in static networking path for local QEMU clusters, enabled with `TALOS_QEMU_STATIC_IP=1`.

When enabled, this change:

- disables DHCP for the QEMU management network;
- assigns each node its already allocated address and default route through a small, compressed `talos.config.early` document;
- persists the same static address in the full machine configuration; and
- uses the first control-plane node directly for the Kubernetes endpoint instead of the host-side load balancer.

The existing QEMU behavior is unchanged unless the environment variable is set. I used an environment variable for this draft to avoid committing to a public CLI interface as it's a **hack only meant for discussion.**

## Why?

On my managed macOS machine, `talosctl cluster create qemu` consistently stalls while applying configuration. Packet captures on the VM bridge show DHCP Discover packets from both guests, but no DHCP Offer is returned. The generated host firewall rules explicitly permit traffic within the QEMU subnet, and changing the CIDR does not help.

The result is that the nodes never receive their allocated addresses and the Talos API at the first control-plane address cannot be reached. Host-side helper services such as the load balancer are also unreliable in this environment, which is why this path uses the control-plane address directly.

An initial workaround used the Linux `ip=` kernel argument. That worked with a v1.14 image on this machine, but it is not robust: with the current arm64 image, `virtio_net` is loaded as a module after the kernel's built-in IP autoconfiguration. The kernel waited 120 seconds, selected `bond0`, and the real QEMU interface (`enp0s6` in that build) appeared only after userspace started.

Using `talos.config.early` avoids depending on PCI-derived interface names or on the NIC being available during kernel IP autoconfiguration. In an end-to-end test from current `main`, the real NIC appeared at 1.3 seconds, the static address was applied at 2.4 seconds, the full machine configuration was accepted at 6.5 seconds, and both the control-plane and worker nodes reached Kubernetes `Ready`.

I am opening this as a draft as this is not meant to be merged, simply for discussion.

