## [Talos 1.9.0-beta.0](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.9.0-beta.0) (2024-12-02) Welcome to the v1.9.0-beta.0 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Auditd Talos Linux now starts a auditd service by default. Logs can be read with `talosctl logs auditd`. ### `talosctl cgroups` The `talosctl cgroups` command has been added to the `talosctl` tool. This command allows you to view the cgroup resource consumption and limits for a machine, e.g. `talosctl cgroups --preset memory`. ### cgroups version 1 Support for cgroupsv1 is deprecated, and will be removed in Talos 1.10 (for non-container mode). ### Custom search domains for Talos nodes Talos now allows to supports specifying custom search domains for Talos nodes using new config field `machine.network.searchDomains` For the host it will look something like this: ``` nameserver 127.0.0.53 search my-custom-search-name.com my-custom-search-name2.com ``` For the pods it will look something like this: ``` search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local my-custom-search-name.com my-custom-search-name2.com nameserver 10.96.0.10 options ndots:5 ``` ### Device Selectors Talos now supports matching on permanent hardware (MAC) address of the network interfaces. This is specifically useful to match bond members, as they change their hardware addresses when they become part of the bond. ### Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) Starting with Talos 1.9, the `i915` and `amdgpu` DRM drivers will be dropped from the Talos squashfs. There will be new system extensions named `i915` and `amdgpu` that would contain both the drivers and firmware packaged together. Upgrades via Image Factory will automatically include the new extensions if previously `i915-ucode` or `amdgpu-firmware` were used. ### Image Cache Talos now supports providing a local [Image Cache](https://www.talos.dev/v1.9/talos-guides/configuration/image-cache/) for container images. ### Kube APIServer Authorization Config Starting with Talos 1.9, `.cluster.apiServer.authorizationConfig` field supports setting [Kubernetes API server authorization modes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authorization/#using-configuration-file-for-authorization) using the `--authorization-config` flag. The machine config field supports a list of `authorizers`. For eg: ```yaml cluster: apiServer: authorizationConfig: - type: Node name: Node - type RBAC name: rbac ``` For new cluster if the Kubernetes API server supports the `--authorization-config` flag, it'll be used by default instead of the `--authorization-mode` flag. By default Talos will always add the `Node` and ` RBAC` authorizers to the list. When upgrading if either a user-provided `authorization-mode` or `authorization-webhook-*` flag is set via `.cluster.apiServer.extraArgs`, it'll be used instead of the new `AuthorizationConfig`. Current authorization config can be viewed by running: `talosctl get authorizationconfigs.kubernetes.talos.dev -o yaml` ### OCI Base Runtime Spec Talos now allows to [modify the OCI base runtime spec for the container runtime](https://www.talos.dev/v1.9/advanced/oci-base-spec/). ### Registry Mirrors In versions before Talos 1.9, there was a discrepancy between the way Talos itself and CRI plugin resolves registry mirrors: Talos will never fall back to the default registry if endpoints are configured, while CRI plugin will. > Note: Talos Linux pulls images for the `installer`, `kubelet`, `etcd`, while all workload images are pulled by the CRI plugin. In Talos 1.9 this was fixed, so that by default an upstream registry is used as a fallback in all cases, while new registry mirror configuration option `.skipFallback` can be used to disable this behavior both for Talos and CRI plugin. ### talosctl disks The command `talosctl disks` was removed, please use `talosctl get disks`, `talosctl get systemdisk`, and `talosctl get blockdevices` instead. ### talosctl wipe The new command `talosctl wipe disk` allows to wipe a disk or a partition which is not used as a volume. ### udevd Talos previously used `eudev` to provide `udevd`, now it uses `systemd-udevd` instead. ### Component Updates * Linux: 6.12.1 * containerd: 2.0.0 * Flannel: 0.26.1 * Kubernetes: 1.32.0-rc.0 * runc: 1.2.1 * CoreDNS: 1.12.0 Talos is built with Go 1.23.3. ### User Namespaces Talos Linux now supports running Kubernetes pods with user namespaces enabled. Refer to the [documentation](https://www.talos.dev/v1.9/kubernetes-guides/configuration/usernamespace/) for more information. ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Noel Georgi * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Dmitry Sharshakov * Joakim Nohlgård * Jean-Francois Roy * Nico Berlee * Steven Kreitzer * Utku Ozdemir * blablu * Adolfo Ochagavía * Alessio Moiso * Dan Rue * David Backeus * Devin Buhl * Eddie Wang * Florian Ströger * Hexoplon * Jakob Maležič * Jasmin * Justin Garrison * KBAegis * Mike Beaumont * Mohammad Amin Mokhtari * Nebula * OliviaBarrington * Philip Schmid * Philipp Kleber * Remko Molier * Robby Ciliberto * Roman Ivanov * Ryan Borstelmann * Rémi Paulmier * Sam Stelfox * Serge Logvinov * Sergey Melnik * Spencer Smith * SpiReCZ * Steven Cassamajor * Tim Jones * Variant9 * adilTepe * egrosdou01 * ekarlso * naed3r * nevermarine * solidDoWant * sophia-coldren ### Changes

## [Talos 1.9.0-alpha.3](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.9.0-alpha.3) (2024-11-25) Welcome to the v1.9.0-alpha.3 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### AppArmor Talos Linux starting with v1.9 will ship with SELinux LSM enabled by default. If you need to use AppArmor LSM add the following to the machine configuration: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - -selinux - lsm=lockdown,capability,yama,apparmor,bpf - apparmor=1 ``` ### Auditd Talos Linux now starts a auditd service by default. Logs can be read with `talosctl logs auditd`. ### `talosctl cgroups` The `talosctl cgroups` command has been added to the `talosctl` tool. This command allows you to view the cgroup resource consumption and limits for a machine, e.g. `talosctl cgroups --preset memory`. ### Device Selectors Talos now supports matching on permanent hardware (MAC) address of the network interfaces. This is specifically useful to match bond members, as they change their hardware addresses when they become part of the bond. ### Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) Starting with Talos 1.9, the `i915` and `amdgpu` DRM drivers will be dropped from the Talos squashfs. There will be new system extensions named `i915` and `amdgpu` that would contain both the drivers and firmware packaged together. Upgrades via Image Factory will automatically include the new extensions if previously `i915-ucode` or `amdgpu-firmware` were used. ### Registry Mirrors In versions before Talos 1.9, there was a discrepancy between the way Talos itself and CRI plugin resolves registry mirrors: Talos will never fall back to the default registry if endpoints are configured, while CRI plugin will. > Note: Talos Linux pulls images for the `installer`, `kubelet`, `etcd`, while all workload images are pulled by the CRI plugin. In Talos 1.9 this was fixed, so that by default an upstream registry is used as a fallback in all cases, while new registry mirror configuration option `.skipFallback` can be used to disable this behavior both for Talos and CRI plugin. ### talosctl disks The command `talosctl disks` was removed, please use `talosctl get disks`, `talosctl get systemdisk`, and `talosctl get blockdevices` instead. ### talosctl wipe The new command `talosctl wipe disk` allows to wipe a disk or a partition which is not used as a volume. ### udevd Talos previously used `eudev` to provide `udevd`, now it uses `systemd-udevd` instead. ### Component Updates * Linux: 6.6.60 * containerd: 2.0.0 * Flannel: 0.26.0 * Kubernetes: 1.32.0-beta.0 * runc: 1.2.1 Talos is built with Go 1.23.3. ### User Namespaces Talos Linux now supports running Kubernetes pods with user namespaces enabled. Refer to the [documentation](https://www.talos.dev/v1.9/kubernetes-guides/configuration/usernamespace/) for more information. ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Noel Georgi * Dmitry Sharshakov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Joakim Nohlgård * Jean-Francois Roy * Utku Ozdemir * blablu * Adolfo Ochagavía * Alessio Moiso * Dan Rue * David Backeus * Eddie Wang * Florian Ströger * Hexoplon * Jakob Maležič * KBAegis * Mike Beaumont * Nebula * Nico Berlee * OliviaBarrington * Philip Schmid * Philipp Kleber * Remko Molier * Robby Ciliberto * Roman Ivanov * Ryan Borstelmann * Sam Stelfox * Serge Logvinov * Sergey Melnik * Spencer Smith * SpiReCZ * Steven Cassamajor * Steven Kreitzer * Tim Jones * Variant9 * adilTepe * ekarlso * naed3r * nevermarine * solidDoWant * sophia-coldren ### Changes

## [Talos 1.9.0-alpha.2](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.9.0-alpha.2) (2024-11-08) Welcome to the v1.9.0-alpha.2 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### AppArmor Talos Linux starting with v1.9 will ship with SELinux LSM enabled by default. If you need to use AppArmor LSM add the following to the machine configuration: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - -selinux - lsm=lockdown,capability,yama,apparmor,bpf - apparmor=1 ``` ### Auditd Talos Linux now starts a auditd service by default. Logs can be read with `talosctl logs auditd`. ### `talosctl cgroups` The `talosctl cgroups` command has been added to the `talosctl` tool. This command allows you to view the cgroup resource consumption and limits for a machine, e.g. `talosctl cgroups --preset memory`. ### udevd Talos previously used `udevd` to provide `udevd`, now it uses `systemd-udevd` instead. ### Component Updates Linux: 6.6.59 containerd: 2.0.0 Flannel: 0.26.0 Kubernetes: 1.32.0-beta.0 runc: 1.2.1 Talos is built with Go 1.23.2. ### User Namespaces Talos Linux now supports running Kubernetes pods with user namespaces enabled. Refer to the [documentation](https://www.talos.dev/v1.9/kubernetes-guides/configuration/usernamespace/) for more information. ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Noel Georgi * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Dmitry Sharshakov * Joakim Nohlgård * Jean-Francois Roy * Utku Ozdemir * blablu * Adolfo Ochagavía * Dan Rue * David Backeus * Eddie Wang * Florian Ströger * Hexoplon * Jakob Maležič * KBAegis * Mike Beaumont * Nebula * Nico Berlee * Philip Schmid * Philipp Kleber * Remko Molier * Robby Ciliberto * Ryan Borstelmann * Serge Logvinov * Spencer Smith * Steven Cassamajor * Tim Jones * adilTepe * ekarlso * naed3r * nevermarine * solidDoWant ### Changes

## [Talos 1.8.0](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.8.0) (2024-09-23) Welcome to the v1.8.0 release of Talos! Starting with Talos v1.8.0, only standard assets would be published as github release assets. These include: * `cloud-images.json` * `talosctl` binaries * `kernel` * `initramfs` * `metal` iso and disk images * `talosctl-cni-bundle` All other release assets can be downloaded from [Image Factory](https://www.talos.dev/latest/talos-guides/install/boot-assets/#image-factory). Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Node Annotations Talos Linux now supports configuring Kubernetes node annotations via machine configuration (`.machine.nodeAnnotations`) in a way similar to node labels. ### Workload Apparmor Profile Talos Linux can now apply the default AppArmor profiles to all workloads started via containerd, if the machine is installed with the AppArmor LSM enforced via the extraKernelArgs. Eg: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - security=apparmor ``` ### Bridge Interface Talos Linux now support configuring 'vlan_filtering' for bridge interfaces. ### Machine Configuration via Kernel Command Line Talos Linux supports supplying zstd-compressed, base64-encoded machine configuration small documents via the kernel command line parameter `talos.config.inline`. ### CNI Plugins Talos Linux now bundles by default the following standard CNI plugins: * `bridge` * `firewall` * `flannel` * `host-local` * `loopback` * `portmap` The Talos bundled Flannel manifest was simplified to remove the `install-cni` step. ### Accessing `/dev/net/tun` in Kubernetes Pods Talos Linux ships with `runc` 1.2, which [drops](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/3468) legacy rule to expose `/dev/net/tun` devices by default in the container. If you need to access `/dev/net/tun` in your Kubernetes pods (e.g. running Tailscale as a Kubernetes pod), you can add use [device plugins](https:/www.talos.dev/v1.8/kubernetes-guides/configuration/device-plugins/) to expose `/dev/net/tun` to the pod. ### Diagnostics Talos Linux now shows diagnostics information for common problems related to misconfiguration via `talosctl health` and Talos dashboard. ### Disk Management Talos Linux now supports [configuration](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/disk-management/#machine-configuration) for the `EPHEMERAL` volume. ### Extensions in Kubernetes Nodes Talos Linux now publishes list of installed extensions as Kubernetes node labels/annotations. The key format is `extensions.talos.dev/` and the value is the extension version. If the extension name is not valid as a label key, it will be skipped. If the extension version is a valid label value, it will be put to the label; otherwise it will be put to the annotation. For Talos machines booted of the Image Factory artifacts, this means that the schematic ID will be published as the annotation `extensions.talos.dev/schematic` (as it is longer than 63 characters). ### DNS Forwarding for CoreDNS pods Usage of the host DNS resolver as upstream for Kubernetes CoreDNS pods is now enabled by default. You can disable it with: ```yaml machine: features: hostDNS: enabled: true forwardKubeDNSToHost: false ``` Please note that on running cluster you will have to kill CoreDNS pods for this change to apply. The IP address used to forward DNS queries has changed to the fixed `169.254.116.108` address. For those upgrading from Talos 1.7 with `forwardKubeDNSToHost` enabled, the old Kubernetes service can be cleaned up with `kubectl delete -n kube-system service host-dns`. ### Installer Talos Linux installer now never wipes the system disk on upgrades, which means that the flag `--preserve` is always set for `talosctl upgrade`. ### `talos.halt_if_installed` kernel argument Starting with Talos 1.8, ISO's generated from Boot Assets would have a new kernel argument `talos.halt_if_installed` which would pause the boot sequence until boot timeout if Talos is already installed on the disk. ISO generated for pre 1.8 versions would not have this kernel argument. This can be also explicitly enabled by setting `talos.halt_if_installed=1` in kernel argument. ### Slim Kubelet Image Kubelet container image includes various utilities that kubelet might use to perform various tasks. Starting with Kubernetes 1.31.0, `kubelet` image now includes less utilities, as the in-tree CSI plugins were removed in Kubernetes 1.31.0. This reduces `kubelet` image size and potential attack surface. For Kubernetes < 1.31.0, there will be two images built: * `v1.x.y` (default, fat) * `v1.x.y-slim` (slim) For Kubernetes >= 1.31.0, there will be same two images built, but the default tag would point to slim image: * `v1.x.y` (default, slim) * `v1.x.y-fat` (fat) ### KubeSpan Extra announced endpoints can be added using the [`KubespanEndpointsConfig` document](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/network/kubespan/#configuration). ### Default Node Labels Talos Linux on config generation now adds a label `node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers` by default for the control plane nodes. ### PCI Devices A list of PCI devices can now be obtained via `PCIDevices` resource, e.g. `talosctl get pcidevices`. ### Metal images Starting with Talos 1.8, `console=ttyS0` kernel argument is removed from the metal images and installer. If running virtualized in QEMU (For eg: Proxmox), this can be added as an extra kernel argument if needed via Image Factory or using Imager. This should fix slow boot or no console output issues on most bare metal hardware. ### NVIDIA GPU Support Starting with Talos 1.8.0, SideroLabs would ships extensions for both LTS and Production versions of NVIDIA extensions. For more details see the CHANGELOG of [extensions](https://github.com/siderolabs/extensions/releases). Upgrades with an exisiting schematic id from Image Factory would keep the existing LTS version of the NVIDIA extension. ### Removing parts of the configuration using `$patch: delete` syntax Talos Linux now supports removing parts of the configuration using the `$patch: delete` syntax similar to the kubernetes. More information can be found [here](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/patching/#strategic-merge-patches). ### Platform Support Talos Linux now supports Apache CloudStack platform. ### kube-proxy Talos Linux configures kube-proxy >= v1.31.0 to use 'nftables' backend by default. ### Secure Boot Talos Linux now can optionally include well-known UEFI (Microsoft) SecureBoot keys into the auto-enrollment UEFI database. ### Custom Trusted Roots Talos Linux now supports adding [custom trusted roots](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/certificate-authorities/) (CA certificates) via `TrustedRootsConfig` configuration documents. ### Device Extra Settle Timeout Talos Linux now supports a kernel command line argument `talos.device.settle_time=3m` to set the device extra settle timeout to workaround issues with broken drivers. ### Component Updates Kubernetes: 1.31.1 Linux: 6.6.52 containerd: 2.0.0-rc.4 runc: 1.2.0-rc.3 etcd: 3.5.16 Flannel: 0.25.6 Flannel CNI plugin: 1.5.1 CoreDNS: 1.1.13 Talos is built with Go 1.22.7. ### ZSTD Compression Talos Linux now compresses kernel and initramfs using ZSTD. Linux arm64 kernel is now compressed (previously it was uncompressed). ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Noel Georgi * Artem Chernyshev * Utku Ozdemir * Dmitry Sharshakov * Justin Garrison * Spencer Smith * Steve Francis * Bernard Gütermann * Jean-Francois Roy * Konrad Eriksson * Serge Logvinov * Tim Jones * doctor_ew * Amadeus Mader * Andrew Rynhard * Anthony ARNAUD * Attila Oláh * Birger J. ## [Talos 1.8.0-beta.1](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.8.0-beta.1) (2024-09-16) Welcome to the v1.8.0-beta.1 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Starting with Talos v1.8.0, only standard assets would be published as github release assets. These include: * `cloud-images.json` * `talosctl` binaries * `kernel` * `initramfs` * `metal` iso and disk images * `talosctl-cni-bundle` All other release assets can be downloaded from [Image Factory](https://www.talos.dev/latest/talos-guides/install/boot-assets/#image-factory). Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Node Annotations Talos Linux now supports configuring Kubernetes node annotations via machine configuration (`.machine.nodeAnnotations`) in a way similar to node labels. ### Workload Apparmor Profile Talos Linux can now apply the default AppArmor profiles to all workloads started via containerd, if the machine is installed with the AppArmor LSM enforced via the extraKernelArgs. Eg: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - security=apparmor ``` ### Bridge Interface Talos Linux now support configuring 'vlan_filtering' for bridge interfaces. ### Machine Configuration via Kernel Command Line Talos Linux supports supplying zstd-compressed, base64-encoded machine configuration small documents via the kernel command line parameter `talos.config.inline`. ### CNI Plugins Talos Linux now bundles by default the following standard CNI plugins: * `bridge` * `firewall` * `flannel` * `host-local` * `loopback` * `portmap` The Talos bundled Flannel manifest was simplified to remove the `install-cni` step. ### Diagnostics Talos Linux now shows diagnostics information for common problems related to misconfiguration via `talosctl health` and Talos dashboard. ### Disk Management Talos Linux now supports [configuration](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/disk-management/#machine-configuration) for the `EPHEMERAL` volume. ### Extensions in Kubernetes Nodes Talos Linux now publishes list of installed extensions as Kubernetes node labels/annotations. The key format is `extensions.talos.dev/` and the value is the extension version. If the extension name is not valid as a label key, it will be skipped. If the extension version is a valid label value, it will be put to the label; otherwise it will be put to the annotation. For Talos machines booted of the Image Factory artifacts, this means that the schematic ID will be published as the annotation `extensions.talos.dev/schematic` (as it is longer than 63 characters). ### DNS Forwarding for CoreDNS pods Usage of the host DNS resolver as upstream for Kubernetes CoreDNS pods is now enabled by default. You can disable it with: ```yaml machine: features: hostDNS: enabled: true forwardKubeDNSToHost: false ``` Please note that on running cluster you will have to kill CoreDNS pods for this change to apply. The IP address used to forward DNS queries has changed to the fixed `169.254.116.108` address. For those upgrading from Talos 1.7 with `forwardKubeDNSToHost` enabled, the old Kubernetes service can be cleaned up with `kubectl delete -n kube-system service host-dns`. ### Installer Talos Linux installer now never wipes the system disk on upgrades, which means that the flag `--preserve` is always set for `talosctl upgrade`. ### `talos.halt_if_installed` kernel argument Starting with Talos 1.8, ISO's generated from Boot Assets would have a new kernel argument `talos.halt_if_installed` which would pause the boot sequence until boot timeout if Talos is already installed on the disk. ISO generated for pre 1.8 versions would not have this kernel argument. This can be also explicitly enabled by setting `talos.halt_if_installed=1` in kernel argument. ### Slim Kubelet Image Kubelet container image includes various utilities that kubelet might use to perform various tasks. Starting with Kubernetes 1.31.0, `kubelet` image now includes less utilities, as the in-tree CSI plugins were removed in Kubernetes 1.31.0. This reduces `kubelet` image size and potential attack surface. For Kubernetes < 1.31.0, there will be two images built: * `v1.x.y` (default, fat) * `v1.x.y-slim` (slim) For Kubernetes >= 1.31.0, there will be same two images built, but the default tag would point to slim image: * `v1.x.y` (default, slim) * `v1.x.y-fat` (fat) ### KubeSpan Extra announced endpoints can be added using the [`KubespanEndpointsConfig` document](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/network/kubespan/#configuration). ### Default Node Labels Talos Linux on config generation now adds a label `node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers` by default for the control plane nodes. ### PCI Devices A list of PCI devices can now be obtained via `PCIDevices` resource, e.g. `talosctl get pcidevices`. ### Metal images Starting with Talos 1.8, `console=ttyS0` kernel argument is removed from the metal images and installer. If running virtualized in QEMU (For eg: Proxmox), this can be added as an extra kernel argument if needed via Image Factory or using Imager. This should fix slow boot or no console output issues on most bare metal hardware. ### NVIDIA GPU Support Starting with Talos 1.8.0, SideroLabs would ships extensions for both LTS and Production versions of NVIDIA extensions. For more details see the CHANGELOG of [extensions](https://github.com/siderolabs/extensions/releases). Upgrades with an exisiting schematic id from Image Factory would keep the existing LTS version of the NVIDIA extension. ### Removing parts of the configuration using `$patch: delete` syntax Talos Linux now supports removing parts of the configuration using the `$patch: delete` syntax similar to the kubernetes. More information can be found [here](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/patching/#strategic-merge-patches). ### Platform Support Talos Linux now supports Apache CloudStack platform. ### kube-proxy Talos Linux configures kube-proxy >= v1.31.0 to use 'nftables' backend by default. ### Secure Boot Talos Linux now can optionally include well-known UEFI (Microsoft) SecureBoot keys into the auto-enrollment UEFI database. ### Custom Trusted Roots Talos Linux now supports adding [custom trusted roots](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/certificate-authorities/) (CA certificates) via `TrustedRootsConfig` configuration documents. ### Device Extra Settle Timeout Talos Linux now supports a kernel command line argument `talos.device.settle_time=3m` to set the device extra settle timeout to workaround issues with broken drivers. ### Component Updates Kubernetes: 1.31.1 Linux: 6.6.51 containerd: 2.0.0-rc.4 runc: 1.2.0-rc.3 etcd: 3.5.16 Flannel: 0.25.6 Flannel CNI plugin: 1.5.1 CoreDNS: 1.1.13 Talos is built with Go 1.22.7. ### ZSTD Compression Talos Linux now compresses kernel and initramfs using ZSTD. Linux arm64 kernel is now compressed (previously it was uncompressed). ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Noel Georgi * Artem Chernyshev * Utku Ozdemir * Dmitry Sharshakov * Justin Garrison * Spencer Smith * Steve Francis * Bernard Gütermann * Jean-Francois Roy * Konrad Eriksson * Serge Logvinov * doctor_ew * Amadeus Mader * Andrew Rynhard * Anthony ARNAUD * Attila Oláh * Birger J. ## [Talos 1.8.0-beta.0](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.8.0-beta.0) (2024-09-09) Welcome to the v1.8.0-beta.0 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Starting with Talos v1.8.0, only standard assets would be published as github release assets. These include: * `cloud-images.json` * `talosctl` binaries * `kernel` * `initramfs` * `metal` iso and disk images * `talosctl-cni-bundle` All other release assets can be downloaded from [Image Factory](https://www.talos.dev/latest/talos-guides/install/boot-assets/#image-factory). Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Node Annotations Talos Linux now supports configuring Kubernetes node annotations via machine configuration (`.machine.nodeAnnotations`) in a way similar to node labels. ### Workload Apparmor Profile Talos Linux can now apply the default AppArmor profiles to all workloads started via containerd, if the machine is installed with the AppArmor LSM enforced via the extraKernelArgs. Eg: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - security=apparmor ``` ### Bridge Interface Talos Linux now support configuring 'vlan_filtering' for bridge interfaces. ### Machine Configuration via Kernel Command Line Talos Linux supports supplying zstd-compressed, base64-encoded machine configuration small documents via the kernel command line parameter `talos.config.inline`. ### CNI Plugins Talos Linux now bundles by default the following standard CNI plugins: * `bridge` * `firewall` * `flannel` * `host-local` * `loopback` * `portmap` The Talos bundled Flannel manifest was simplified to remove the `install-cni` step. ### Diagnostics Talos Linux now shows diagnostics information for common problems related to misconfiguration via `talosctl health` and Talos dashboard. ### Disk Management Talos Linux now supports [configuration](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/disk-management/#machine-configuration) for the `EPHEMERAL` volume. ### Extensions in Kubernetes Nodes Talos Linux now publishes list of installed extensions as Kubernetes node labels/annotations. The key format is `extensions.talos.dev/` and the value is the extension version. If the extension name is not valid as a label key, it will be skipped. If the extension version is a valid label value, it will be put to the label; otherwise it will be put to the annotation. For Talos machines booted of the Image Factory artifacts, this means that the schematic ID will be published as the annotation `extensions.talos.dev/schematic` (as it is longer than 63 characters). ### DNS Forwarding for CoreDNS pods Usage of the host DNS resolver as upstream for Kubernetes CoreDNS pods is now enabled by default. You can disable it with: ```yaml machine: features: hostDNS: enabled: true forwardKubeDNSToHost: false ``` Please note that on running cluster you will have to kill CoreDNS pods for this change to apply. The IP address used to forward DNS queries has changed to the fixed `169.254.116.108` address. For those upgrading from Talos 1.7 with `forwardKubeDNSToHost` enabled, the old Kubernetes service can be cleaned up with `kubectl delete -n kube-system service host-dns`. ### Installer Talos Linux installer now never wipes the system disk on upgrades, which means that the flag `--preserve` is always set for `talosctl upgrade`. ### `talos.halt_if_installed` kernel argument Starting with Talos 1.8, ISO's generated from Boot Assets would have a new kernel argument `talos.halt_if_installed` which would pause the boot sequence until boot timeout if Talos is already installed on the disk. ISO generated for pre 1.8 versions would not have this kernel argument. This can be also explicitly enabled by setting `talos.halt_if_installed=1` in kernel argument. ### Slim Kubelet Image Kubelet container image includes various utilities that kubelet might use to perform various tasks. Starting with Kubernetes 1.31.0, `kubelet` image now includes less utilities, as the in-tree CSI plugins were removed in Kubernetes 1.31.0. This reduces `kubelet` image size and potential attack surface. For Kubernetes < 1.31.0, there will be two images built: * `v1.x.y` (default, fat) * `v1.x.y-slim` (slim) For Kubernetes >= 1.31.0, there will be same two images built, but the default tag would point to slim image: * `v1.x.y` (default, slim) * `v1.x.y-fat` (fat) ### KubeSpan Extra announced endpoints can be added using the [`KubespanEndpointsConfig` document](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/network/kubespan/#configuration). ### Default Node Labels Talos Linux on config generation now adds a label `node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers` by default for the control plane nodes. ### PCI Devices A list of PCI devices can now be obtained via `PCIDevices` resource, e.g. `talosctl get pcidevices`. ### Metal images Starting with Talos 1.8, `console=ttyS0` kernel argument is removed from the metal images and installer. If running virtualized in QEMU (For eg: Proxmox), this can be added as an extra kernel argument if needed via Image Factory or using Imager. This should fix slow boot or no console output issues on most bare metal hardware. ### NVIDIA GPU Support Starting with Talos 1.8.0, SideroLabs would ships extensions for both LTS and Production versions of NVIDIA extensions. For more details see the CHANGELOG of [extensions](https://github.com/siderolabs/extensions/releases). Upgrades with an exisiting schematic id from Image Factory would keep the existing LTS version of the NVIDIA extension. ### Removing parts of the configuration using `$patch: delete` syntax Talos Linux now supports removing parts of the configuration using the `$patch: delete` syntax similar to the kubernetes. More information can be found [here](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/patching/#strategic-merge-patches). ### Platform Support Talos Linux now supports Apache CloudStack platform. ### kube-proxy Talos Linux configures kube-proxy >= v1.31.0 to use 'nftables' backend by default. ### Secure Boot Talos Linux now can optionally include well-known UEFI (Microsoft) SecureBoot keys into the auto-enrollment UEFI database. ### Custom Trusted Roots Talos Linux now supports adding [custom trusted roots](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/certificate-authorities/) (CA certificates) via `TrustedRootsConfig` configuration documents. ### Device Extra Settle Timeout Talos Linux now supports a kernel command line argument `talos.device.settle_time=3m` to set the device extra settle timeout to workaround issues with broken drivers. ### Component Updates Kubernetes: 1.31.0 Linux: 6.6.49 containerd: 2.0.0-rc.4 runc: 1.2.0-rc.3 etcd: 3.5.15 Flannel: 0.25.6 Flannel CNI plugin: 1.5.1 CoreDNS: 1.1.13 Talos is built with Go 1.22.7. ### ZSTD Compression Talos Linux now compresses kernel and initramfs using ZSTD. Linux arm64 kernel is now compressed (previously it was uncompressed). ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Noel Georgi * Artem Chernyshev * Utku Ozdemir * Dmitry Sharshakov * Justin Garrison * Spencer Smith * Steve Francis * Bernard Gütermann * Jean-Francois Roy * Konrad Eriksson * Serge Logvinov * doctor_ew * Amadeus Mader * Andrew Rynhard * Anthony ARNAUD * Attila Oláh * Birger J. ## [Talos 1.8.0-alpha.2](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.8.0-alpha.2) (2024-09-02) Welcome to the v1.8.0-alpha.2 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Starting with Talos v1.8.0, only standard assets would be published as github release assets. These include: * `cloud-images.json` * `talosctl` binaries * `kernel` * `initramfs` * `metal` iso and disk images * `talosctl-cni-bundle` All other release assets can be downloaded from [Image Factory](https://www.talos.dev/latest/talos-guides/install/boot-assets/#image-factory). Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Node Annotations Talos Linux now supports configuring Kubernetes node annotations via machine configuration (`.machine.nodeAnnotations`) in a way similar to node labels. ### Workload Apparmor Profile Talos Linux can now apply the default AppArmor profiles to all workloads started via containerd, if the machine is installed with the AppArmor LSM enforced via the extraKernelArgs. Eg: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - security=apparmor ``` ### Bridge Interface Talos Linux now support configuring 'vlan_filtering' for bridge interfaces. ### CNI Plugins Talos Linux now bundles by default the following standard CNI plugins: * `bridge` * `firewall` * `flannel` * `host-local` * `loopback` * `portmap` The Talos bundled Flannel manifest was simplified to remove the `install-cni` step. ### Diagnostics Talos Linux now shows diagnostics information for common problems related to misconfiguration via `talosctl health` and Talos dashboard. ### Extensions in Kubernetes Nodes Talos Linux now publishes list of installed extensions as Kubernetes node labels/annotations. The key format is `extensions.talos.dev/` and the value is the extension version. If the extension name is not valid as a label key, it will be skipped. If the extension version is a valid label value, it will be put to the label; otherwise it will be put to the annotation. For Talos machines booted of the Image Factory artifacts, this means that the schematic ID will be published as the annotation `extensions.talos.dev/schematic` (as it is longer than 63 characters). ### DNS Forwarding for CoreDNS pods Usage of the host DNS resolver as upstream for Kubernetes CoreDNS pods is now enabled by default. You can disable it with: ```yaml machine: features: hostDNS: enabled: true forwardKubeDNSToHost: false ``` Please note that on running cluster you will have to kill CoreDNS pods for this change to apply. The IP address used to forward DNS queries has changed to the fixed `169.254.116.108` address. For those upgrading from Talos 1.7 with `forwardKubeDNSToHost` enabled, the old Kubernetes service can be cleaned up with `kubectl delete -n kube-system service host-dns`. ### Installer Talos Linux installer now never wipes the system disk on upgrades, which means that the flag `--preserve` is always set for `talosctl upgrade`. ### `talos.halt_if_installed` kernel argument Starting with Talos 1.8, ISO's generated from Boot Assets would have a new kernel argument `talos.halt_if_installed` which would pause the boot sequence until boot timeout if Talos is already installed on the disk. ISO generated for pre 1.8 versions would not have this kernel argument. This can be also explicitly enabled by setting `talos.halt_if_installed=1` in kernel argument. ### Slim Kubelet Image Kubelet container image includes various utilities that kubelet might use to perform various tasks. Starting with Kubernetes 1.31.0, `kubelet` image now includes less utilities, as the in-tree CSI plugins were removed in Kubernetes 1.31.0. This reduces `kubelet` image size and potential attack surface. For Kubernetes < 1.31.0, there will be two images built: * `v1.x.y` (default, fat) * `v1.x.y-slim` (slim) For Kubernetes >= 1.31.0, there will be same two images built, but the default tag would point to slim image: * `v1.x.y` (default, slim) * `v1.x.y-fat` (fat) ### Default Node Labels Talos Linux on config generation now adds a label `node.kubernetes.io/exclude-from-external-load-balancers` by default for the control plane nodes. ### PCI Devices A list of PCI devices can now be obtained via `PCIDevices` resource, e.g. `talosctl get pcidevices`. ### Metal images Starting with Talos 1.8, `console=ttyS0` kernel argument is removed from the metal images and installer. If running virtualized in QEMU (For eg: Proxmox), this can be added as an extra kernel argument if needed via Image Factory or using Imager. This should fix slow boot or no console output issues on most bare metal hardware. ### NVIDIA GPU Support Starting with Talos 1.8.0, SideroLabs would ships extensions for both LTS and Production versions of NVIDIA extensions. For more details see the CHANGELOG of [extensions](https://github.com/siderolabs/extensions/releases). Upgrades with an exisiting schematic id from Image Factory would keep the existing LTS version of the NVIDIA extension. ### Platform Support Talos Linux now supports Apache CloudStack platform. ### kube-proxy Talos Linux configures kube-proxy >= v1.31.0 to use 'nftables' backend by default. ### Secure Boot Talos Linux now can optionally include well-known UEFI (Microsoft) SecureBoot keys into the auto-enrollment UEFI database. ### Custom Trusted Roots Talos Linux now supports adding [custom trusted roots](https://www.talos.dev/v1.8/talos-guides/configuration/certificate-authorities/) (CA certificates) via `TrustedRootsConfig` configuration documents. ### Device Extra Settle Timeout Talos Linux now supports a kernel command line argument `talos.device.settle_time=3m` to set the device extra settle timeout to workaround issues with broken drivers. ### Component Updates Kubernetes: 1.31.0 Linux: 6.6.47 containerd: 2.0.0-rc.4 runc: 1.2.0-rc.2 etcd: 3.5.15 Flannel: 0.25.6 Flannel CNI plugin: 1.5.1 CoreDNS: 1.1.13 Talos is built with Go 1.22.6. ### ZSTD Compression Talos Linux now compresses kernel and initramfs using ZSTD. Linux arm64 kernel is now compressed (previously it was uncompressed). ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Noel Georgi * Utku Ozdemir * Artem Chernyshev * Dmitry Sharshakov * Justin Garrison * Spencer Smith * Steve Francis * Bernard Gütermann * Jean-Francois Roy * Konrad Eriksson * Serge Logvinov * doctor_ew * Amadeus Mader * Andrew Rynhard * Anthony ARNAUD * Attila Oláh * Birger J. ## [Talos 1.8.0-alpha.1](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.8.0-alpha.1) (2024-07-08) Welcome to the v1.8.0-alpha.1 release of Talos! *This is a pre-release of Talos* Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues. ### Workload Apparmor Profile Talos Linux can now apply the default AppArmor profiles to all workloads started via containerd, if the machine is installed with the AppArmor LSM enforced via the extraKernelArgs. Eg: ```yaml machine: install: extraKernelArgs: - security=apparmor ``` ### Bridge Interface Talos Linux now support configuring 'vlan_filtering' for bridge interfaces. ### Diagnostics Talos Linux now shows diagnostics information for common problems related to misconfiguration via `talosctl health` and Talos dashboard. ### DNS Forwarding for CoreDNS pods Usage of the host DNS resolver as upstream for Kubernetes CoreDNS pods is now enabled by default. You can disable it with: ```yaml machine: features: hostDNS: enabled: true forwardKubeDNSToHost: false ``` Please note that on running cluster you will have to kill CoreDNS pods for this change to apply. ### PCI Devices A list of PCI devices can now be obtained via `PCIDevices` resource, e.g. `talosctl get pcidevices`. ### Component Updates Kubernetes: 1.30.2 Linux: 6.6.36 containerd: 2.0.0-rc.3 runc: 1.2.0-rc.2 etcd: 3.5.14 Flannel: 0.25.3 Flannel CNI plugin: 1.5.1 Talos is built with Go 1.22.5. ### ZSTD Compression Talos Linux now compresses kernel and initramfs using ZSTD. Linux arm64 kernel is now compressed (previously it was uncompressed). ### Contributors * Andrey Smirnov * Dmitriy Matrenichev * Noel Georgi * Utku Ozdemir * Artem Chernyshev * Dmitry Sharshakov * Spencer Smith * Justin Garrison * Steve Francis * Bernard Gütermann * Konrad Eriksson * Andrew Rynhard * Attila Oláh * Birger J. author: mauro-agent
body:
## Summary

Investigated how long a Hadron UKI takes to reach a usable boot. The
systemd-boot menu itself is fast. After the menu, boot can stall for several
minutes on a fully black screen with zero console output, then the firmware
resets and the whole cycle repeats.

## Setup

- Image: `quay.io/kairos/hadron:v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-v4.3.0`
- Built with `auroraboot build-uki` (`quay.io/kairos/auroraboot:v0.27.1`),
  `--secure-boot-enroll if-safe`, keys from `auroraboot genkey`
- QEMU + OVMF: `OVMF_CODE.secboot.fd`, blank `OVMF_VARS.fd` (Setup Mode),
  virtio ESP image, blank virtio target disk, swtpm-backed TPM 2.0 device
- Serial console captured to a file, periodic framebuffer screendumps taken
  through the QEMU monitor

## What I saw

1. First boot: systemd-boot auto-enrolls PK/KEK/db from
   `/loader/keys/auto`, then reboots. Fast, expected.
2. The Kairos boot menu appears and counts down 5s to 1s. Fast, expected.
3. The screen goes fully black. Confirmed with a screendump: a solid black
   frame, not just missing serial output.
4. Serial (`ttyS0`) stays silent for the whole stall, even though the baked
   cmdline lists `console=ttyS0 console=tty1`. No kernel banner, no
   immucore log lines, nothing.
5. The guest vCPU stays pinned near 100% the whole time (checked with `ps`
   on the host). It is actively busy, not idle-waiting on a timeout or a
   missing device.
6. After roughly 200 to 320 seconds (it varied per cycle), the VM
   force-resets back to firmware and the cycle repeats from step 2. I saw 4
   cycles in a row over about 20 minutes, same pattern every time, no
   kernel console output in any of them.
7. Retested with a software TPM attached (swtpm, `tpm-tis` device), to rule
   out "no TPM" as the cause. Same behavior.

Because no kernel-level output ever reaches serial, not even the first
kernel banner line that normally shows up within milliseconds on a working
boot, and the guest is CPU-busy the whole time, this looks like the hang
happens before Linux gets control at all. That points at systemd-boot or
the UKI stub's own verification/measurement path, not at immucore.

## A separate, distinct finding: immucore's SecureBoot halt is invisible on serial

In an earlier attempt (SecureBoot enrollment off, no real key enrollment),
boot reached the kernel and immucore normally. immucore correctly detected
SecureBoot was off and called `RebootOrWait("Secure boot is not enabled",
nil)` (`immucore/internal/utils/common.go:143`), which lands on `select {}`
since `rd.immucore.rebootonfailure` was not set. That message rendered on
the framebuffer (confirmed by screendump) but never showed up on serial,
even with `console=ttyS0` listed first on the cmdline. This is likely
because `console=ttyS0 console=tty1` makes `tty1` (the last `console=`)
the target for `/dev/console`, and immucore's own logger writes there,
while kernel dmesg lines go to every registered console. Worth a note, or
routing a fatal boot-blocking message like this through kmsg too, since
anyone debugging over serial only (the normal case for headless or remote
hardware) sees nothing at all when this fires.

## What I ruled out

- Missing TPM device: retested with swtpm attached, no change.
- The immucore SecureBoot-disabled halt above: that is a separate, fast
  (about 1.8s), well-understood, near-idle hang. It is not this stall.

## Caveat

This investigation started from a report that reaching the systemd-boot
menu was fast, followed by about 2.5 minutes on a blank screen, then about
1 minute on a splash screen, on kairos-init v0.17.3 with AuroraBoot v0.27.
My test used a newer kairos-init (about v4.3.0) in QEMU with OVMF, not real
hardware, so the root cause may not be identical. The shape and the rough
timing (a silent multi-minute stall right after the menu) line up closely
enough that I think they are worth investigating together.

This is not an agent, Mauro used AI to help write this.
title: Hadron UKI: silent multi-minute stall + reboot loop after SecureBoot menu, before kernel boot

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

his is more of a UX/polishment story. Currently any kairos/hadron build shows default grub and console log is displayed directly. https://github.com/kairos-community/hadron-desktop does already have a boot animation (during early initramfs, so user doesn't see the console drop) and GRUB settings to slightly improve its appearance.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A default animation (like hadron-desktop) that is for kairos (and still having a specific one for hadron when loading hadron) that starts early initramfs and if the user press ESC the logs is displayed (should be a toggle switch).  As like other pieces of kairos, this should be swappable so downstream consumers can apply theirs and/or disable it entirely (by e.g. removing the binary).

We also want to have a minimal grub themeing (maybe just colors and or kairos logo) that can be then customized by downstream consumers

author: mauromorales
body:
**Repository: `kairos-io/kairos-lab`.** Filed here because that repository points every issue at this one.

Follow-ups from QA on #4431's fix (kairos-io/kairos-lab#22, merged as `6874086`). None of these blocked that merge. The reported bug is fixed and the default path is correct on real hardware. These are gaps in the same code.

Evidence comes from a physical Apple Silicon Mac whose interfaces match the original report: `en0` inactive, `en1` Wi-Fi holding the default route, `awdl0` active.

## 1. The validator ignores the virtual interface filter

`DetectBridgeIfaceCandidates()` drops the interfaces `vmnet-bridged` cannot bridge onto, using `isDarwinVirtualInterface()`. `validateBridgeIface()` only looks at link status, so an explicit `-bridge-if` walks past the filter:

```
ValidateBridgeIface("awdl0") -> nil
```

`awdl0` is AirDrop, and it reports `status: active` on a real Mac, so this is not theoretical. The config review has the same hole: option 8 accepts free text with no check.

The tool therefore still accepts an interface it knows in the same file is unusable, which is the failure shape #4431 was about.

**Fix:** reject `isDarwinVirtualInterface(name)` inside `validateBridgeIface()`, with its own message, and let the config review use the same path.

## 2. A misspelled interface is reported as a link problem

```
ValidateBridgeIface("en9") -> bridge interface en9 reports no link status, so the VM would
boot with no network and no DHCP lease (interfaces with a link: en1; ...)
```

`en9` does not exist. `ifconfig en9` fails, `darwinRun()` returns `""`, and `""` is indistinguishable from an interface that genuinely reports no status. The user reads a hardware diagnosis for a typo.

**Fix:** check the name against `parseDarwinIfaceList()` first, and say "no such interface".

## 3. Switching to bridged inside the config review produces an error with no interface name

The interface is resolved in `runStart` before `reviewVMConfig`, and only when `-network bridged` was already on the command line. Start in user mode, change option 7 to `bridged`, leave option 8 alone, and `[1/3] Preparing networking` prints:

```
bridge interface  reports no link status, so the VM would boot with no network and no DHCP
lease (interfaces with a link: en1; use -bridge-if to pick one, or -network user for
port-forwarded access)
```

The name is empty, so there is a double space where it should be. The advice is wrong for this path too: the user is inside an interactive review, so the answer is option 8, not a flag on a command that is already running.

This is still an improvement on the old behaviour, which used `en0` silently here. Only the message is wrong.

**Fix:** resolve again after the review when the mode is bridged and the interface is still empty.

## Checklist

- [ ] 1. Validator rejects virtual interfaces
- [ ] 2. Unknown interface says so
- [ ] 3. Re-resolve after the config review

---

*This issue was written with AI assistance. A human attends it.*
title: kairos-lab: three follow-ups on the macOS bridge interface resolution

author: ci-robbot
body:
## Summary
Explore the feasibility of compiling the Hadron userland with [Fil-C](https://fil-c.org), a memory-safe implementation of C and C++. Fil-C enables running existing C/C++ software with zero or minimal changes while catching all memory safety errors as panics.

## Background
Fil-C combines concurrent garbage collection and invisible capabilities (InvisiCaps) to enforce memory safety without requiring unsafe blocks. It supports advanced C/C++ features like threads, atomics, exceptions, signal handling, `longjmp`/`setjmp`, and shared memory. Notably, it has been used to successfully port complex systems like Wayland, libinput, Weston, and even a full memory-safe Linux userland.

Key benefits:
- Zero or minimal code changes for existing C/C++ projects.
- No `unsafe` keyword—every potentially unsafe operation is checked.
- Supports FFI to unsafe code but limits it.
- Has successfully run CPython, OpenSSH, GNU Emacs, and Wayland in memory-safe mode.

## Objective
Conduct a spike to assess the viability of building and running Hadron's userland components (e.g., init system, system daemons, core utilities) using Fil-C. Focus on:

- Compiling core components (e.g., `init`, `systemd`, `dbus`, `networkd`, `udev`, `crond`, `sshd`) with Fil-C.
- Verifying runtime behavior and stability.
- Identifying compatibility issues or performance overhead.
- Assessing whether Fil-C can provide memory safety **out-of-the-box** for Hadron.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A report detailing the success/failure rate of compiling key userland components with Fil-C.
- [ ] A list of components that require modifications (if any), and why.
- [ ] Evidence of successful runtime execution of at least 3 core components.
- [ ] Performance comparison (if possible) with standard C compilation.
- [ ] Recommendation on whether to pursue Fil-C integration long-term.

## Resources
- [Fil-C Official Site](https://fil-c.org)
- [Fil-C Programs That Work](https://fil-c.org/programs_that_work.html)
- [Fil-C Porting Example: Wayland + Weston](https://fil-c.org/pizlix.html)
- [Concurrent GC Paper](https://fil-c.org/fugc.html)
- [InvisiCaps Paper](https://fil-c.org/invisicaps.html)

## Notes
This spike is inspired by the successful porting of complex userland components like Wayland and Weston with Fil-C using just 'about a day's work'. The goal is to evaluate whether a similar outcome is achievable for Hadron, potentially delivering **memory safety by default** without sacrificing compatibility.
title: Spike: Compile Hadron userland with Fil-C for memory safety

author: mauromorales
body:
## Why

The riscv64 epic (#4419) defines done as "a riscv64 Kairos image boots under emulation and on real hardware". Every riscv64 result so far comes from QEMU. A StarFive VisionFive 2 is now in hand, so the hardware half can be tested. This issue tracks that manual test run and its results.

## The board

- StarFive VisionFive 2 (Waveshare), JH7110, 8 GB LPDDR4, 40 pin GPIO, WiFi module.
- Vendor wiki, with specs, boot process and flashing instructions: https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/VisionFive2
- Firmware as shipped: `U-Boot 2021.10 (Feb 12 2023), Build: jenkins-VF2_515_Branch_SDK_Release-24`, model `VF7110B1-2253`.
- Serial console: a USB to UART adapter on header pins 6, 8 and 10, at 115200 8N1.

## Facts already established on this hardware

These come from a first session with the board powered on. Please do not re-derive them.

1. **The board does not ship with EDK II.** It ships the vendor U-Boot. GRUB still loads, because that U-Boot carries an EFI loader of its own. The earlier plan assumed a TianoCore EDK II firmware. That is something you flash, not something a factory board has.
2. **USB is not a boot path today.** The vendor U-Boot has USB compiled out. `usb` is not a recognised command and `boot_targets` is `mmc0 dhcp`. A factory board boots from microSD, eMMC or network only.
3. **microSD cards over 128 GB do not boot** on this board, per StarFive. A 32 GB card works.
4. **eMMC and SDIO3.0 boot modes have a known low probability boot failure.** Keep the DIP switches at the factory SPI flash default.
5. **The boot chain reaches the kernel handoff and stops there.**

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| U-Boot EFI loader loads `BOOTRISCV64.EFI` | works |
| GRUB 2.12 starts, reads the ESP, renders the menu | works |
| GRUB loads the kernel from `recovery.img` | works |
| Kernel handoff | fails, OpenSBI traps |

```
sbi_trap_error: hart0: trap handler failed (error -2)
sbi_trap_error: hart0: mcause=0x0000000000000005 mtval=0x0000000040048060
sbi_trap_error: hart0: mepc=0x0000000040004cac
cannot read pmic power register
```

`mepc` points inside OpenSBI, not the kernel. The dump is identical across three attempts, so it is deterministic. Prime suspect: the vendor firmware is too old for a 6.x kernel. Ubuntu documents the vendor U-Boot on this board as not EBBR compatible.

## Tasks

- [ ] Flash a current U-Boot and OpenSBI to the SPI flash. This is recoverable through the DIP switches, and it also restores USB.
- [ ] Boot the riscv64 ISO again and confirm the kernel starts.
- [ ] Install to disk. The ISO live path does not pass `install-mode` today, so the installer never runs on its own. Use `kairos-agent manual-install <cloud-config> --device <target>` from the live shell.
- [ ] Confirm the first boot of the installed system, and a login as the cloud-config user.
- [ ] Start k3s and confirm `kubectl get nodes` reports the node Ready.
- [ ] Test an A/B upgrade, then a rollback.
- [ ] Test a state reset.
- [ ] Answer #4089 on hardware: does the UPX packed immucore run on real silicon, or is the crash specific to QEMU TCG? The boot must reach immucore first.

## Artifacts under test

The riscv64 images from the `kairos-riscv64-v0.1.3` release in https://github.com/mauromorales/homelab: the ISO as a release asset, and the raw disk image at `quay.io/mauromorales/kairos-riscv64:0.1.3-img`. On any host that is not riscv64, pull the raw image with `--platform linux/riscv64`.

## Storage

The install target is a 32 GB microSD card. A/B upgrades rewrite the disk often, so an NVMe drive in the M.2 M-key slot is better for endurance. microSD is adequate for validation, and it is the only guaranteed ROM boot path until the firmware is replaced.

## Out of scope

U-Boot as a first class Kairos bootloader. The board reaches GRUB through U-Boot's EFI loader, which is the same UEFI plus GRUB path every other Kairos target uses.

## Related

- #4419, the riscv64 tracking epic
- #4089, the UPX packed immucore crash under QEMU TCG
- https://github.com/mauromorales/homelab/issues/55, the ISO live boot path misses `install-mode`
- https://github.com/mauromorales/homelab/issues/56, the raw image boots to an unauthenticated recovery login

---

*This issue was written with AI assistance. A human attends it.*
title: riscv64: manual hardware validation on a StarFive VisionFive 2

author: itxaka-agent
body:
Split off from #112.

`auditd` cannot land in Kairos until its log directory survives A/B upgrade. Right now `/var/log/audit` lives on the ephemeral rootfs and is wiped on every upgrade or reset. This defeats the entire point of shipping auditd.

## Required change

Make `/var/log/audit` a bind mount from the state (COS_PERSISTENT) partition, mounted before `auditd.service` starts, and included in the immucore mount table so it comes up on every boot including recovery mode.

## Work items

- [ ] Add `/var/log/audit` to the immucore persistent mount list.
- [ ] Ensure the mount is present before `auditd.service` starts (systemd `RequiresMountsFor=` or an equivalent OpenRC dep).
- [ ] Preserve the directory across `kairos-agent reset` — reset must not wipe audit trails on operator machines.
- [ ] Consider file mode / SELinux label carry-over — audit expects the directory to be owned by `root:root` mode `0700`. Persistence layer must not clobber that on remount.
- [ ] Verify behavior on both A/B upgrade and recovery mode boot.

## Prerequisite for

- kairos-io/kairos#4626 — auditd cannot land in kairos-init without this.

## Non-goals

- Shipping auditd itself — that lands in the kairos-init CIS L1 issue once this is done.
- Log forwarding or centralization — separate feature request.

## Definition of done

- `/var/log/audit` contents survive an A/B upgrade round-trip on every base distro.
- `/var/log/audit` contents survive a `kairos-agent reset` on operator-configured machines.
- auditd, when installed on top of this, sees its historical log lines after upgrade.

---

*Filed by [`itxaka-agent`](https://github.com/itxaka-agent) as split of #112. Approved by @itxaka.*
title: immucore: persist /var/log/audit across A/B upgrades

author: mauromorales
body:
**Repository: `kairos-io/kairos-lab`.** Filed here because that repository points every issue at this one.

## What happens

The `scan-pr / osv-scan` check fails on every pull request. It has failed on every branch since 2026-07-17. The last success was 2026-06-19.

Two separate problems produce that one red check.

### 1. `go.mod` pins a Go version with 10 open stdlib advisories

`go.mod` on `main` says `go 1.26.4`. OSV reports ten advisories against the standard library at that version:

```
| GO-2026-4970 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.5 |
| GO-2026-5856 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.5 |
| GO-2026-5026 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-5942 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-5972 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-6088 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-6089 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-6090 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-6091 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
| GO-2026-6218 | stdlib | 1.26.4 | fixed in 1.26.6 |
```

All ten clear with one line: `go 1.26.6` or later.

### 2. The scanner's own toolchain is older than the repository's, so `govulncheck` never runs

```
Failed to run code analysis (govulncheck) on '/github/workspace/go.mod' because
govulncheck: loading packages: err: exit status 1: stderr:
go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26.4 (running go 1.25.7; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
```

The reusable workflow (`google/osv-scanner-action/.github/workflows/osv-scanner-reusable.yml@v2.3.3`, called from `.github/workflows/osv-scanner-pr.yaml`) carries its own Go, currently 1.25.7, with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` so it cannot fetch a newer one. Bumping `go.mod` to 1.26.6 does not fix this. It widens the gap.

So the reachability analysis, which is the part that tells a real risk from a theoretical one, produces nothing today. Only the version match against `go.mod` runs.

## Why it matters

A check that is always red teaches everyone to ignore it. #22 merged with this job failing, correctly, because the failure predates it and has nothing to do with its diff. The next pull request that introduces a genuine advisory will look exactly the same.

## Suggested fix

- [ ] Bump `go.mod` to `go 1.26.6` or later, and confirm `build-test` still passes on both legs.
- [ ] Give the scan job a toolchain that can load the module, or accept that `govulncheck` cannot run and say so in the workflow, so the failure is a decision rather than a surprise.

Note that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is already correct here. It uses `go-version-file: go.mod`, so the build and test legs always match the module.

---

*This issue was written with AI assistance. A human attends it.*
title: kairos-lab: osv-scan fails on every PR, from a stale go.mod and a scanner toolchain that cannot load it

author: itxaka-agent
body:
Split from kairos-io/kairos#112 (see kairos-io/kairos#4626, kairos-io/kairos#4627, kairos-io/kairos#4628, kairos-io/kairos#4629 for the rest of the CIS work).

Add `auditd` and its userspace tools (`auditctl`, `augenrules`, `ausearch`, `aureport`) to the Hadron package set so kairos-init images built on top of Hadron can ship a working CIS **Section 4 — Logging and Auditing** baseline.

## Why Hadron specifically

Distro-based Kairos images (Ubuntu, openSUSE, RHEL, Rocky, Debian, Alpine) can pull auditd from the upstream package repositories. Hadron builds its own userland from source through the mussel toolchain, so nothing lands unless it is explicitly added to the build. Without this issue closed, the kairos-init CIS L1 issue (kairos-io/kairos#4626) can never satisfy Section 4 on Hadron-based images.

## Scope

- Add the `audit` userspace (upstream: https://github.com/linux-audit/audit-userspace) as a new build stage in the Hadron Dockerfile, cross-compiled through mussel for `amd64`, `arm64`, and `riscv64`.
- Ship the `auditd` binary, `auditctl`, `augenrules`, `ausearch`, `aureport`, and the `libaudit`/`libauparse` shared libraries in the final rootfs.
- Add an init unit (systemd or OpenRC depending on Hadron's current init) that starts `auditd` early enough to catch boot-time events.
- Ship a minimal `/etc/audit/auditd.conf` and an empty `/etc/audit/rules.d/` directory. The CIS baseline rules themselves land in kairos-io/kairos#4626 on the kairos-init side.
- Verify kernel audit support (`CONFIG_AUDIT=y`, `CONFIG_AUDITSYSCALL=y`) is enabled in the Hadron kernel config; enable it if missing.

## Prerequisites

- kairos-io/kairos#4629 — `/var/log/audit` must persist across A/B upgrades before auditd is actually useful. Ship the package first, wire persistence second, land the rules third.

## Non-goals

- The CIS baseline audit rules — those belong in kairos-io/kairos#4626, not here.
- Remote log forwarding (audispd plugins for `syslog`/`remote`) — separate feature request.
- Hardening `auditd.conf` beyond the upstream defaults — belongs in kairos-io/kairos#4626 alongside the rules.

## Definition of done

- `auditd --version` works on a booted Hadron-based Kairos image on all three architectures.
- The daemon starts at boot and writes to `/var/log/audit/audit.log`.
- Binary size impact is documented on the PR (mussel-compiled audit userspace is small, but should be measured).
- kairos-io/kairos#4626 can install its baseline rules on top without pulling in a second copy of the userland.

---

*Filed by [`itxaka-agent`](https://github.com/itxaka-agent) after @itxaka's follow-up on kairos-io/kairos#112. Approved by @itxaka before posting.*
title: hadron: add auditd + audit userspace to the package set

body:
Split off from #112.

Publish a single documentation page that maps every CIS control ID (both **CIS Distribution Independent Linux L1** and **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark L1**) to one of:

- **Implemented in X** (link to the kairos-init step, hook, or provider flag).
- **Not applicable because Y** (with a written justification — e.g. "boot loader password conflicts with UKI + TPM sealed boot").
- **Open — tracking issue #N**.

## Why this exists

Without a control matrix, "Kairos supports CIS" is not a claim we can make honestly. Auditors ask for the matrix, not for a blog post.

## Format

Two tables — one per benchmark — with columns: `Control ID`, `Title`, `Status`, `Evidence / Justification / Tracking Issue`.

Live in the docs repo (`kairos-io/kairos-docs`) under a new `security/cis.md` page. Cross-link from the security landing page and from every kairos-init hardening step's godoc comment.

## Work items

- [ ] Import the CIS Distribution Independent Linux L1 control list into the page skeleton.
- [ ] Import the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark L1 control list into the same page (separate table).
