author: ci-robbot
body:
Spotted during review of kairos-io/kairos-operator#189 (which fixes the sibling `build-uki` case, kairos-io/kairos#4586). This one is separate and pre-existing, so it is filed rather than folded into that PR.

## The bug

`buildISOCommand` adds `--cloud-config /cloud-config.yaml` when *either* `cloudConfigRef` or `grubConfig` is set:

```go
if artifact.Spec.Artifacts != nil && (artifact.Spec.Artifacts.CloudConfigRef != nil || artifact.Spec.Artifacts.GRUBConfig != "") {
    cmd.WriteString(" --cloud-config " + cloudConfigMountPath)
}
```

But `builderVolumeMounts` only mounts that path under `cloudConfigRef`:

```go
if artifact.Spec.Artifacts != nil && artifact.Spec.Artifacts.CloudConfigRef != nil {
    mounts = append(mounts, corev1.VolumeMount{Name: "cloudconfig", MountPath: cloudConfigMountPath, ...})
}
```

`grubConfig` mounts something else entirely, `/iso/iso-overlay/boot/grub2/grub.cfg`. Nothing else in the package creates `/cloud-config.yaml`.

So an OSArtifact that sets `spec.artifacts.grubConfig` and no `cloudConfigRef` builds a command pointing at a file that does not exist in the container.

## Reproduction

Against `main`, with `grubConfig` set and `cloudConfigRef` unset:

```
cmd = auroraboot --debug build-iso --override-name x --date=false --output /artifacts \
      --arch amd64 --cloud-config /cloud-config.yaml dir:/rootfs

mounts: artifacts -> /artifacts
        rootfs    -> /rootfs
        config    -> /iso/iso-overlay/boot/grub2/grub.cfg

passes --cloud-config: true ; /cloud-config.yaml mounted: false
```

## Fix

Gate the flag on `cloudConfigRef` alone, matching what is actually mounted. `grubConfig` already reaches the ISO through its own overlay mount, so it never needed `--cloud-config`.

The same over-broad condition was in `buildUKICommand` and is being removed there in kairos-io/kairos-operator#189; this is the last place it survives.

Worth confirming how `auroraboot build-iso` behaves on a missing `--cloud-config` path before picking the fix: if it errors, this is a broken build for anyone using `grubConfig` alone, and if it warns and continues, it is only noise.
title: kairos-operator: `buildISOCommand` passes `--cloud-config` at a path nothing mounts when only `grubConfig` is set

author: ci-robbot
body:
Found while QA'ing [kairos-operator#182](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos-operator/pull/182). Filing here because kairos-operator has issues disabled (per kairos-operator#177).

## The bug

An `OSArtifact` that asks for `uki.iso: true` and `netboot: true` never completes. The `build-netboot` init container fails:

```
auroraboot --debug netboot /artifacts/qa182-uki-iso-netboot-uki.iso /artifacts qa182-uki-iso-netboot
ERR opening file inside iso error="target file /rootfs.squashfs does not exist"
```

`auroraboot netboot` extracts `/rootfs.squashfs`, and a `build-uki` ISO does not contain one. So the UKI ISO can never be a netboot source, and the build is dead on arrival for that combination. Reproduced with `iso: false` and with `iso: true`; the ISO flag makes no difference, because the source is chosen by the UKI flag alone.

## Why it happens

`isoBasenameForNetboot` (`internal/controller/job.go:521`) diverts the netboot source to the UKI ISO whenever `uki.iso` is set:

```go
func isoBasenameForNetboot(artifact *buildv1alpha2.OSArtifact, artifacts *buildv1alpha2.ArtifactSpec) string {
	artifactName := artifact.ArtifactNameFor(buildv1alpha2.OSArtifactKindISO)
	if artifacts != nil && artifacts.UKI != nil && artifacts.UKI.ISO {
		return ukiArtifactName(artifact)
	}
	return artifactName
}
```

The branch is not needed. The unsigned `build-iso` container is added whenever netboot is requested, and always has been:

```go
// job.go:285
if artifacts.ISO || artifacts.Netboot {
	inits = append(inits, buildIsoContainer)
}
```

That gate predates the UKI branch: `artifacts.ISO || artifacts.Netboot` came in with `ab9be79` (v0.1.0 API prep), while the UKI branch arrived later in #159 and was only renamed in #178. So `/artifacts/<name>.iso` is guaranteed to exist on every netboot build, and it is the one file that actually holds a squashfs.

## The fix

Read the unsigned ISO, unconditionally. Two existing unit tests currently pin the broken behaviour (`uses NameOverride.UKI as-is` and `appends -uki to metadata.name`), which is why CI is green today.

## Side note, not part of this

When `nameOverride.uki` is set, `ukiArtifactName` drops the `-uki` suffix, so `build-uki` and `build-iso` can be told to write the same path. `build-iso` runs second and wins, so the user silently loses the UKI ISO. Separate bug, worth its own issue if anyone hits it.
title: operator: netboot reads the UKI ISO when uki.iso is set, so the build always fails on /rootfs.squashfs

author: jimmykarily
body:
`./kairos-agent upgrade ` produces lots of warnings like:

```
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/MokManager.efi (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/bootx64.efi (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/grub.efi (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/boot/arm64/loader/grub2/fonts/unicode.pf2 
(extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/boot/grub2/grub.cfg (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/boot/grub2/i386-pc/acpi.mod (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/boot/grub2/i386-pc/adler32.mod (extension)
...
```

because we scan `/run /initramfs/live` for config files: https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos-agent/blob/e6b3e5092e5f566f8f266108e91eb86d3c6a371d/main.go#L36

author: ebourgeois
body:
## Summary

`kairos-operator`'s `OSArtifact` controller unconditionally appends
`--cloud-config` to the `auroraboot` invocation whenever
`ArtifactSpec.CloudConfigRef` is set, regardless of whether the artifact
being built is a classic ISO/cloud-image (`build-iso`, which supports
`--cloud-config`) or a Trusted Boot / UKI artifact (`build-uki`, which does
**not** support it at all). Any `OSArtifact` that sets both
`spec.artifacts.uki` and `spec.artifacts.cloudConfigRef` fails immediately
on CLI flag parsing, before any actual build work happens.

## Environment

- `kairos-operator`: current `main` (commit range including PR #73, "Fix
  --cloud-config flag ignored in ISO and UKI builds")
- `AuroraBoot`: current `main` (`internal/cmd/build-uki.go` / `pkg/uki/uki.go`)
- `OSArtifact` CRD: `build.kairos.io/v1alpha2`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create an `OSArtifact` with both:
   - `spec.artifacts.uki: {iso: true, keysVolume: <secret-set-with-PK.auth-etc>}`
   - `spec.artifacts.cloudConfigRef: {name: <secret>, key: <key>}`
2. Let kairos-operator create the build Job/Pod.
3. Observe the `build-uki-iso` container's log.

## Actual behavior

```
+ auroraboot --debug build-uki --name <name> --output-dir /artifacts --output-type iso \
    --public-keys /uki-keys --tpm-pcr-private-key /uki-keys/tpm2-pcr-private.pem \
    --sb-key /uki-keys/db.key --sb-cert /uki-keys/db.pem \
    --cloud-config /cloud-config.yaml dir:/rootfs
Incorrect Usage: flag provided but not defined: -cloud-config
```

`auroraboot build-uki --help` confirms there is no `--cloud-config` flag in
the UKI build path at all (only `--overlay-rootfs`, `--overlay-iso`, and the
Secure-Boot/TPM-signing flags). The build Job fails immediately, before
`auroraboot` does any actual work.

## Expected behavior

Either:
- `buildUKICommand` should not append `--cloud-config` when building a UKI
  artifact (mirroring the existing, correct handling of `--arch`, which the
  code already omits for UKI builds with an explicit comment noting
  `build-uki` doesn't support it), and the `OSArtifact` controller should
  reject/validate that `cloudConfigRef` + `uki` is an unsupported
  combination at admission time rather than fail at build time; or
- `auroraboot build-uki` gains equivalent cloud-config injection support
  (e.g. writing the config into the built rootfs at a well-known path before
  the UKI is assembled), so the two artifact kinds have parity.

## Root cause (as far as we could tell from source)

`kairos-operator/internal/controller/job.go`, `buildUKICommand`:

```go
// Note: auroraboot build-uki does not support --arch; arch is not passed.
if artifact.Spec.Artifacts != nil && (artifact.Spec.Artifacts.CloudConfigRef != nil || artifact.Spec.Artifacts.GRUBConfig != "") {
    fmt.Fprintf(&cmd, " --cloud-config %s", "/cloud-config.yaml")
}
```

The comment directly above this block already flags that `build-uki` lacks
`--arch` support and correctly omits it, the same care wasn't applied to
`--cloud-config` two lines later. Introduced by PR #73 ("Fix --cloud-config
flag ignored in ISO and UKI builds"), which fixed flag *ordering*
(`urfave/cli` drops flags placed after positional args) but didn't verify
`build-uki` accepts the flag in the first place. Confirmed against
`AuroraBoot/internal/cmd/build-uki.go`'s full flag list and
`pkg/uki/uki.go`'s `Options` struct: no `--cloud-config` flag and no
cloud-config field anywhere in the UKI build path.

## Workaround (consumer-side, until fixed upstream)

Don't set `cloudConfigRef` when `spec.artifacts.uki` is set. Bake the
cloud-config content in via the ISO-overlay mechanism instead
(`spec.artifacts.overlayISOVolume` / `auroraboot build-uki --overlay-iso`,
which build-uki *does* support), placing the file at whichever path
`auroraboot`'s own `--cloud-config` handling would have used internally —
this needs confirming against `auroraboot`'s source for the classic
`build-iso --cloud-config` path so the file lands somewhere Kairos's
installer actually reads it back from.

## References

- `kairos-operator/internal/controller/job.go` — `buildUKICommand`
- `kairos-operator` PR #73 — "Fix --cloud-config flag ignored in ISO and UKI builds"
- `AuroraBoot/internal/cmd/build-uki.go` — full flag definitions
- `AuroraBoot/pkg/uki/uki.go` — `Options` struct (no cloud-config field)
- Discovered while implementing Trusted Boot / UKI support in `banlieue`
  (`docs/adr/0041-vmimage-trusted-boot-uki-support.md`)
title: kairos-operator: `buildUKICommand` passes `--cloud-config` to `auroraboot build-uki`, which has no such flag

author: ci-robbot
body:
## The bug

`copyFile` in `agent/pkg/uki/common.go:145` returns `error`, and calls
`panic(err)` on the two failures it is most likely to see:

```go
func copyFile(src, dst string) error {
	sourceFile, err := os.Open(src)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer sourceFile.Close()

	destinationFile, err := os.Create(dst)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
```

Both call sites are in `installEntry` (`agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go:169` and
`:176`), and both check the returned error and log a message naming what
they were copying. Those checks are dead code for a missing source or an
uncreatable destination, which are exactly the cases they were written for.

There is no `recover()` anywhere in `agent/`, `sdk/` or `cmd/`, so the
panic terminates `kairos-agent` with a Go stack trace.

## Where it bites

`installEntry` is the whole of the UKI **recovery upgrade** and
**single-entry upgrade** paths:

```go
	if i.spec.RecoveryUpgrade() {
		i.cfg.Logger.Infof("installing entry: recovery")
		return i.installRecovery()
	}

	if i.spec.Entry != "" { // single entry upgrade
		i.cfg.Logger.Infof("installing entry: %s", i.spec.Entry)
		return i.installEntry(i.spec.Entry)
	}
```

It dumps the upgrade source into a temp dir and then opens
`<tmp>/EFI/kairos/norole.efi` from it. A source that is not a UKI artifact
set has no such file, so `kairos-agent upgrade --recovery --source <a plain
OS image>` on a trusted-boot machine dies on

```
panic: open /tmp/1234567890/EFI/kairos/norole.efi: no such file or directory
```

instead of saying which file it wanted and could not find. The destination
`os.Create` is the same shape for a full or unwritable ESP.

This also happens with `/efi` already remounted read-write by
`MountRWPartition` a few lines earlier. The deferred `cleanup.Cleanup` does
still run during the unwind, so the partition is remounted, but the ESP is
left mid-write: the second `copyFile` panicking leaves the new `.efi` in
place with the old `.conf` beside it.

## Reproduction

The panics are already pinned as expected behaviour in
`agent/pkg/uki/common_extra_test.go:289`:

```go
It("panics when the source is missing", func() {
	Expect(func() {
		_ = copyFile(filepath.Join(dir, "missing"), filepath.Join(dir, "dst"))
	}).To(Panic())
})

It("panics when the destination dir is missing", func() { ... })
```

Confirmed on `master` (`d0102329`), both fire:

```
PANICKED on missing source: open .../missing.efi: no such file or directory
PANICKED on missing destination dir: open .../nonexistent/dst.efi: no such file or directory
```

## The fix

Return the errors the signature already promises, wrapped with the path, and
flip the two specs to assert an error and no panic. Same class as #4533.

Note `copyFile` also closes both handles twice (a `defer Close()` plus an
explicit `Close()` at the end), so the deferred close returns
`file already closed` and it is discarded. Worth cleaning up in the same
change, since the final `Close()` is the one that reports a failed flush.

Not in scope, but found next door: `installEntry` uses `os.Open`, `os.Create`
and `os.MkdirTemp` directly rather than `i.cfg.Fs`, unlike the rest of the
package, which is why it cannot be driven by the existing `vfst` harness in
`upgrade_test.go`.

---

<sub>Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.</sub>
title: uki: copyFile panics instead of returning its error, killing a recovery or single-entry upgrade mid-write

Currently, the boot starts with a message to go over the webUI or showing QR code (only if provider-kairos is enabled).

While the QR code is a nice feature, it requires the user to install a specific CLI for it. Now that we have a nice installer TUI, it makes sense to consolidate into that one instead, and, make it front-facing. The TUI could inherit what the current default boot live does, and show as first message that the installation can be conduceted also on the webui or there - and we keep still a manual boot entry, but we basically fold interactive into the default one.

author: ci-robbot
body:
Filed here because `kairos-io/AuroraBoot` has issues disabled. The work lands in AuroraBoot.

## The symptom

`OSV-Scanner PR Scan` is red on **every** AuroraBoot pull request and on **every** `push` to `main` since 2026-09-02. Last green `push` run on `main` was [33462360484](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/actions/runs/33462360484) (2026-09-01).

Because it fails on everything, it carries no signal per PR: an author cannot tell their branch from the baseline, so the check gets ignored, and a vulnerability that a branch actually introduces would look identical to the current noise.

## It is not a scanner misconfiguration

Worth stating up front, because a permanently-red scanner usually is. This one is not: the scan is doing its job and reporting six real, fixable advisories that are all present on `main`. From the `main`-push run [34149252528](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/actions/runs/34149252528):

| Advisory | Sev | Ecosystem | Package | On main | Fixed in | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GO-2026-6354 | | Go | `golang.org/x/crypto` | 0.55.0 | 0.56.0 | `go.mod` |
| GO-2026-6355 | | Go | `golang.org/x/crypto` | 0.55.0 | 0.56.0 | `go.mod` |
| [GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc) | **High 8.7** | Go | `google.golang.org/grpc` | 1.82.1 | 1.83.1 | `go.mod` |
| [GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) | Medium | npm | `qs` (dev) | 6.15.3 | 6.16.0 | `e2e/web/package-lock.json` |
| [GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx) | Medium | npm | `qs` (dev) | 6.15.3 | 6.16.0 | `e2e/web/package-lock.json` |
| [GHSA-p498-v437-472g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p498-v437-472g) | Medium | npm | `@humanfs/node` (dev) | 0.16.7 | 0.16.8 | `ui/package-lock.json` |

The scanner's own words: `6 vulnerabilities can be fixed.`

The one that actually matters is **GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc**, gRPC-Go heap memory exhaustion via HTTP/2 DATA frame fragmentation, High. Confirmed against the GitHub advisory API: vulnerable `<= 1.83.0`, first patched `1.83.1`. The rest are dev-only npm and the two x/crypto entries.

## Why renovate did not clear it on its own

Both Go packages are `// indirect`, which renovate is not bumping here, so they sit at whatever a transitive requirement pulls in.

The `qs` one is more interesting, and is the part likely to recur. `e2e/web/package.json` carries a deliberate `overrides` pin:

```json
"overrides": {
  "qs": "6.15.3"
}
```

That override was added in `cada37a` (#538) precisely to raise `qs` above a *then*-current advisory, because `@cypress/request` requests `^6.15.2` and would otherwise resolve low. It works, but written as an exact version it is a ceiling as well as a floor, so each new `qs` advisory re-reds the scan and needs a manual edit. #585 was that edit last time. This is the second occurrence.

## Second finding: govulncheck never runs, so nothing is reachability-filtered

Quieter, and it changes how the Go rows above should be read. In the same log:

```
Failed to run code analysis (govulncheck) on '/github/workspace/go.mod' because
govulncheck: loading packages: err: exit status 1: stderr:
go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26.6 (running go 1.26.2; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
```

`osv-scanner-action` v2.3.8's container ships Go 1.26.2 with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, and AuroraBoot's `go.mod` declares `go 1.26.6`. The toolchain cannot be upgraded in-container, so the call-graph pass is skipped.

Consequences:

- Every Go advisory is reported on **module presence alone**, with no check that the vulnerable symbol is reachable from AuroraBoot. So the Go rows may include vulns AuroraBoot cannot reach, and the noise floor is structurally higher than it needs to be.
- It is a **soft** failure. The scan proceeds and exits on the findings, so this line scrolls past in a job that was going to be red anyway. It has been silently true since the `go.mod` bump crossed 1.26.2.

This one is upstream-bound: it clears when the action image ships a Go at least as new as our `go.mod`, or if the workflow stops pinning `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`. Not fixable from this repo beyond lowering the `go` directive, which is not worth doing for a scanner.

## Fix

Bumping the four packages clears all six advisories, which turns the check back into a signal.

- `golang.org/x/crypto`, `google.golang.org/grpc`, and the `qs` override: covered by the PR linked below.
- `@humanfs/node` 0.16.7 to 0.16.8: already covered by dependabot [AuroraBoot#774](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/pull/774), so it is deliberately left out to avoid a duplicate bump. **Both need to land for the scan to go green.**

For the recurrence, worth a maintainer decision separately: the `qs` override could be dropped entirely now that `@cypress/request`'s `^6.15.2` range resolves to a patched version on its own, which removes the stale-pin failure mode rather than resetting its clock.

## Acceptance criteria

- `OSV-Scanner PR Scan` is green on a `push` to `main`.
- A red scan on a PR again means something about that PR.
- The govulncheck toolchain gap is either resolved upstream or recorded as knowingly accepted.
title: AuroraBoot: OSV-Scanner PR Scan red on every PR and every main push since 2026-09-02

author: ci-robbot
body:
Filed here because `kairos-io/go-nodepair` has issues disabled. The work lands in go-nodepair.

## The symptom

`OSV-Scanner PR Scan` is red on **every** go-nodepair pull request, and has been since 2026-06-29. The last green run was [on 2026-06-24](https://github.com/kairos-io/go-nodepair/actions/workflows/osv-scanner-pr.yaml). Every run in the 47 since then has failed, on renovate branches and human branches alike.

Because it fails on everything it carries no per-PR signal, so the check gets ignored, and an advisory a branch actually introduces would look identical to the baseline noise.

## Why nobody noticed it drift

The workflow still carries the template's branch names:

```yaml
# Change "main" to your default branch if you use a different name, i.e. "master"
on:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches:
      - main
```

This repository's default branch is `master`. So the scan has **never run on the default branch**: no baseline exists, and a newly published advisory is invisible until it reddens somebody's unrelated PR.

## What is actually being reported

The logs and the SARIF artifact both 403 from a runner-less box, so I reconstructed the findings locally: the Go vulnerability database is a Go module (`golang.org/x/vulndb`), so it can be pulled through the module proxy and matched against `go.mod` with `x/mod/semver`, and the GitHub Advisory Database has a REST endpoint. Ten findings on `master`, from both sources:

| ID | Module | Have | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GO-2026-5066 | `golang.org/x/image` | 0.41.0 | 0.43.0 |
| GO-2026-5062 | `golang.org/x/image` | 0.41.0 | 0.43.0 |
| GO-2026-5061 | `golang.org/x/image` | 0.41.0 | 0.43.0 |
| GO-2026-4961 | `golang.org/x/image` | 0.41.0 | 0.42.0 |
| GO-2026-6222 | `golang.org/x/image` | 0.41.0 | 0.45.0 |
| GO-2026-6179 | `golang.org/x/mod` | 0.38.0 | 0.40.0 |
| GO-2026-6180 | `golang.org/x/mod` | 0.38.0 | 0.40.0 |
| GO-2026-6099 | `github.com/quic-go/webtransport-go` | 0.10.0 | 0.11.1 |
| GO-2024-3218 | `github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-kad-dht` | 0.41.0 | **none** |
| GO-2026-5932 | `golang.org/x/crypto` (openpgp) | 0.56.0 | **none** |

Eight of the ten have a fixed release. Only the last two cannot be bumped.

## What broke the streak, and what piled on after

`GO-2026-5066` (out-of-bounds strip offset in `x/image/tiff`) landed in the Go database at 2026-06-26 20:04 UTC, between the last green run on 06-24 and the first red one on 06-29. That is the one that ended the streak.

The rest arrived on top of an already-red check, which is exactly the failure mode this issue is about:

| Landed | ID |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-06-18 | GO-2026-5061, GO-2026-5062 |
| 2026-06-26 | **GO-2026-5066** |
| 2026-07-07 | GO-2026-5932 |
| 2026-07-08 | *(`GO-2024-3218` ignore expires)* |
| 2026-08-13 | GO-2026-6179, GO-2026-6180 |
| 2026-08-14 | GO-2026-6222 |
| 2026-08-18 | GO-2026-6099 |

`GO-2024-3218` deserves its own line. It was never a new finding: `osv-scanner.toml` already suppresses it, with `ignoreUntil = 2026-07-08` and a reason ending "Re-evaluate before expiry." The date passed and nothing was re-evaluated, because by then the check had already been red for nine days and the expiry could not be distinguished from the noise. A dated ignore only works on a check somebody still reads.

## Which ones are reachable

`govulncheck` is not run by this workflow, so everything above is reported on module presence alone. Checking by hand with `go list -deps ./...`:

- **`x/image`: reachable.** `golang.org/x/image/tiff`, `webp` and `vp8l` are all in the build; `disintegration/imaging` registers them as decoders and `qrcode.Scan` calls `image.Decode` on a PNG file it wrote from a screenshot. Worth bumping on its merits.
- **`x/mod`: not in the build at all.** Bump it anyway, it is free.
- **`x/crypto/openpgp`: not in the build.** `go list -deps` reaches `blake2b`, `blake2s`, `sha3`, `salsa20` and `cryptobyte`, and no openpgp package. This advisory is against the package being unmaintained, so no fixed release will ever exist; it needs a justified ignore.
- **`go-libp2p-kad-dht`: in the build**, transitively via edgevpn, and affected at every version. Also ignore-only.

There is a third permanent entry already in the file, `GHSA-q7pp-wcgr-pffx` on `disintegration/imaging`. It is correct and it stays: `imaging` is archived at 1.6.2 from 2019, the Go database reviewed the same report and excluded it as `NOT_A_VULNERABILITY` (GO-2023-2039), and the vulnerable path is unreachable anyway (pixterm's `ansimage` only calls `imaging.Resize`, `Fill` and `Fit` on an already-decoded `image.Image`).

## Fix

Opened as [kairos-io/go-nodepair#80](https://github.com/kairos-io/go-nodepair/pull/80):

1. Bump `x/image` to 0.45.0, `x/mod` to 0.40.0 and `webtransport-go` to 0.11.1, clearing eight of the ten.
2. Point the `push` and `merge_group` triggers at `master`, so the default branch gets a baseline.
3. Renew `GO-2024-3218` and add `GO-2026-5932` to `osv-scanner.toml`, each with why it cannot be bumped and why it does not apply here.

One thing worth a maintainer's call rather than mine: both dated entries now expire on 2027-09-10, which schedules a red check for a day when there is still nothing to bump. The alternative is to drop `ignoreUntil` entirely and let them sit as permanent suppressions like the `imaging` one. I kept the dates because a suppression nobody rereads is how this issue happened, but I am happy to flip them.

## Acceptance criteria

- `OSV-Scanner PR Scan` is green on a `push` to `master`.
- A red scan on a PR again means something about that PR.

## Related

Same class as #4532, which was the AuroraBoot version of this.

🤖 Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.
title: go-nodepair: OSV-Scanner PR Scan red on every PR since 2026-06-29, and never runs on the default branch

author: mauromorales
body:
## Context

Preparing a Kairos release today involves manually tracking state across many repositories, issues, PRs, dependency versions, and CI pipelines. Maintainers assemble this picture by opening multiple GitHub tabs, scanning Renovate PRs, checking the [kairos-io/security](https://github.com/kairos-io/security) repo, and working through a release issue checklist like [#4095](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4095).

This is error-prone and time-consuming. We want a single place that answers:

> **Can we release now? If not, what specifically needs to happen?**

This issue tracks designing (and ideally prototyping) an interactive **release readiness dashboard** for Kairos maintainers.

Related: [#4122](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4122) (dependency upgrade strategy spike) — the dashboard should integrate with whatever upgrade workflow we land on there.

## Goal

Build (or extend) a tool that gives maintainers an at-a-glance, interactive view of release readiness across the Kairos ecosystem, replacing much of the manual tab-hopping currently required when cutting a release.

## Starting point: extend [plugdash](https://github.com/Itxaka/plugdash)

[@Itxaka](https://github.com/Itxaka)'s [plugdash](https://github.com/Itxaka/plugdash) is a strong foundation. It already provides:

- A plugin-based dashboard server (Go binary + embedded web UI)
- GitHub plugins for releases, PRs, issues, CI status, milestones, stale items, review queue
- `dependency-freshness` — compares direct `go.mod` / `package.json` deps vs latest releases
- `osv-vulns` — known vulnerabilities for a package version
- `file-version` — reads pinned dependency values from files on a repo branch (e.g. kairos-init version in the Dockerfile)
- `docker-image` — checks whether expected image tags exist in a registry
- Config-as-code via YAML (`--config`), SSE live updates, and a hybrid UI + declarative tracker model

Evaluate extending plugdash (upstream contributions and/or Kairos-specific plugins/config) rather than building a separate tool from scratch.

## What the dashboard should show

### Release readiness summary

A top-level widget (or dedicated view) that gives a clear **go / no-go** signal for the current target release, e.g.:

- 🟢 **Ready** — all blockers resolved, checklist complete, CI green
- 🟡 **Blocked** — N items need attention (with links)
- 🔴 **Not ready** — critical blockers (CVEs, failing CI, open release-critical issues)

### Dependency & version bumps

Surface what is out of date or mismatched across Kairos-related repos:

| Component | Current (pinned) | Latest | Action needed |
|-----------|------------------|--------|---------------|
| kairos-init | … | … | bump + release |
| osbuilder | … | … | up to date |
| k3s (×3 versions) | … | … | update |
| auroraboot | … | … | bump |
| … | | | |

Leverage existing plugdash plugins (`dependency-freshness`, `file-version`, `github-releases`, `docker-image`) and identify gaps.

### Open tickets & PRs blocking release

- Issues/PRs tagged for the target milestone or release label
- Open Renovate/update PRs that need merging before release
- Critical/high-priority issues from [kairos-io/security](https://github.com/kairos-io/security)
- Docs repo open PRs that should land before release
- Stale release-related items needing a decision (close, defer, or fix)

### CI & artifact health

- CI status across key repos (`kairos`, `kairos-init`, `osbuilder`, `kairos-agent`, …)
- Release artifact completeness for latest/pre-release tags (ISOs, checksums, multi-arch images)
- Workflow health trends (recent failure rate)

### Release checklist (interactive)

Embed the release checklist from our [release issue template](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/release.md) — as used in [#4095](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4095) — as an interactive checklist widget:

- [ ] **Stage 0 - Finishing Touches**
  - [ ] Check for critical CVEs in internal components
  - [ ] Verify binary versions in kairos-init Makefile
  - [ ] Bump and release kairos-init if needed
  - [ ] Bump kairos-init version in kairos Dockerfile
  - [ ] CI tests passing
  - [ ] Kairos docs PRs merged
  - [ ] osbuilder at desired version
  - [ ] k3s versions correct (latest 3 available)
  - [ ] Consider cutting rc/alpha
- [ ] **Stage 1 - Manual testing** (generic hardware + RPi scenarios)
- [ ] **Stage 3 - Release** (tag, update release notes, trigger docs CI)
- [ ] **Stage 4 - Announcement** (blog post)

Checklist state should persist (per release target / milestone) and contribute to the go/no-go signal.

## Interactive actions

The dashboard should not just display state — it should let maintainers **act** from it:

- **Request a dependency bump** — trigger an upgrade PR (via Renovate dashboard checkbox, Updatecli, or whatever workflow [#4122](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4122) recommends)
- **Mark checklist items done** — with optional link/comment
- **Retry a failed CI run** (if feasible via GitHub API)
- **Open/create a release issue** pre-populated from current dashboard state
- **Snooze / defer** a non-blocking item to a future release

Start with read-only visualization; define which actions are feasible in v1 vs. later.

## Repositories & components to track

At minimum, the dashboard should cover:

- `kairos-io/kairos`
- `kairos-io/kairos-init`
- `kairos-io/osbuilder`
- `kairos-io/kairos-agent`
- `kairos-io/kairos-docs`
- `kairos-io/security`
- Key container images on quay.io (auroraboot, kairos images, …)
- k3s version pins

Document the full list during the spike.

## Questions to answer

1. **Extend plugdash vs. fork vs. separate tool** — what's the right contribution model?
2. **New plugins needed** — what can't existing plugdash plugins do today? (e.g. cross-repo version matrix, release checklist persistence, go/no-go aggregation)
3. **Data sources** — GitHub API, Renovate Dependency Dashboard, OSV, quay.io, file pins across repos — what's the integration plan?
4. **Release target model** — how do we scope the dashboard to a specific version (e.g. v4.1.1)? Milestone? Release issue? Manual selector?
5. **Hosting** — run locally, shared maintainer instance, CI artifact, or deployed service?
6. **Auth & permissions** — read-only for most viewers; which actions need elevated tokens?
7. **Relationship to release issues** — does the dashboard replace, supplement, or sync with issues like [#4095](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4095)?

## Deliverables

- [ ] Inventory of existing plugdash plugins vs. Kairos release needs (gap analysis)
- [ ] Wireframe or screenshot mockup of the release readiness view
- [ ] Working PoC (plugdash config and/or new plugins) demonstrating at least:
  - Go/no-go summary for a target release
  - Dependency/version bump matrix for key components
  - Embedded release checklist
- [ ] List of interactive actions feasible for v1
- [ ] Recommendation: upstream to plugdash vs. Kairos-specific layer
- [ ] Follow-up implementation issue(s)

## Out of scope

- Automating the release itself (tagging, publishing assets) — this is about **visibility and decision support**
- Replacing the release issue template entirely (at least initially — the dashboard should complement it)

## References

- [Itxaka/plugdash](https://github.com/Itxaka/plugdash) — plugin dashboard server
- [plugdash plugin catalog](https://github.com/Itxaka/plugdash/blob/main/docs/PLUGIN_CATALOG.md)
- [Release issue template](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/release.md)
- [Kairos release v4.1.1 (#4095)](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4095) — example release issue with checklist
- [#4122](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4122) — dependency upgrade strategy spike
title: [SPIKE] Release readiness dashboard — visualize blockers, bumps, and release actions

- `efi-key-enroller`: missing `administrators` (want `admin`); missing `maintainers` (want `maintain`); missing `contributors` (want `triage`)

author: ci-robbot
body:
## What happens

When `scan shipped bundle` fails, neither the job log nor the check-run annotation says **which** advisory tripped it. The whole message is:

```
##[error]1 unignored advisories (1 findings) in the shipped bundle.
Bump the affected component, or add a dated entry to osv-scanner.toml with a reason.
```

The findings table is written, but only to two places that are hard to reach:

- `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which renders in the web UI and is not exposed by the REST API at all (`check-runs` returns `output.summary: null` for this job);
- the `osv-scan` artifact, whose download redirects to `productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`, which 403s for anything but a browser session.

The ignored findings, by contrast, are printed to the log in full by osv-scanner itself, one `... has been filtered out because: ...` line each. So the log tells you everything about the advisories that do not matter and nothing about the one that does.

## Why it matters

This is a required release gate: `release.yaml` and `release-arm.yaml` call it via `workflow_call` and every publishing job depends on it. When it goes red during a release, the first question is always "which advisory", and today that question cannot be answered from the log, the API, or the artifact.

Concretely, today: GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv was published at 18:01 UTC and put containerd `< 2.3.5` in range, which reddened the gate on the first branch built after it (#4550). Identifying it took a diff of the package lists of two builds plus a search of golang/vulndb and the GHSA database, because the failing run would not name it. The bump is #4575.

## Fix

Two small changes to the `Report and enforce` step in `.github/workflows/release-scan.yml`:

1. `tee` the report block to stdout as well as the step summary, so the table is in the log;
2. put the advisory IDs in the `::error::` annotation, so they are readable through the check-runs API without opening the web UI.

## Note, not part of this

`osv-scanner.toml` currently carries 8 ignore entries that match nothing in the bundle, printed on every run as `osv-scanner.toml has unused ignores:`. The 7 containerd ones went dead when provider-kairos was absorbed into the monorepo, which builds containerd/v2 2.3.x. Worth a separate cleanup.

🤖 Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler
title: CI: release scan fails without naming the advisory; the findings table is only in the step summary and a 403ing artifact

author: ci-robbot
body:
Filed here because issues are tracked in this repo; the code is in `kairos-io/AuroraBoot`.

## What happens

`e2e-tests` on AuroraBoot goes red with two of the three `build-uki` specs failing in the same run, always on the same step:

```
mount: /tmp/iso: WARNING: source write-protected, mounted read-only.
mount: /dev/loop2 mounted on /tmp/iso.
losetup: /tmp/iso/efiboot.img: failed to set up loop device: No such file or directory
losetup: device node /dev/loop4 (7:4) is lost. You may use mknod(1) to recover it.
umount: /tmp/efi: not mounted.
```

Last seen on [run 34119723290](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/actions/runs/34119723290) (`19 Passed | 2 Failed`), on kairos-io/AuroraBoot#776, a PR that touches only the reset lifecycle and nothing near this code.

## Why

`e2e/build_uki_test.go:127` shells into `docker run --privileged` and loop-mounts twice: once for the ISO, once for `efiboot.img` inside it.

```bash
LOOP_ISO=$(losetup --find --show %[1]s)
mount -v -t iso9660 "$LOOP_ISO" /tmp/iso
LOOP_EFI=$(losetup --find --show /tmp/iso/efiboot.img)
mount -v "$LOOP_EFI" /tmp/efi
```

`.github/workflows/tests.yml:124` runs the suite with `ginkgo -p`, so the three specs run side by side, each in its own container, each wanting two loop devices off the one host kernel. Two things break:

1. **`losetup --find` is not atomic.** It asks the kernel for a free index with `LOOP_CTL_GET_FREE`, which *reports* an index without claiming it. Concurrent callers are handed the same one and only one wins. Both failing specs above name the same `/dev/loop4`, which is the race caught in the act.
2. **A container's `/dev` is a snapshot taken at container start.** Once the parallel specs have the low indices bound, the kernel has to create `loop4` to satisfy the next request. That node lands in the host's devtmpfs, not in the container's snapshot, so opening it fails `ENOENT` - which is exactly what `device node /dev/loop4 (7:4) is lost` reports.

The second point is why this is not a retry-able flake. `LOOP_CTL_GET_FREE` keeps returning the same free-but-invisible index for as long as the other specs hold theirs, which is minutes.

The three specs share `/tmp/iso` and `/tmp/efi` as fixed paths too. That is harmless today because each spec gets its own container and so its own mount namespace, but it is one `-v /tmp:/tmp` away from being a second collision.

## Fix

Stop using loop devices. `xorriso -osirrox` extracts the ESP out of the ISO and mtools reads the FAT image directly - which is how `build-uki` writes it in the first place (`mformat`/`mmd`/`mcopy` in `pkg/uki/uki.go:935-973`). Both binaries are already in the auroraboot image (`Dockerfile:47,57`). Nothing gets mounted, so the parallel specs share nothing.
title: AuroraBoot e2e: build-uki specs race on host loop devices under ginkgo -p

author: mauro-agent
body:
## What happens

A version bump in `kairos-init`'s `Makefile` fails CI with a 404 if it lands shortly after the component's release is published, because **a GitHub release exists before its assets finish uploading**, and the download has only a 10-second retry budget.

Observed on kairos-io/kairos-init#433, twice in the same run:

| time (UTC) | event |
|---|---|
| 08:50:33 | `kairos-agent` `v2.31.2` release **published** — tag exists, tarballs do not |
| 08:52:48 → 08:52:58 | `make` downloads, six 404s, gives up after ~10s |
| 08:53:08 | `Tests` and `Unit tests` both fail at `Makefile:85` |
| **08:54:13** | **assets finish uploading** |

The window was about 3 minutes 40 seconds. The retry budget covered 10 seconds of it.

```
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
make: *** [Makefile:85: pkg/bundled/binaries/kairos-agent] Error 2
```

Re-running after the upload finishes is green with no change, which is what makes this easy to dismiss as a flake.

## Why it is easy to misread

Three things point away from the real cause:

1. **It looks like the bump is wrong.** The failing target names the component just bumped.
2. **It looks branch-specific.** The same job passes on branches that do not touch `Makefile`, because buildx serves the download layer from cache and never fetches. Only a `Makefile` change busts that cache, so only a version bump exposes it.
3. **Every URL is valid by the time anyone investigates.** Checked afterwards, every constructed URL — all components, all architectures, FIPS and non-FIPS — returns 200.

## The download

```make
curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 2 $($*_URL) | tar -xz -C $(OUTPUT_DIR)
```

`--retry 5 --retry-delay 2` is a fixed ~10 seconds. Asset upload for a multi-architecture release is routinely minutes.

## Two fixes, and the second is the better one

**1. Widen the retry window here.** Add `--retry-max-time` so a download tolerates a release still uploading:

```make
curl -fsSL --retry 10 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 6 --retry-max-time 300 $($*_URL) | ...
```

Cheap, local, and it only makes `kairos-init` patient. It does not stop the underlying race, and every other consumer of these releases keeps hitting it.

**2. Do not publish the release until its assets are uploaded.** In the component repositories' release workflows, create the release as a **draft**, upload the assets, then flip it to published. GitHub then never shows a release whose downloads 404.

This is the real fix, because the tag becoming visible is what tells everyone downstream the artifacts exist. Anything watching for a release — a person, a bot, another pipeline — currently gets told too early.

Both are worth doing. 1 is a one-line change in `kairos-init` and guards against a slow upload; 2 removes the class.

## Not a blocker for anything today

kairos-io/kairos-init#433 goes green on a re-run. Filing so the next person to bump a pin shortly after a release does not spend the afternoon on it.

<sub>🤖 Filed by `mauro-agent`, an AI agent operated by @mauromorales, at his request and with his review.</sub>
title: Version bumps 404 when a release's assets are still uploading

author: ci-robbot
body:
**Kairos version:** `master` (`d17464a2`), and every released `kairos-agent` that ships the UKI code path.

**CPU architecture, OS, and Version:** all, trusted boot / UKI only.

## Describe the bug

`kairos-agent` panics with `assignment to entry in nil map` during a UKI **install**, **upgrade** or **reset** if any `.conf` file on the EFI partition cannot be read. The user gets a Go stack trace in the middle of the operation instead of an error naming the file.

The panic comes from [`AddSystemdConfSortKey`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/common.go#L174-L216):

```go
conf, err := sdkutils.SystemdBootConfReader(path)
if err != nil {
	log.Errorf("Error reading conf file to extract values %s: %s", conf, path)
}
...
conf["sort-key"] = sortKey        // conf is nil here
```

`SystemdBootConfReader` returns `nil, err` on both of its failure paths ([`sdk/utils/utils.go#L436-L459`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/sdk/utils/utils.go#L436-L459)): a failed `os.Open`, and a `scanner.Err()`. The error is logged but not returned, the walk callback carries on, and line 204 writes to the nil map.

Two smaller things in the same three lines:

- The `Errorf` arguments are **swapped and incomplete**. The format is `"...%s: %s"` and the args are `conf, path`, so the first `%s` gets the (nil) map and the second gets the path. `err` is never printed. Even the log that is supposed to explain the failure does not name it.
- Skipping the file and continuing would not be a fix either: the write at line 204-211 rebuilds the whole file from the map, so proceeding with an empty map would truncate the entry to a bare `sort-key 0001` and drop `title`, `uki`/`efi` and `sort-key`'s siblings. That entry would not boot. The panic is currently the only thing preventing that.

## Why it matters

The function is not an edge path. It runs over the **entire ESP mountpoint** on all three lifecycle operations:

- [`agent/pkg/uki/install.go#L182`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/install.go#L182)
- [`agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go#L108`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go#L108)
- [`agent/pkg/uki/reset.go#L92`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/reset.go#L92)

and it matches every `*.conf` that is not `loader.conf`, anywhere under that mountpoint.

A panic there is worse than a failed upgrade. It happens after `DeployImage` and after the artifact set has been copied into place, so the ESP is already half-rewritten. There is no unwinding: the deferred remount of the ESP back to read-only does not run for the process that took the panic, and `immucore`'s boot-failure reporting ([`immucore/internal/utils/bootfailure.go`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/immucore/internal/utils/bootfailure.go)) has no error to classify because the agent died without producing one.

This is also the odd one out. The two neighbours in the same walk over the same files handle a read failure correctly: `removeDefaultKeysFromLoaderConf` returns the error ([`common.go#L219-L223`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/common.go#L219-L223)) and so does `upgradeEfiKeysInLoaderEntries` ([`common.go#L273-L277`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/common.go#L273-L277)).

## To Reproduce

The current behaviour is already pinned by a test that treats the panic as expected, [`agent/pkg/uki/common_extra_test.go#L338-L352`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/common_extra_test.go#L338-L352):

```go
It("panics on unreadable conf files", func() {
	// when the conf reader fails the error is only logged and the
	// returned nil map is written to, which panics
```

Standalone:

```go
dir := t.TempDir()
p := filepath.Join(dir, "active.conf")
os.WriteFile(p, []byte("title Kairos\nuki /EFI/kairos/active.efi\n"), 0644)
os.Chmod(p, 0000)

AddSystemdConfSortKey(vfs.OSFS, dir, sdkLogger.NewKairosLogger("test", "debug", true))
```

```text
panic: assignment to entry in nil map
```

The permission bit is just the cheapest trigger in a test; `kairos-agent` runs as root, so on a real machine the reachable ones are the I/O paths:

- `os.Open` or a read returning `EIO` on the vfat ESP. That partition is mounted read-only in normal operation and is only remounted read-write for exactly these operations, so a bad block or a directory entry damaged by an unclean shutdown surfaces here first.
- `scanner.Err()` returning `bufio.ErrTooLong` for a `.conf` with no newline in its first 64 KiB, which is what a `.conf`-named file whose contents got replaced by garbage looks like.

**Expected behavior:** the operation fails with an error that names the file and the underlying cause, e.g. `adding sort key: reading /efi/loader/entries/active.conf: input/output error`.

## Fix

Return the read error, wrapped with the path, and fix the `Errorf` call so the log says which file and why. The characterisation test becomes an assertion that the error is returned and that the file is left untouched.

I am picking this up.
title: kairos-agent panics with "assignment to entry in nil map" on UKI install/upgrade/reset when a conf on the ESP cannot be read

author: ci-robbot
body:
## The bug

`provider-decentralized-k8s` failed on `master` in
[run 34251428760](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34251428760)
with the VM never starting:

```
VM Aborted.
stdout:
stderr: Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
qemu-system-x86_64: failed to initialize kvm: Permission denied
```

The `Enable KVM group perms` step in that same job is **green**. So `/dev/kvm`
was accessible when the step ran and not accessible thirteen seconds later
when qemu opened it. `Permission denied` and not `No such file or directory`,
so the device node existed the whole time.

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/reusable-qemu-test.yaml:239` is:

```yaml
- name: Enable KVM group perms
  run: |
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y libvirt-clients libvirt-daemon-system libvirt-daemon virtinst bridge-utils qemu-system-x86 qemu-utils acl udev mkisofs swtpm ovmf curl
    sudo setfacl -m u:runner:rwx /dev/kvm
```

The step runs under `bash -e`, so a failing `setfacl` would have reddened it.
It did not. The ACL was set and then lost.

Installing the qemu/libvirt stack triggers udev. `udevadm trigger` is
asynchronous: it queues the events and returns, and udevd applies the packaged
`/dev/kvm` ownership (`root:kvm`, `0660`) whenever it gets to them. Nothing in
this step waits for that queue to drain, so the ordering is a race between
udevd and `setfacl`, and an ACL applied first is simply overwritten.

Timeline from the run:

```
17:38:26.7  Setting up qemu-system-common
17:38:27.2  Setting up libvirt-daemon-system
17:38:30.8  apt finishes, setfacl runs, exits 0
17:38:32.0  step ends green
17:38:42.0  spec starts the VM
17:38:45.0  Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
```

## Why only this cell

`reusable-qemu-test.yaml:133`:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ inputs.test == 'provider-decentralized-k8s' && 'ubuntu-24.04' || 'fast' }}
```

`provider-decentralized-k8s` is the only cell on a GitHub-hosted runner, so it
is the only one that installs libvirt and qemu from scratch on every run. On
the self-hosted `fast` label they are already present, `apt-get install` is a
no-op, nothing triggers udev, and the race never opens.

## Two things worth fixing

1. **The ACL does not survive a udev re-trigger.** A rule in
   `/etc/udev/rules.d/` outranks the packaged one, so the mode holds no matter
   when udevd processes the event. `udevadm settle` then closes the window
   left by the postinst triggers.
2. **The failure surfaces in the wrong place.** The step that owns `/dev/kvm`
   passes, and the suite dies minutes later on a spec that has nothing to do
   with permissions. A `test -w /dev/kvm` at the end of the step would name
   the real problem in two seconds.

The same step exists in `.github/workflows/_uki-test.yaml:166`.

Note this is distinct from #4557: that one is about the panic swallowing the
logs, this one is about why the VM aborted in the first place.
title: CI: provider-decentralized-k8s aborts with "Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied" although Enable KVM group perms is green

author: mauro-agent
body:
## What

`agent/pkg/config`'s Ginkgo suite has an intermittently failing spec: **"Reads properly the cloud config for upgrade"** (`agent/pkg/config/spec_test.go:852`).

## Reproduction

On `master` at `7fc1a761` (unrelated to #4540, which only adds a new file):

```sh
go test ./agent/pkg/config/... --ginkgo.focus="Reads properly the cloud config for upgrade" -count=1
```

Run in isolation (`--ginkgo.focus` runs only this one spec, out of 197 in the suite, so it's not order-dependence on a sibling spec), repeated in a loop:

- First batch: **9 failures out of 15 consecutive runs.**
- A later batch, same machine, same command: **0 failures out of 20 runs.**

So it reproduces reliably in some conditions and not at all in others. I did not find a root cause, just confirmed it's real:

- It's not caused by kairos-io/kairos#4540 (the PR I was reviewing when I found it) — #4540 only adds a new file, `agent/pkg/config/fuzz_test.go`, no production code, and the flake reproduces on plain `master` with that file present or absent.
- It's not sibling-spec order dependence — a focused run of just this one spec still fails intermittently.
- The clustering (all failures in one batch, all passes in another, rather than an even scatter) suggests something environment- or timing-sensitive rather than pure randomness in the test data itself, but I don't have a confirmed explanation. Worth checking with `-race`, and worth checking whether `dir`, `runner`, `fs`, `mounter`, or `ci` (the shared fixtures this spec and its neighbors read) have any per-run setup that could be slow or racy on a loaded machine.

## Not included

I didn't capture the actual assertion failure text from a failing run (the batch that had 9 failures logged only the `FAIL` summary line, not per-run `--ginkgo.v` detail; by the time I reran with full verbose output enabled, it stopped reproducing). Whoever picks this up will likely need to loop the command above a few times to catch one live.
title: agent/pkg/config: intermittent failure in "Reads properly the cloud config for upgrade"

author: ocalzi
body:
## Context

mudler/yip PR #329 fixes `provider_hetzner.go` to use Hetzner's native `/hetzner/v1/` metadata API.

PR: https://github.com/mudler/yip/pull/329

## Why this matters

kairos-agent (now part of this repo) embeds yip. Without this fix, the Hetzner datasource `Probe()` fails on all Hetzner servers after **2026-08-01** (when Hetzner removed EC2-compatible metadata routes — https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2026-08-01-removed-metadata-routes).

Result: no cloud-config applied → Kairos nodes install without k3s config, SSH keys, or hostname. All current Kairos ISO releases are broken for Hetzner automated provisioning.

## Request

1. Once mudler/yip#329 is merged and a yip release is tagged, bump the yip dependency
2. Cut a new kairos-agent release
3. Build and publish a new Kairos ISO so users can update `kairos_iso_id` in their provisioning configs
title: bump yip: fix Hetzner native metadata URLs (EC2-compat removed 2026-08-01)

author: nianyush
body:
**Kairos version:**
kairos-agent `v2.27.5`

**CPU architecture, OS, and Version:**
<!-- Not captured; disk is NVMe. Please add `uname -a` output if available. -->

**Describe the bug**

When `install.partitions.persistent.size` is set to a **fixed** value *and* an
`install.extra-partitions` entry is also defined, the extra partition is created
on disk but ends up **without a `PARTLABEL`**, so it cannot be located via
`/dev/disk/by-partlabel/<name>` after installation. The GPT is also left in an
inconsistent state.

If `persistent.size` is left unset, the same config works correctly and the
extra partition is found by partlabel as expected.

**To Reproduce**

Install a node with the following cloud-config:

```yaml
#cloud-config
install:
  partitions:
    persistent:
      size: 300000
  extra-partitions:
    - name: data_partition
      size: 300000
      label: SYSTEM_DATA
      fs: ext4
stages:
  after-install-chroot:
    - commands:
        - wipefs -a /dev/disk/by-partlabel/data_partition
      if: "blkid -t TYPE=ext4 /dev/disk/by-partlabel/data_partition >/dev/null 2>&1"
      name: Wipe SYSTEM_DATA to raw for Piraeus
```

After installation, `/dev/disk/by-partlabel/data_partition` does not exist and
the partition has no `PARTLABEL`.

**Expected behavior**

The extra partition `data_partition` should be created with its configured
name/partlabel (and requested size) and be resolvable at
`/dev/disk/by-partlabel/data_partition` — exactly as it is when
`persistent.size` is not set.

**Logs**

```console
root@edge:~# lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,PARTLABEL,PARTTYPENAME
NAME          SIZE FSTYPE LABEL          PARTLABEL  PARTTYPENAME
loop0           8G ext2   COS_ACTIVE
nvme1n1       1.7T
├─nvme1n1p1    64M vfat   COS_GRUB       efi        EFI System
├─nvme1n1p2     5G ext4   COS_OEM        oem        Linux filesystem
├─nvme1n1p3  19.7G ext4   COS_RECOVERY   recovery   Linux filesystem
├─nvme1n1p4    25G ext4   COS_STATE      state      Linux filesystem
├─nvme1n1p5   293G ext4   COS_PERSISTENT persistent Linux filesystem
└─nvme1n1p6   293G
```

```console
root@edge:~# sgdisk -p /dev/nvme1n1

Warning! Secondary partition table overlaps the last partition by
33 blocks!
You will need to delete this partition or resize it in another utility.
Disk /dev/nvme1n1: 3750748848 sectors, 1.7 TiB
Model: VO001920KXVYF
Sector size (logical/physical): 512/4096 bytes
Disk identifier (GUID): 2CEFF841-4C1D-5A14-8E46-ED3AEB621093
Partition table holds up to 128 entries
Main partition table begins at sector 2 and ends at sector 33
First usable sector is 34, last usable sector is 3750748814
Partitions will be aligned on 2048-sector boundaries
Total free space is 2014 sectors (1007.0 KiB)

Number  Start (sector)    End (sector)  Size       Code  Name
   1            2048          133119   64.0 MiB    EF00  efi
   2          133120        10618879   5.0 GiB     8300  oem
   3        10618880        51988479   19.7 GiB    8300  recovery
   4        51988480       104368127   25.0 GiB    8300  state
   5       104368128       718768127   293.0 GiB   8300  persistent
   6       718768128      3750748847   1.4 TiB     8300  data_partition
```

**Additional context**

Key observations that point at a corrupt/inconsistent GPT rather than the
`wipefs` step:

- `lsblk` (kernel view) reports `nvme1n1p6` as **293 GiB** with **no**
  FSTYPE/LABEL/PARTLABEL.
- `sgdisk -p` (on-disk primary GPT) reports partition 6 as `data_partition`
  sized **1.4 TiB** — i.e. it grabbed all remaining space instead of the
  requested `300000`, and its size disagrees with the kernel's view.
- `sgdisk` warns: `Secondary partition table overlaps the last partition by
  33 blocks!` — the backup GPT header was not relocated to the end of the disk.
- The kernel view (`lsblk`) and on-disk GPT (`sgdisk`) disagree on both the size
  and the name of p6, so udev never creates the `by-partlabel/data_partition`
  symlink.
- The `after-install-chroot` `wipefs -a` step only wipes filesystem signatures
  (which explains the missing `FSTYPE`), but it does **not** remove a GPT
  partition name — so it cannot account for the missing `PARTLABEL`.

**Trigger:** the problem only appears when `persistent.size` is set to a fixed
value. Removing the fixed `persistent.size` makes the extra partition come up
correctly with its partlabel. This suggests the size/offset computation for
extra partitions (or the final GPT/backup-header write) is wrong when persistent
has a fixed size, leaving the partition table inconsistent.
title: fix: extra-partition PARTLABEL missing after install when persistent partition size is fixed

author: ci-robbot
body:
## What is happening

When a test VM dies, the e2e suite exits with a raw Go panic instead of a failed spec. Ginkgo never writes a report, `AfterEach` never runs, and so `gatherLogs()` never runs either and the logs artifact is uploaded empty.

Seen on master in [run 34251428760](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34251428760), job `test-standard / provider-decentralized-k8s`:

```
VM Aborted.
stdout:
stderr: Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
qemu-system-x86_64: failed to initialize kvm: Permission denied

Exit status: 1
panic: Your Test Panicked
	Fail(fmt.Sprintf("\nVM Aborted.\nstdout: %s\nstderr: %s\nserial: %s\nExit status: %s\n",
	/home/runner/work/kairos/kairos/tests/tests_suite_test.go:453
...
created by github.com/spectrocloud/peg/pkg/machine.monitor in goroutine 37
```

followed, at the end of the job, by:

```
##[warning]No files were found with the provided path: tests/**/logs/*. No artifacts will be uploaded.
```

## Why

`tests/tests_suite_test.go:437` passes a `types.OnFailure` callback that calls Ginkgo's `Fail()`. peg does not call that callback from a Ginkgo node; it calls it from a goroutine it starts itself, in `pkg/machine.monitor`:

```go
func monitor(ctx context.Context, p *process.Process, f func(p *process.Process)) context.Context {
	newCtx, cancelFunc := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	go func() {
		...
		if !p.IsAlive() {
			code, err := p.ExitCode()
			if err != nil || code != "0" {
				f(p)     // <- our callback, on peg's goroutine
			}
```

`Fail()` works by panicking, and Ginkgo can only rescue that panic in goroutines it owns. Any other goroutine needs `defer GinkgoRecover()`, which the callback does not have. Ginkgo's own panic text says exactly this.

## What it costs

Every spec file that gathers logs on failure is affected, which is all 20 of them (`gatherLogs(vm)` in an `AfterEach` guarded by `CurrentSpecReport().Failed()`). So for the whole VM-abort class of failure, and that includes real product crashes and not only the KVM case above, we get:

- no Ginkgo report and no `Summarizing N Failures` block,
- no `AfterEach`, so no VM logs, no serial, no `dmesg`, no `kairos-agent logs` tarball, and an empty artifact,
- the actual reason buried under 30 lines of Ginkgo boilerplate about `GinkgoRecover`.

## Reproduction without KVM

peg lets you override the VM binary, so the whole path can be driven on a machine with no qemu. Copy `tests/go.mod`/`go.sum` and the `OnFailure` closure into a scratch module, then:

```go
m, _ := machine.New(
	types.QEMUEngine,
	types.WithProcessName("/bin/false"), // a qemu that cannot start
	types.WithStateDir(stateDir),
	types.WithSSHPort("42424"),
	types.OnFailure(onFailure),          // verbatim from tests_suite_test.go
)
m.Create(context.Background())
Eventually(func() string { out, _ := m.Command("echo ping"); return out }, ...).Should(Equal("ping\n"))
```

That reproduces the CI panic exactly. Adding `defer GinkgoRecover()` at the top of the callback turns it into a normal `[FAILED]` with the `AfterEach` running.

## Fix

`defer GinkgoRecover()` at the top of the `OnFailure` callback.

One consequence worth knowing: `GinkgoRecover` marks the spec failed but does not interrupt the goroutine running the spec, so a VM that never boots will now keep the spec in `vm.EventuallyConnects(1200)` for its full 20 minutes before the run ends, where today the panic kills the process in seconds. Short-circuiting that wait once the VM process is known dead is a separate change; peg's `monitor` already returns a context that is cancelled when the process exits, and `startVM()` already returns it.

🤖 Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.
title: e2e: a dead VM panics the whole suite instead of failing the spec, so no logs are ever collected

author: ci-robbot
body:
## Description

On a node that has never had a system extension installed, the **first** `kairos-agent sysext install` always fails:

```
$ rm -rf /var/lib/kairos          # a node with no extensions yet
$ kairos-agent sysext install "http://example.com/hello.sysext.raw"
ERR failed installing system extension error="failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: mkdir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: file exists"

$ kairos-agent sysext install "http://example.com/hello.sysext.raw"   # second attempt
INF System extension http://example.com/hello.sysext.raw installed
```

The second attempt succeeds, because the failed first attempt left the directory behind.

`kairos-agent sysext list` on the same clean node fails the same way, for the same reason.

I hit this while QA-ing #4482 on a booted VM. It is not from that PR, it reproduces on `master` (`ca70432b` at the time, still present on `d17464a2`).

## Root cause

`sysextDir` and `confExtDir` in `agent/pkg/action/sysext.go` carry a trailing slash:

```go
sysextDir  = "/var/lib/kairos/extensions/"
confExtDir = "/var/lib/kairos/confexts/"
```

With no `--active` / `--passive` / `--recovery` / `--common` flag, `dirFromBootState` returns the bare constant, and it goes straight to `vfs.MkdirAll`. `go-vfs`'s `MkdirAll` is not safe against a trailing slash:

```go
// twpayne/go-vfs/v5 mkdirall.go
err := fileSystem.Mkdir(path, perm)          // ENOENT, parent missing
...
case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
    parentDir := filepath.Dir(path)          // strips the slash -> the SAME dir
    MkdirAll(fileSystem, parentDir, perm)    // recursion creates the leaf
    return fileSystem.Mkdir(path, perm)      // creates it a second time -> EEXIST, returned raw
```

`filepath.Dir("/var/lib/kairos/extensions/")` is `"/var/lib/kairos/extensions"`, so the recursion creates the leaf itself, and the outer call then tries to create it again and returns a bare `file exists`.

This only fires when a **parent** is also missing. That is why the existing `should create the target dir if it does not exist` spec does not catch it: it removes only `/var/lib/kairos/extensions` and leaves `/var/lib/kairos`, so the first `Mkdir` succeeds and the recursive branch is never taken.

Affects all three `vfs.MkdirAll` call sites in that file: `getDirExtensions`, `EnableExtension` and `InstallExtension`.

## Impact

The obvious symptom is a confusing error on a fresh node that goes away if you run the command twice. The sharper one is on bundled extensions: #4482 correctly aborts an `upgrade` when a bundled extension fails to install, so on a fresh node the operator gets neither the extension nor the OS upgrade:

```
executing command f1: upgrade
--> Failed: install sysext/hello: exit status 1: ...
    failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: mkdir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: file exists
```

First use on a clean node is the common case for that feature.

## Reproduce in a unit test

Against `agent/pkg/action`, with a test FS where `/var/lib/kairos` does not exist:

```
failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: mkdir /tmp/go-vfs-vfst.../var/lib/kairos/extensions: file exists
failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/confexts/:   mkdir /tmp/go-vfs-vfst.../var/lib/kairos/confexts: file exists
```

The suite's `BeforeEach` pre-creates `/var/lib/kairos/extensions`, which is why no existing spec covers a genuinely clean node.

## Fix

Drop the trailing slash from the constants, and clean the path before handing it to `vfs.MkdirAll` so the invariant does not depend on how the constants happen to be written.

I have this working with regression specs and will open a PR.
title: kairos-agent sysext install fails on the first run on a node with no extensions: trailing slash in sysextDir breaks vfs.MkdirAll

author: ci-robbot
body:
## The bug

AuroraBoot builds its OpenAPI docs with an **unpinned** copy of the `swag` CLI, in three places:

```
Dockerfile:63          RUN go install github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@latest
Dockerfile.riscv64:12  RUN go install github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@latest
Makefile:113           @which swag >/dev/null 2>&1 || go install github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@latest
```

`github.com/swaggo/swag v1.16.6` is already a **direct require** in `go.mod`, and `docs/docs.go`, `docs/swagger.json` and `docs/swagger.yaml` are committed. So the generator and the library it generates against are pinned independently, and the committed output is generated by whatever `swag` happened to be published, or, in the `make openapi` case, by whatever `swag` happened to be on the developer's `PATH` — `which swag` accepts any version, including one from a different project.

## Why it is worth fixing

**It has already turned CI red.** AuroraBoot [run 34282024388](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/actions/runs/34282024388) died 13 minutes into `Build local image`:

```
go: github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@latest: Get "https://proxy.golang.org/...":
dial tcp: lookup proxy.golang.org on 10.43.0.10:53: i/o timeout
```

Every image build makes a live, unpinned fetch against the module proxy, so proxy or cluster-DNS trouble fails a build that has no reason to touch the network for a tool it already has a version for. I noted this while triaging kairos-io/kairos#4553 and said it was worth separating; this is that issue.

**Two more consequences beyond the flake:**

- A `swag` release can change the generated docs with no code change in this repo, and nothing in CI checks `docs/` for freshness, so the drift is silent.
- It is an unpinned build-time dependency in the supply chain of a signed release artifact.

## Suggested fix

Pin the CLI to the version `go.mod` already names, using the Go 1.24+ `tool` directive:

```
tool github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag
```

Then `go build -o /usr/local/bin/swag github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag` in the Docker stages (still cacheable, since it only needs `go.mod`/`go.sum`) and `go tool swag init ...` in the Makefile. Renovate then bumps CLI and library together instead of letting them drift.

Verified locally on `main` @ `9893f50`: the pinned v1.16.6 regenerates `docs/` **byte-for-byte identical** to what is committed, so this is a determinism fix and not a behaviour change.

PR: kairos-io/AuroraBoot#TBD

🤖 Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.
title: AuroraBoot: swag CLI is installed with @latest, so docs generation is unpinned and every image build makes a live proxy fetch

author: mauro-agent
body:
## What happened

On AuroraBoot's node detail page (fleet admin UI), editing a node's labels and saving leaves the page blank (white screen). The label save itself succeeds server-side — the value is actually persisted — but the UI crashes right after.

Reproduces identically via `http://localhost:9099` directly (bypassing any reverse proxy in front of it), so it's not a proxy artifact.

## Browser console

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized)
  :9099/api/v1/nodes/1

Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')
  at Ku (index-*.js:49:16808)
  at ho, sc, wc, ju, Ou, Du, hu, sd (React internals)
  at MessagePort.D
```

## What's confirmed from source (`kairos-io/AuroraBoot`, `ui/src`)

- `components/StatusBadge.tsx` calls `status.toLowerCase()` with no guard against `status` being `undefined`:
  ```ts
  const style = statusStyles[status.toLowerCase()] ?? "bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground";
  ```
  If a node-shaped object with a missing/undefined `status` ever reaches this component, it crashes the whole render tree, not just that badge.
- `api/client.ts`'s `apiFetch` on a 401 clears the token and does `window.location.href = "/login"`, then throws. That navigation isn't synchronous, so other in-flight requests/renders can still execute in the window before the redirect actually happens.
- `pages/NodeDetail.tsx`'s `handleSaveLabels` has no try/catch around `await setLabels(id, labels)`.

## What's NOT confirmed — left as an open question

Why the failing request is to `/api/v1/nodes/1` specifically. `1` is not a plausible UUID for the node actually being viewed (its own URL was a real UUID). Did not trace where that literal `1` comes from — grepped `NodeDetail.tsx` and its `useUIWebSocket` message handler and found no reference to a hardcoded `1` there, so it originates somewhere else on the page not yet identified.

## Suggested fix (the confirmed half)

Guard `StatusBadge` against `status` being falsy/undefined regardless of the root cause above — a 401 (or any other error-shaped response reaching a component expecting a `Node`) should never be able to crash the whole page to a blank screen. Worth pairing with a try/catch in `handleSaveLabels` that surfaces a visible error toast instead of letting the exception propagate silently.

---

AI assisted this issue. A human is attending and directed it.
title: AuroraBoot: saving a node label crashes the admin UI to a blank page
