author: ci-robbot
body:
`kairos register` and the `provider-qrcode-install` spec both call `nodepair.Send` with `context.Background()`. go-nodepair waits for the peer inside `waitNodes`, which loops until the context ends. With no deadline on that context, a node that never joins the pairing network means neither caller ever returns.

## What it costs in CI

The `provider-qrcode-install` leg on run [34125670036](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34125670036) sat in one step for **58m43s**:

```
STEP: registering with a screenshot @ 09/07/26 14:11:34.416
Sending registration payload, please wait
Not enough nodes
Not enough nodes
...                                        (every 10s, for 58 minutes)
[TIMEDOUT] in [It] - tests/provider_install_qrcode_test.go:41

  At [By Step] registering with a screenshot (Step Runtime: 58m43.325s)

Ran 1 of 34 Specs in 3581.602 seconds
FAIL! - Suite Timeout Elapsed -- 0 Passed | 1 Failed | 0 Pending | 33 Skipped
```

`Not enough nodes` is printed by go-nodepair's `waitNodes`, not by the guest. The host never saw the VM announce presence on the ledger, and it had nothing telling it to stop looking.

Because nothing bounds the step, the thing that eventually ends the run is the **ginkgo suite timeout**. That is the worst available failure mode: it ends the whole suite, so the other **33 specs are skipped** and the leg reports no signal at all. One pairing failure costs an hour of runner time and the entire `test-standard` result.

Same signature today on #4468, #4476 and #4494, which is what made me look. A green run of the same spec is 303s.

## Same hang in the shipped CLI

[`provider/internal/cli/register.go:128`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/provider/internal/cli/register.go#L128) has the identical shape. A user who runs `kairos register` against a node that is not in pairing mode, or is on another network, gets

```
Sending registration payload, please wait
Not enough nodes
Not enough nodes
```

forever, with no timeout, no error and no exit. There is no flag to bound it.

## Note on `Send`'s return value

Adding a deadline is necessary but not sufficient. `nodepair.Send` returns `nil` when the context ends:

```go
PAIRING:
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return nil          // <- not an error
```

So a caller that only checks the returned error cannot tell an expired deadline from a delivered payload. It has to check `ctx.Err()` after `Send` returns.

## Suggested fix

1. Give the e2e harness `register()` a deadline, and fail the spec on `ctx.Err()`. Pairing failures then cost minutes, report against the step that hung, and leave the other 33 specs to run.
2. Add `--timeout` to `kairos register` so the CLI reports what went wrong instead of hanging. `0` keeps today's wait-forever behaviour.

## Not fixed by this

This bounds and attributes the failure. It does not fix whatever stopped the two peers finding each other in that run. If the flake persists after the wait is bounded, the failure will at least land with `gatherLogs` output and a named step to work from.

Related to #4489, which is the same symptom, suite timeout eats the run, from a different cause: there the per-step `Eventually` ceilings were larger than the suite budget rather than absent.
title: kairos register never times out: an unpaired node hangs the CLI forever and burns the whole ginkgo suite budget in provider-qrcode-install

author: ci-robbot
body:
`kairos-io/entangle-proxy` has not published a container image since **2023-10-04**. Every push to `master` since then has built nothing, because the publish workflows fail at the registry login step. The result is that merged fixes, including a CVE bump, never reach a user.

Filing here per the repo's own README pointer (entangle-proxy#28).

## What fails

Both workflows in that repo (`.github/workflows/image.yml` and `.github/workflows/kubectl-image.yml`) fail on the `docker/login-action` step:

```
##[group]Run docker/login-action@v4
with:
  registry: quay.io
  logout: true
##[error]Username and password required
```

Note what is **not** in that `with:` block: `username` and `password`. The step is written as

```yaml
      - name: Login to DockerHub
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: quay.io
          username: ${{ secrets.QUAY_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.QUAY_PASSWORD }}
```

so both secrets resolve to empty in this repository. The action then refuses to log in, and `docker/build-push-action` with `push: true` never runs.

## How long

Every push-to-master run on record for both workflows has failed:

| Date | `build container images` | `build kubectl container images` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-01 (`4cc9284c`) | failure | failure |
| 2026-07-06 (`0ac038af`) | failure | failure |
| 2026-07-06 (`85adcfe8`) | failure | failure |
| 2026-06-25 (`7caafde3`) | failure | failure |
| 2026-06-08 (`e7558338`) | failure | failure |

I pulled the logs for the four most recent runs of `image.yml` and all four show the identical `Username and password required` error (runs `33486063659`, `28773602862`, `28773149023`, `28188111608`). Logs for the 2026-06-08 run have aged out, so I could not confirm that one directly.

**This is not the `docker/login-action` v4 bump.** That bump (entangle-proxy#19) merged on 2026-07-06, and the 2026-06-25 run was already failing the same way on the previous version. The secrets are the problem, not the action version.

## What the registry actually holds

`quay.io/kairos/entangle-proxy` has 14 active tags. The three most recent:

```
c951f90a   Wed, 04 Oct 2023 15:19:38 -0000
latest     Wed, 04 Oct 2023 15:19:38 -0000
64c6b62d   Tue, 05 Sep 2023 13:14:36 -0000
```

`c951f90a` is the commit "Configure automerge for patch updates". So `:latest` is a build of the tree as it stood in October 2023.

`quay.io/kairos/kubectl`, which is also built out of this repo, is frozen at the same commit and the same day.

## Why it matters

**A merged CVE fix is not shipped.** entangle-proxy#21 ("chore(deps): bump x/crypto, x/net and go to fix CVEs", merged 2026-06-08) moved the module off

```
golang.org/x/crypto v0.0.0-20220214200702-86341886e292
golang.org/x/net    v0.0.0-20220127200216-cd36cc0744dd
```

to `v0.52.0` and `v0.55.0`, and the go directive from 1.18 to 1.26.4. None of that is in any published image. Anyone pulling `quay.io/kairos/entangle-proxy` today still gets the 2022-era `x/crypto` and `x/net`.

**The documented install path is worse than `:latest`.** The README tells users to install with helm:

```
helm install kairos-entangle-proxy kairos/entangle-proxy
```

`charts/entangle-proxy/values.yaml` in kairos-io/helm-charts leaves `image.tag` and `image.kubectlTag` empty and falls back to the chart's `appVersion`, which in `Chart.yaml` (chart version `0.0.5`) is `v0.1.2`. `quay.io/kairos/entangle-proxy:v0.1.2` was pushed on **2022-11-11**. So the documented install deploys an image that is nearly four years old, two years older than `:latest`.

**The dependency PR queue is pointless until this is fixed.** There are nine open renovate/dependabot PRs on entangle-proxy right now, some open since 2023. Merging any of them changes nothing that a user can pull.

## Suggested fix

Either is fine, and this needs a maintainer with org-level access; I cannot set secrets.

1. **Set the secrets.** Add `QUAY_USERNAME` / `QUAY_PASSWORD` to entangle-proxy, or grant the repo access to the org-level secrets if they are scoped to selected repositories. Worth checking whether the scoping changed during the repo access standardization in #4291, since the oldest failure on record is close to that work.
2. **Move to GHCR**, which is what the rest of the org has been converging on. `docker/login-action` against `ghcr.io` with `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` and `packages: write` needs no configured secret at all, and removes this failure mode permanently. This changes the image coordinates, so the helm chart and the docs would need to follow.

Whichever way it goes, the chart's `appVersion` should also be bumped once a real image exists again, otherwise the helm install path stays on the 2022 image.

## Unrelated small thing found while looking

`go.mod` on entangle-proxy `master` has the same require line twice:

```
	github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 v2.32.0
	github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 v2.32.0
```

This came from merging two renovate PRs for the same upgrade (#10 on 2026-06-25 and #24 on 2026-07-06). The Go toolchain tolerates a duplicate require at an identical version, so nothing is broken and I confirmed `go list -m` is clean; `go mod tidy` will drop the second line whenever someone next touches the file.

---

Reported by mudler's triage bot (`@ci-robbot`). Everything above is from the run logs, the quay.io tag API and the repository contents; no ISO build or cluster deploy was involved.
title: entangle and entangle-proxy publish no images: the quay secrets are not scoped to those two repos, so :latest is frozen at 2024-07-11 and 2023-10-04

author: mauromorales
body:
## Summary Kairos has grown from an immutable meta-distribution into a full lifecycle platform, but our **product naming and documentation entry points** have not kept up. New users must learn overlapping codenames (Kairos, Hadron, AuroraBoot, kairos-init, Kairos Factory, kairosctl, two different WebUIs) before they know what to download or run. This issue proposes a **team-aligned approach** (docs and product presentation only — no code in this ticket) to: 1. Present **Kairos as a suite of job-oriented products** 2. Split overloaded names (especially AuroraBoot) into clear product surfaces 3. Restructure documentation around **generalized personas** with real-world proof links 4. Offer **three maturity levels** on every path: GUI → automation → internals --- ## Problem | Today | User confusion | |---|---| | **Kairos** | Project, framework, and often “the OS” | | **Hadron** | Feels like a second project to adopt | | **AuroraBoot** | Builds artifacts, netboots, runs fleet dashboard/API/key store | | **Kairos Factory** vs **kairos-init** vs **factory** (SaaS) | Multiple “build” entry points | | **kairosctl** | Sounds like the main CLI; covers P2P only | | Two **WebUIs** | Install UI on node (:8080) vs AuroraBoot fleet UI | **Goal:** Users discover Kairos by **job**, not by subsystem. Repo/codenames stay in GitHub; docs, homepage, and CLI UX lead with product names. --- ## Principles - **Kairos = the suite** (CNCF project + umbrella brand). Not “a Linux distro.” - **Product names = jobs** — the name answers what the user is trying to do. - **Progressive disclosure** — simple front door; depth is opt-in. - **Codenames stay internal** — `AuroraBoot`, `immucore`, etc. remain in repos/releases. - **Two learning paths, one story** — GUI for onboarding → CLI/pipelines for production → internals for extenders. Every persona and product page exposes all three, clearly labeled. - **Personas are generalized** — inspired by real adopters; proof is an external blog or docs link, not a partnership call-out. --- ## Relationship diagram ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph umbrella ["Kairos — the suite"] K[Kairos] end subgraph products ["Proposed product names (user-facing)"] F[Kairos Factory
build & extend OCI images] B[Kairos Builder
produce boot artifacts] P[Kairos Provision
install machines at scale] FL[Kairos Fleet
track & operate nodes] O[Kairos Operator
K8s-native day-2] L[Kairos Lab
local VMs for learning] end subgraph artifacts ["What runs on hardware"] I[Kairos Images] H[Hadron — default Linux base] BY[Other bases
Ubuntu, RHEL, Alpine, …] end subgraph onnode ["On-node (advanced / contributor)"] A[Kairos Agent] IM[Kairos Immucore] EN[Kairos Encrypt] end K --> F K --> B K --> P K --> FL K --> O K --> L F --> I B --> I I --> H I --> BY P --> I FL --> I O --> I I -.-> A I -.-> IM I -.-> EN ``` **Install-time UI (separate from Fleet UI):** ```mermaid flowchart LR LIVE[Live media / first boot] INS[Kairos Installer
WebUI on node :8080] LIVE --> INS INS --> I[Kairos Image on disk] ``` --- ## Naming map: today → proposed ### User-facing products | Today | Proposed name | One-line job | Why | |---|---|---|---| | kairos-init + “Kairos Factory” concept | **Kairos Factory** | Turn any container base into a Kairos OCI image | Matches Dockerfile/CI mental model | | AuroraBoot `build-*` / artifact commands | **Kairos Builder** | ISO, cloud, raw, UKI from an OCI image | Separates “extend the OS” from “produce boot media” | | AuroraBoot netboot / USB mass-install | **Kairos Provision** | Install machines without touching each one | “Bootstrapper” undersells the user goal | | AuroraBoot fleet server + dashboard + API + node manager | **Kairos Fleet** | Build, deploy, register, and manage nodes | v4.1.0 control-plane scope deserves its own name | | Kairos Operator | **Kairos Operator** *(unchanged)* | Day-2 ops via Kubernetes CRDs | Already clear | | Install WebUI (port 8080) | **Kairos Installer** | Configure & install from live media | Distinguishes from Fleet UI | | kairos-lab | **Kairos Lab** | Local VMs for demos and PoCs | Friendly name, Kairos prefix | | AuroraBoot CLI (long term) | **`kairos` CLI** with subcommands | Single entry point | `kairos build`, `kairos provision`, `kairos fleet`, etc. | | Hadron | **Hadron** *(unchanged)* | Default minimal Linux base | Always framed **“Hadron by Kairos”** | | Ubuntu/Alpine/… artifacts | **Kairos on Ubuntu**, etc. | Same lifecycle, chosen base | Retire “flavor” in intro content | | Core / Standard | **Kairos Base** / **Kairos Kubernetes** *(optional, defer?)* | With or without bundled K8s | Team decision | ### On-node / advanced (docs only, prefixed) | Today | Proposed doc name | |---|---| | kairos-agent | **Kairos Agent** | | immucore | **Kairos Immucore** | | kcrypt | **Kairos Encrypt** (or keep Kcrypt) | | provider-kairos | **Kubernetes options (k3s / k0s)** — never lead with repo name | | kairosctl | **`kairos network`** subcommand | ### Not user-facing products `osbuilder`, `enki`, `elemental-cli`, most `provider-*` repos, `entangle`, `meta-kairos` — contributor/legacy references only. **Open decision:** Is **Kairos Builder** a separate product, or a Factory sub-capability (“Factory → Artifacts”)? Recommendation: separate if AuroraBoot split is real. --- ## AuroraBoot split | AuroraBoot capability today | Becomes | |---|---| | `build-iso`, `build-uki`, disk.\*, cloud images | **Kairos Builder** | | Netboot, pixiecore, USB workflows | **Kairos Provision** | | Fleet server, dashboard, API, node manager, SB key store | **Kairos Fleet** | | Binary/docker image | Implementation of all three; long-term **`kairos` CLI** | Repo name can stay `AuroraBoot`. Docs/marketing should not lead with “AuroraBoot” on persona or product pages. --- ## Documentation maturity model Every persona and product page exposes three tracks: | Level | Audience | Typical tools | |---|---|---| | **1 — Guided** | First touch, PoC | Kairos Lab, Kairos Installer, Kairos Fleet UI | | **2 — Automate** | Platform engineer in prod | Kairos Factory in Dockerfile, Builder CLI, CI, Operator CRDs | | **3 — Extend** | Contributors, OEMs, hard edge | Kairos Immucore, stages, trusted boot, custom boards, providers | Level 1 pages must include explicit **“Ready to automate?”** bridges to Level 2. --- ## Persona landing pages New top-level section (working title: `/start/` or `/personas/`). Each page is a **generalized use case**; proof is an external link. ### Hub | Persona | Tagline | Primary products | Proof | |---|---|---|---| | Edge AI fleet operator | Remote GPU/edge devices, long lifecycle, flaky networks | Factory → Builder → Provision → Operator | [CNCF: edge AI platform integration](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2025/12/29/how-to-integrate-kairos-architecturally-into-an-edge-ai-platform/) | | Regulated platform team | Committed enterprise distro, auditability, GitOps | Factory → Builder → Operator | [CNCF: platform at scale (RBC)](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/05/13/building-a-cloud-native-platform-from-the-ground-up-with-kairos-k0rdent-and-bindy/) | | Greenfield evaluator | “Try immutable K8s in an afternoon” | Lab → Installer → Fleet (GUI) | Quickstart / video | | Factory / OEM shipper | Pre-flash devices before they leave the warehouse | Builder → Provision → Fleet | Edge AI blog (pre-flash/provisioning angle) + v4.1.0 Fleet notes | | Trusted hardware gateway | Network-access hardware in untrusted environments | Factory → Builder (trusted boot) → Provision → Fleet | [DeEEP Network / NerdNode docs](https://docs.deeep.network/) | --- ### Persona 1 — Edge AI fleet operator **Generalized story:** Remote sensing / inference devices (e.g. NVIDIA Jetson class) deployed in the field; decade-long product life; flaky connectivity; cannot dispatch technicians for firmware, GPU stack, or OS updates. **Needs:** - Stay on a familiar base (Ubuntu + vendor stack baked in Dockerfile) - Freeze the stack; eliminate snowflake nodes - Remote, safe OS upgrades (A/B fallback) - K3s (or similar) on device; upgrades via private registry + Operator **Product mapping:** Factory (Dockerfile + kairos-init) → Builder (board artifact) → Provision (mass flash) → Operator (registry-driven upgrades). Lab for early exploration. **Maturity tracks:** L1 — edge device quickstart + Installer; L2 — Factory CI → registry → Operator; L3 — custom boards, overlays, boot chain. **Proof:** https://www.cncf.io/blog/2025/12/29/how-to-integrate-kairos-architecturally-into-an-edge-ai-platform/ --- ### Persona 2 — Regulated platform team **Generalized story:** Large hybrid K8s estate; compliance requirements (audit trails, no drift); must keep an approved enterprise Linux base; OS images treated like application containers. **Needs:** - Immutable nodes — no package managers on production - OS image CI/CD: build, integration-test, publish immutable OCI tag - Declarative node config (cloud-config) in GitOps - Digest-pinned audit trail for “what ran on that node on that date?” **Product mapping:** Factory (approved base + security + enterprise auth) → Builder (VM/cloud artifacts) → Operator (GitOps-driven rollouts). Adjacent tools (k0rdent, bindy, etc.) linked as platform context, not conflated with Kairos products. **Maturity tracks:** L1 — boot one test VM from a published image; L2 — full Factory pipeline + Flux-managed cloud-config; L3 — enterprise integration (SSSD, NM, CA chains), compliance artifacts. **Proof:** https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/05/13/building-a-cloud-native-platform-from-the-ground-up-with-kairos-k0rdent-and-bindy/ --- ### Persona 3 — Greenfield evaluator **Generalized story:** Engineer or team evaluating immutable K8s; wants confidence before committing to a pipeline. **Product mapping:** Kairos Lab → Hadron image → Kairos Installer → intro to Kairos Fleet GUI. **Maturity tracks:** L1 — Hadron quickstart (primary); L2 — first automated upgrade, Factory intro; L3 — BYOI, trusted boot, Operator. --- ### Persona 4 — Factory / OEM shipper **Generalized story:** Devices built in a lab/warehouse; must leave identical; field install is plug-and-power-on; provisioning in the field is minimal (certs/config only). **Product mapping:** Factory (golden image) → Builder (ISO/USB/cloud) → Provision (mass install) → Fleet (phone-home / node list) → Operator or Fleet for upgrades. **Maturity tracks:** L1 — Fleet UI build → deploy → see nodes; L2 — Builder + Provision in CI; L3 — secure boot keys, airgap registries. --- ### Persona 5 — Trusted hardware gateway *(DeEEP Network / NerdNode pattern)* **Generalized story:** Operator ships managed hardware to customers or hosts. Devices provide **network access** into the operator’s infrastructure — a high-risk surface if the wrong OS can boot. Hardware must only run the operator’s approved, attested stack. Thousands of nodes managed remotely; security and boot integrity are product requirements, not nice-to-haves. **Public docs context (DeEEP Network):** - Devices require specific security features; preloaded from factory with secret keys and a **trusted boot chain**; public keys registered to establish hardware is safe for the network ([how it works](https://docs.deeep.network/introduction/how-it-works.md)) - MS-01 hardware: TPM 2.0, encrypted RAM, **complete boot validation** ([MS-01-DeEEP](https://docs.deeep.network/hardware/ms-01-deeep.md)) - NerdNode background: millions of edge devices managed remotely in untrusted physical locations ([NerdNode](https://docs.deeep.network/about/nerdnode.md)) *Note: DeEEP’s public documentation does not name Kairos explicitly; this persona is modeled on their published security and hardware model.* **Needs:** - Only signed/approved system images can boot on fleet hardware - Factory-defined OS with operator stack baked in - Trusted boot / measured boot artifacts - Remote lifecycle without physical access - Optional: fleet registration after first boot **Product mapping:** Factory (trusted boot profile) → Builder (UKI / SB-enabled artifacts) → Provision (factory preload) → Fleet (key store, node manager) → Kairos Encrypt / Immucore (L3). **Maturity tracks:** L1 — trusted boot quickstart + Installer; L2 — Factory pipeline with SB keys; L3 — Immucore, attestation, custom hardware. **Proof:** https://docs.deeep.network/ (especially [how it works](https://docs.deeep.network/introduction/how-it-works.md), [NerdNode](https://docs.deeep.network/about/nerdnode.md), [MS-01-DeEEP](https://docs.deeep.network/hardware/ms-01-deeep.md)) --- ## Proposed doc IA (structure only) ``` /start/ ← Persona hub /start/edge-ai-fleet/ /start/regulated-platform/ /start/quick-eval/ /start/factory-shipper/ /start/trusted-hardware/ /products/ /products/factory/ /products/builder/ ← split from auroraboot.md /products/provision/ ← split from auroraboot.md /products/fleet/ ← split from auroraboot.md /products/operator/ ← existing operator-docs /products/lab/ /products/installer/ /reference/ ← unchanged depth /contributors/ ← repo names, architecture, ADRs /glossary/ ← product name ↔ repo name ``` Each `/products/*` page gets L1 / L2 / L3 tabs. --- ## Messaging one-liners | Topic | Line | |---|---| | What is Kairos? | Immutable Linux platform for fleets and Kubernetes — from image build to install, upgrade, and recovery. | | What is Hadron? | Kairos’s default minimal Linux base — not a separate platform. | | What happened to AuroraBoot? | Engine behind **Kairos Builder**, **Kairos Provision**, and **Kairos Fleet**. | | Do I need all components? | No — pick a persona; see only what’s relevant. | --- ## Suggested rollout | Phase | Scope | |---|---| | **0** | Team agrees on naming table + persona list (this issue) | | **1** | Persona hub + adopter-inspired pages + glossary (kairos-docs) | | **2** | Split AuroraBoot docs into Builder / Provision / Fleet | | **3** | Homepage + `what-is-kairos` rewrite | | **4** | CLI alias (`auroraboot` → `kairos`) — separate release ticket | --- ## Open team decisions - [ ] **Kairos Builder** — separate product vs Factory sub-capability? - [ ] **Core/Standard rename** — now or defer? - [ ] **`kairos` CLI timeline** — docs-only rebrand first, or wait for binary rename? - [ ] **SaaS `factory` repo** — rename to **Kairos Factory Cloud**? - [ ] **Hadron site** (hadron-linux.io) — navigation coupling with kairos.io docs? - [ ] **Trusted hardware persona** — full page vs cross-cutting profile linked from others? --- ## Acceptance criteria (for follow-up work) - [ ] Team sign-off on naming table and persona set - [ ] kairos-docs issue(s) opened for Phase 1 IA - [ ] Glossary page: product name ↔ repo/codename - [ ] AuroraBoot reference doc split plan documented - [ ] Homepage “Choose your mission” → “Choose your persona” wireframe agreed
title: Proposal: Kairos product naming, persona-driven docs, and progressive disclosure

author: mauromorales
body:
## Problem

In AuroraBoot Artifact Builder, selecting **Standard** variant with **K3s** (or K0s) does not include the Kubernetes provider in the generated cloud-config baked into the artifact. The UI collects `kubernetesDistro` / `kubernetesVersion` for image build (kairos-init `-p k3s`), but `buildCloudConfig` never emits the runtime enablement block.

On first boot, Kairos expects provider config in cloud-config, e.g.:

```yaml
k3s:
  enabled: true
```

(or `k0s.enabled: true` for K0s — see [Kairos configuration reference](https://kairos.io/docs/reference/configuration/)).

Without this, a "Standard + K3s" artifact installs as plain OS even though the builder UI implied Kubernetes.

## Expected behavior

- UI exposes K3s / K0s choice for Standard variant (already present)
- Generated cloud-config (preview + backend) includes the matching provider stanza with `enabled: true`
- Review step YAML matches what is actually baked at build time

## Fix

[AuroraBoot#584](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/pull/584)

## Related

- [AuroraBoot#580](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/pull/580) — phone-home / install-agent fixes (merged)
- kairos-io/kairos#4184 — k3s version tag UX in Artifact Builder
title: AuroraBoot: standard variant must emit k3s/k0s in baked cloud-config

author: mauromorales
body:
## Problem

Recent bugs in the AuroraBoot install-agent / phone-home / artifact onboarding path were only caught by manually running AuroraBoot UI, building an artifact, booting a node, and confirming it appeared in the Nodes UI. None of the **CI-gated** AuroraBoot tests cover that golden path.

Examples from recent work (see [kairos-io/AuroraBoot#580](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/pull/580), #4152):

- Install-agent shell script broken by a heredoc typo (script never finished; phone-home config swallowed)
- Script used bash-only syntax while Import page and docs pipe to `sh`
- `kairos-agent-phonehome` systemd unit hardcoded `/usr/sbin/kairos-agent` → `203/EXEC` on images where the binary lives under `/usr/bin`
- k3s version tag format issues in Artifact Builder (needs full tag, e.g. `v1.35.5+k3s1`)
- Artifact upgrade failing when `/tmp` (tmpfs) is too small for the downloaded artifact

These are integration/product bugs: they span UI config → artifact build (kairos-init) → first boot → registration → UI visibility.

> **Note:** Issues are disabled on the [AuroraBoot repo](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot); tracking here alongside related AuroraBoot/agent work.

## What AuroraBoot has today

| Layer | Location | CI? | Gap |
|-------|----------|-----|-----|
| Cypress smoke | `e2e/web/cypress/e2e/smoke.cy.js` | ✅ | SPA shell + public `/install-agent` strings only; no login, no builder, no VM |
| UI unit smoke | `ui/src/test/smoke.test.tsx` | ✅ | Login screen render in jsdom only |
| Integration | `test/integration/` | ✅ | In-process API with **mock** artifact builder — no real builds or VMs |
| Fleet E2E | `test/e2e/` | ❌ | Real server + builder + QEMU, but **not wired into CI**; uses API + manual datasource cloud-config, not Artifact Builder / UI flow |
| CLI boot E2E | `./e2e/` | ✅ (KVM) | ISO/UKI/raw bootability only — no fleet server, no nodes, no UI |

Closest existing tests in AuroraBoot:

- `test/e2e/import_test.go` — vanilla ISO + install-agent script → node in **API** (not UI; import path only)
- `test/e2e/call_home_test.go` — phone-home registration, but phonehome is injected via **datasource ISO**, not baked by Artifact Builder
- `test/e2e/upgrade_test.go` — API artifact build + upgrade; still no UI; ISO setup is separate from builder output

## Proposal: golden-path fleet smoke E2E

Add an end-to-end smoke test that mirrors what users actually do:

```
AuroraBoot (compose/container) → build artifact (Auto-register / phonehome baked in)
  → boot VM from produced ISO → node registers → visible in Nodes UI
```

### Minimum scope (MVP)

One happy-path per **two distro families** (to cover different build paths):

1. **Hadron** — pre-built Kairos image (`quay.io/kairos/hadron:…`), e.g. “Hadron + K3s” template from Artifact Builder
2. **One auto-kairosified base** — e.g. **Ubuntu 24.04** template (vanilla Docker base → kairos-init path)

For each distro, assert at least:

- Artifact build completes via the same code path the UI uses (REST API is acceptable initially if it mirrors UI payloads; UI-driven test is better long-term)
- `registerAuroraBoot` / phonehome config is baked into the artifact (not injected via a separate datasource workaround)
- VM boots, installs, and `kairos-agent-phonehome` reaches `active`
- Node appears in `GET /api/v1/nodes` with expected group and reaches Online
- **UI assertion**: authenticated visit to `/nodes` shows the registered node (Cypress/Playwright)

Optional follow-ups (can be separate issues / later phases):

- Import path: vanilla ISO + `curl …/install-agent | sh` (already partially in `import_test.go`)
- Artifact upgrade after registration
- WebSocket / live status updates in UI
- Additional distros (Fedora, Debian, …) on a slower/nightly matrix

### CI integration

`test/e2e/` already exists but requires `KAIROS_BASE_IMAGE`, `ISO`, or `HADRON_REPO` and is not run on PRs. Suggested approach:

- New workflow job (e.g. `fleet-smoke-e2e`) on `ubuntu-latest` **with KVM** (similar to existing `./e2e` jobs in AuroraBoot)
- Pull Hadron image from quay; use `ubuntu:24.04` for the second path
- Run a focused subset (not necessarily the full Ginkgo suite) with a reasonable timeout
- Gate on `main` first; consider optional/required on PRs once runtime is stable

Exact runtime/cost tradeoffs TBD — even a single-distro smoke on `main` nightly would be a big improvement over today.

### Why two distros?

- **Hadron**: primary Kairos-native image path; k3s/Standard variants; matches many production templates
- **Ubuntu (or similar)**: exercises auto-kairosify from a vanilla base — different kairos-init inputs and failure modes

One distro alone would miss bugs that only show up on the other path.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] Document how to run the smoke locally (`make …` or `go test ./test/e2e/…`)
- [ ] CI job runs at least Hadron + Ubuntu golden paths on a schedule or on `main`
- [ ] Test fails if phone-home service does not start or node never registers
- [ ] Test includes a UI check that the node is listed on `/nodes` after login
- [ ] Existing `test/e2e` tests are either reused, refactored, or explicitly superseded for the builder-baked phonehome path

## References

- [AuroraBoot#580](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/pull/580) — install-agent / phone-home fixes
- #4152 — heredoc bug
- #4178 — systemd ExecStart path
- #4184 — k3s version UX
- #4185 — upgrade `/tmp` preflight
title: AuroraBoot: add fleet smoke E2E (Artifact Builder → boot → node in UI)

author: ci-robbot
body:
Create a GitHub issue to investigate and address the failure of boot assessment in systemd-boot 258, which is causing the passive boot to not be properly triggered in CI. This issue is specifically observed in the `uki` test suite and appears to be related to changes in systemd-boot 258, as the same ISO passes in older builds where systemd-boot 257 was used. The failure manifests as the system repeatedly attempting to boot the active image without properly transitioning to the passive fallback, even after multiple failures. This behavior is inconsistent with the expected automatic boot assessment and may be due to a regression in systemd-boot 258's boot counting or fallback logic.

The issue is reproducible locally when using the latest `auroraboot:latest` image, which pulls in the updated systemd-boot 258. However, using an older `auroraboot` version (e.g., from 2 weeks ago) does not exhibit the problem. This confirms that the root cause is tied to the systemd-boot 258 update.

Given the impact on CI and the fact that the failure is not due to ISO or test configuration, a dedicated issue should be created to track this regression and ensure that the boot assessment functionality is restored before the next release.
title: Boot assessment failure in systemd-boot 258 (passive boot not triggered)

author: ci-robbot
body:
We currently have a configuration that makes entire directories like /etc and /var writable and persistent. While this is flexible, it's not optimal for security, auditability, and system cleanliness.

The current approach:
- Makes /etc, /var, and /srv fully writable and persistent
- Creates empty directories for components like k0s, k3s, etc. that may not be used by all users
- Creates a large number of mount points (e.g., for cilium, etc.) that aren't necessary for all configurations

Proposal:
Modify Kairos to dynamically add only the necessary bind mounts for specific Kubernetes distributions based on user configuration. For example:
- If k0s is selected, add /etc/k0s as a persistent path
- If k3s is selected, add /etc/k3s as a persistent path
- If rke2 is selected, add /etc/rke2 as a persistent path

This would result in:
1. Reduced attack surface (only necessary paths are persistent)
2. Cleaner, more auditable configuration
3. Fewer unnecessary mounts
4. Better resource usage
5. More tailored experience for different Kubernetes distributions

We could implement this by extending the current configuration system to conditionally add mounts based on the selected Kubernetes distribution, similar to how we handle different system requirements through bundles.
title: Improve persistent storage configuration to only include necessary paths for specific Kubernetes distributions

author: ci-robbot
body:
Slack: https://spectrocloud.slack.com/archives/C062AL1PC10/p1752659367307619

The current configuration reference documentation for Kairos is a single, monolithic YAML file, which makes it difficult to navigate and understand. To improve usability, I propose structuring the documentation into logical sections and separating specific configurations into dedicated pages. Here's a suggested approach:

### Proposed Structure
1. **Top-Level Sections**
   - **Install**: Configuration options specific to installation
   - **Reset**: Settings related to system reset
   - **Upgrade**: Parameters for upgrade processes
   - **Networking**: Network-related configurations
   - **Storage**: Storage configuration details

2. **Component-Specific Pages**
   - **k3s Configuration**: Separate documentation for k3s-specific settings
   - **k0s Configuration**: Dedicated page for k0s configurations
   - **Common Settings**: Shared configurations across components

3. **Enhancements**
   - Use Markdown for better formatting and navigation
   - Add descriptions, default values, and examples for each config
   - Implement sidebar navigation for easy access

### Example Format
```markdown
# Install Configuration
## k3s
- `cluster_name`: String (Default: "kairos")
- `kube_api_server`: String (Default: "https://api.k8s.example.com")

## k0s
- `control_plane`: Boolean (Default: true)
```

This would significantly improve developer experience and reduce confusion. I'm happy to help implement this if the maintainers agree.
title: Improve Configuration Reference Docs by Structuring into Sections and Separate Pages

author: Itxaka
body:
Now that we know that boot assesment for trusted boot is working we should think about adding checks that depend on boot-complete so we have sanity checks when running trusted boot.

Some examples:

 - make k0s/k3s services dependant of boot-complete. So if the k8s provider service does not come up, the entry is marked as not valid
 - make some services that check things in the system like /oem is mounted or persistant is there
 - make a service that ADVISES the user if the entry wasnt marked as valid. So something that on login or MOTD or whatever shows that the current entry did not complete the boot and the tries left. Currently systemd does not provide anything like this out of the box so maybe we could talk with them about adding something similar? Currently if your boot entry is marked as not correct or valid there is nothing that reboots or anything, its just exhausts things. So it could be as well not marked as good but you can still boot onto it. So what happens on the third reboot? IT will fallback to passive without notice, you dont know why. so a service or MOTD that advises if the entry consumed a try but was not marked as good its IMHO necessary.
title: feat: Add boot assesment checks to trusted boot flavors

author: jimmykarily
body:
With all those artifacts we have and their big names, it's hard to find the one you are looking for in the github release page.

Our naming now is more structured and is based solely on the flavors.json and the naming.sh script. For example with a script like the following, all artifact names can be generated:

```
~/workspace/kairos/kairos (master)*$ cat all-artifacts.sh 
#!/bin/bash
# https://stackoverflow.com/a/58009121

cat .github/flavors.json | jq -c '.[]' |
while IFS=$"\n" read -r c; do
    FAMILY=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.family') && export FAMILY
    FLAVOR=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.flavor') && export FLAVOR
    FLAVOR_RELEASE=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.flavorRelease') && export FLAVOR_RELEASE
    VARIANT=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.variant') && export VARIANT
    TARGETARCH=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.arch') && export TARGETARCH
    MODEL=$(echo "$c" | jq -r '.model') && export MODEL
    REGISTRY_AND_ORG=quay.io/kairos && export REGISTRY_AND_ORG
    KAIROS_VERSION=$(git describe --always --tags --dirty) && export KAIROS_VERSION
    ./naming.sh container_artifact_name
done | sort
```

We could generate a static page with every release that allows users to search for an artifact using drop down menus for each "input" field. E.g.

select box -> family
select box -> flavor
select box -> type (iso, img etc)
...


and the form would output all mathing artifacts in a text area box of a `ul` or something like that.
title: Artifact search form

author: mauromorales
body:
With Equinix Metal you only get serial access to the console of the physical server. Hence, to deploy Kairos there over iPXE and have working console access, a couple of changes are needed:

- In the .ipxe boot file used to boot the node, we need to set the console=tty0 console=ttyS1,115200n8 dracut parameter
- In the rootfs.squashfs file for Kairos, we need to edit the /etc/cos/bootargs.cfg file and modify the console= options to match those used in the .ipxe file

This allows Kairos (openSUSE) to iPXE boot with serial access, as well as have working serial access upon the next boot from local HDD.

However, to install Kubernetes onto it, it downloads a new container OS image (e.g. Ubuntu), which overwrites /etc/cos/bootargs.cfg with its own version. This typically has boot options that are not compatible with serial access. Typically it’s wrong console= options and sometimes there’s also a vga=795 option in there that breaks serial access.
We would like to find a way to manage the bootargs across OS images, so that we can add, edit and delete boot arguments as needed, without requiring the building of custom OS images.

[Original request slack link](https://spectrocloudcommunity.slack.com/archives/C04B1833NEA/p1677748481223689)
title: :sparkles: iPXE installation via serial console on Equinix Metal

author: mudler
body:
Currently the `k3s` and `k3s-agent` are two separated blocks, which makes the configuration cumbersome and less intuitive.

The proposal is to switch away from two separate blocks, and streamline only one block that can be used for both.

For example, consider the current status quo:

```yaml
k3s:
  args: ..
k3s-agent:
  args: ...
```

we could switch away to something more simple as:

```yaml
k3s:
  args: ..
  server: true
```

So, instead of laying down both systemd settings, we could also generate them in runtime with the appropriate service, allowing the user full customization of how the k3s bins should run.

## Action items

- [ ] Merge `k3s` and `k3s-agent` blocks into `k3s`
- [ ] Add an additional field to optionally discriminate between server and agent, otherwise fall back to all the config provided by the user
- [ ] Optional: generate the services files in runtime. This might not be necessary at all, so at dev discretion
title: merge k3s and k3s-agent config blocks

author: ci-robbot
body:
Re-filing [kairos-io/kairos-installer#21](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos-installer/issues/21) here, because `kairos-io/kairos-installer` was archived on 2026-08-26 and is read-only, so the original cannot be commented on or worked from. Original ask, by @mudler:

> As we are already migrating the webui installation here, it would make sense to also ship a MCP server so the installation can be driven by agents too

## Where the code actually sits now

- The installer is in this repo at [`installer/`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/tree/master/installer), built as `kairos-installer` by `Makefile:185-186` and shipped to `/system/installer/kairos-installer`. Today it is TUI only ([`installer/main.go`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/installer/main.go)).
- The webui is still separate, at [`agent/internal/webui/webui.go`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/agent/internal/webui/webui.go) behind `webui.Start`, so the migration the issue refers to has not landed yet.

## Why this is cheaper than it looks

The machine-readable install driver already exists and is deliberately frontend-agnostic. [`sdk/agentrun`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/sdk/agentrun/agentrun.go) documents itself as "the installer side of the kairos-agent installer contract" and has no TUI dependencies: `Run(agentBin, cfgPath, source, finishAction, onEvent, onLog)` shells out to `kairos-agent manual-install` with `KAIROS_AGENT_PROGRESS` set and turns its JSON-Lines stdout into typed `ProgressEvent`s with a fixed `StepPartition`/... vocabulary.

So an MCP server is a third frontend on the same contract, not new install logic. The tool surface roughly maps onto what the TUI already calls:

| MCP tool | backed by |
|---|---|
| `list_prerequisites` | [`installer/prereqs`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/tree/master/installer/prereqs) plugin discovery |
| `list_disks` / `get_install_options` | the sources the TUI's install-options page reads |
| `install` | `agentrun.Run`, streaming `ProgressEvent` back as MCP progress |
| `collect_debug_bundle` | `installer/internal/debugbundle.GenerateBundle`, already reachable non-interactively via `--collect-debug-bundle` |

## Open questions before anyone writes code

1. Does this ship as a mode of the `kairos-installer` binary (`kairos-installer --mcp`, stdio transport) or as its own binary? A flag keeps the artifact count and the `Makefile` unchanged.
2. stdio only, or also the HTTP transport? An agent driving an install over the network on a live-booted, unauthenticated machine is a very different security story from stdio.
3. Is `install` allowed to be destructive without a confirmation tool call? It repartitions a disk.

Not picking this up yet, flagging it for a scoping decision on 1 and 2 first.
title: feat: ship an MCP server so agents can drive the installation

## Spike: propose a function-based documentation restructure

**Type:** spike — a quick, reviewable proposal the team can agree on *before* we
commit to the bulk documentation rewrite.

### Context
Outcome of the naming & versioning discussion (2026-07-20). The team aligned on
tackling **documentation and naming first**, ahead of the harder backend/repo
restructuring. This ticket scopes **only the documentation-structure slice** —
the broader naming, versioning, and architecture proposal lives in #4208; this
spike is one piece of that.

### Aligned decisions this spike builds on
- Documentation should move to a **function/goal-oriented model**, not user-persona categories.
- **AuroraBoot** is positioned as the primary user-facing entry point / flagship tool.

### Goal
Produce a lightweight proposal (not the rewrite itself) the team can review and
sign off on, so the subsequent bulk work has an agreed target.

### Suggestions to evaluate in the spike
- **Split the docs into two tracks:** *user docs* (function/goal-based, task pathways) vs *developer docs* (advanced/custom, internals).
- **Organize by function/activity** (e.g. provisioning, fleet management, upgrades/lifecycle) in a hierarchy — mirroring the Red Hat/OpenShift model, so field teams and users can find components by purpose.
- **Lead with AuroraBoot as the front door:** frame the getting-started path through AuroraBoot to hide architectural complexity, while still letting users consume individual components à la carte.
- **Task-oriented entry points** ("provision a node", "manage a fleet", "upgrade from Kubernetes") rather than component-first navigation.

### Deliverable
A proposed documentation information architecture — a sitemap/outline with
section descriptions (as a doc or draft PR) — for team review and agreement. **No
bulk content rewrite in this spike.**

### Reference
Part of #4208 (Kairos product naming, persona-driven docs, and progressive
disclosure). This spike addresses the documentation-restructure portion only.
title: Spike: propose function-based documentation restructure (AuroraBoot as flagship entry point)

author: mauromorales
body:
## Summary

  This issue proposes changes to how Kairos providers are orchestrated so that
  provider responsibilities are clearer, providers can compose on top of each other,
  and install/bootstrap flows can target multiple providers safely.

  ## Current behavior

  - provider-kairos currently exposes both runtime and init-time events in a single
    plugin factory (provider-kairos/internal/provider/start.go):
      - Runtime: EventInstall, EventBootstrap, EventChallenge, EventRecovery,
        EventRecoveryStop, EventInteractiveInstall
      - Init-time: InitProviderInstall, InitProviderInfo
  - kairos-init triggers provider build/install via InitProviderInstall (kairos-init/
    pkg/stages/steps_install.go, ProviderBuildInstallEvent).
      - It loops over configured providers and publishes one event per configured
        provider.
      - All loaded plugins are subscribed to the same event, and each plugin receives
        each publish.
  - provider-kairos handles InitProviderInstall in BuildEvent and self-filters by
    payload provider name (provider-kairos/internal/provider/buildEvent.go).
  - kairos-init provider info handling currently stores only a single provider info
    payload in /etc/kairos-release fields (KAIROS_SOFTWARE_VERSION,
    KAIROS_SOFTWARE_VERSION_PREFIX) and already has a TODO noting this does not model
    multiple providers (kairos-init/pkg/stages/steps_init.go).

  ## Problem

  - Installation concerns are split between init and provider logic in a way that
    makes composition harder.
  - The current event fan-out model can cause providers to process repeated install
    requests unless they self-filter correctly.
  - Provider dependencies/composition (provider A depending on provider B/C
    functionality) are not first-class.
  - Event contracts for provider-to-provider coordination are implicit.

  ## Proposal

  1. Extract Kubernetes installation ownership from init and move it into providers.
  2. Extend orchestration to support multiple providers as a first-class workflow.
  3. Ensure a provider does not attempt to install multiple Kubernetes versions in
     the same flow.
  4. Support functional providers that depend on other providers.
      - Example: a self-coordination provider depending on Kubernetes + kube-vip +
        edgevpn.
  5. Keep init-driven provider install event dispatch.
      - init still sends install event(s) to providers.
  6. Keep bootstrap-driven provider bootstrap event dispatch.
      - bootstrap sends bootstrap event(s) to providers.
  7. Define provider event contracts explicitly.
      - Following Ettore’s suggestion: providers emit/listen to events, and handlers
        act only when relevant listeners exist.

  ## PoC

  - Add provider-capi as proof of concept.
  - Clarification: this is a Kairos provider named provider-capi, not a Cluster API
    infrastructure provider.

  ## Follow-up (if PoC succeeds)

  If the PoC validates the model, we should evaluate decomposing provider-kairos into
  smaller capability providers (for example: k3s, k0s, edgevpn, self-coordination),
  with the exact split decided later based on maintainability and compatibility
  constraints.

  ## Acceptance criteria

  - Multi-provider install/bootstrap flows are supported and deterministic.
  - Provider dependency/composition is represented via defined events.
  - Duplicate/competing Kubernetes version installs are prevented by design.
  - A PoC provider-capi demonstrates the new model end-to-end.
title: feat: Refactor Kairos provider model for composability and multi-provider   orchestration

author: ci-robbot
body:
## Feature Request: Factory Reset via Kairos Operator

### Current Limitation
The Kairos Operator currently detects Kairos nodes and tracks versions during initialization but lacks a mechanism to trigger a **factory reset** on nodes. Users must manually execute `kairos reset` on each node (e.g., `kairos reset --force`), which is:
- Time-consuming for multi-node clusters
- Error-prone during testing cycles
- Inconsistent with Kubernetes' declarative workflow

### Proposed Solution
Add a **Custom Resource (CR)** to enable factory resets via the operator:
```yaml
apiVersion: kairos.io/v1alpha1
kind: FactoryResetRequest
metadata:
  name: factory-reset-node-01
spec:
  nodeName: node-01
  # Optional: Add `version: "v1.0.0"` to reset to a specific version
```

**Operator Workflow:**
1. Operator watches for `FactoryResetRequest` CRs.
2. Upon creation, triggers `kairos reset` on the target node(s).
3. Updates CR status with success/failure and version details.

### Why This Matters
- **Testing Efficiency**: Eliminates manual resets during development (e.g., "a lot lololol" resets as noted in chat).
- **Consistency**: Uses the same node-checking logic already in the operator (`oneTimeBootstrap`).
- **Declarative UX**: Users run `kubectl apply -f reset-request.yaml` instead of SSHing into nodes.
- **Cross-Distro Ready**: Works for k3s, k0s, and other Kubernetes distributions.

### Implementation Notes
- Leverage existing node version tracking to report reset status.
- Ensure compatibility with all supported distributions (k3s/k0s).
- Do not require new registry or image builds (uses existing `kairos-agent` binaries).

---

**Example Use Case**  
```bash
# Create a reset request for a node
kubectl apply -f <<EOF
apiVersion: kairos.io/v1alpha1
kind: FactoryResetRequest
metadata:
  name: reset-node-01
spec:
  nodeName: node-01
EOF
```
title: Add Factory Reset Capability to Kairos Operator

author: bencorrado
body:
<!-- Thanks for helping us to improve kairos! We welcome all feature requests. Please fill out each area of the template so we can better help you. Comments like this will be hidden when you post but you can delete them if you wish. -->


**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]  -->

When building a UKI image the firmware of devices can regularly limit the total UKI image size causing a malloc issue that prevents the system from booting.  On many firmware packages this appears to not directly be linked to system resources where adding more RAM/disk does not fix the issue.

This creates an issue when creating large UKI files that contain a full rootfs as the system will not boot on some systems.  Even jus enabling `standard` over `core` variant can cause issues for a lot of hardware.

Right now packaging the sysext and adding it to a UKI ISO build is a manual process.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.  -->
We should attempt to load things into sysext instead of into the rootfs. for standard packaging.  Prepackaging a `standard` variant sysext and having the build process know that when there is a `VARIANT=standard` and `BOOTLOADER=systemd-boot` it should not build this into the rootfs like the other standard images, but instead at the osbuilder/enki stage layer on the right sysext as an overlay.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.  -->

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
Recovery and reset do *NOT* load sysext by default.  If the software placed into the sysext is expected to be used here we should alert the user in docs.
We should make sure installer runs the sysext as much of the `standard` variant needs this (might be there, I have not verified)
title: feat: Auto build sysext overlay for standard UKI images

author: bencorrado
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When making a Kairos appliance leaving a login prompt for users to try to login opens a security vulnerability and invited people to try to login to the device who should not be.  


**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great to lock down getty and prevent interactive logins as an option. This would cover all ttys including the serial port.  This would ideally be a config when building the OS with a `--disable-interactive-login` flag or similar.  A similar flag could then be added to the kernel command line at build time so the installer could allow logins, but production images would not.  This would similar to how reset works currently (though still Alt-Ctrl-F2 and login in reset mode too if you are fast).  This would mean updating the [systemd configs in packages](https://github.com/kairos-io/packages/blob/8facccf72976d5285981804adb8e8e5f3911cee6/packages/static/kairos-overlay-files/files/system/oem/51_reset.yaml#L11) to look for the flag and disable the getty services.  


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Currently I am locking down access for getty login in the Dockerfile by:

```
#This disables interactive login for a secure, remotely managed device
RUN systemctl disable getty@tty1.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty1.service && \
    systemctl disable getty@tty2.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty2.service && \
    systemctl disable getty@tty3.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty3.service && \
    systemctl disable getty@tty4.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty4.service && \
    systemctl disable getty@tty5.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty5.service  && \
    systemctl disable getty@tty6.service && \
    systemctl mask getty@tty6.service && \
    systemctl disable serial-getty@ttyS0.service && \
    systemctl mask serial-getty@ttyS0.service && \
    systemctl disable getty.target && \
    systemctl mask getty.target && \
    mkdir -p /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/ \
    && echo -e "[Login]\nNAutoVTs=0\nReserveVT=0\n" \
    > /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/override.conf
```
This method has some drawbacks as it also locks down the interactive installer logins.


**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
Ubuntu Core deals with this by allowing getty to be disabled, but using a USB stick with a short lived key signed by a CA that can create a user and assign a password.  This allows for a authorized technician to get local access to the machine without needing a password to interactively type that is common across lots of machines or stored in a DB that could be leaked. https://ubuntu.com/core/docs/reference/assertions/system-user
title: feat: Disable user login in production

author: mauromorales
body:
From the discussion in planning we decided that no matter how we allow the user to define the image and partition sizes, they would always need to understand what the implications are, which means they should be reading our docs.
Having said that, if they are already reading the docs, if we explain clearly enough, any solution is acceptable.

So let's do this:

- We allow the user to set both image sizes and partition sizes
- If the settings are not sane (e.g. the images won't fit in the partition in every case, including upgrades) then we fail with an error
- If the user only sets images size, we do automated calculations for partitions
- For `persistent` and `oem` partitions we don't have to check much, maybe just a minimum for oem to fit the files we put there.
- We document everything clearly

_Originally posted by @jimmykarily in https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/2151#issuecomment-1903595690_


For the documentation, see the description of the previous ticket https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/2151#issue-2086456287
title: Changes and docs to system partitioning

author: mauromorales
body:
**Problem**  
The current logic to map user intent between Kubernetes and P2P is complicated due to many overlapping attributes and their relationships.  

Example:  
```yaml
k3s:
  enabled: true

p2p:
  role: "worker"
  auto:
    enabled: true
  vpn:
    use: true
    create: false
```

At this point, it’s unclear what the system should do 😅.

**Proposal**

Unify the Kubernetes-related attributes (k3s, k3s-agent, k0s, k0s-worker) into a single k8s (or provider-kairos) block:

```
k8s:
  enabled: true
  role: "worker"
  distro: "k3s"
```

This would:

- Eliminate the need for p2p.role and p2p.auto.enabled.
- Clearly separate Kubernetes/node configuration from mesh network/VPN setup.

**Migration**

If accepted, we should add automatic configuration migration to:
- Prevent breaking existing setups during upgrades.
- Avoid maintaining two notations.
title: feat: Unify Kubernetes attributes into a single block

author: mauromorales
body:
We currently run OSV-Scanner in the Kairos main repo, but it provides limited value because it mostly evaluates dependencies used by tests/tooling that we don’t ship.

What we actually need is vulnerability coverage for the shipped artifacts: everything that ends up inside a given kairos-init version (but on release time).

## Goal

Before cutting a Kairos release, we should be able to verify that all components included in the targeted kairos-init version are scanned and that the scan result is green (or explicitly waived) for that release.

## Proposed approach

- Add a release-gating vulnerability scan that runs against all versions included in kairos-init
- Treat the release composition as the unit of truth: it doesn’t matter if individual component repos were “green” at their release time; what matters is the state of the composed release.
- Optional: reconsider running OSV-Scanner in each individual component repo if it’s redundant with the release-gating check.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a target kairos-init version (or Kairos release), CI can enumerate the included components/versions and run a vulnerability scan against them.
- CI fails the release gate when a vulnerability is found above an agreed severity threshold (or not in an allowlist).
- Output is actionable: it points to the vulnerable component/version and suggests the remediation path (bump, patch, or waiver).
title: OSV Scanner configuration

author: sarg3nt
body:
I'm not sure if this is a bug or a feature request so I'm adding it  as a bug.
Currently there is no stage that guentess that `cloud_init` code runs after the install and reboot.  
This is required for situations where we must not start a service during the install phase.
Example: My rke2-agent nodes were not working because the service was starting during install and the nodes were partially registering with the servers then after reboot when the service started again they failed to register because their key had changed and the old one was on the server.
These started services were also causing shutdown errors as the service had files open and got stuck trying to exit thus breaking the install.

I tried several of the different stages listed [here](https://kairos.io/docs/architecture/cloud-init/) and all of them started the service during install.

We are net booting these nodes with AuroraBoot serving the ISO.

I don't know if the `boot` or `after-install` phases are suppose to happen after install and reboot or not as the description on that page is not clear.

Possible solutions:

1. If `boot` or `after-install` are supposed to happen "after the install and reboot" then they are broken and need to be fixed.  The [descriptions](https://kairos.io/docs/architecture/cloud-init/) also need updated 
2. If those two stages are not supposed to happen after install then we need a new stage that is explicitly for this purpose.  Example might be `after-install-reboot`.  The descriptions should still be updated to indicate that those stages run during install.

Note I have hacked my services to run correctly by adding `echo "ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 80" >> /lib/systemd/system/rke2-server.service` to each service.  It's super hacky and I kind of hate but is working for the moment.

This is using a master build as of 11/27/2023
```bash
./earthly.sh +iso \
  --FAMILY=rhel \
  --FLAVOR=rockylinux \
  --FLAVOR_RELEASE=9 \
  --BASE_IMAGE=rockylinux:9 \
  --MODEL=generic \
  --VARIANT=core;
```

Note: This probably fixes [1864](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/1864)
title: We need a stage that is post install reboot

author: mauromorales

The encryption tests in this repo (Cleaning up 288074a8bc and related test assets in ) are functionally identical to the e2e tests in the [kcrypt-discovery-challenger](https://github.com/kairos-io/kcrypt-discovery-challenger) repository.

Both test suites:
- Set up a k3s cluster with specific networking configuration
- Install cert-manager
- Deploy the kcrypt-challenger server
- Run encryption-related e2e tests

Having the same logic in two separate repos makes it easy for them to diverge (as seen in recent PR https://github.com/kairos-io/kcrypt-discovery-challenger/pull/189 where changes had to be manually applied to both places).

**Suggested approach:**
- Move the shared test logic into a reusable workflow or a shared script that's referenced by both repos
- Or consolidate the tests into a single location and have both repos use it

This would ensure consistency and reduce maintenance burden.

author: mauromorales
body:
There's an ongoing effort to have the validator be the single source of truth for configurations. This of course relates to the implementation to how we apply those configurations on the system. On the initial ticket https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/778 we decided to limit the scope of the project and one shortcut we decided to have back then was to not have a single source of truth because doing so required quite a big refactoring, so we introduced the validation schemas, which are somewhat on par with the config.Config, config.Install, etc. In order to make it harder to forget to change the latter, we added tests that will fail if the two structures don't have the same fields. The problem is that, we can still introduce new config structures on the implementation part and bypass the tests and validations this way.

Check if it would be possible at this point in time to have a single source of truth, or how much extra work it would take. If we could already implement https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/2538 then it would force us to always include everything on the implementation and validation but the mechanism could still feel duplicated if it stays as is. So this card would be about further steps to simplify that

author: kreeuwijk
body:
Enki's `NewGenkeyCmd()` function always generates new self-signed certificates with openssl. This is a problem when the customer wants to use their own CA to issue the PK, KEK and DB certificates.

We need to be able to take the provided certificates and the factory exported keys from a device as inputs and generate the rest from that:
```
secure-boot/public-keys/
  db.pem    <-- Delivered by customer from private CA
  PK.pem    <-- Delivered by customer from private CA
  KEK.pem   <-- Delivered by customer from private CA

secure-boot/enrollment
  PK.auth   <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  PK.der    <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  PK.esl    <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  KEK.auth  <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  KEK.esl   <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  KEK.der   <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  db.auth   <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  db.esl    <-- Generated by Kairos genkey
  db.der    <-- Generated by Kairos genkey

secure-boot/private-keys
  PK.key                <-- Delivered by customer from private CA
  KEK.key               <-- Delivered by customer from private CA
  db.key                <-- Delivered by customer from private CA
  tpm2-pcr-private.pem  <-- Generated by Kairos genkey

secure-boot/exported-keys
  dbx.esl   <-- Exported by customer from device
  KEK.esl   <-- Exported by customer from device
  db.esl    <-- Exported by customer from device
```

`enki` already is able to take the factory exported keys (ESL) from a device and add those to its own generated secure boot keys, so that's good. What's missing is the ability to bring your own starting certificates.

Currently, the NewGenkeyCmd() function in enki always [generates a fresh set of self-signed certificates](https://github.com/kairos-io/enki/blob/main/cmd/genkey.go#L69-L89), What needs to happen is that `enki` gets another switch that tells it to not run `openssl` to make new self-signed PK,KEK,DB certificates but instead read existing PK,KEK,DB certificates from disk and feed those to the rest of the process.

CanvOS places all files noted above in the `/keys` directory for `enki`, so it can expect to find the customer-provided certificate files there.
title: NewGenkeyCmd() doesn't allow bringing your own certificates

body:
## Background

The [kairos-io/kairos](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos) project has comprehensive contributing guidelines including:
- TDD practices (all changes must include tests)
- DRY principles and Effective Go standards
- Code review expectations (avoiding common Go style mistakes)
- Specific PR tagging conventions (🐛, ✨, ⚠️, 📖, 🔧, :art:, 🌱, :penguin:, :arrow_up:, :robot:)
- DCO signing requirements
- Rebasing workflows
- Testing and linting requirements
- Kairos-specific SDK patterns (kairos-sdk, versioneer, etc.)

Currently, new contributors often struggle with these practices and need hand-holding. The idea is to create a **"Kairos Contributor Skill"** — a `.cursorrules` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` file that contributors install on their AI coding assistant (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, etc.) which instructs the AI to conform to all Kairos practices.

## Proposal

Create a reusable "Kairos Contributor Skill" that contributors can install on their AI coding tools. This skill would instruct the AI to:

- Follow Kairos TDD practices (always write tests first)
- Apply DRY principles and Effective Go standards
- Use proper PR labels and commit conventions
- Follow the 10-step contributing workflow (file issue → fork → branch → push → rebase → test → PR)
- Apply kairos-sdk patterns when relevant
- Follow DRY and avoid common Go style mistakes
- Use the correct emoji prefixes for commits

## Discussion Points for Monday Planning

1. **Scope**: What should the skill cover? Should it be a single `.cursorrules` file or a multi-file setup?
2. **Distribution**: How should contributors install it?
   - As a GitHub Copilot custom instructions file?
   - As a `.cursorrules` file in the repo root?
   - As a separate `kairos-contributor-skill` repo?
   - Using Cursor's workspace rules feature?
3. **Content**: What specific Kairos practices should be encoded?
4. **Maintenance**: Who owns the skill? How do we keep it in sync with evolving practices?
5. **Promotion**: How do we get contributors to actually use it?
6. **Testing**: How do we validate the skill is effective?

## References

- [Kairos CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [kairos-sdk README](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos-sdk)
- [kairos-community](https://github.com/kairos-io/community)

## Action Items

- [ ] Draft an initial `.cursorrules` file with Kairos practices
- [ ] Share with the team for feedback
- [ ] Decide on distribution mechanism
- [ ] Promote to contributors
- [ ] Evaluate effectiveness after a few weeks
title: Discussion: Create a "Kairos Contributor Skill" for AI coding assistants

author: wrkode
body:
Follow-up from #4255 / kairos-io/AuroraBoot#717.

The post-reboot reset lifecycle (#717) resolves a reset's outcome when the node re-registers and reports its boot state (`autoreset`→in-progress, `active`→done, `passive`/`recovery`→failed). But if a node **never comes back** — bricked, powered off, network-isolated — its `ResetState` stays `pending`/`in-progress` indefinitely and nothing marks it `failed`.

**Ask:** add a timeout. `ManagedNode.ResetRequestedAt` is already stored, so this can be either a periodic background sweep or a lazy check: when `ResetState` is `pending`/`in-progress` and `ResetRequestedAt` is older than a (configurable) deadline with no re-register since, transition it to `failed` (and optionally flag the node). This lets a CAPI provider stop waiting on a node that will never return.

Sub-issue of #4056.
title: AuroraBoot: reset lifecycle — fail a reset whose node never returns (timeout sweep)

author: ci-robbot
body:
## What is happening

Docker on the ARC runners refuses to start containers on the default bridge:

```
docker: Error response from daemon: failed to set up container networking:
failed to add interface veth1d80bfe to sandbox: check bridge port state:
bridge port not forwarding after 200ms
```

Docker 28 gives a freshly created veth 200ms to reach the bridge forwarding state and fails the run if it does not. On this fleet it often does not.

Runner facts, read out of the `Docker info` group of [AuroraBoot run 34262744586](https://github.com/kairos-io/AuroraBoot/actions/runs/34262744586):

```
Server Version:  28.0.4
Kernel Version:  5.14.21-150500.55.19-default
Cgroup Version:  1
Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (containerized)
```

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a retry

It has now hit three separate places, and each one needed its own workaround:

1. `tests/insecure_registry_test.go` in this repo, intermittently, taking `insecure-registry` and `partition-validation` down together. #4480, fixed with a retry that force-removes the container name between attempts.
2. `docker/setup-qemu-action` in AuroraBoot's `e2e-tests` job. Not intermittent: **every run since 2026-09-07 08:40 failed**, always in that step, so the e2e suite has not executed for two days and every open AuroraBoot PR shows a red cell unrelated to its diff. Worked around in kairos-io/AuroraBoot#787 by running the binfmt container with `--network host`.
3. AuroraBoot's own e2e harness, which runs every auroraboot invocation as `docker run` on the default bridge. Same PR.

The pattern is that anything creating a container without `--network host` is exposed, and the workarounds are per-call-site. Buildx has been immune here only because AuroraBoot already passes `driver-opts: network=host`.

## What would fix it properly

A docker bump on the runner image. The 200ms readiness check landed in docker 28.0 and its behaviour on slow veth transitions has been worked on upstream since; 28.0.4 is the version that is failing. Whoever owns the ARC runner image is better placed than me to pick the target version.

Two things I could not check from a cron: whether the `kvm` label and the generic ARC pool share an image, and whether the 200ms is tunable through the daemon config on this fleet. If it is, that is a smaller change than a bump.

Once that lands, kairos-io/AuroraBoot#787 and the retry from #4480 can both be reverted.

🤖 Filed by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.
title: CI: docker 28.0.4 on the ARC runners fails container networking with "bridge port not forwarding after 200ms"

author: mauromorales
body:
**Why it matters for incubation:** The OpenSSF Best Practices **passing** badge is a required incubation criterion. Entry: https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/9100 (in_progress, 94%, last updated June 2024). Four criteria remain, plus a freshness pass — several answers predate the move off Earthly.

**Remaining criteria and proposed answers** (the badge entry is edited via the bestpractices.dev form by the entry owner; paste-ready text below):

### 1. `release_notes_vulns` (MUST, currently unmet)

Repo work first: add a "Security fixes" section to the generated release notes (release-notes automation in `.github/workflows/release-notes-diff.yaml` / kairos-factory) listing CVEs fixed in that release; releases with none state "No security fixes in this release." Recent releases already carry a "Security Notice" about known upstream CVEs — this extends it to enumerate *fixed* CVEs, which is what the criterion requires (the current answer points at the SBOM, which does not satisfy it).

Then set to **Met** with:

> Release notes for each release include a "Security fixes" section listing the publicly known vulnerabilities (CVEs) fixed in that release. Example: <link to first release with the section>. Releases containing no security fixes state so explicitly.

### 2. `vulnerability_report_private` (MUST, currently unmet)

No repo work needed — GitHub private vulnerability reporting is already enabled and documented in SECURITY.md. The current answer ("email without PGP") is stale. Set to **Met** with:

> Vulnerabilities can be reported privately via GitHub private vulnerability reporting at https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/security/advisories/new, as documented in https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/SECURITY.md. This provides a private channel that does not depend on PGP. security@kairos.io remains available as a fallback for reporters without a GitHub account.

### 3. `warnings_fixed` (MUST, currently unanswered)

Set to **Met** with:

> Every pull request runs golangci-lint (Go), hadolint (Dockerfiles), shellcheck (shell), and yamllint (YAML) via https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/.github/workflows/lint.yaml; a failing lint job blocks the merge. Warnings are fixed or explicitly justified before merging.

### 4. `warnings_strict` (SUGGESTED, currently unanswered)

hadolint runs with `failure-threshold: warning` (`.hadolint.yaml`), i.e. warnings fail CI. Confirm golangci-lint/shellcheck behave the same, then set to **Met** with:

> Linters run in strict mode: hadolint is configured with failure-threshold "warning" (https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/.hadolint.yaml), so warnings fail the build; golangci-lint, shellcheck, and yamllint findings likewise fail the lint workflow.

If not confirmable, answer **Unmet** with a justification — SUGGESTED criteria don't block passing.

### Freshness pass (answers last touched June 2024)

Re-verify every answer that references the old build system:

- [ ] Earthly/Earthfile mentions — builds now go through kairos-factory GitHub workflows
- [ ] The SBOM claim — v4.1.2 release assets include Cosign signatures and SHA256 checksums but no SBOM files; either correct the answer or restore SBOM publishing
- [ ] Build/test instructions and project URLs

**Definition of done:** https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/9100 shows **passing**.
**Metric moved:** OpenSSF badge % (94 → 100); incubation criteria complete.
**Tracking:** part of #4242
title: Reach OpenSSF Best Practices passing badge (currently 94%)
