author: ci-robbot
body:
Refs #4618.

Triaging #4618 turned up a second, smaller problem that is entirely ours: when
the UKI boot paths give up, the operator is told nothing.

## The bug

`RebootOrWait` logs the failure and then halts. That log never reaches serial:

- immucore's logger writes to stderr (`zerolog.NewConsoleWriter` defaults to
  `os.Stderr`, `sdk/types/logger/logger.go:73-77`).
- `immucore.service` in the initramfs is `StandardOutput=journal+console`
  (`kairos-init/pkg/bundled/bundled.go:153`), and systemd's `console` is
  `/dev/console`.
- `/dev/console` aliases only the **last** `console=` on the cmdline. Kairos
  UKIs bake `console=ttyS0 console=tty1`, so that is `tty1`.

So the reason lands on the framebuffer and nowhere else, and a headless or
remote machine gets a silent halt. Both callers are UKI failure paths that
matter: `Secure boot is not enabled` and `Unlocking partitions failed`
(`immucore/pkg/state/steps_uki.go:161,542`).

`HaltWithBanner` already got this right; `RebootOrWait` was the asymmetry.

## The change

Paint the reason on every console `ConsoleDevices()` derives from the cmdline,
reusing the helpers `HaltWithBanner` uses, and include the error text. A
machine about to halt cannot be asked for its journal, so that line is the only
diagnostic that exists.

I used the explicit per-console write rather than `/dev/kmsg` because it does
not depend on the printk console level, which immucore itself lowers to `1` in
`silenceKernelLogs` and which a `quiet` cmdline lowers too. Either would have
worked from `RebootOrWait` today, but only one stays working.

## Verification

`go test ./immucore/internal/utils/` — 162 specs pass (158 before).

The new specs are mutation-checked, each caught by the spec that should catch it:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| write to the last console only (i.e. the bug) | `[FAIL] writes the message to every console, not only the last one` |
| `failureLine` drops the error | `[FAIL] includes the error, which is the only diagnostic a headless boot gets` |

`go build ./immucore/... ./cmd/...` clean, `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean on both
touched files.

## Scope

This does not close #4618. The multi-minute stall and firmware reset there are
pre-kernel and firmware-side; this only makes the Kairos-side failures that do
get reached say so on serial.
title: fix(immucore): show the halt reason on every console, not just video

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override
> any action taken here.

Refs: #4629

## What this does

Adds a step to `kairos-init/pkg/bundled/cloudconfigs/00_rootfs.yaml`'s `initramfs:` stage that creates `/var/log/audit` as `root:root 0700` on every boot. This is foundational for `auditd` (tracked separately in #4626, merged as #4650): once auditd ships, its log directory now exists with the mode it expects before the service can start.

`/var/log` has been in `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS` since 2025-05-05, so `/var/log/audit`, as a subdirectory of that already-persistent mount, already survives a normal A/B upgrade with no new mount-table entry. Nothing was added to `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS` for this PR — immucore rsyncs each listed path into `/usr/local/.state/<name>.bind` and bind-mounts it back; listing `/var/log/audit` too would nest a second bind-mount target inside a directory that is already one, for no benefit.

The new step runs in the `initramfs:` stage specifically because immucore executes that stage after the persistent bind mounts land (`dag_normal_boot.go` / `dag_in_ram.go` weak-dep, `dag_uki_boot.go` strong-dep `OpInitramfsHook` on `OpMountBind`), so the chmod/chown lands on the real persistent backing directory rather than the ephemeral one about to be shadowed — and it runs on every boot, so a directory inherited from an older install with a loose mode gets tightened, not just accepted.

## What this does not do

- **Does not close #4629.** The issue's definition of done also requires `/var/log/audit` to survive a `kairos-agent reset`. Recovery/autoreset mode intentionally omits `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS` entirely — reset means wiping `COS_PERSISTENT` back to factory state — so there is nothing for this PR to bind-mount there. The issue's own reporter already flagged this as an open design question in a comment ("Im not sure reset is possible unless we save stuff to /tmp then restore it"); solving it needs a save/restore hook in `kairos-agent`'s reset flow, a different repo, and is left as follow-up rather than attempted here.
- Does not touch SELinux label carry-over (no policy ships for this path on this base).
- Does not add a `RequiresMountsFor=` anywhere — the mount is established by immucore inside the initramfs, before `/sbin/init` runs, and there is no `auditd` unit in this repo yet.

## Verification (rule 3a, high-risk: touches immucore/kairos-init persistent-mount and permission handling)

Unit tests: `kairos-init/pkg/bundled/audit_log_dir_test.go`, 7 new Ginkgo specs against the embedded `00_rootfs.yaml`, parsed with yip's real schema and driven through yip's real `plugins.EnsureDirectories`. `go test ./kairos-init/pkg/bundled/... ./kairos-init/pkg/validation/...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, `golangci-lint` all clean.

Full QEMU verification with a real disk install — see the `QEMU verification` comment on this PR for the build/boot detail and screenshots. Summary: golden-path install confirms `/var/log/audit` is `0700 root:root` and genuinely backed by the persistent partition (matching device/inode between `/var/log/audit` and its `/usr/local/.state/var-log.bind/audit` backing path); an older-install path pre-seeded at `0755` gets tightened back to `0700` on reboot; a real A/B upgrade round-trip (genuine active/passive slot swap, not an in-place overwrite) shows the directory's `ctime` moving on the post-upgrade boot while its `mtime` does not — the new step re-asserting ownership/mode on a directory it did not create — with the pre-upgrade marker file and mode intact; and a recovery-mode boot confirms the directory is still created (ephemerally, as expected, since no persistent mount exists there) without blocking boot.

## Related

- Split off from #112 (CIS).
- Unblocks #4629's downstream consumer #4626 / #4650 (merged) and kairos-io/hadron#4637 (in flight) for the parts of the audit-log requirement that don't depend on reset semantics.

## Audit trail

Full chronological summary of what each role did: https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4629#issuecomment-5683610678
title: feat(kairos-init): create /var/log/audit as root:root 0700

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override any
> action taken here.

Two defects in `Elemental.PartitionAndFormatDevice` (`agent/pkg/elemental/elemental.go`).

`partitioner.NewDisk` opens the install target and we only closed it on the happy
path, so the three early `return err` paths — failed `disk.NewPartitionTable`,
`disk.ReReadPartitionTable`, `disk.GetPartitionTable` — leaked the fd. A plain
`defer disk.Close()` is not an option: go-diskfs zeroes its receiver in `Close()`,
so every successful install would have panicked on the second close. Instead a
guarded `closeDisk()` closure sits behind the `defer`, and the happy-path close
stays exactly where it was in program order (before `syscall.Sync()`, the udevadm
settle and mkfs) while the three leaking returns are now covered too.

Second one: the `ReReadPartitionTable` retry loop breaks on success, but was
followed by an unconditional extra call whose error was the one actually checked,
so a successful retry got silently discarded. Now we check the loop's own result
and the redundant call is gone. Two cosmetic bugs rode along in the same block:
the loop counter started at 0 so the first failure slept for 0 seconds, and the
debug log always printed "Waiting 5 seconds" regardless of the real wait. The loop
variable is renamed from `i` to `attempt` since it shadowed the existing
`i sdkSpec.SharedInstallSpec` parameter, which is likely how both bugs got in.

Four commits, in the usual three phases: capture (a test that passes against the
buggy code), fix, then flip (the same test inverted into a regression guard). The
fourth pins the guard's error assertion to an exact `invalid partition type`
substring instead of accepting any error, so it can't quietly stop exercising the
leak path if error timing changes upstream.

`go test ./agent/pkg/elemental/...` is green (70/70) both after the fix and after
the pin. The fd leak is covered by a differential fd-count test. The retry-loop
half is not independently black-box testable with the current file-backed disk
harness — go-diskfs `ReReadPartitionTable` no-ops for anything that isn't a real
block device — so that half is verified by reading the code, called out here
rather than skipped without saying so.

Audit summary: https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4610#issuecomment-5660935339

Fixes: #4610
title: fix(install): close the disk fd and honor the reread retry result

author: ci-robbot
body:
## Summary

Two same-symptom bugs in the install block: a user config validated against the published schema but was silently ignored by the agent. Both come from tag mismatches, not code paths.

### `install.no_format` vs `install.no-format`

- Schema declared `no_format` (`sdk/schema/install_schema.go:13`)
- Runtime read `no-format` (`sdk/types/install/install.go:18`, `agent/pkg/implementations/spec/spec.go:36,300`)

A user who followed the published schema disabled nothing. Renames the JSON tag on `NoFormat` to `no-format`.

### `install.passive` aliased to `install.recovery-system`

The `Passive` field carried `mapstructure:"recovery-system"` in both the SDK type and the schema, colliding with the `Recovery` line above:

```go
Recovery images.Image `... mapstructure:"recovery-system" ...`
Passive  images.Image `... mapstructure:"recovery-system" ...`  // wrong
```

The runtime's yaml path never exercised the collision (`spec.InstallSpec.Passive` has no tag), so `kairos-agent install` was fine. But `sdk/types/install.Install` is what providers and any other SDK consumer decode into via mapstructure — for them, `install.passive` was dropped and `install.recovery-system` leaked into `Passive`.

Fixes the `mapstructure` tag on `Passive` in both places.

### Tests

Two new unit tests in `sdk/types/install/install_test.go`:

- `TestPassiveDoesNotAliasRecovery` decodes `{passive: {size: 1234}, recovery-system: {size: 5678}}` and asserts each field gets its own value.
- `TestNoFormatDecodesFromKebabCase` decodes `{no-format: true}` and asserts `Install.NoFormat` is set.

Extends `sdk/schema/install_schema_test.go` with a `no-format: true` acceptance case.

Refs #1016 (Tier 0 in [that audit](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/1016#issuecomment-5546907520)). Tiers 1 to 3 still wait on @mauromorales's scope decision.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./sdk/types/install/... -v`
- [ ] `go test ./sdk/schema/... -v`
- [ ] `go test ./agent/pkg/config/...` (schema parity check)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fix(install): align install schema keys with what the runtime reads

author: ci-robbot
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`/etc/systemd` is one of the `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS` in `00_rootfs.yaml`, so it is a persistent state bind. Before immucore binds it, `op.MountBind` syncs the image copy into the state directory with `internalUtils.SyncState`, which runs `rsync -aquAX` with no `--delete`. The sync is therefore purely additive: a unit symlink written by an earlier image outlives that image.

Ubuntu's `ssh.service` carries `Alias=sshd.service`, so enabling it leaves `/etc/systemd/system/sshd.service -> /usr/lib/systemd/system/ssh.service` in persistent state. Move the node to an image whose real unit is named `sshd.service`, such as Hadron, and that target no longer exists. `/etc` wins over `/usr` in systemd's unit load path, so the dangling symlink shadows the packaged unit:

```
LoadState=not-found
LoadError=org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit "Unit sshd.service not found."
```

The node boots, Kubernetes reports it Ready, and SSH is refused on every node. As @Itxaka noted on the issue, this is not specific to sshd: any unit that two base images name differently hits it.

A new boot step, `quarantine-stale-units`, moves such a symlink out of the unit load path after the persistent binds are mounted and before `switch_root`, so systemd in the real root never loads it. It runs in the normal-boot, UKI and in-RAM DAGs.

**Nothing is deleted.** The symlink is renamed into `/etc/systemd/kairos-stale-units/`, keeping its name and its target. That directory is inside the same persistent `/etc/systemd` bind, on the same filesystem (so the move is an atomic rename, not a copy that can half-fail), and in none of systemd's unit load paths. Restoring one is a single `mv`. An entry already parked under the same name is replaced only when it points at the same target; a different target gets a numbered suffix so the older evidence survives.

The rule for what gets moved is deliberately narrow, so that a move can only ever reveal a unit that works:

- Only symlinks directly in `etc/systemd/system`. The enablement symlinks under `.wants/` and `.requires/` shadow nothing, and a unit that a sysext provides is not merged yet at this point in the boot, so its enablement symlink legitimately dangles here.
- Only symlinks whose target is missing, and only on a genuine `ENOENT`. Any other stat error says nothing about the target.
- Never a mask. Its target is `/dev/null`, which the sysroot has no device node for yet, checked both literally and after resolution so a relative mask is not unmasked by accident.
- Only when a resolvable unit of the same name exists outside `/etc`, under `usr/local/lib`, `usr/lib` or `lib`.

The step never fails the boot. A node that boots with one stale symlink left in place is where we already are today, so taking the boot down over it would be a regression.

On an affected node the image already ships the right enablement symlink: Hadron runs `systemctl preset-all` at build time, which writes `/etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/sshd.service`, and the rsync copies it into the state directory. Once the shadowing symlink is out of the way, `sshd.service` resolves and starts.

**Verification**:

```
CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./immucore/...
CGO_ENABLED=0 go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.6.2 run ./immucore/internal/utils/... ./immucore/pkg/state/... ./immucore/pkg/dag/...
```

Both green, lint at 0 issues.

`QuarantineStaleUnitSymlinks` has unit tests for the reported case and for each thing the rule must not touch: a target that exists, a `/dev/null` mask, a relative mask, a stat error that is not `ENOENT`, a dangling symlink with no packaged unit behind it, a dangling `.wants/` entry, a relative target, a packaged unit found under `/lib`, and a missing unit directory. There are also specs for the parking itself: the parked symlink keeps its target, an already parked entry with a different target survives under a suffix, and an identical one is reused rather than piling up per boot. `QuarantineStaleUnitsDagStep` has a test that runs the step through a herd graph against a temporary rootdir and reads the parked symlink back, plus a DAG-shape test pinning the step between `mount-bind` and `initramfs-hook`.

Mutation-checked the new specs: skipping the rename fails three of them, and overwriting a parked entry instead of suffixing it fails the collision spec.

Not verified in a real boot: reproducing it needs a node upgraded from an Ubuntu image to Hadron.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #4085
title: fix(immucore): move stale unit symlinks out of the systemd load path

author: ci-robbot
body:
Phases 2 and 3 of #4298, with the two additions @mudler asked for on top: versions in the config, and a way to ignore signatures.

Until now an extension could only be installed by hand, one at a time, from the one catalog whose URL was compiled into the agent. There was no config field at all.

## Phase 2: configurable, additive catalogs

A new top level `extensions` block:

```yaml
extensions:
  catalogs:
    - https://extensions.example.org/releases.json
    - https://kairos-io.github.io/hadron-layers/releases.json
```

Catalogs are searched **in order, first match wins**, so a node can put its own index ahead of the default one and override what a name means. When a later catalog also publishes the name, the one that was ignored is logged rather than silently dropped.

One rule, not two: an unset list means the built-in default, and a set list replaces it. Anyone who wants the default plus their own lists both, which is more typing than a magic `extra_catalogs` field but has no merge order to remember.

A catalog that cannot be fetched or parsed is logged and skipped, so one unreachable index does not make every extension unresolvable. If *none* could be read, the error names every URL and its reason, so a typo is diagnosable.

`--catalog` becomes repeatable and still takes precedence over the config.

## Versions in the config

```yaml
install:
  extensions:
    - fwupd                     # newest version published
    - fwupd@2.1.7               # exact version
    - name: git
      version: ">= 2.50, < 3"   # semver constraint
```

Resolution order matters and is deliberate:

1. An empty version means the layer's own `latest`.
2. A version that **matches a published tag exactly** selects that tag. This comes before constraint matching so layers whose versions are not semver (`stable`, `2026.09`) still work.
3. Anything else is read as a semver constraint (`Masterminds/semver`, already a dependency) and the highest published version satisfying it wins.

## Phase 3: declarative selection at install time

```yaml
install:
  extensions:
    - k3s
    - oci://ghcr.io/example/tools.sysext.raw
    - /run/initramfs/live/extra.sysext.raw
```

This is the #3068 acceptance criteria that was never implemented. An entry is a plain string, or a mapping when the constraint contains a space and so cannot be written after an `@`. A bare name resolves through the catalogs; anything with a scheme, and any absolute path, is taken as one image and refuses a version.

The catalogs are fetched **once**, and only if some entry actually needs them, so a config naming nothing but URIs installs with no network access to any index.

Where the extensions land:

- **UKI**: the EFI extension directories. `SysExtPostInstall` already mounts the EFI partition and creates `active.efi.extra.d` / `passive.efi.extra.d`, so the download happens inside that window, staged through a temporary directory so the same image is not pulled once per boot state.
- **Otherwise**: the persistent partition, at `/usr/local/.state/var-lib-kairos.bind/extensions`, which is the bind source immucore mounts over `/var/lib/kairos`. immucore's first-boot sync is `rsync -aquAX` with no `--delete`, so what is staged survives it. There is a test pinning that path, because if either side changes the extensions land somewhere nothing reads.

## Ignoring signatures

The gap I flagged in the spec: systemd refuses an extension that does not satisfy the image policy on `systemd-sysext` / `systemd-confext`, and kairos-init sets that policy to require a signature under Trusted Boot (`root=signed+absent`) and dm-verity otherwise (`root=verity+absent`). Catalog extensions are published unsigned by design, so on such a node they are downloaded, enabled, and then **silently not merged**.

`extensions.ignore_signatures: true` is the opt-out. It writes a cloud config to `/oem` (the same mechanism `ssh_hardening` uses, so it survives an upgrade) that drops a permissive `--image-policy` into both units:

- Named `zz-kairos-ignore-signatures.conf` so it sorts **after** kairos-init's `kairos.conf` and `kairos-uki.conf`. systemd applies drop-ins in lexical order and the last `ExecStart` is the one that counts; a name sorting earlier would be silently overridden. There is a test on that ordering.
- `ExecStart=` and `ExecReload=` are reset before being set, otherwise the override is appended to the strict one and the unit runs two refreshes.
- Followed by `daemon-reload` and a restart, because the units have already started with the strict policy by the time the boot stage runs. Without that the setting would only take effect on the second boot.
- Off by default, and it logs a warning when used. Under Trusted Boot, refusing an unsigned extension is the point of Trusted Boot.

## One move

`parseURI` and the three download sources move from `agent/pkg/action` into a new `agent/pkg/extensions`. The install hooks need to download an extension, and `agent/pkg/action` imports the hooks, so the hooks cannot import it back. `action.InstallExtension` stays as a wrapper, so nothing outside changes.

## Tests

- Shorthand and mapping parsing, `name@version` vs a digest-pinned `@sha256:` reference, reference detection per scheme, and a marshal round-trip that proves a space-bearing constraint comes back out as a mapping.
- Semver constraints against a catalog with several versions, exact-tag precedence, and a layer whose tags are not semver at all.
- Multi-catalog: first wins, shadowing reported, additive lookup in both directions, and an error that names every catalog it looked in.
- One unreachable catalog out of two still resolves; none reachable fails with both URLs named; no temporary files left behind.
- `InstallDeclared` over a mixed list: two catalog names, an OCI reference and a local path, asserting what each one pulled and into which directory, and that the catalogs were fetched once rather than once per extension. A URI-only list must not touch a catalog.
- The full config surface validates against the JSON schema, and an extension with no name is rejected.
- The cloud config the signature opt-out installs: both units covered, drop-in name sorts last, `ExecStart`/`ExecReload` reset, policy accepts an unprotected image, reload and re-merge present.
- A cloud config read off disk the way the agent reads it, asserting the values arrive in `cfg.Extensions` and `cfg.Install.Extensions` with `fwupd@2.1.7` split into name and version.

`agent/pkg/utils` and `sdk/sysext` fail locally for want of rsync and a Docker daemon, on this branch and on `master` alike.

## Not in this PR

- Phase 1 (#4486) is the blocker that makes install-by-name actually work; this PR is the layer above it and the two do not overlap in code.
- Docs for the new config keys. Worth a kairos-docs PR once the shape is agreed here rather than before.
- Phase 4 (named triggers such as `k3s: true` implying the k3s extension) is cheap on top of this: a static map from config key into the same list. Phases 5 and 6 are unchanged from the spec.

Refs #4298
title: feat(extensions): declarative extensions, configurable catalogs, versions

author: ci-robbot
body:
Refs #4340. PR 3 of the split, on top of #4574 (`feat/webui-into-installer`),
so review that one first; this diff is only the four new files and the handler
rewrite.

## What changes

The web UI was the last install frontend not on the `sdk/agentrun` contract. It
shelled out to `/usr/bin/kairos-agent` by hand, wrote the process output to two
files, and tailed them into the websocket as HTML built by a 150-line
ANSI-to-CSS converter. The browser decided an install had finished by looking
for a `[COMPLETE]` substring in that text.

It calls `agentrun.RunWithOutput` now, like the TUI and the MCP server, and
`/ws` carries one JSON object per frame:

```json
{"type":"step","step":"partition"}
{"type":"log","message":"a line of agent output"}
{"type":"error","message":"no target device found"}
{"type":"done","ok":true}
```

`progress.html` renders the step ids as a checklist beside the log instead of
scraping the log for them. `ansiToHTML`, `formatLogLine`, `go-processmanager`
and `nxadm/tail` are gone; `nxadm/tail` drops out of `go.mod` with them.

The stream is replayed from the start of the run rather than from whenever the
socket opened, because the browser only reaches `progress.html` through a
redirect **after** the install has been submitted. On the old code a reload
re-read the two files; on an in-process run there is nothing to re-read, so the
run keeps its own transcript and readers take it by index.

## Four things that follow from the move

- **The agent is resolved, not hardcoded.** `agentrun.ResolveAgentBin` instead
  of `/usr/bin/kairos-agent`, so `KAIROS_AGENT_BIN` and the `PATH` fallback work
  here as everywhere else, and a missing agent is reported on the form instead
  of as an install that starts and immediately stops.
- **The device goes into the cloud-config**, not a `--device` flag, because that
  is the argument shape `agentrun.Command` builds and what the TUI already does.
  It is written last and unconditionally: an `install.device` left in the pasted
  YAML must not outrank the device the operator typed into the field next to it.
- **Both finish boxes ticked resolves to reboot.** Two flags used to be handed to
  the agent, and `hooks.Lifecycle` checks `ShouldReboot` before `ShouldShutdown`,
  so this is what the machine already did. It is only now said in one place.
- **The transcript is teed into `debugbundle.AgentOutputLog`**, the same file the
  TUI writes, so an install driven from the browser lands in a debug bundle too.

## Two behaviour changes worth naming

`manual-install` is now invoked with `--use-default-dirs`, because
`agentrun.Command` always passes it. The web UI was the odd one out here: the
TUI passes it and `kairos-agent install` scans the same user config dirs.

Log lines reach the page as text through `textContent` rather than as
server-built markup through `innerHTML`. The old path escaped `&<>` on its way
through the ANSI converter, so this is not a fix for a live hole, but the sink
is no longer one.

## Verification

`go test ./installer/...` is green, 43 specs in `internal/webui`. The new ones
drive a real `httptest` server and a real websocket against a shell-script stub
agent, so the JSON on the wire is asserted rather than the callbacks behind it:
progress replay after the run has ended, a resubmit not starting a second
install, a failed install being retriable, and a missing agent rendering on the
form.

Mutation-checked, each reverted then restored:

| revert | spec that fails |
| --- | --- |
| poweroff wins over reboot | `is reboot when both boxes are ticked` |
| only set `install.device` when absent | `overrides a device left in the pasted config` |
| drop the replay-window clamp in `since` | `resumes a reader whose position fell out of the replay window` (slice bounds panic) |
| rename one step id in `progress.html` | `lists exactly the agent's steps, in the order the agent emits them` |

What I could not run: the page itself. There is no usable JS runtime or browser
on this box, so `progress.html` is covered by specs that read the embedded asset
(the step table matches `agentrun.Steps`, every message type has a `case`, no
`innerHTML`) and by review, not by executing it. Worth a look in a live boot
before merge.

## Next

PR 4 of the split is the AuroraBoot grub reorder; PR 5 is the TUI's first
screen. Both are outside this repo's `installer/` and outside this diff.
title: feat(installer): stream the web UI's install from agentrun

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override
> any action taken here.

Implements the CIS Distribution Independent Linux v2.0.0 Level 1 "1.x —
Initial setup" controls in `kairos-init`, as a new skippable stage
`GetCISHardeningStage` (`cisHardening`) that runs after cleanup so a package
removal calling `userdel` cannot undo the account-database modes.

- Filesystem module blocklist under `/etc/modprobe.d/cis-blocklist.conf` for
  `cramfs`, `freevxfs`, `jffs2`, `hfs`, `hfsplus`, `udf` (1.1.1.1-1.1.1.6),
  following the existing precedent at `29_blacklist.yaml`.
- Warning banner content in `/etc/issue.net` (1.7) — only `/etc/issue` was
  written before this.
- File permission tightening on `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/gshadow`,
  `/etc/group` and their `-` backups (6.1), via symbolic chmods guarded on
  the file existing, so they only ever subtract bits and never fabricate a
  backup that a shadow utility hasn't created yet.

Deliberately out of scope this round, left for follow-up: SELinux enforcing
mode (1.6, flagged in the issue as needing its own spike), sysctl hardening
(3.x), auditd (4.x — blocked on #4629, which needs `/var/log/audit`
persistence across A/B upgrades first), PAM/login.defs (5.x), and
chrony/timesyncd verification (6.x). This PR only closes a subset of
#4626's checklist, so it does not carry a closing keyword.

This is a high-risk change under the operator's ground rules (it touches
account-database permissions and a boot-time filesystem blocklist), so it
went through a real build-and-boot verification before opening: a live ISO
was built from this branch, booted under QEMU/KVM, and an unprivileged user
was created and used to `su - root` through a real PAM password prompt to
confirm the tightened `/etc/shadow` permissions do not break login. See the
`QEMU verification` comment on this PR for the full detail and screenshot.

Went through two review rounds after the initial draft. The first cut cited
the wrong CIS section (1.1, Filesystem Configuration) for the
account-database permission controls, which actually fall under 6.1 (System
File Permissions) — fixed in all three places that mentioned it. The second
round caught a `kairos-init/README.md` paragraph that overclaimed what
shipped: it read as full CIS L1 coverage (SELinux/sysctl/auditd/PAM/time-sync
are all still deferred), implied the `/etc/issue.net` banner shows on SSH
logins (sshd's `Banner` directive isn't wired up here), and said
`/etc/passwd`/`/etc/group` lose read access when only the shadow files and
backups actually do. Both are corrected on the branch.

Full audit trail, including the per-round reviewer verdicts: https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4626#issuecomment-5676725370

Refs #4626
title: feat(kairos-init): CIS L1 initial setup controls

author: ci-robbot
body:
The third PR @mudler asked for on #1697, and not the one I offered. I said I
would take the `blkid` forks and the double `syscall.Sync()`. The `blkid` half
is here. The `Sync()` half I am not doing blind, and I ask about it below.

While reading `DiskFSType` for the fork I found a panic in it, so this is two
commits: the panic first, the fork second.

## The panic

`DiskFSType` parses BusyBox blkid's output by taking the last field and
splitting it on `=`:

```go
typeFs := splitted[len(splitted)-1]
typeFsSplitted := strings.Split(typeFs, "=")
if len(typeFsSplitted) < 1 {
        KLog.Logger.Debug().Str("what", typeFs).Msg("typeFs split")
        return "ext4"
}
finalFS := typeFsSplitted[1]
```

`len(typeFsSplitted) < 1` never holds. `strings.Split` answers with one
element for a string with no separator in it, never zero:

```
Split("TYPE=\"ext4\"") -> len=2 ["TYPE" "\"ext4\""]  ; [1] safe
Split("/dev/sda2:")    -> len=1 ["/dev/sda2:"]       ; [1] panics
Split("")              -> len=1 [""]                 ; [1] panics
```

So the fallback the guard was written to give is unreachable, and a last field
carrying no `=` panics on `index out of range [1] with length 1`. The guard has
to be `< 2`.

The `=` is normally there, because BusyBox prints `TYPE="ext4"` as the last
tag. It is not there when blkid names a device it found no tags for
(`/dev/sda2:`), and `DiskFSType` runs on the state device, on overlay backing
devices and on every custom-mount source, on every mount attempt. A panic there
takes immucore down in the initramfs instead of falling back to `ext4`.

Only BusyBox images reach this branch, which is why it has stayed hidden.

## The fork

`DiskFSType` ran `blkid --help` on every call to decide which blkid it is
talking to. That answer cannot change while immucore runs, and `DiskFSType` is
called just-in-time inside the `MountOPWithFstab` retry loop, once per attempt:

```go
default:
        // check fs type just-in-time before running the OP
        if t != "tmpfs" {
                fsType := internalUtils.DiskFSType(what)
```

So every attempt forked a second blkid to learn what the first attempt already
knew. It now runs once, behind `sync.OnceValue`. The per-device query stays per
call, because its answer differs per device.

## What I did not touch, and why

The other half of what I offered was the double `syscall.Sync()`:

```go
func Mount(source string, target string, fstype string, flags uintptr, data string) (err error) {
        Sync()
        defer Sync()
        return syscall.Mount(source, target, fstype, flags, data)
}
```

`syscall.Sync()` flushes every mounted filesystem and blocks until it is done,
and this runs it twice around each `internalUtils.Mount` call. On the face of it
neither one has anything to flush: nothing immucore wrote needs to be on disk
for a `mount(2)` to work, and `mount(2)` writes no file data.

But `git log -L` says these are yours and deliberate, immucore#288
`fix(mount): call sync before/after operations`, and the commit message does
not record what they fixed. So I am not reverting your fix on a reading of the
code. @mudler what did #288 fix? If it was durability across an unclean
shutdown in a specific window, `syncfs(2)` on the filesystem actually involved
would give the same guarantee without stalling on every other mounted
filesystem, and I will do that instead. If you would rather it just came out,
say so and it comes out.

## Verification

`DiskFSType` had no tests. It has 9 specs now, over both blkid flavours, the
fallbacks, and the caching. `blkid` moves behind a var so the specs can answer
for it without a blkid binary present. Both commits were checked against a
mutant:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| guard back to `len(typeFsSplitted) < 1` | 3 specs fail with `runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1` |
| `blkid --help` asked per call again | `asks blkid which blkid it is only once` fails |

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./immucore/...
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/internal/utils
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/cmd
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/op
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/state

$ CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run --timeout=12m    # v2.13.2, from .golangci-version
0 issues.
```

Cut from `master`. It touches only `immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go`, so it
does not collide with #4457, #4458 or #4461, and needs none of them merged
first.

Part 4 of #1697. It does not close it; #4458 does.

## What is not verified

No boot. The panic is reproduced in a spec, not on a BusyBox image, and I have
not measured the fork saving on a real boot, so I am not claiming a number for
@pataha's stall. Two forks per attempt going to one is the change; how much of
those 10 to 15 seconds it is worth needs a boot to say.
title: fix(immucore): fix a DiskFSType panic and its fork per attempt

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4607.

## The bug

`MountBind`'s prepare callback rsyncs the image path into the persistent state
dir on **every** boot, and it does so with `-X`:

- [`immucore/pkg/op/fs.go:96-101`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/immucore/pkg/op/fs.go#L96-L101) `CreateIfNotExists(rootMount)`, `CreateIfNotExists(stateDir)`, `SyncState(rootMount, stateDir)`
- [`immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go:104`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go#L104) `rsync -aquAX <src> <dst>`

`--xattrs` makes the destination's attribute set *match* the source's, which
includes deleting one the destination has and the source does not.

When the OS image does not ship the bind-mount path, `CreateIfNotExists`
creates the source directory itself, in the initramfs, before any policy is
loaded, so it has no `security.selinux` at all. The destination is the real
`.bind` state dir and does have one once something has relabelled it. Boot 0
looks correct, boot 1 onwards strips the label back off, same inode with a
ctime bumped by rsync setting attrs. Files created under it at runtime keep
their labels, because they are not in the source and there is no `--delete`.
That asymmetry is what was reported while QA'ing #4519.

`-u` does not protect it: `--update` compares mtimes on files, and directory
attributes are applied regardless.

## The change

Keep `-X`, because the image does ship legitimate attributes that have to
propagate downward, and instead put back anything the sync removed from the
state dir root.

Only the two roots can disagree this way. Everything below the source comes out
of the OS image and was labelled at build time, so `-X` keeps doing the right
thing there. An attribute the sync gave a *new* value is left alone, since the
source is entitled to an opinion. It is only removal that is never wanted.

No recursive `restorecon` over the persistent tree, and no behaviour change for
anything that is not a directory the initramfs invented.

## Verification

Locally, against a real rsync 3.5.0, since this box has no container runtime:

```
$ go test ./immucore/internal/utils/ -count=1
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/internal/utils	0.562s
```

The specs drive `SyncState` itself rather than asserting on the command string.
Tests run unprivileged and only root may write the `security` namespace, so
they use a `user.` attribute; rsync applies the same delete rule to every
namespace it handles, so the path under test is the real one. They skip
cleanly where `rsync` is absent or the filesystem stores no xattrs.

Checked the new spec is not vacuous by replacing the restore with a no-op:

```
[FAIL] SyncState [It] keeps an attribute the source does not have
```

Two guard specs cover the other direction: the source's own value still wins,
and content still copies.

`go vet` and `golangci-lint run` are clean on the package, and the full
`./immucore/...` suite passes.

## Not in scope

The agent-side sync went the other way and never grew this problem:
[`agent/pkg/utils/common.go:182-189`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/agent/pkg/utils/common.go#L182-L189)
uses `--archive --acls` with no `-X`, above a `TODO` asking this exact
question. The two sync paths still disagree. Worth settling, but not here.
title: fix(immucore): stop the state sync stripping the bind dir's label

author: jimmykarily
body:
…p-image pushes

GHCR has no expires-after equivalent and no bulk-delete: mass tag cleanup is one DELETE per version through the container-packages REST API. The install-upgrade UKI test in kairos-io/kairos#4646 pushes a uniquely-tagged upgrade image every run, so those versions were accumulating forever, and the same applies to the pr-N tags the kairos-init and kcrypt-challenger image builds push on every PR update.

The composite action .github/actions/ghcr-cleanup takes a newline-separated list of ghcr.io refs and deletes each one via a small Go program. Go instead of shell so the code stays readable past the parse-list / resolve-scope / paginate / DELETE-per-version control flow, and so the httptest-backed table tests can cover the edge cases (nested-package URL encoding, org-vs-user endpoint fallback, tag shared across versions, pagination, DELETE failure) without spinning up a real registry. Missing tags, missing packages, and non-ghcr.io refs are warnings by default so `if: always()` post-steps don't mask a green test.

Wired in at two sites:

- _uki-test.yaml: a post-step reads build/upgrade_image_name and runs the action against the freshly-pushed upgrade tag. Runs `if: always()` so a failed ginkgo suite still cleans up.
- pr.yaml: a final cleanup-ghcr job (needs: all leaf tests + the arm build) removes the pr-N kairos-init and kcrypt-challenger tags. Fork PRs are still gated by the same authorize environment the rest of the pipeline uses.

Master's :master-scratch tags are intentionally left alone: they get overwritten on every push (no accumulation), and after `promote-images` copies the manifest to :master via buildx imagetools create, deleting the scratch package version could take :master with it. The ISO OS image tags pushed by build-iso -> reusable-factory also accumulate per commit SHA on master and per matrix cell on PR -- their tag shape includes git-describe VERSION across the whole build-iso matrix, so cleaning them up needs its own pass and is deferred.

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4524.

`nodepair.Send` blocks inside go-nodepair's `waitNodes` until its context ends. Both callers in this tree passed `context.Background()`, so a node that never joined the pairing network meant neither call ever returned.

**In CI.** `provider-qrcode-install` sat in `registering with a screenshot` for **58m43s** on [run 34125670036](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34125670036), printing go-nodepair's `Not enough nodes` every 10 seconds, until the ginkgo suite timeout ended it. The suite timeout ends the *whole run*, so the leg reported `1 failed, 33 skipped` and gave no signal about anything else. Same signature right now on #4468, #4476 and #4494.

**In the CLI.** `kairos register` has the identical shape. Point it at a node that is not in pairing mode and it prints `Sending registration payload, please wait` and never comes back. No timeout, no error, no flag to bound it.

## What this does

**Both callers get a deadline, and both check `ctx.Err()`.** The second half matters: `Send` returns `nil` on `ctx.Done()`, so a caller that only inspects the returned error cannot tell an expired deadline from a delivered payload.

**`kairos register` grows `--timeout`,** defaulting to 15m, and reports what went wrong:

```
the node did not pair within 15m0s. Check that it is booted in pairing mode and
reachable on the same network, then retry with a longer --timeout
```

`--timeout 0` keeps the old wait-forever behaviour. **This is the one judgment call in the PR** and the only user-visible behaviour change: a finite default trades "waits forever on a network that will never pair" for "gives up after 15m on a network that would have paired at minute 16". Say the word and I will flip the default to 0 so the flag is opt-in.

**The e2e harness `register()` is capped at 10m,** three times the 191s a green pairing costs. A pairing failure now fails that spec, with `gatherLogs` output and the step named, and the other 33 specs still run.

**The two remaining ceilings in the qrcode spec are capped too,** for the reason in #4489: the spec must not be able to outlast the suite budget however it fails. Worst case goes from unbounded to 50m against a 60m budget, and every step keeps at least 3x its measured cost.

| step | measured green | was | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EventuallyConnects` | ~30s | 20m | 10m |
| wait for QR code | 12s | 10m | 10m |
| `register` | 191s | unbounded | 10m |
| reboot to installed | 66s | 30m | 10m |
| cmdline after reboot | <1s | 10m | 10m |
| **spec total** | **303s** | **unbounded** | **50m** |

## Verification

- `go build ./provider/...`, `go vet ./provider/internal/cli/`, `go vet ./...` in `tests/`, `gofmt -l` all clean (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, go1.26.8).
- `go test ./provider/internal/cli/` passes: 22 specs, up from 18 on `master`, so the four new ones do run.
- The new `pairingContext` spec was checked against the pre-fix behaviour: with `pairingContext` reverted to `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` it fails on `bounds the wait when given a positive timeout`, and passes once restored.
- The e2e paths are not runnable here (no docker, no KVM). The `tests/` changes are compile-checked and reviewed only.

## What this does not fix

It bounds and attributes the hang. It does not fix whatever stopped the two peers finding each other in that run. If the flake survives, the next occurrence will at least arrive in minutes with logs and a named step instead of as a silent hour.
title: fix(register): bound the pairing wait instead of hanging forever

author: ci-robbot
body:
`RotateToken` has lived in `provider/internal/cli/token/rotate.go` as a public function since the c3os days, but nothing has ever exposed it. The pre-monorepo `provider-kairos` never registered a rotate command either — I checked its archived tree — so kairos-io/kairos#6 (opened Feb 2022) still had no end-to-end path for a user to rotate a network token via the CLI.

This wires `kairos provider rotate-token` as a thin adapter over the existing function. The library keeps the actual work.

## Behaviour

```
kairos provider rotate-token [--config-dir DIR ...] [--api URL] \
    [--root-dir DIR] [--restart] NEW_TOKEN
```

- Rewrites `p2p.network_token` in every config file under `--config-dir` (default `/etc/kairos` and `/oem`, the writable subset of the standard user config dirs).
- Reuses the shared `--api` flag from `networkAPI`, so it inherits the same edgevpn socket default as the other commands.
- `--root-dir` (default `/`) is where the edgevpn service files get written; matches the existing `SetupVPN` call sites in `provider/bootstrap.go`.
- `--restart` reloads the edgevpn service so a running node picks up the new token in place.
- The token can come from a positional arg, `--token`, or `$TOKEN`. Positional wins.

## Tests

`start_internal_test.go` now checks that `rotate-token` is reachable from `NewApp`, that its documented defaults are the ones the code sets, and that omitting the token surfaces a helpful error rather than a silent no-op.

## Follow-up

Once this is in, the docs PR mudler asked for on #6 can document a real command instead of a manual "edit `/oem/*.yaml` and restart edgevpn" recipe.

Refs #6
title: feat(provider): wire the rotate-token CLI

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4038.

`kairos-agent bootentry` on a UKI system cannot select an entry it just
printed, if the system has exactly four loader entries and they carry an
extra-cmdline suffix. That is the reporter's layout:

```
/efi/EFI/kairos/
  active.efi
  passive.efi
  recovery_install-mode_stylus.registration.efi
  statereset_install-mode_stylus.registration.efi
```

## What goes wrong

`selectBootEntrySystemd` reads the entries off the ESP, then throws them away:

```go
originalEntries := entries
// when there are only 4 entries, we can assume they are either cos ... fallback, recovery or statereset
if len(entries) == len(cnst.UkiDefaultMenuEntries()) {
	entries = cnst.UkiDefaultMenuEntries()
}
err = entryInList(cfg, entry, entries)
```

`UkiDefaultMenuEntries()` is the fixed list `cos, fallback, recovery, statereset`.
The substitution is there so a caller can pass a bare role name on an install
whose entries carry a suffix, and it works for that. But it also makes the four
real names unrepresentable: validation now runs against a list that does not
contain any of them.

So `listBootEntriesSystemd` offers `recovery install-mode_stylus.registration`
in its selection prompt, the user picks it, and the very next step answers:

```
ERR entry recovery install-mode_stylus.registration does not exist
```

The list-then-select flow cannot select what it listed, and a cloud-init stage
that spells the entry out in full fails the same way. The count test is also
incidental: a system with four entries that are not the default four gets its
list replaced by names that do not exist on disk, and selecting one of those
would write a `LoaderEntryOneShot` pointing at a missing `.conf`.

## The fix

Drop the substitution and resolve the requested name against the entries that
are really on the ESP:

- an exact match wins;
- failing that, the name is treated as a bare role and matched against entries
  beginning with it followed by a space, so `recovery` still selects
  `recovery install-mode_stylus.registration`. That is what the install, reset
  and upgrade paths pass, and it is what the docs tell a user to type;
- `active` is still accepted as an alias for `cos`, now carrying its suffix
  across rather than dropping it.

A bare role that matches two entries is now an error naming both. It used to
resolve to whichever one `WalkDirFs` returned last, which is directory order,
not a choice.

Resolution also moved above the RW remount, so a bad name no longer remounts
the ESP before failing.

## Tests

Two new specs in `agent/pkg/action/bootentries_test.go`:

- the reporter's exact four-entry layout: the names `listSystemdEntries`
  produces are selectable, the bare roles still resolve, and `registration`
  (the name from the original report, which was never an entry) is still
  rejected. This spec fails on `master` with the reporter's error verbatim.
- an ambiguous bare role errors instead of guessing, and naming one of the two
  entries exactly still works.

`go test ./agent/pkg/action/` is green (213 specs), as is `golangci-lint run`
at the pinned `v2.13.2`. The pre-existing `agent/pkg/utils` `SyncData` failure
on my box is `rsync` missing locally, not this change.

## Note

`cnst.UkiDefaultMenuEntries()` now has no callers outside its own tests. I left
it in place rather than widen the diff, but it can go if you would rather not
keep a dead exported helper.

## What this does not fix

the earlier reviewer read the original report as two problems, and this is the second one.
`--select registration` was never valid: `registration` is a fragment of the
extra-cmdline suffix, not an entry. After this change the same system accepts
`recovery install-mode_stylus.registration`, which is the name the tool prints.
Whether the `after-reset` flow itself passes a valid name still wants a check on
real hardware, which I cannot do here.
title: fix(uki): select a boot entry by the name bootentry prints

author: ci-robbot
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**

`PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS` in the shipped `00_rootfs.yaml` listed `/usr/libexec`.
Immucore rsyncs each of those paths from the booted slot into
`/usr/local/.state/<path>.bind` and then bind-mounts that directory back over
the slot (`immucore/pkg/op/fs.go:76`). The sync is `rsync -aquAX`
(`immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go:104`), and `--update` keeps whichever side
has the newer file.

So the directory is shared between the two slots, and the newer image wins it.
Boot a newer active image and its `/usr/libexec` is promoted into the shared
copy; roll back to the older passive image and it gets the newer helpers rather
than its own.

The reporter in #4304 hit this as a broken `sudo` after rolling back across an
Ubuntu release:

```text
sudo: /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.42' not found
      (required by /usr/libexec/sudo/libsudo_util.so.0)
```

The older slot booted fine, but its `/usr/libexec` was hidden behind content
built against a glibc it does not ship, so administrative access was lost.

**The fix**

Drop `/usr/libexec` from the list, and write the rule into the file so the list
does not grow another entry with the same failure mode: only machine-owned
state belongs there, because anything under `/usr` is image content and
persisting it merges one slot's binaries into the other.

The entry looks legacy rather than deliberate. It arrived with the wholesale
import of the old rootfs layout (`kairos-init#61`, May 2025), which added it
twice; `kairos-init#124` removed one of the two copies a month later. Nothing
in this repo writes to `/usr/libexec` at runtime, and nothing references it
outside this one line.

**Scope**

This is the smallest fix for the reported breakage. It deliberately does not
touch the sync semantics, which #4304 also discusses:

- `--update` is there on purpose (`immucore#525`) to protect user-modified
  state, so it cannot simply be dropped for `/etc/ssh` or `/etc/systemd`.
- The sync has no `--delete`, so removed files outlive the image that wrote
  them. I hit that same class of bug from a different direction in #4452.

Both are worth their own change. `/etc/ssl/certs` and `/etc/sysconfig` are in
the same list and are equally image-owned, but neither is the reported
regression, so they are left for a follow-up that can be tested on its own.

**Upgrade behaviour**

An existing install keeps a stale `/usr/local/.state/usr-libexec.bind` on the
persistent partition. Nothing binds it once this config lands, and
`00_rootfs.yaml` is reset on upgrade, so it is inert. No cleanup step is
needed for the fix to take effect.

**Testing**

New `kairos-init/pkg/bundled/rootfs_layout_test.go` parses the embedded
`00_rootfs.yaml` and asserts no persistent path lives under `/usr/lib*`, that
`/usr/libexec` specifically is gone, and that the machine-owned entries are
still there. Verified it fails on the pre-fix config:

```console
$ go test ./kairos-init/pkg/bundled/...   # with /usr/libexec restored
[FAILED] /usr/libexec is image content, persisting it breaks rollback
FAIL! -- 50 Passed | 2 Failed

$ go test ./kairos-init/...               # with the fix
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/bundled
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/kernel
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/stages
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/system
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/validation
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/pkg/values
```

The prefix check is `/usr/lib` and not `/usr` because `/usr/local` is the
persistent partition itself, mounted as a volume rather than bind-mounted out
of one.

No boot test: reproducing the reported failure needs two images built against
different glibc versions and a rollback between them, which is beyond what a
config-list change warrants. The end-to-end effect is that immucore stops
emitting one fstab bind entry.


## Behaviour change worth stating

`RW_PATHS` is `/var /etc /srv` and the only writable `/usr` path is the
`/usr/local` volume, so dropping `/usr/libexec` from `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS`
also makes it read-only after boot rather than merely non-persistent. That is
intended: it is image content. Nothing in the repo writes there, and the
Kubernetes flexvolume directory that would (`volume-plugin-dir`,
`kubelet-plugins`) is not referenced anywhere in tree. The entry itself has no
recorded rationale - it arrived wholesale in kairos-init `f43bd71`, inherited
from the old layout list.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**

Fixes #4304
title: fix(kairos-init): stop persisting /usr/libexec across slots

author: jimmykarily
body:
Two small, unrelated bugs surfaced during QA of #4502 (the boringcrypto to Go
native FIPS 140-3 migration). Neither is caused by that work; both are
long-standing. Fixing them here so they stop biting.

1. `images/Dockerfile` used bash's `==` inside a `RUN` line, but Docker's `RUN`
   shell is `/bin/sh`, which is `dash` on Debian and Ubuntu bases. The test
   errored out and fell through to the "not FIPS" branch, so
   `docker build --build-arg FIPS=fips` on a Debian-family base silently
   produced a non-FIPS image while still publishing it under the FIPS name.
   POSIX `=` works in both shells.
2. `kairos-init validate` was checking that the initrd contained a
   `kairos-agent` binary. It doesn't, and shouldn't: `kairos-agent` runs
   after switch-root in normal userland, not from initramfs. Only immucore
   runs from the initrd. Dropped the bogus assertion so the validator stops
   reporting a failure on every built image.

Refs kairos-io/kairos#4502
title: fix: two bugs found during #4502 FIPS QA (Debian build-arg, initrd validate)

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #2958.

## What was broken

The agent's own console runs every stage command as `sh -c <command>` (`agent/pkg/cloudinit/console.go:44`), so the shebang only ever mattered in one of the two shapes a command can take:

- `commands: [/path/to/script.sh]` pointing at an executable script. Fine. `sh` forks and execve's the path, and the kernel reads the shebang.
- an inline block whose text starts with `#!`. Broken. The text goes to `sh -c`, which reads the shebang as a comment and runs the body itself.

The second shape is quiet, which is the worst part. With a non-bash `/bin/sh`, bash-only syntax is dropped, yip exits 0, and the stage reports as done:

```yaml
stages:
  test:
    - name: "inline bash script"
      commands:
        - |
          #!/bin/bash
          if [[ "foo" == "foo" ]]; then echo ok > /tmp/marker.txt; fi
```

`/tmp/marker.txt` is never written and nothing says so.

@mauromorales suspected on the issue that this came from the console differing per distribution. It does not. yip's `StandardConsole` and the agent's `cloudInitConsole` both use `sh -c`, so they behave identically; what varies is only whether a given distribution's `/bin/sh` happens to be bash, which hides the bug rather than causing it.

## What this changes

Only the pin. mudler/yip#333 fixed this **above** the `Console` interface, in the `commands` plugin: a command starting with `#!` is written to a private 0700 file and run by path, so the kernel reads the first line and starts the interpreter the author named. Commands without a shebang go through untouched.

Because the fix sits above the interface, the agent's own console inherits it with no code change. That is the whole reason this PR is a bump plus specs and not a second implementation of the same logic in `agent/pkg/cloudinit`.

## The pin is a pseudo-version, and why

`v1.26.1-0.20260902132557-8b1bbf1c6b6e`. yip's latest release is `v1.26.0`, tagged 2026-08-26, a week before #333 merged on 2026-09-02.

The saving grace is that yip `master` is `v1.26.0` **plus that one commit** and nothing else:

```
$ gh api /repos/mudler/yip/compare/v1.26.0...master --jq '.ahead_by'
1
```

So the pin drags in exactly the fix, no collateral. @mudler if you would rather this land on a tag, cut a yip release and I will repoint the pin at it; the diff will be otherwise identical.

## Verification

`CGO_ENABLED=0`, against `master` (`d17464a2`) as the baseline and against this branch.

The new specs are a real red/green, not a green-only guard. On the old pin, three of them fail:

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./agent/pkg/cloudinit/...
Summarizing 3 Failures:
  [FAIL] ... [It] is a path to the script, not the script itself
  [FAIL] ... [It] is read by the interpreter the shebang names
  [FAIL] ... [It] keeps bash-only syntax working, which is what #2958 reported
Ran 21 of 21 Specs
FAIL! -- 18 Passed | 3 Failed
```

The third one fails with the reported shape of the bug, from the real console:

```
failed to run #!/bin/bash
words=(one two three)
printf '%s' "${words[1]}" > /tmp/.../marker
: exit status 2
command output:
sh: syntax error: unexpected "("
```

With the bump, `ok github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/pkg/cloudinit`.

Two of the specs are hermetic (FakeRunner: assert the console is handed a path, and that a command *without* a shebang is still passed verbatim). Three run for real through `RealRunner`, so bash actually interprets the script; one of them asserts the temp script is cleaned up afterwards.

No regressions anywhere else. I ran `go build ./...` and the full `./agent/... ./immucore/... ./sdk/... ./installer/...` suite in both trees and diffed:

- byte-identical results apart from timings
- same 3 pre-existing failures in both (`agent/pkg/action`, `agent/pkg/utils`, `sdk/sysext`), which are local-environment gaps on my box, not this change
- same pre-existing `kairos-init/pkg/bundled` embed build error in both (`pattern binaries/edgevpn: no matching files found`, the binaries are fetched by `make`)

One thing to flag in `go.sum`: `go mod tidy` also pruned two stale `go-containerregistry v0.22.0` lines. That is pre-existing untidiness left by #4500, which bumped the module to v0.22.1 in `go.mod` without tidying `go.sum`. Unrelated to the bump but I did not want to hand-edit `go.sum` to hide it.

## Note on the docs

kairos-io/kairos-docs#289 documents the explicit `bash /path/to/script.sh` form. That stays correct and worth keeping; this makes the inline shebang form work as written rather than replacing the documented option.
title: test(cloudinit): cover a shebang at the start of a stage command

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #2149

Round 2, after @Itxaka asked for a generic service object rather than the narrow fix: `sdk/machine/openrc` and `sdk/machine/systemd` are gone, and every caller that used to branch on the init system now states what the service is instead.

## The new shape

`sdk/machine/service` holds four things:

- **`Spec`** describes a service in the terms every init system shares: a name, an optional instance, a root to write under, and a `NoReload`. The parts that genuinely differ live in `Spec.Init`, keyed by flavor, so nothing outside a spec ever names an init system.
- **`Service`** is the whole of what an init system can do with a service: `Name`, `WriteUnit`, `OverrideCmd`, `EnvFile`, `SetEnv`, `Start`, `StartBlocking`, `Stop`, `Restart`, `Enable`, `Disable`. Where an init system cannot express one, the backend returns an error rather than reporting success for something that did not happen.
- **`Backend`** builds services for one init system. `systemd` and `openrc` are two files of about 100 lines each. Supporting runit or s6 is a third file and a `Register` call, with no caller touched.
- **`Noop`** implements `Service` by doing nothing, to embed when only part of the interface means anything. The openrc getty stand-in is three lines because of it.

```go
svc, err := service.New(service.Spec{
	Name: "k0scontroller",
	Init: map[service.Flavor]service.InitSpec{
		service.OpenRC:  {Unit: K0sControllerOpenrc, EnvFile: "/etc/k0s/k0scontroller.env"},
		service.Systemd: {Unit: K0sControllerSystemd},
	},
})
```

`service.EnvFilePlaceholder` in a unit body is substituted with the resolved env file when the unit is written, which is the generic version of round 0's finding 1: a unit that sources its env file cannot drift from whatever writes to it, because neither side spells the path out.

## What that deletes

| Gone | Now |
|---|---|
| `machine.K3s()`, `K3sAgent()`, `K0s()`, `K0sWorker()` | `service.New(services.K3sSpec(name))` |
| `machine.K3sEnvUnit()`, `machine.K0sEnvUnit()` | `services.K3sSpec` / `K0sSpec`, next to the unit bodies |
| `sdk/machine/openrc`, `sdk/machine/systemd` | `sdk/machine/service` |
| the `if utils.IsOpenRCBased()` pair in 6 call sites | one `Spec` each |
| `K0sServices`' two 25-line branches | a loop over `K0sServiceNames` |

Net 204 insertions against 647 deletions. `machine.Service` stays as an alias of `service.Service`, so callers holding the interface keep compiling.

Knowledge moves to whoever owns it. That k3s reads `/etc/rancher/k3s/<unit>.env` and k0s reads `/etc/k0s/<unit>.env` is a fact about k3s and k0s, so it now sits in `provider/internal/services` beside their unit bodies. The SDK keeps only what is true of any service: that systemd units live in `/etc/systemd/system` and take a drop-in, that openrc scripts live in `/etc/init.d` and take `command_args`, and that `/etc/sysconfig/<name>` is the systemd convention for an env file.

`bootstrap.go` shows the effect. It used to resolve the env file, write it, then build a service in a branch and check for `nil` to mean "could not detect OS". Now:

```go
svc, err := node.Service()
...
if err := svc.SetEnv(svcEnv); err != nil {
```

## Two bugs fixed on the way

- `WriteUnit` refuses an empty unit body. k3s packages its own openrc script and systemd unit, so a spec that carries no body for it would previously have truncated the packaged file and left the service unable to start.
- The systemd drop-in directory was created `0600`. systemd cannot traverse a directory it cannot execute, so `override.conf` was unreadable. It is `0700` now.

## Deliberately left alone

`machine.Getty(i)` on openrc ignores `i` and runs `chvt 2`, which is what it did before. It looks wrong next to the systemd side, which starts `getty@tty<i>`, but changing which console Kairos switches to is a behaviour change that wants its own PR and a reason. There is a comment saying so.

## Verification

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./sdk/machine/... ./provider/...
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/sdk/machine	0.006s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/sdk/machine/service	0.004s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/provider/internal/cli	0.245s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/provider/internal/provider	0.019s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/provider/internal/role/p2p	15.024s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/provider/internal/services	0.003s
```

Every test from `sdk/machine/openrc/unit_test.go` is carried over. On top of them:

- `provider/internal/services/k3s_test.go` pins all eight service/init env file paths (`k3s`, `k3s-agent`, `k0scontroller`, `k0sworker` on openrc and systemd) against what `machine.K3sEnvUnit`/`K0sEnvUnit` returned. Getting one wrong means the provider writes the token and arguments to a file the service never reads, and the node comes up with the defaults and no error anywhere, so it is worth a test that fails instead.
- `TestK0sSpecUnitSourcesItsOwnEnvFile` writes the real unit into a temp root, reads it back, and asserts the path it sources is the one `OverrideCmd` then writes to. That is the round-0 drift finding, as a test.
- `TestEveryBackendWritesTheUnitItIsGiven`, `TestEveryBackendSetsEnv` and `TestEnvFileIsNotPrefixedWithRoot` run over `Flavors()`, so a new backend is covered by them the moment it registers.
- `TestRegisterAddsABackend` registers a fake `runit` backend and builds a service from it, which is the "generic for any system underlying" claim as a test rather than as a paragraph.

I mutation-checked the three guards this PR rests on, rather than trusting a green run: breaking the placeholder substitution fails `TestOpenRCWriteUnit` and `TestK0sSpecUnitSourcesItsOwnEnvFile`, removing the empty-unit guard fails `TestWriteUnitRefusesAnEmptyUnit`, and removing openrc's env-file requirement fails `TestOpenRCOverrideCmdWithoutEnvFile`. The last one passed at first for the wrong reason (writing to the temp root errors anyway), so it now asserts the error text.

**Not verified:** no Alpine + k0s node was booted, so the end-to-end openrc bootstrap is still unproven. Everything above is unit level. `golangci-lint` is not available on this box either.

<details>
<summary>Round 1 description, for the narrow fix that is now the first two commits</summary>

`openrc.ServiceUnit.OverrideCmd` carried the k3s-specific `TODO` from 2024: it looked up `utils.K3sBin()` and wrote to `/etc/rancher/k3s/<name>.env`, so on an openrc host running k0s it either aborted with `no k3s binary found (?)` or wrote `command_args` to a file the k0s unit does not read. The fix strips the leading binary from the command the caller already resolved, adds an env file to the service, and makes the k0s openrc scripts source it. Both commits are still in this PR; the refactor generalizes them rather than replacing them.

</details>
title: refactor(machine): make services generic over the init system
