author: riccardomenegazzo
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Concurrent bundle E2E jobs currently overwrite the same mutable Quay tag, so a VM can install another run's bundle. This change pushes to GHCR using caller-scoped tags and passes the immutable build digest to the test.

- Push to `ghcr.io/kairos-io/kairos/bundles-test`, with `pr-<number>` and `master-scratch` tags.
- Authenticate with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and remove the reusable workflow's Quay secrets.
- Define the bundle repository once, use it for both push and digest export, and validate the tag and build digest.
- Require `BUNDLE_IMAGE` explicitly. There is no legacy tag fallback.
- Render the datasource from exactly one placeholder and check that the selected image appears once in the installed config.
- Register cleanup after each resource is created, so missing input does not trigger cleanup against an uninitialized VM.

Rebased onto `b2c341f9`. The obsolete release workflow change is dropped: upstream removed those QEMU jobs. Existing upstream timeout and workflow changes are preserved.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #4310

**Rollout and accepted tradeoffs**

- This PR's `pull_request_target` run uses the base-branch reusable workflow, which does not export `BUNDLE_IMAGE`. The bundles cell is therefore expected to fail with the explicit missing-input assertion before merge. [Jimmy confirmed this is acceptable](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/pull/4451#discussion_r3949468491). After merge, callers supply the digest through the updated workflow.
- Before the first updated bundles run can succeed, a maintainer must ensure the new `kairos/bundles-test` GHCR package is **public** and linked to this repository with Actions write access. Seed the package if necessary, set its visibility to public, and verify an anonymous pull of its digest. The VM has no registry credentials. Package visibility has not been verified from this environment.
- GHCR has no Quay-style `expires-after` label. Package retention is deliberately outside this PR, matching the existing CI packages. [Jimmy explicitly accepted this tradeoff](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/pull/4451#discussion_r3931310085); this change does not implement automatic expiry.

**Validation**

On the revised files:
- `git diff --check` and `gofmt`: clean.
- Parsed the workflow YAML and rendered bundle datasource.
- Executed the actual Bash tag/digest validators with valid, empty, malformed, and length-boundary inputs; verified the exact exported digest reference.
- Checked caller tags and package permissions, the single repository definition, removal of Quay fallback/secrets, and cleanup registration order.

Docker and KVM are unavailable here, so the revised Go E2E suite has not been compiled or run locally. The earlier [independent QA run](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/pull/4451#issuecomment-5614116453) passed the digest-pinned bundle test on the previous revision; it is not a run of this new commit.

The previous CI revision passed its bundles cell, unit tests, and lint. Its two failed jobs were `encryption-remote-auto` (cert-manager deployments did not become Available) and `provider-qrcode-install` (suite timeout while waiting in node pairing). Neither log implicates bundle image selection; their status must be reassessed on the rebased run.
title: :robot: Isolate bundle E2E images on GHCR

author: mauro-agent
body:
OpenSSF Scorecard's Token-Permissions check flags `master.yaml`, `release.yaml` and `pr.yaml` for granting `contents`/`packages`/`id-token`/`security-events` write at the top level.

Every job in these three files either calls a local reusable workflow (which already declares its own, narrower `permissions:` block: GitHub intersects caller and callee permissions, so the callee already caps the effective token regardless of the caller's grant) or runs privileged inline steps directly (`promote-images`' docker push, or jobs like `authorize` and the k3s/k0s version lookups that use `GITHUB_TOKEN` for nothing at all). The broad top-level grant was therefore already unused by most jobs, just undeclared as such.

Narrowed each workflow's top-level `permissions:` to `contents: read`, and added an explicit job-level `permissions:` block wherever a job needs more, matching exactly what its reusable callee (or inline step) already requires. This does not change what any job's token can actually do at runtime; it only makes each job's real requirement visible in the declaration, which is what Scorecard's static check inspects.

Verified: all three files parse as valid YAML, and every added job-level block was cross-checked against the exact `permissions:` the called reusable workflow (or inline step) already declares, so no job loses access it currently uses.

Draft, per this project's kairos-io write process. Awaiting review before moving out of draft.
title: fix(ci): scope master/release/pr workflow permissions per job

author: ci-robbot
body:
PR 2 of the split in kairos-io/kairos#4340. PR 1 was #4568 (branding into the sdk) and the guard fixes were #4570, both merged.

## Why

The live CD ships two install frontends as two services: `kairos-webui.service` serves the web UI out of the agent, the installer binary serves the terminal UI. Folding interactive into the default boot entry (#4340) puts both on one boot, and they cannot stay two processes competing for `:8080`.

## What

`agent/internal/webui` -> `installer/internal/webui`, served by the installer binary alongside the TUI. `--no-tui` serves only the web UI.

`kairos-agent webui` now delegates to the resolved installer with `--no-tui`, exactly the way `interactive-install` already delegates. That deviates from my spec, which said to drop the subcommand: delegating keeps the web installer inside the swappable-installer contract, so an image shipping its own installer serves its own web UI, and it leaves the unit file, the openrc script and `logs.go`'s journal list untouched. `--no-tui` is documented in `installer/README.md` as part of the drop-in contract.

Three things the move needed:

- `installer/` imports nothing from `agent/` today, deliberately. `DefaultWebUIListenAddress` moves to `sdk/constants`, next to the installer contract, where the agent's live-console message reads it too.
- **echo's default logger writes JSON to stdout**, banner and port included, and that would land on top of the TUI's alt screen. The logger is injectable now; the installer points it at `/var/log/kairos/webui.log`, the path the openrc unit already uses, and falls back to `io.Discard` rather than stdout when that file cannot be opened.
- the `/install` handler called `log.Fatalf` on a tempfile error. In-process that would take the TUI down with it, so it renders the error to the browser instead.

## The one boot-wiring change

The `boot` stage in `52_installer.yaml` no longer enables `kairos-webui` on an interactive boot, where the installer serves the web UI in-process. Its negative match mirrors the interactive stage's guard term for term (plain substring, both keywords), so no cmdline can satisfy both. Non-interactive and keyword-free live boots are unaffected.

## Verification

- Built the installer and ran `--no-tui`: `GET /` returns 200 with `<title>WebUI System Installer</title>`, `POST /validate` returns the schema error for a bad cloud-config, and echo's banner goes to stdout for the journal.
- Ran it in default (TUI) mode with no tty: the web UI still answers 200 on `:8080`, and **nothing** from echo reaches stdout or stderr, only bubbletea's own "could not open a new TTY". That is the property that matters, verified rather than assumed.
- New guard spec pins "the boot stage refuses every cmdline the interactive stage claims". Mutation-checked: restoring the old `live_mode`-only guard fails it.
- New spec pins `kairos-agent webui` passing `--no-tui`. Mutation-checked: dropping the flag fails it.
- `installer/main_test.go` covers both logger branches, file and fallback.
- `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues) and the specs for `./installer/...`, `./agent/internal/agent/...` and `./kairos-init/pkg/validation/...` are green.

Not verified here: a real live boot. The one behaviour I could not exercise locally is systemd actually skipping the unit on an interactive entry; that is asserted at the guard level only.

## Not in this PR

Pointing the web UI at `sdk/agentrun` for typed progress over the websocket, so the ANSI-to-HTML converter and the log tailing go away. That is PR 3 of the split and is a bigger behaviour change than a move.

Also note #4550 (the MCP server) is still open. When it lands, its `mcp.Handler()` becomes one more route on this server rather than a second listener.
title: feat(installer): serve the web UI from the installer, one process per boot

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override
> any action taken here.

Adds `install.oem_files`, a cloud-config key that drops named cloud-config
files into the OEM partition during install so they are applied on the
installed system's first boot.

```yaml
install:
  oem_files:
    - name: foo
      content: |
        #cloud-config
        ...
```

Follows the shape ci-robbot's triage comment sketched on the issue: a shared
`mountOEM`/`writeCloudConfig` helper factored out of the three places that
were each hand-rolling this (`mounts.go`, `ssh_hardening.go`,
`phonehome/config.go` is untouched, the other two now share the helper), and
a new `OEMFiles` hook that runs first in `Finish.Run`, ahead of `Encrypt`, so
an `encrypted_partitions: [oem]` install still backs the files up.

Went through two review rounds after the initial draft. The first cut
resolved the OEM directory by mounting `COS_OEM` itself and fell back to
`/usr/local/cloud-config`/`/etc/kairos` on the *running installer's*
filesystem when that mount failed -- those files were silently discarded on
reboot, and `/etc/kairos` was never a yip stage source in the first place.
The install pipeline already mounts OEM before `PostInstall` runs and aborts
the whole install if it can't, so the fix drops the fallback entirely:
`OEMFiles` now reads the mountpoint off the install spec it was already
being handed, writes through the installer's own filesystem abstraction, and
fails the install loudly if OEM isn't mounted instead of writing somewhere
that disappears on reboot.

Known non-blocking nits (not addressed in this PR, flagged by review):

- The schema description says the file name goes in "without the yaml
  extension"; the actual rule (and the docs) allow `.yaml`/`.yml` to pass
  through unchanged -- the description is just narrower than the code.
- `oemFileName` gets called twice in `OEMFiles.Run`, making the second
  error check unreachable.
- Two entries resolving to the same file name (e.g. `foo` and `foo.yaml`)
  silently let the later one win.

Fixes: #149
title: feat(agent): install.oem_files to drop cloud-config files into the OEM partition

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes the live half of #1378.

## What changed

The immucore dracut unit generated by kairos-init declared `Requires=systemd-udev-settle.service`. It now declares `Wants=`, keeping the `After=` ordering.

## Why

`systemd-udev-settle.service` is deprecated upstream. systemd 261.2, which Hadron ships, still installs it, so nothing is broken today. Two things make `Requires=` a hazard anyway:

1. **dracut installs it optionally.** Both forks list it under `inst_multiple -o` in their systemd-udevd module ([dracut-ng `modules.d/11systemd-udevd/module-setup.sh:49`](https://github.com/dracut-ng/dracut-ng/blob/main/modules.d/11systemd-udevd/module-setup.sh#L49), same in dracutdevs `01systemd-udevd`), and `-o` skips silently when the file is not on the host. Nothing else pulls the unit in either: dracut links only `systemd-udevd.service` and `systemd-udev-trigger.service` into `sysinit.target.wants`, so immucore's `Requires=` is the sole reason it runs. When systemd drops the unit, or a distro strips it, `Requires=` on a unit that is not in the initramfs makes `immucore.service` fail to load. Nothing builds the mount layout and the image does not boot, from a dependency change rather than from anything in this repo.
2. **The unit carries `TimeoutSec=180`.** Under `Requires=`, a host whose udev does not settle spends three minutes waiting and then does not run immucore at all. That is exactly the state `immucore/internal/utils/bootfailure.go:116-124` exists to report.

`Wants=` behaves identically in every case where the unit is present and succeeds, and turns both of those into "immucore runs anyway".

## What this does not do

It does not remove the dependency, which is what #1378 ultimately asks for. The settle ordering is still load-bearing: `resolveMountSource` ([`immucore/pkg/state/steps_shared.go:282-293`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/immucore/pkg/state/steps_shared.go#L282-L293)) calls `lookup.MountSourceForLabel` exactly once, and `MountCustomMountsDagStep` treats a failed lookup as a mount failure. The 30s retry in `MountOPWithFstab` only covers the mount syscall, which is reached after resolution already succeeded. So immucore has to learn to wait for its own labelled devices before `After=systemd-udev-settle.service` can go.

I left that out on purpose. It changes what happens on every boot, it needs a decision on how to treat labels that are legitimately allowed to be absent (`MountCustomMountsDagStep` already tolerates a missing `COS_OEM`, so a naive retry loop burns its whole timeout on boots without one), and it wants a QEMU boot test across flavours. Options are laid out in [my comment on the issue](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/1378#issuecomment-5510070162).

## Verification

- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./kairos-init/pkg/bundled/` passes, 51 specs.
- Two new specs in the existing `immucore_service_test.go`, both checked to be load-bearing:
  - restoring `Requires=systemd-udev-settle.service` fails `only wants the deprecated udev settle unit`;
  - deleting the `After=systemd-udev-settle.service` line fails `still orders itself after the udev settle unit`.
- `go vet ./kairos-init/pkg/bundled/`, `gofmt -l` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: all clean. (`immucore/internal/utils/cloudinit_test.go` is unformatted on `master` already and is not touched here.)
- Grepped the tree: no other reference to `Requires=systemd-udev-settle` remains, and the `udevadm settle` calls in `sdk/kcrypt/lock.go`, `agent/pkg/uki/reset.go` and `immucore/pkg/state/steps_uki.go` are direct invocations, unaffected by this.

`immucore/README.md` documented the old ordering and now notes that the unit is only wanted.

Not boot-tested. The change is a one-word dependency relaxation whose effect is nil whenever the settle unit works, so I did not think an ISO build was warranted; say so if you would rather see one.
title: fix(kairos-init): want, not require, systemd-udev-settle

author: thebhdn
body:
Ladies and gentlemen,

Potentially closes https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/114

This PR brings(I hope) selinux back to the menu.

Brief summary:

- Generate `file_contexts.subs` from kairos `/usr/local/.state/*` bind mounts, so persistent backing paths are labeled according to their logical destinations.
- Create `.subs` explicitly as `file_context_t`, since SELinux needs that file itself to be correctly labeled before it can use the substitutions.
- Run `load_policy -i` before `restorecon` cuz at that initramfs stage SELinux may be enabled by the kernel command line, but the policy is still not loaded yet. In that state getenforce reports Disabled, and policy-based relabeling cannot work correctly. `load_policy -i` activates the installed SELinux policy so restorecon can resolve and apply the expected contexts.
- Keep early boot permissive with `selinux=1 enforcing=0` so policy can be loaded and the filesystem relabeled safely before enforcement starts.
- Run a final relabel after Kairos finishes creating late files, then `setenforce 1` if user enabled it.

Configration:

```yaml
install:
  selinux:
    enabled: true # false
    mode: enforcing # permissive
```

By default selinux is disabled, and permissive is the default mode. Tested on Rocky & leap distros.
title: feat: selinux support (non-uki)

author: ci-robbot
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A node whose `config_url` is unreachable boots exactly like a node that never had one. `fetchRemoteConfig` retries three times and then returns an empty config with a nil error, and does the same when the remote file has no valid `#cloud-config` header. Neither path prints anything, on the console or in the journal. The only symptom the user sees is that none of their configuration applied, and finding out why takes `rd.shell`.

Both paths now print a warning. The local-file paths in the same collector already warn for the same class of problem (`warning: skipping %s because it has no valid header`), so the wording follows them.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- The warning goes to **stderr**, not stdout. The kcrypt discovery plugin speaks JSON over stdout and passes `NoLogs: true` to the collector for exactly that reason. Writing to stderr means the warning cannot corrupt that protocol, and it needs no change to the exported `MergeConfigURL` signature to thread a `nologs` flag through.
- The URL is printed with its **query string redacted**. A templated `config_url` can carry a token or a machine identifier, and the console and journal are the wrong place for those.

`retry.Attempts(3)` became a named `configURLAttempts` const so the count in the message cannot drift from the count in the loop.

**How to verify**:

```sh
go test ./sdk/collector/ -args -ginkgo.focus="cannot be used"
```

Three new specs: fetch failure warns and boot continues, missing header warns, and a `?token=supersecret` query never reaches the warning.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Refs #923

This is the first half of that issue. The second half, routing warnings like this one to the boot messages instead of `journalctl`, was always scoped separately and is not addressed here. Leaving #923 open for it.
title: fix(config): warn when a config_url cannot be used

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override any
> action taken here.

Fixes: #835

## What

Some Kairos targets never got the `systemd-resolved` dracut module added to their initramfs, so DNS never resolved that early in boot — the "no DNS at initramfs stage" half of #835 (the other half, the `dns:` cloud-config stage on `systemd-resolved` hosts, lives in `mudler/yip` and is out of scope here; see the takeover comment on the issue).

`kairos-init/pkg/stages/steps_init.go` now adds `systemd-resolved` to the dracut network-module list wherever `systemd-networkd` drives the initramfs and the module is actually available on the build root (both the `systemd-resolved` daemon binary and `resolvectl` present, matching what the module's own `check()` requires). This closes the gap for Ubuntu 21.04–22.04*, Debian, and openSUSE/SLES.

\* **Ubuntu 22.04 is not fixed by this PR.** Its packaged dracut (051, across every jammy suite) predates the upstream `systemd-resolved` dracut module, which only landed at dracut 054. No installable package closes this gap today; that's documented in a code comment rather than silently left as a mystery or forced (forcing an unavailable module makes dracut abort the whole image build — see below).

Also fixed along the way: the module-availability probe originally checked only the `systemd-resolved` daemon binary. The module's own `check()` requires `resolvectl` too, and dracut hard-aborts the entire image build (no initramfs produced) when a module forced via `add_dracutmodules` fails its `check()`. Left unchanged, on a root with the daemon but not `resolvectl`, this fix would have turned "missing DNS" into "build fails outright" — worse than the original bug. The probe now checks both binaries.

The RedHat family (outside Fedora-with-networkd) and Ubuntu ≤20.04 are deliberately left alone: their dracut modules (`network-manager`, `network`/`network-legacy`) already write `/etc/resolv.conf` themselves, so they already have working DNS in the initramfs.

## Verification

Unit tests cover the module-selection logic (table-driven, `kairos-init/pkg/stages/steps_init_test.go`) against both fabricated build roots and facts confirmed against real, published Kairos container images (`quay.io/kairos/core-*`) and the real Ubuntu package archive for the jammy-dracut-version claim. No ISO was built and no VM was booted for this ticket — the change is internal to kairos-init's build-time dracut module selection, with no existing isolated repro short of the full image-build pipeline.

Full round-by-round audit trail (what each review round found, and how each finding was resolved or empirically verified): https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/835#issuecomment-5632796718
title: fix(kairos-init): add systemd-resolved to more distros' initramfs, safely

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4567.

## Root cause

The spec is not racy or order dependent. It calls out to Docker Hub.

`"Reads properly the cloud config for upgrade"` builds its config with a real
`config.ScanNoLogs`, so the config carries the real `OCIImageExtractor`. The
spec then overrides `Runner`, `Fs`, `Mounter`, `CloudInitRunner` and `Logger`,
but never `ImageExtractor`. The fixture sets:

```yaml
upgrade:
  recovery: true
  recovery-system:
    source: oci:busybox
```

and `NewUpgradeSpec` -> `setUpgradeSourceSize` -> `GetSourceSize` takes the
`source.IsDocker()` branch, which calls `GetOCIImageSize` and resolves the
manifest against `index.docker.io`. Any registry failure fails the spec as
`failed calculating size`. Anonymous Docker Hub pulls are rate limited per IP
over a time window, which is why the failures cluster into batches instead of
scattering evenly.

## Evidence

Point the process at a dead proxy and exactly one spec in the suite of 197
breaks, the reported one:

```
[FAILED] Unexpected error:
    failed initializing spec: failed calculating size: Get "https://index.docker.io/v2/":
    proxyconnect tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
occurred
In [It] at: agent/pkg/config/spec_test.go:862
```

| suite run | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| registry reachable | 192 passed | 192 passed |
| registry unreachable | 191 passed, **1 failed** | 192 passed |

Focused spec duration also drops from 1.4s to 0.011s, since the round trip is
gone even on the happy path.

## The change

Test only, no production code.

The whole `Config from cloudconfig` block repeated the same five override
lines in every spec, so it becomes one `useTestDoubles` helper that also
injects a `FakeImageExtractor`. A spec added to that block later cannot reach
a registry by accident.

The mock is not just a stub. `recovery-system.source` becomes a value distinct
from `system.source`, and the spec now asserts that a recovery upgrade sizes
the recovery source, which was untested. Deleting the injection does not
silently restore the network call, it fails to compile.

## Verification

`CGO_ENABLED=0`, no C compiler on this machine, so `-race` was not run.

- 40 focused runs: 0 failures
- 10 full suite runs: 0 failures
- full suite with the registry unreachable, two ways (refused connection and a
  blackholed address): 192 passed, 0 failed both times
title: test(config): stop the upgrade cloud-config spec calling docker.io

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4603.

`GetURL` left `grab.Request.NoResume` at its zero value, so grab treated an existing destination as a partially completed download of the same URL. Nothing in this path checksums anything, so an unrelated leftover file decided the result:

| Local file vs remote | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| shorter | `Range: bytes=<localsize>-`, appends, returns `nil` | full re-download |
| longer | `bad content length`, every retry fails the same way | full re-download |
| same size | keeps the stale file, returns `nil` | full re-download |

The first row is the one that matters. `InstallExtension` downloads into the persistent `/var/lib/kairos/extensions` under a name taken from the URI, so re-installing a sysext whose remote artifact had grown wrote `old bytes 0..N` + `new bytes N..end` and exited 0. The `file://` and `oci://` sources in the same interface already overwrite (`sysext.go:470` opens with `O_TRUNC`), so `https://` was the only one that behaved this way.

## Verification

Four specs in `agent/pkg/implementations/http`, all against `httptest` with `http.ServeContent` so Range requests are honoured the way a real artifact host does. No network.

Against master the corruption is explicit:

```
Expected
    <string>: OLD-CONTENT-THAT-IS-LONGER-THAN-THE-OLD-ONE
to equal
    <string>: NEW-CONTENT-THAT-IS-LONGER-THAN-THE-OLD-ONE
```

The first 11 bytes are the stale file and the rest is the remote body. `GetURL` returned `nil`.

Mutating the one added line back to `false` fails all four (`0 Passed | 4 Failed`); with it, `4 Passed`. The full `http` suite passes including the two pre-existing specs that download from github.com. `go build ./agent/...` and `go vet` are clean. `agent/pkg/utils` is 190 passed / 5 failed, and the five are the `SyncData` specs that need `rsync`, which is not installed on this box.

## The trade

`NoResume = true` means a genuinely interrupted large download restarts instead of resuming. That is the right way round while nothing validates the resumed bytes: there is no checksum, no ETag and no `If-Range` here. If resume is wanted back later it needs one of those first.

I first wrote this as "delete the destination, then download", but mutation testing showed the deletion was dead code once `NoResume` was set, including for a directory destination, so it is gone.
title: fix(agent): do not resume an HTTP download onto an existing file

author: ci-robbot
body:
Closes #1799

## What

`kairos-agent upgrade` never touched the EFI partition, so a signed-shim
rotation, a `grub.cfg` schema change or a grub CVE bump only reached
installed nodes if the operator ran a reinstall. `Grub.Install` runs
from install and reset only. UKI upgrades already refresh the ESP
through `agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go`.

This wires the ESP-copy tail of `Grub.Install` into the GRUB upgrade
path, gated on an ESP that has room to fit the new bytes.

## How

- `copyShim`, `copyGrub` and `writeEfiGrubCfg` in `agent/pkg/utils/grub.go`
  move from constant paths to `(sourceDir, efiDir)` parameters. `Install`
  keeps its behaviour by passing `cnst.ActiveDir` and `cnst.EfiDir`.
- A new `Grub.RefreshESP(sourceDir, efiDir, stateLabel, systemgrub)`
  method runs the shim + grub + `EFI/boot/grub.cfg` copy sequence, so the
  upgrade path can call the same write path `Install` uses without
  running `grub2-install` again.
- `CheckESPRefreshSpace` in `agent/pkg/utils/grub_esp_space.go` sizes the
  shim and grub bytes the refresh will write and compares that against
  the free space plus the bytes the current shim and grub at the target
  give back on rewrite. That handles both the first-ever refresh (no
  existing files, `needed` compared against raw `Bavail`) and the
  common signed-shim rotation (same-sized replacement always fits).
- `UpgradeAction.refreshESP` in `agent/pkg/action/upgrade.go` mounts the
  ESP RW between the after-upgrade-chroot hook and `UnmountImage`, so
  the source image is still mounted at `upgradeImg.MountPoint`. Failure
  modes are graded:
  - No EFI partition (BIOS GRUB): skip cleanly.
  - Mount fails: warn and skip. A machine whose ESP has gone unhappy
    still gets its active image swap. Matches the rebranding step
    above.
  - Space check fails: warn and skip, since a partial write would leave
    the ESP inconsistent.
  - Write starts and fails: return the error, since that indicates a
    real regression worth surfacing.

## Test plan

- [x] `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./agent/pkg/utils/ -run TestWhitebox`
  passes the 6 new `CheckESPRefreshSpace` specs. The 5 pre-existing
  SyncData failures are the local `rsync` gap, not this change.
- [x] `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./agent/pkg/action/ -run TestActionSuite`
  passes all 211 upgrade specs. The 1 pre-existing `render_template`
  failure was there before this change.
- [x] `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./agent/... ./sdk/... ./immucore/...`
  clean.
- [ ] Real-hardware upgrade on a GRUB EFI system: confirm the ESP
  `shim.efi` / `grub.efi` / `EFI/boot/grub.cfg` timestamps advance
  after an `upgrade` run.
- [ ] Real-hardware upgrade on a BIOS GRUB system: confirm the upgrade
  completes and logs the "No EFI partition on this machine, skipping
  ESP refresh" debug line.
title: fix(upgrade): refresh the shim, grub and grub.cfg on the ESP

author: ci-robbot
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**

Fixes the two TODOs #2267 was filed for:

- [`agent/pkg/uki/install.go#L112`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/c80ae704/agent/pkg/uki/install.go#L112) - "Check if the size of the files we are going to copy, will fit in the partition. If not stop here."
- [`agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go#L49`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/c80ae704/agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go#L49) - "Get the size of the efi partition and decide if the images can fit before trying the upgrade."

**The problem**

Both UKI paths write the artifact set more than once, and neither counted the copies.

Install dumps the source as the `norole` set and then copies that set into `active`, `passive`, `recovery` and `statereset`, so the peak is five sets and four persist. `NewUkiInstallSpec` sizes the EFI partition at `max(15GiB, 3 * source)`, which is both a different multiplier and only a default: `unmarshallFullSpec` runs after it and lets a cloud-config override the size, and a `no-format` install reuses whatever partition is already there. Nothing verified the result.

Upgrade dumps the new set, copies `active` over `passive`, then copies the new set over `active`. `NewUkiUpgradeSpec` does compare the source size against the EFI free space, but only at one copy, which is less than the rotation needs.

The upgrade case is the one that hurts. `overwriteArtifactSetRole` deletes the target role before it copies anything into it, so the order is: delete `passive`, copy `active` over it, delete `active`, copy the new set over that. A copy that runs out of room part way has already destroyed both entries the machine could have booted.

**The fix**

New `agent/pkg/uki/space.go`. The sizes are only exact once the set is on disk, so each check runs after the dump and before the first copy, and measures the same files `copyArtifactSetRole` copies and `removeArtifactSetWithRole` deletes.

- Install needs `len(roles) * norole <= free`.
- The rotation needs `max(active, new) <= free + passive`. Deleting `passive` happens before either copy and is what funds both of them, so it is credited rather than ignored. A machine with no `passive` yet pays the full set.

Free space is read with `unix.Statfs` via `Bavail`, so root-reserved blocks are not counted as usable.

`NewUkiUpgradeSpec`'s existing one-copy check is left alone. It is cheap and it runs before the image is pulled, so it is still worth having as an early gate.

**Validation**

`go test ./agent/pkg/uki/...` - 93 specs, all pass. 17 are new.

Both call sites have a regression test that fails without the fix:

- `upgrade_test.go` "refuses to rotate when the EFI partition can not hold both copies". Reverting the `checkSpaceForUpgradeRotation` call makes it fail with `rotating active to passive: deleting role passive: remove /efi/EFI/Kairos/passive.efi`, i.e. the rotation started and `passive` was already gone. That is the exact harm.
- `install_test.go` "refuses to install when the EFI partition can not hold a copy per role". Reverting the `checkSpaceForInstall` call makes it fail, and makes the suite take 47s instead of 0.14s, because it spends that time actually copying until the disk fills.

The oversized artifacts in those tests are sparse files, so they cost no disk.

Also ran `go build ./agent/...`, `go vet ./agent/...`, `golangci-lint run ./agent/pkg/uki/...` (v2.13.2, matching `.golangci-version`, 0 issues), and `go test ./agent/...`. The only failure in the wider agent suite is `agent/pkg/utils` `SyncData`, which needs `rsync` in `$PATH`; it fails the same way on a clean `master` on this box.

Not boot-tested in QEMU. Reproducing it for real means installing onto an undersized ESP, and the changed code is a pure size comparison in front of copies whose behaviour is unchanged when the check passes.

**Deliberately out of scope**

`installEntry`, used by single-entry and recovery upgrades, has the same class of gap: it copies one `.efi` and one `.conf` from a tmpdir over the existing entry, and a new file larger than `old + free` corrupts that entry. It needs a different check (the source is in a tmpdir on another filesystem, and `copyFile` truncates the destination first, which partly self-funds), so I kept it out rather than widen this diff. Happy to add it here if you would rather it landed together.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**

Fixes #2267

---

Note: this repo's PR pipeline runs under `pull_request_target` with a maintainer-reviewed `fork-pr-builds` environment gate for fork PRs, so checks may sit at `action_required` until someone approves the run.

🤖 Opened by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler.
title: fix(uki): check EFI free space before writing artifact sets

author: ci-robbot
body:
The agent half of the extensions design, ported onto the monorepo as @mudler asked in kairos-io/AuroraBoot#526. Companion to kairos-io/AuroraBoot#771.

The original branch, kairos-io/kairos-agent#1226, was closed without merging when the repo moved here. This is that work re-landed against `agent/`, plus the drift the monorepo picked up since.

## What was missing

AuroraBoot can already drive sysext and confext lifecycle on a node and can bundle extensions with an OS upgrade. The agent had no command for either, so both paths dead-ended at the fleet server.

## What this adds

**An `extension` command.** `install`, `enable`, `disable` and `remove` map onto the existing `kairos-agent sysext|confext` subcommands. `install` runs install and then enable, so the operator's single Install action card is one round trip rather than two.

The scope flag is placed before the positional name on purpose. urfave/cli stops parsing flags at the first positional argument, so a trailing `--common` makes the `enable` Before hook reject the call with "extension name required". There is a spec pinning the argument order.

**Bundled extensions on upgrade.** `upgrade` and `upgrade-recovery` take an optional `extensions` argument holding a JSON array of `{type, name, source}`. `CommandData.Args` is a `map[string]string`, hence JSON in a string rather than a nested structure.

Two behaviours worth calling out:

- A failure installing any extension aborts before the OS upgrade runs, so a node never reboots into a half-applied state. The spec asserts no reboot is scheduled on that path.
- An extension already enabled under any of the four scopes keeps that scope. Without this, a compound upgrade would silently move an operator's `--common` extension back to `--active`.

**A filename fix in `httpSource.Download`.** It took `filepath.Base` of the raw URI, so a signed source such as `https://aurora/.../foo.sysext.raw?token=abc` landed on disk as `foo.sysext.raw?token=abc`. That name has no `.raw` suffix, which is what `ListExtensions` matches on, so the extension became invisible right after a successful download. It now takes the basename of the URL *path*.

## Deltas from #1226

Three, all because the monorepo moved on:

1. `rebootScheduler` already exists here as a test seam, but `handleUpgrade` and `handleReboot` still called `scheduleReboot()` directly. #1226 would have added a second seam next to it. Instead the two direct calls now go through the existing var, so there is one seam rather than two.
2. #1226 hardcoded `/var/lib/kairos/extensions` and `/var/lib/kairos/confexts` in the phonehome package. Those paths are unexported constants in `agent/pkg/action`, so this exports `ExtensionDirFromBootState` and the handlers call it. No duplicated path literals.
3. Tests are internal (`package phonehome`), matching `handlers_test.go` which is already internal here. That drops the ~70 lines of `export_test.go` seam boilerplate #1226 needed for its external test package.

One unrelated change: `"upgrade-recovery"` is now the `commandUpgradeRecovery` constant. Adding the recovery-scope branch made it the 5th occurrence, which is exactly the repo's `goconst` threshold.

## Verification

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./agent/internal/phonehome/... ./agent/pkg/action/...
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/phonehome  1.573s
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/pkg/action          4.117s
```

45 new specs in the phonehome suite (97 total) and 10 in the action suite (222 total), all confirmed to actually run rather than skip:

```
$ go test ./agent/pkg/action/... -args -ginkgo.focus='extensionFileNameFromURI|ExtensionDirFromBootState'
Ran 10 of 222 Specs
SUCCESS! -- 10 Passed | 0 Failed
```

Lint is clean against the pinned `v2.13.2`:

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run ./agent/internal/phonehome/... ./agent/pkg/action/...
0 issues.
```

Not verified on hardware. Every spec fakes the shell-out to `kairos-agent`, so what is covered is the argv this builds and the ordering guarantees, not the extension merge itself. A booted check of the `?token=` filename fix would be worth doing before release.
title: feat(phonehome): accept an extension command and bundle extensions in upgrade

author: ci-robbot
body:
Prerequisite for kairos-io/kairos#4340, PR 5 of the split.

## Why this is not the grub reorder

The next step in the split was meant to be the AuroraBoot grub reorder that
makes `install-mode-interactive` the default live entry. It is a two-line
change, and shipping it now would break every unattended install, starting
with this repo's own acceptance suite.

`tests/tests_suite_test.go` boots the ISO with `types.WithISO(...)` and nothing
else: no cmdline, no entry selection. So `set default=0` is what boots. Every
suite that installs from the live CD therefore relies on the default entry
being `install-mode`, and asserts it:

- `expectDefaultService` wants `kairos-installer.service` loaded and enabled
- `expectStartedInstallation` wants `/usr/bin/kairos-agent install` in `ps`

Under the reorder, `52_installer.yaml` enables `kairos-interactive` instead and
neither holds. The same is true outside CI for anyone who boots a Kairos ISO
with an autoinstall datasource: today it installs, after the reorder it stops
at a TUI.

So the reorder needs this first.

## The change

`interactive-install` scanned no config at all. It resolved an installer and
launched it, unconditionally. `install` does scan, and when it finds
`install.auto: true` it installs without any UX (`install.go:131`).

This makes `interactive-install` do the same check before it resolves an
installer, and extracts that install-mode branch into `runAutoInstall` so the
two entrypoints share one implementation rather than growing two.

The scan is deliberately identical to `install`'s: `ensureDataSourceReady()`
first, then the same three collector options. Without the wait, a config still
being written by the datasource reads as absent, which is the race that
function exists to close. A scan error is not fatal; it just means there is
nothing unattended to honour, so the installer runs as before.

`interactive-install` now passes `constants.GetUserConfigDirs()`, as the
`install` command already does.

## Behaviour

| live boot | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| interactive entry, no config | installer | installer |
| interactive entry, config without `install.auto` | installer | installer |
| interactive entry, config with `install.auto: true` | installer, config ignored | unattended install |
| install-mode entry, any config | unchanged | unchanged |

Someone who picks the interactive entry by hand *and* ships an
`install.auto: true` config now gets the install. That is the reading I went
with: `install.auto` is an explicit "do not ask me" in the config, and
`Kairos (manual)` is still there for a shell. Worth saying out loud since it is
a judgment call, not a forced one.

## Verification

`go test ./agent/internal/agent/` passes, 3 new specs. Mutating the new branch
to never fire (`false && autoInstallRequested(cc)`) fails
`installs without asking when install.auto is set` on the assertion that the
installer was not reached, so the spec is testing the branch and not its
neighbours. The installer is a shell script behind `KAIROS_INSTALLER` that
touches a marker file, which is how "delegated" and "did not delegate" are told
apart. `go vet` and `gofmt` clean; `agent/pkg/cmd` tests pass.

The `install.go` half is a pure extraction: same statements, same order.

Not verified here: a real live boot. There is no way to exercise
`RunInstall` past `CheckConfigForUsers` on this box, so the auto path is
covered up to the point where the install starts, and by the fact that
`install` has always taken exactly these statements.

## What still blocks the reorder

One more thing, and it is not this PR. The default entry today also runs the
QR/nodepair pairing flow for provider-kairos (`install.go`, the
`bus.Manager.Publish(events.EventChallenge, ...)` path). The interactive entry
does not. Issue #4340 says the QR code becomes the TUI's job, which is phase 6
of the split ("the TUI's first screen"), so the reorder has to come after it,
not before. Revised order: this, then phase 6, then the grub flip.
title: fix(install): let an unattended config win over the interactive installer

author: itxaka-agent
body:
We have reinvented "call X, if it fails wait a growing amount and try
again up to N times" at least ten times across this repo, each copy with
its own backoff shape, its own off-by-ones and its own dead code. This
adds `sdk/retry` — a thin wrapper over `github.com/avast/retry-go`, which
was already vendored via immucore, so no new dependency — and migrates
every one of those loops to it. Pure refactor otherwise: behavior is kept
bug-for-bug except for two timing tweaks called out below, both strictly
positive.

`sdk/retry` is deliberately thin. `Do`, `Unrecoverable`, `IsRecoverable`
and the `Option`/`RetryableFunc`/`OnRetryFunc`/`RetryIfFunc` types are
aliases/re-exports of retry-go's own, so any raw retry-go option composes
with our helpers. On top of that:

- `WithFixedDelay`, `WithLinearBackoff` (the Kth retry waits K units),
  `WithLinearBackoffFromZero` (first retry is free — the shape several
  call sites actually had), `WithExponentialBackoff` (pair with
  `WithMaxDelay`) — delay shapes retry-go has no ready-made option for
- `WithUnlimitedAttempts()` for ctx/timeout-bound loops with no natural
  attempt cap; it forces `LastErrorOnly(true)` too, because retry-go
  otherwise preallocates an `[]error` sized to Attempts
- `ExponentialDelay(base, n, max)` so call sites that log "reconnecting
  in %s" can compute the exact upcoming delay — retry-go's `OnRetry`
  callback isn't told the delay it is about to apply
- `PollUntil(ctx, interval, timeout, checkFirst, check)` + `ErrTimeout`,
  the "wait for a condition" sibling of `Do`, for the call sites that
  were waiting on a filesystem path or a partition label appearing
- `Defaults()` (10 attempts, exponential from 200ms capped at 10s,
  last-error-only) as a starting point. None of the 10 migrated call
  sites use it — they all needed a specific documented shape — it's there
  for future callers so the next one doesn't hand-roll a loop again

Migrated call sites:

- `sdk/kcrypt/encryptor.go:67-131, 326-378, 448-523` — three
  near-identical `unlockPartition` methods (remote KMS, TPM w/ PCR, local
  TPM NV), 10 attempts / linear 1s..9s each. Now one `retry.Do` plus two
  package consts
- `sdk/kcrypt/unlock.go:66-116` (`luksUnlock`) — 3 attempts, same linear
  shape, keeps the per-retry `UdevAdmSettle` side effect
- `sdk/kcrypt/lock.go:303-316` (`waitDevice`) — fixed 1s delay; a
  `UdevAdmSettle` failure was and still is a permanent bail-out, now said
  out loud with `retry.Unrecoverable`
- `immucore/internal/utils/common.go:468-496` (`GetState`) — already used
  avast/retry-go directly, now goes through the helper
- `immucore/pkg/op/mount.go:22-93` (`MountOPWithFstab`) — fixed interval
  bounded by a timeout, now `WithUnlimitedAttempts` + `WithContext` on a
  `context.WithTimeout`
- `immucore/pkg/state/steps.go:125-166` (`WaitForSysrootDagStep`) — poll
  for two paths, now `PollUntil`
- `immucore/internal/utils/partitions.go:281-297`
  (`WaitForKairosPartitions`) — same poll shape, now `PollUntil`
- `immucore/pkg/state/steps_uki.go:576-588` — 5-attempt UKI livecd
  device-by-label lookup, linear from zero (0s,1s,2s,3s)
- `agent/internal/phonehome/client.go:274-328` (`Run`) — the two
  near-identical exponential-backoff-with-cap-and-ctx-cancel loops
  (registration, reconnect) in one function, now
  `WithExponentialBackoff` + `WithMaxDelay` + `WithUnlimitedAttempts` +
  `WithContext`, with `ExponentialDelay` feeding the log line
- `agent/pkg/elemental/elemental.go:86-98`
  (`PartitionAndFormatDevice`) — 5-attempt partition table reread, linear
  from zero

**Correction to the original audit:** it listed `GetState` as
`immucore/pkg/mounts/mounts.go:468-496`. That path does not exist in this
repo — there is no `immucore/pkg/mounts` directory at all. The real file
is `immucore/internal/utils/common.go` and the line range 468-496 was
exactly right. Flagging it rather than quietly "fixing" the audit, since
reviewers working from that document should know which entries are stale.

**Pre-existing bugs found and deliberately left alone**, each worth its
own follow-up:

- `agent/pkg/elemental/elemental.go`: the retry loop's result is thrown
  away. Right after the loop `disk.ReReadPartitionTable()` is called
  again unconditionally and *that* error is what gets returned, so a
  successful retry can still be undone by the redundant call failing, and
  any error the loop produced never surfaces
- same file: the `Waiting %d seconds before next attempt` debug line
  always printed a literal `5`, never the real 0/1/2/3s wait

The one thing that could not be preserved: `MountOPWithFstab` had a
`case <-c.Done()` branch for context cancellation where
`c := context.Background()`, i.e. a context that can never be canceled.
The branch was dead code; centralizing the timeout removes it.

**The two timing changes**, disclosed rather than snuck in:

- `waitDevice`, the UKI cdrom loop and the partition table reread loop
  each slept one more time after their last failed attempt, right before
  falling out of the loop with failure — nobody reads that delay.
  retry-go, like every retry engine, doesn't sleep after the final
  attempt, so migrating drops it. The exhausted/failing path finishes one
  backoff unit sooner; success behavior is untouched and nothing gets
  longer
- `WaitForSysrootDagStep` used `select { default: time.Sleep(2s) }`, so
  ctx cancellation and the overall timeout were only checked every 2s
  because the sleep itself wasn't interruptible. `PollUntil` selects each
  cycle, so shutdown is honored immediately instead of up to ~2s late

12 files changed, 643 insertions, 218 deletions. `go build` and `go test`
across `sdk/`, `immucore/`, `agent/`, `cmd/`, `installer/`, `provider/`
and `internal/`; `sdk/retry` ships 12 test funcs covering Do,
Unrecoverable, every backoff shape and PollUntil, and the timing-sensitive
specs that already exercised the migrated code
(`immucore/pkg/op/mount_test.go`, `agent/internal/phonehome/client_test.go`,
`agent/pkg/elemental/elemental_test.go`) pass unmodified. Two known
failures are pre-existing and confirmed on unmodified master via
`git stash`: kairos-init doesn't build (missing `binaries/edgevpn` embed
pattern) and `sdk/collector`'s `TestConfig` has 4 failing specs. Neither
is touched here.

Signed-off-by: itxaka-agent <itxaka-agent@users.noreply.github.com>
title: refactor: one retry helper instead of 10 hand-rolled backoff loops

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override any
> action taken here.

Fixes: #1157

## What

Adds a dracut-`rd.break`-style breakpoint to immucore's boot DAG: `rd.immucore.break=<step>[,<step>...]` (repeatable) stops the boot right before the named step and hands the console to an interactive shell, resuming the DAG when that shell exits.

## Why

There was no way to pause a boot that is otherwise succeeding in order to look around mid-boot — the only existing shell drop is `DropToEmergencyShellWithError`, which only fires on a real DAG failure and never returns (it execs and replaces the process). This is a different, additive mechanism: a child process the caller waits on, not a process replacement.

## How

- One hook point: `TimedCallback` (`immucore/pkg/state/timing.go`), which nearly every DAG step already routes through, checks the requested step names against the one currently running.
- Valid step names are the `Op*` constants the DAG is built from — `immucore --dry-run` prints the full resolved DAG (and, as of this PR, echoes which breakpoint steps were actually requested) so an operator can check spelling against their own boot configuration before rebooting into it.
- The breakpoint shell is a new fork-and-wait helper, not a reuse of the existing exec-and-replace one: it opens the console read-write, tries to give itself its own session so job control works, falls back to sharing immucore's session if the console already belongs to one, and falls back further to inherited stdio (with a warning that names the likely outcome) if no console can be opened at all.
- Breakpoints are serialized with a mutex since the DAG runs independent steps concurrently.

## Verified

Built a test ISO and booted it under QEMU/KVM. With `rd.immucore.break=wait-for-sysroot`: DAG dump → breakpoint banner → live interactive shell (proved live, not a frozen console) → `exit` → boot resumes and completes normally. Control boot with no flag: identical DAG shape and timings, zero breakpoint output — confirmed no-op when the flag is absent. The boot-timeline shows shell dwell time is excluded from step timing as designed. Full logs and the exact QEMU/build commands are in the audit trail linked below.

## Review

Went two rounds. Round 0 flagged a flaky test barrier, a stale README pointer, an oversized diff from an incidental gofmt re-indent, and a fallback warning message that didn't match what the operator would actually observe under the real deployed systemd unit — the latter two verified empirically (one confirmed via a synthetic gofmt repro, one confirmed via checking systemd's actual `StandardInput=` default and the generated unit file) before being published. A fifth finding was dropped after empirical verification showed its suggested fix didn't work as described. Round 1 confirmed all four fixes land correctly and approved with no further comments.

Full chronological audit trail (every phase, every round, every verdict): https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/1157#issuecomment-5585208900
title: feat(immucore): add rd.immucore.break breakpoints

author: mauro-agent
body: ## What `kairos-init/pkg/bundled/alpineInit/initramfs-init` (the alpine-derived netboot init script) uses a bash-only `[[ ]]` glob test to detect the `root=live:` cmdline argument: ```sh [[ $x = root=live:* ]] || continue ``` ## Why it breaks Busybox builds without `CONFIG_ASH_BASH_COMPAT` can't parse `[[ ]]` at all. Hadron's own busybox config (`files/busybox/minimal.config` in kairos-io/hadron) explicitly disables both `CONFIG_ASH` and `CONFIG_ASH_BASH_COMPAT`. On a Hadron-based image netbooted with `root=live:`, the init script dies at this exact line, before it ever reaches the `wget` that fetches the squashfs. PID 1 exits, and the kernel panics with `Kernel panic - not syncing: No working init found. Try passing init= option to kernel.` Reproduced live tonight: AuroraBoot netbooted a Hadron+k0s image successfully up through kernel+initrd delivery (confirmed in server logs), the target machine never requested the squashfs at all, and hit exactly this panic. ## Fix Replaced the bashism with a POSIX `case` statement, portable to any busybox ash build: ```sh case "$x" in root=live:*) ;; *) continue ;; esac ``` Verified the resulting script parses cleanly under a real `busybox sh -n`. This is not an agent, Mauro used AI to help write this.
title: fix(kairos-init): use POSIX case instead of [[ ]] in netboot init

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4546

@mudler asked for a PR on this, so here it is. Revised after his review: the MCP server is served over HTTP by `kairos-installer` itself, not on stdio.

## What it is

```
kairos-installer                     # TUI on the terminal, MCP on http://<host>:8090/mcp
kairos-installer --mcp-address ""    # TUI only
```

A third frontend on the contract the TUI and the web UI already use. `sdk/agentrun` describes itself as "the installer side of the kairos-agent installer contract" and has no TUI dependencies: it turns `kairos-agent manual-install` into a stream of typed `ProgressEvent`s. Everything here does is expose the same information the TUI screens show and make the same install call the TUI makes.

| Tool | Backed by | Writes anything? |
|---|---|---|
| `list_disks` | `installer/internal/disks` | no |
| `list_prerequisites` | the `tui-check-*` plugins | no |
| `apply_prerequisites` | the same plugins, apply round | yes, whatever the plugin does |
| `get_install_options` | agent discovery, disks, `agentrun.Steps` | no |
| `install` | `agentrun.RunWithOutput` | **repartitions a disk** |
| `collect_debug_bundle` | `debugbundle.GenerateBundle` | writes the bundle |

`install` streams `ProgressEvent`s back as MCP progress notifications when the client sends a progress token, and returns the steps it reached either way.

## Transport

Streamable HTTP, on `:8090` at `/mcp`, started by `kairos-installer` alongside the TUI the way `kairos-webui` is started alongside it today. An agent reaches the installer the same way a person reaches the web UI, over the network, instead of having to spawn a process on the machine first.

Nothing new has to be enabled in the live image: `kairos-agent interactive-install` already execs `/system/installer/kairos-installer`, so the interactive boot entry gets the MCP server with it.

`mcp.Handler()` returns the server as an `http.Handler`. When the web UI moves into `installer/` for #4340 it mounts on that mux and `ListenAndServe` goes away; until then `ListenAndServe` is the standalone listener.

Three things follow from being on a port rather than a pipe:

- **The one-install guard moved onto the shared `Server`.** On stdio, one client per process gave it for free. Over HTTP anyone can open a second session, so without this a client got a second wipe by reconnecting. `TestSecondInstallIsRefusedOnANewHTTPSession` covers it.
- **Cross-origin protection is on.** The machine drawing the TUI has a browser on it, and a page the operator opens must not be able to POST an install. The SDK's localhost/`Host` header check is left on too, so a rebound DNS name is refused.
- **The transport logs to the installer log.** It must never write to the terminal the TUI is drawing on, so the SDK's `slog` and `http.Server.ErrorLog` both go to the zerolog writer.

A port that will not bind is logged, not fatal: the TUI is perfectly usable without it.

## `install` requires explicit confirmation

Four separate things have to hold:

- `confirm=true`. It is a required property of the input schema, so a client cannot omit it, and the handler rejects `false` with an explanation aimed at the model reading it.
- The device has to be an installation candidate *at the moment of the call*, re-scanned rather than taken from an earlier `list_disks`. A hallucinated path and a disk that has since gone are both refused, and the refusal lists what the candidates actually are.
- The tool is annotated `destructiveHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: false`, which is the only signal a client has that it must not be called speculatively.
- One install per boot. A retry after a *failure* is allowed: the disk is already spoiled and refusing would leave the machine stuck.

The confirmed `device`, `source` and `finish_action` are also written into the cloud-config last, so a `cloud_config` naming another disk cannot quietly move the install there. There is a test for exactly that.

## What moved, and why

Two things came out of `installer/internal/tui` so that both frontends give the same answer instead of drifting:

- **which disks are candidates** → `installer/internal/disks`. If the MCP server had its own scan, an agent could offer a disk the interactive installer hides.
- **the prerequisite plugin round-trip** → `installer/internal/checks`. It is a contract with providers (two events, a plugin set, and the rule that a misbehaving plugin is logged rather than fatal), so a second implementation of it would be a second set of bugs.

The TUI keeps its own presentation of both; only the facts moved. Its tests are unchanged and still pass.

One small fix fell out: `ghw` reports a disk model of `"unknown"` rather than nothing when the kernel does not say, which read as a disk whose model is literally called "unknown" once it reached a caller.

## Dependency

`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.7.0`, the official SDK, rather than a hand-rolled JSON-RPC server. It brings 4 transitive deps (`jsonschema-go`, `segmentio/asm`, `segmentio/encoding`, `uritemplate`).

## Verification

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./installer/... && go test -count=1 ./installer/...
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/internal/checks	0.012s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/internal/debugbundle	0.006s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/internal/disks	0.002s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/internal/mcp	0.080s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/internal/tui	0.074s
ok  	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/installer/prereqs	0.004s
```

The tool tests drive the server through a real MCP client, not by calling the handlers directly, so the schemas, annotations and structured output are all exercised as a client would see them. `installer/internal/mcp/http_test.go` adds the HTTP half: tools over a real `httptest` listener, the shared install guard across two sessions, a cross-site POST, and `ListenAndServe` itself binding, serving and shutting down with its context.

I also ran the built binary end to end with the real TUI on a pty, and drove it over HTTP against this machine's real disks:

```
tools=6
list_disks             isError=false /dev/dm-0  100.00 GiB | /dev/sda  320.00 GiB
list_prerequisites     isError=false No prerequisite checks were reported...
get_install_options    isError=true  no kairos-agent binary was found, so nothing can be installed from this machine
install                isError=true  refusing to install: "/dev/definitely-not-here" is not an installation candidate on this machine. The candidates are: /dev/dm-0, /dev/sda.
install                isError=true  refusing to install: confirm was not true. install destroys everything on "/dev/sda"...
cross-site POST                 -> HTTP 403
Host: evil.example.com          -> HTTP 403
bytes written to the TUI's pty  -> 0
```

Because the confirmation logic is the whole point of the PR, I mutation-checked it rather than trusting a green run. Removing the `confirm` check, the candidate-device check, the second-install guard, the rule that the confirmed device wins over `cloud_config`, or the cross-origin wrapper each fails a test, and the refusal tests assert the agent was called zero times rather than only that an error came back.

**Not verified:** no real install was run. There is no VM on this box, so `install` was exercised against a fake `Installer` and by refusal, never by repartitioning a disk. `agentrun` itself is unchanged, so what reaches `kairos-agent` is a cloud-config file and the same arguments the TUI passes, but the end-to-end install driven over MCP is unproven and wants a VM run before this merges. `golangci-lint` is not available here.


---

## Update after review (7f753784)

- **The tool-confirmed finish action now wins.** `reboot`/`poweroff` are `omitempty`, so a `false` rendered no key and a caller's `cloud_config` kept its own value: `finish_action` omitted plus `install: {poweroff: true}` powered the machine off. The keys the tool owns are written back explicitly after the merge. `source` is not one of them when it is empty, because forcing `""` in would override the source `kairos-agent` resolves for itself.
- **The listener has an off-switch on a real boot.** `--mcp-address` was unreachable from the boot path, because `kairos-agent` execs the installer with a fixed argument list. An `mcp:` block in `/etc/kairos/agent.yaml` now takes the same `disable` and `listen_address` the web UI takes, read by the installer itself through `sdk/branding` (which #4568 made reachable from `installer/`). The flag still wins when it is actually passed.
- **The exposure is documented rather than implied away.** The cross-origin wrapper is a browser control: a caller with no `Origin` and no `Sec-Fetch-Site` passes through, which a new test pins. Said plainly in the package doc, `installer/README.md` and the flag help, along with the tools and the port.

```yaml
mcp:
  disable: true                     # do not listen at all
  listen_address: 127.0.0.1:8090    # or listen only on this machine
```
title: feat(installer): ship an MCP server so agents can drive the installation

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4576.

`scan shipped bundle` is a required release gate, and when it fails it does not say which advisory failed it. The table it builds goes only to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (not exposed by the REST API; `check-runs` returns `output.summary: null`) and to the `osv-scan` artifact (download redirects to `productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`, which 403s outside a browser session). Meanwhile osv-scanner prints every *ignored* advisory to the log in full, so the log is detailed about what does not matter and silent about what does.

Two changes to `Report and enforce`:

- `tee` the report block instead of `>>`, so the same table lands in the job log;
- add the advisory IDs to the `::error::` annotation, which *is* readable through the check-runs API.

Nothing else changes: the step summary gets byte-identical content, and the exit code is unchanged.

## Verification

Ran the step's script against a synthetic `osv.json` in both states.

Failing (2 advisories over 3 module versions) - table now in the log, IDs in the annotation, still `exit 1`:

```
| advisory | module |
|---|---|
| `GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv` | `github.com/containerd/containerd/v2@2.3.4` |
| `GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv` | `github.com/foo/bar@1.0.0` |
| `GO-2026-1111` | `github.com/foo/bar@1.0.0` |
::error::2 unignored advisories (3 findings) in the shipped bundle: GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv, GO-2026-1111. Bump the affected component, or add a dated entry to osv-scanner.toml with a reason.
```

Clean - `No unignored advisories.`, `exit 0`. Summary file identical to the log in both cases. `actionlint` clean.

## Why it came up

GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv was published today at 18:01 UTC and put containerd `< 2.3.5` in range, reddening the gate on the first branch built after it. Working out which advisory it was took a package-list diff between two builds plus a search of golang/vulndb and the GHSA database. With this change the run would have said `GHSA-7jxh-36q5-gcqv` on the first line. The bump itself is #4575.
title: fix(ci): name the advisory when the release scan fails

author: ci-robbot
body:
Targets `add-persistent-path` (#4414) as @mudler asked in https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/pull/4414#issuecomment-5615407951, so it lands with that PR rather than after it.

Follow-up to the mode question my QA on #4414 raised. #4414 persists `/etc/ssl/private`, and persisting it is what makes the mode permanent.

## The problem

`/etc/ssl/private` holds the system's private keys, so no distro ships it world-traversable:

| distro | mode | owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debian, Ubuntu (`ssl-cert` installed) | 0710 | root:ssl-cert |
| RHEL, Fedora, SUSE | 0700 | root:root |
| Hadron | **0755** | root:root |

Hadron's value is read straight out of the image, not inferred:

```
$ curl ... ghcr.io/kairos-io/hadron:v0.5.1 (layer sha256:2f1e590d) | tar -tvz | grep etc/ssl/private
drwxr-xr-x 0/0  0 2026-07-07 07:42:26 etc/ssl/private/
```

`ID=hadron` in its `/etc/os-release`, and no `ssl-cert` group in its `/etc/group`.

Once the directory is persisted this stops being cosmetic. immucore creates the backing directory under `/usr/local/.state` and rsyncs the image's copy into it with `-aAX` (`immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go`), mode included. So the base image's mode becomes what the persistent partition carries, and every later boot bind-mounts that. Re-installing does not correct it.

## The change

One bundled cloud config, `01_ssl_private_perms.yaml`, running in the `initramfs` stage. That stage is wired after `OpMountBind` in `immucore/pkg/dag/dag_normal_boot.go`, so the `chmod` applies to the backing directory and not to the empty one it shadows.

It keys on the `ssl-cert` group rather than on an `only_os` distro list:

```sh
if grep -q '^ssl-cert:' /etc/group 2>/dev/null; then
  chown root:ssl-cert /etc/ssl/private
  chmod 0710 /etc/ssl/private
else
  chown root:root /etc/ssl/private
  chmod 0700 /etc/ssl/private
fi
```

The group is the entire reason the 0710 mode exists, so an image that has it wants 0710 and an image that does not wants 0700, whether or not we have heard of the distro. That also means a base image we have never built against gets the right answer without a new entry in a list. `01_extra_binds.yaml` is the `only_os` version of this, and it needs a new branch per distro family; this does not.

Net effect on hadron: 0755 -> 0700. Debian/Ubuntu images keep the 0710 they already have. Anything already correct is a no-op.

## Tests

`kairos-init/pkg/validation/cloudconfigs_ssl_private_test.go`, 6 specs, in the same style as the existing guard specs: they parse the shipped YAML and run the stage body through `sh -c`, the way yip runs it, against a temporary directory and a synthetic `/etc/group`.

```
Ran 6 of 28 Specs in 0.009 seconds
SUCCESS! -- 6 Passed | 0 Failed
```

Covered: the `if` guard fires only when the directory exists; 0755 -> 0700 with no group; 0710 preserved when the group exists; 0755 -> 0710 when the group exists; the group is matched by name and not as a substring (`my-ssl-cert`, or `ssl-cert` appearing in another group's member list, both take the 0700 branch); idempotent when run twice.

Both specs were confirmed to fail on a mutated config (`chmod 0700` -> `0755`, and dropping the `^`/`:` anchors), so they are not passing vacuously.

## What I could not verify here

`chown` is neutralised in the specs, which run unprivileged, so they pin the mode and not the ownership. The ownership half is one line and follows the same branch, but a booted-node check of `stat /etc/ssl/private` on a Debian-based image would confirm it end to end. This box has no rsync, so the mode-through-rsync step is still inferred from `-aAX` rather than executed.
title: fix(cloudconfig): restrict /etc/ssl/private per distro

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4579.

## The bug

`reusable-factory.yaml` builds the `$K8S` tag segment only when the k8s **version** is pinned:

```bash
K8S=""
if [[ -n "$KUBERNETES_VERSION" ]]; then
  K8S="-$KUBERNETES_DISTRO-$SANITIZED_KUBERNETES_VERSION"
fi
```

`kubernetes_version` defaults to `auto`, and `auto` is resolved to the empty string a few lines earlier so kairos-init picks the version itself. `pr.yaml` and `master.yaml` both take that default, so on those paths `$K8S` is always empty and the distro never reaches the tag. Since `VARIANT` is `standard` for every distro, two cells differing only by distro push the **same** tag, and `test-standard` / `test-standard-encryption` pull that tag by rebuilding it in shell. Sixteen qemu cells could boot a k0s image while reporting as k3s coverage, with no error.

The artifact-name block fifty lines below, in the same step, gates on the **distro**. That is the correct test, so the two were inconsistent and this changes `$K8S` to match.

## The change

- `$K8S` (and `DEFAULT_TAG`, and the default artifact name) derive from `KUBERNETES_DISTRO`, appending the sanitized version only when it is non-empty. That also drops the bare trailing dash the artifact name grew under `auto`.
- The tag is rebuilt by hand in two other places, both with `K8S=""` hardcoded. `reusable-qemu-test.yaml` and `_uki-test.yaml` now derive it the same way, so the three sites cannot drift silently.
- `pr.yaml` / `master.yaml` name the distro of the image each test job consumes. `test-standard`, `test-standard-encryption` and the standard UKI cell all run against k3s images and did not say so.
- With the collision gone, an `amd64-standard-k0s` cell. **Image only, `iso: false`** — the k0s provider does its work at build time (kairos-init calls provider `BuildEvent`, which runs the installer script, relocates the binary out of `/usr/local/bin` and writes the service units by hand), so pushing the OS image catches that class of break for the cost of one image build. It is also required rather than merely cheaper: the default `custom_artifact_format` has no `$K8S`, so an ISO here would collide on the artifact name instead.

`release.yaml` is untouched and unaffected: all of its k8s cells pin `kubernetes_version`, so `$K8S` was already non-empty there.

## Verification

I cannot run Actions here, so instead of eyeballing three copies of a tag I wrote a harness that **parses these workflows, extracts the actual `run:` scripts of the three derivation steps, substitutes the `${{ inputs.* }}` expressions for a given cell, and executes them under `bash -e`** — the same shell Actions uses. It then asserts no two build cells land on the same tag, and that each test job's mirror reproduces the tag its build cell pushed.

On this branch:

```
== build-iso cells (pr.yaml / master.yaml), tags as factory-action derives them ==
  amd64-core           hadron-v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  amd64-standard       hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k3s-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  amd64-standard-k0s   hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k0s-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  amd64-standard-uki   hadron-trusted-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k3s-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329-uki
  amd64-core-uki       hadron-trusted-v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329-uki
  amd64-core-fips      hadron-fips-v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  amd64-core-ubuntu-20.04 ubuntu-20.04-core-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329

== test jobs: hand-written tag mirror vs what was built ==
  test-standard (amd64-standard)         OK  hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k3s-...
  test-standard-encryption               OK  hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k3s-...
  test-core (amd64-core)                 OK  hadron-v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-...
  test-uki install-upgrade               OK  hadron-trusted-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-k3s-...-uki
  test-uki boot-assessment               OK  hadron-trusted-v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-...-uki

RESULT: all assertions pass
```

The same binary run against unmodified `master` (a detached worktree at `d0102329`) fails, which is what makes the run above worth anything:

```
  amd64-standard       hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  amd64-standard-k0s   hadron-v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-v4.3.0-37-gd0102329
  ** COLLISION: amd64-standard-k0s and amd64-standard push the same tag

RESULT: FAILED
```

And the release tags come out byte-identical on both sides, confirming the no-op there:

```
  release-k3s    v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-<version>-k3s-v1.34.1-k3s1
  release-k0s    v0.5.1-standard-amd64-generic-<version>-k0s-v1.34.1-k0s.1
  release-core   v0.5.1-core-amd64-generic-<version>
```

All six touched files also parse as YAML.

## Known limits

- The harness is a local tool, not committed here. Three hand-written copies of one tag format is the underlying design problem; extracting the derivation into a single script all three sites call would remove the drift risk permanently, but it means running repo-checked-out code inside the `pull_request_target` pipeline, so I would rather do it as its own PR than fold it in here.
- This buys **build-time** k0s coverage only. Whether a k0s cluster actually comes up is still untested outside release, and is the wider gap noted in #4579.
- The artifact-name half of the same collision is still latent: `custom_artifact_format`'s default carries no `$K8S`, which is why the new cell is image-only. Closing that means changing the format and the two matching download steps.
title: fix(ci): put the k8s distro in the image tag, and build k0s

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override
> any action taken here.

Fixes: kairos-io/kairos#4579

## What this does

`reusable-factory.yaml` derived the `$K8S` image-tag segment from `$KUBERNETES_VERSION`, which resolves to empty under the default `auto` version. On the `pr.yaml`/`master.yaml` paths that meant a k3s cell and a would-be k0s cell push to the exact same tag, with whichever cell finishes last silently winning (`fail-fast: false`). This PR:

- Keys `$K8S` (and the SARIF upload category, and the release/pr/master artifact name) off `$KUBERNETES_DISTRO` instead, matching the pattern the artifact-name block already used correctly.
- Threads `kubernetes_distro` through to `reusable-qemu-test.yaml` and `_uki-test.yaml`, which independently reconstruct the same tag in shell to find the image a test job consumes.
- Adds a build-only (`iso: false`) `amd64-standard-k0s` cell to `pr.yaml`/`master.yaml`, so the k0s provider's build-time work (`BuildEvent`, which does real installation/relocation work — see kairos-io/kairos#4299, which shipped a defect there unnoticed) gets exercised before release day instead of only in `release.yaml`'s tag-triggered `build-iso-k0s` job.
- Adds `.github/scripts/verify_k8s_tag.py` (`make verify-k8s-tag`) as a permanent regression guard: it reads the tag/artifact formats and matrix definitions out of the actual workflow YAML (not retyped literals) and executes the real derivation shell, so a future edit to any of the three copies shows up as a guard failure instead of silent drift.

## Compatibility note for other repos

`reusable-factory.yaml` is called cross-repo (`kairos-io/hadron` is a known consumer, pinned at `master` or a SHA per this repo's README). This change moves the pushed tag for any caller that passes a `kubernetes_distro` with the default `kubernetes_version: auto`: `...-generic-v1.2.3` → `...-generic-k3s-v1.2.3` (or whichever distro they pass). This is the intended fix — the old behavior silently dropped the distro — but it is a visible tag-naming change reaching other repos on merge.

## Review notes carried forward (non-blocking)

Three small items the reviewer flagged in the final round as worth knowing about but not worth another round on:

- `verify_k8s_tag.py` pins a fixed `version` value when modelling the factory's tag derivation, so the `auto`-version branch of the real shell is read but never executed by the harness.
- `reusable-qemu-test.yaml` and `_uki-test.yaml` still hand-type the artifact name (a fourth copy of the format the harness reads but doesn't yet cross-check); untouched by this PR and still correct today.
- One commit (`6f80b707`) is a one-line correction to a comment two commits earlier (`a8336670`) — left as separate commits per this branch's convention of not squashing before merge.

## How this was produced

This PR was opened by an automated triage loop: a coder role implemented the fix, a tester role independently reproduced the bug and re-verified every claim (including two builder-role empirical checks against GitHub's documented SARIF code-scanning behavior), and a reviewer role went through three rounds before approving. Full chronological summary in the linked issue comment below.

Audit trail: https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/issues/4579#issuecomment-5618621306
title: fix(ci): key the k8s image tag off distro, not version, and build a k0s image every push
