author: ci-robbot
body:
Follow-up to #4457, asked for [there](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/pull/4457#issuecomment-5525132840): open a separate PR for the `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` in `state/steps.go` and look at it properly rather than removing it because it looks removable.

## What I found

The sleep is in `WaitForSysrootDagStep`. Unlike the one in #4457 this really is a poll loop, so waiting between attempts is the point. What is wrong is where the wait sits and what it is made of.

**It waits before the first check.**

https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/5fa71229/immucore/pkg/state/steps.go#L131-L141

```go
select {
default:
	time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
	_, err := os.Stat(s.Rootdir)
```

`wait-for-sysroot` is a root node in both DAGs that register it, and most of the graph hangs off it:

| DAG | Steps that depend on `wait-for-sysroot` |
|---|---|
| `dag_live_media.go` | `mount-oem`, `rootfs` stage, `initramfs` stage |
| `dag_in_ram.go` | `ensure-partitions`, `mount-oem`, `rootfs` stage, `write-fstab` |

So the 2 seconds are on the critical path of every livecd, netboot and `kairos.ram` boot. And they are paid in the case the step was written for. `RegisterLiveMedia` says it plainly:

```go
// There is a wait for sysroot to be there, just in case. Not waiting for it, can result in a race condition in which
// sysroot is not ready when we try to mount oem and run stages
```

Dracut has normally already staged `/sysroot` by the time immucore runs, which is why immucore does not mount it here. The wait exists for the race, not for the common case, and the common case is the one that pays.

**The wait is uninterruptible.** `time.Sleep` inside the `default:` arm holds the goroutine for the full interval, so neither `ctx.Done()` nor the deadline channel is looked at until it ends. `rd.immucore.sysrootwait=1` reported `timeout exhausted` after 2 seconds, not 1. The already-canceled context was never affected: a `select` with a `default` arm takes a ready channel first, so a cancel that arrives before the loop is seen at once. Only the deadline overshoots.

## What this changes, and what it deliberately does not

**Corrected after a QA boot** (verdict below, fix in 4ec268f7). The first version of this PR only moved the check ahead of the wait and claimed that saved the 2 seconds. It did not: 14 live boots off one ISO with only the initrd swapped measured `wait-for-sysroot` at 2000-2003 ms on both sides. Dracut logs `Mounted /sysroot` 0.5-0.9 s after immucore starts waiting, so the first check always misses and the second lands at 2 s. Two stats plus one wait cost exactly what one wait plus one stat did.

The reorder was necessary but not sufficient. The interval itself is the problem: 2 seconds is coarser than the event it polls for, so the wait ends at the next round multiple of itself rather than when the sysroot is ready. It is now 100 ms, which is worth roughly 1.1 s on the critical path of every livecd, netboot and `kairos.ram` boot. The cost is `stat` on two paths, and only until the sysroot appears.

The wait is a `select` now instead of a `time.Sleep`, so the deadline and the cancel are honoured when they happen rather than up to an interval later. **The deadline arm takes one last look before giving up.** Without it a `rd.immucore.sysrootwait=` shorter than the interval got a single check and then failed, where the old loop's `default:` arm always granted the first attempt a full interval. QA caught that as a real regression: `sysrootwait=1` booted on master and on this branch came up with no `/oem`, no cloud-init and no users, while systemd still printed `Finished immucore`.

For a sysroot that stays absent, the deadline is unchanged and the step still fails with `timeout exhausted`.

The loop body moved into `waitForSysroot` and the two stats into `missingSysrootPath` so both can be tested, and so the debug line names the path it is actually still waiting on.

I have not touched the sleeps in `steps_uki.go:506`, `steps_uki.go:586` or `internal/utils/common.go`. Those are a different shape and want their own look.

## Verification

```
go test ./immucore/... -count=1     # all green
golangci-lint run ./immucore/pkg/state/...     # 0 issues
```

Both new timing specs stretch `sysrootPollInterval` to 60s, so what they measure is an order of magnitude away from the noise. Ran them against the old loop restored in place, to confirm they are not just decoration:

```
• [TIMEDOUT] waitForSysroot [It] returns before waiting when the sysroot is already there
• [TIMEDOUT] waitForSysroot [It] gives up on the deadline without sitting out the interval
FAIL	github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/state	121.520s
```

against `ok ... 2.498s` on this branch. The cancel spec passes both ways, for the `default`-arm reason above; it is there to keep that behaviour from regressing, not because it catches anything today.

What I cannot check from here: that a real livecd boot is 2 seconds faster. The DAG timing is already logged per step, so `wait-for-sysroot` in the boot timing output should show it on the next ISO.
title: fix(immucore): check for the sysroot before waiting for it

author: itxaka-agent
body:
> Automated triage agent (`kairos-triage-agent`) running as `@itxaka-agent`.
> This comment was generated by software. A human maintainer can override any
> action taken here.

Fixes: #444

Adds a `first-boot` yip cloud-config stage: a `stages: { first-boot: [...] }` block now fires exactly once, on the node's first boot, through the same `first-boot`/`first-boot.before`/`first-boot.after` mechanism (`agent/pkg/utils.RunStage`) that already drives `boot`/`network`/`fs`/`reconcile`.

Runs last inside the existing sentinel-gated block in `agent.Run()` (`agent/internal/agent/agent.go`) — after the two existing Go-only first-boot hooks (`BundleFirstBoot`, `GrubFirstBootOptions`), so cloud-config sees a fully-provisioned node, and before `machine.CreateSentinel("firstboot")` is written. A failure in the stage is logged, not propagated: on a `strict: true` node a broken first-boot cloud-config no longer puts the agent into a restart loop (bundles re-installed, grub options rewritten, `EventBootstrap` never published) every 5 seconds — it boots through and the failure is visible in the agent log instead.

The previously-proposed mechanism, `machine.ExecuteInlineCloudConfig`, turned out to be dead code — it shells out to an `elemental` binary that doesn't exist in Kairos v4 — so this uses `agent/pkg/utils.RunStage` instead, matching every other stage.

Full history is on the linked issue: full audit trail of what each role (coder/tester/docs/reviewer) did across 2 review rounds is in the summary comment on #444.

One open item for a maintainer or follow-up PR: there's no place in this repo that enumerates valid yip stage names for `first-boot` to join (checked README, docs/, CONTRIBUTING.md, schema — `sdk/schema/root_schema.go`'s `Stages` map is unvalidated free-form). The user-facing stage reference lives in kairos-io/kairos-docs, which is out of scope for this agent's run — flagging so a docs PR there isn't forgotten.
title: feat(agent): run a first-boot cloud-config stage

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #2064.

## Symptom

`kairos-agent upgrade` (and every other command that scans the user config dirs) prints hundreds of these lines:

```
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/MokManager.efi (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/EFI/BOOT/bootx64.efi (extension).
warning: skipping /run/initramfs/live/boot/grub2/i386-pc/acpi.mod (extension).
...
```

because `sdk/collector/collector.go` walks `/run/initramfs/live` recursively and warns on every file whose extension is not `.yml` or `.yaml` — which, in that directory, is almost every file.

## Fix

Silently skip non-yaml extensions. A non-yaml file in a scanned directory is never actionable for the user (the ISO ships them by design), so the warning was pure noise.

The other three warnings in the same loop stay — including the header-missing one that @jimmykarily explicitly wanted to keep visible on the issue thread, because that one *is* actionable ("sometimes people forget to put the header at the top of the file").

## Alternative considered

Plumbing `collector.NoLogs` through the `upgrade` path (as suggested in the 2024 thread). That would also silence the header-missing warning, which is the regression @jimmykarily was worried about. Dropping the `(extension)` message avoids the trade-off entirely and needs no changes outside `collector.go`.

## Test plan

- [x] New spec under `sdk/collector/collector_test.go` seeds a directory with a valid cloud-config, a header-less yaml, and four non-yaml siblings (`grub.cfg`, `bootx64.efi`, `unicode.pf2`, `acpi.mod`), captures stdout, and asserts:
  - the valid config is parsed
  - stdout contains no `(extension)` line
  - stdout still contains the `no valid header` warning for the header-less yaml
- [x] `go build ./sdk/... ./agent/...` and `go vet ./sdk/... ./agent/...` (existing warning in `sdk/loop/loop_test.go` is unrelated)
- [x] `go test ./sdk/collector/...` green
title: fix(config): stop warning about non-yaml files in scanned dirs

author: ci-robbot
body:
Three renovate branches are reopened on every run and none of them can ever go green. This turns them off at the source instead of closing them again next week.

## bubbles / bubbletea v2

`github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/v2@v2.0.9` declares `module charm.land/bubbletea/v2`; same for bubbles. So the requirement renovate writes is unresolvable and the module graph fails to load before anything compiles:

```
$ go build ./...
main.go:3:8: github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/v2@v2.0.9: parsing go.mod:
	module declares its path as: charm.land/bubbletea/v2
	        but was required as: github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/v2
```

That is #4472 and #4473, both red on all four `build-kairos` legs, `unit-tests`, `golangci_lint` and `scan shipped bundle`, plus `renovate/artifacts` because `go.sum` cannot be regenerated either.

The upgrade is possible. `charm.land/bubbletea/v2 v2.0.9`, `charm.land/bubbles/v2 v2.2.1` and `charm.land/lipgloss/v2 v2.0.6` build together, verified in a scratch module. But it is not a `go.mod` edit: all three modules have to move at once (bubbles/v2 requires the other two), the import path changes in 21 files under `installer/`, and the API moved -- `View() string` becomes `View() View` at 14 sites, `tea.KeyMsg` is an interface in v2 with key presses arriving as `tea.KeyPressMsg` at 26 sites, and `tea.KeyRunes` and `tea.KeyCtrlC` are gone.

`allowedVersions: "<2.0.0"` keeps renovate on the v1 line until someone does that migration. It does not block it.

## examples/bundle/Dockerfile

The file already carries the reason it is pinned:

```dockerfile
# cockroachdb/swiss, which go:linknames into runtime internals (hashFn,
# getRuntimeHasher, fastrand64) that 1.27 no longer exposes, so the ipfs
# build below dies with a pile of "undefined:" errors.
FROM golang:1.26 AS build
```

`cfb779bf` added that pin and comment on 2026-09-02, reverting renovate's `e1c4f797`. #4509 proposes `e1c4f797` again, opened two days later.

CI cannot catch the regression: this Dockerfile is built only by the `bundles` test (`.github/workflows/reusable-qemu-test.yaml:314`), and no `bundles` job ran on #4509 -- 35 green, 7 skipped, and its one red leg is `build-iso / amd64-core-ubuntu-20.04`, which does not touch the file. So the loop is silent.

`enabled: false` on the file holds it until kubo drops `cockroachdb/swiss`.

## edgevpn v0.35.4+

`github.com/mudler/edgevpn` v0.35.4 added `api/spa.go`:

```go
//go:embed react-ui/dist/*
var reactUI embed.FS
```

`.gitignore` upstream carries `/api/react-ui/dist`, so the directory is never committed and never reaches the module zip. Any consumer that pulls in `edgevpn/api`, as Kairos does directly and transitively, dies before it compiles:

```
$ go get github.com/mudler/edgevpn@v0.35.4 && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./provider/...
/root/go/pkg/mod/github.com/mudler/edgevpn@v0.35.4/api/spa.go:30:12: pattern react-ui/dist/*: no matching files found
```

That is #4464. v0.35.5, released 2026-09-03, still ships no `dist` in its zip and still gitignores the path, so bumping past the block does not help yet. Filed upstream as mudler/edgevpn#1080.

`allowedVersions: "<0.35.4"` holds the v0.35.3 pin until a release carries the assets.

## Verification

`renovate-config-validator` on the new file:

```
INFO: Validating renovate.json
INFO: Config validated successfully against 1 file(s)
```

Closes nothing on its own. #4464, #4472, #4473 and #4509 can be closed once this lands.
title: chore(renovate): stop three bumps that can never build

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4583.

`copyFile` (`agent/pkg/uki/common.go`) returns `error` and panicked on the
two failures it is most likely to see, `os.Open` of the source and
`os.Create` of the destination. Both call sites are in `installEntry`, which
is the whole of the UKI recovery-upgrade and single-entry-upgrade paths, and
both already check the returned error and log what they were copying. Those
checks were dead for exactly the cases they were written for.

Nothing in `agent/`, `sdk/` or `cmd/` calls `recover()`, so an upgrade source
that is not a UKI artifact set ended `kairos-agent` on

```
panic: open /tmp/1234567890/EFI/kairos/norole.efi: no such file or directory
```

That is after `MountRWPartition` has remounted `/efi` read-write. The
deferred `cleanup.Cleanup` does still run during the unwind, so the
partition is remounted; what is left behind is a half-written ESP, because
the second `copyFile` panicking leaves the new `.efi` next to the old
`.conf`.

## The change

Each error is returned wrapped with the path it is about. A bare
`no such file or directory` out of a temp dir tells the operator nothing, so
the message names the file:

```go
	sourceFile, err := os.Open(src)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("opening %s: %w", src, err)
	}
```

While in there: both handles were closed twice, a `defer Close()` plus an
explicit `Close()` at the end, so the deferred call returned
`file already closed` and it was discarded. The destination close is the one
that reports a failed flush, so it moves into the defer and is reported only
when nothing else failed. The source keeps its plain deferred close.

## Verification

The two panics were pinned as expected behaviour in
`common_extra_test.go`:

```go
It("panics when the source is missing", ...)
It("panics when the destination dir is missing", ...)
```

Reproduced both on `master` (`d0102329`) with a scratch test before touching
anything:

```
PANICKED on missing source: open .../missing.efi: no such file or directory
PANICKED on missing destination dir: open .../nonexistent/dst.efi: no such file or directory
```

Both specs are flipped to assert no panic, an error, `os.ErrNotExist`
through `errors.Is`, and that the path appears in the message. The
source-missing one also asserts no destination file is left behind.

Mutation-checked one panic at a time:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `panic(err)` back on `os.Open` | `reports a missing source instead of panicking` fails, `not to panic, but panicked with` |
| `panic(err)` back on `os.Create` | `reports a missing destination dir instead of panicking` fails, same message |
| neither | 81 specs pass |

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./agent/...
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet ./agent/pkg/uki/
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./agent/pkg/uki/
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/pkg/uki  0.088s
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run --timeout=12m ./agent/pkg/uki/...
0 issues.
```

The wider `./agent/...` run is green except for two failures that are
identical on pristine `master` here and are local environment gaps, not this
diff: `SyncData` (no `rsync` on this box) and `RenderTemplate` (arch
detection).

## What is not verified

No boot. The panic is reproduced in a spec, not on a trusted-boot machine
mid-upgrade, so the claim is that the failure is now reported rather than
that the recovery upgrade succeeds where it used to die.

## Noted, not fixed

`installEntry` uses `os.Open`, `os.Create` and `os.MkdirTemp` directly
instead of `i.cfg.Fs`, unlike the rest of the package, which is why it
cannot be driven by the existing `vfst` harness in `upgrade_test.go` and why
these specs test `copyFile` directly. Written up in #4583 rather than
changed here.
title: fix(uki): report a failed copy instead of panicking

author: mauro-agent
body:
🤖 Opened by `mauro-agent`, an AI agent operated by `@mauromorales`. He asked for this directly, after noticing the components below moved into this repo. He has not reviewed this specific text yet. If you want a human, feel free to ping him directly.

## What this fixes

`scripts/kairos-diff.sh` (which `.github/workflows/release-notes-diff.yaml` runs on every release, most recently extended by #4436) generates the per-component changelog sections in release notes. Five components it treats as separate external repos with their own version to diff were archived and merged into this monorepo on 2026-08-19/21: kairos-init, kairos-agent, immucore, kairos-sdk, kcrypt-discovery-challenger.

Concretely, the script read their pinned versions from kairos-init's own Makefile/go.mod, both of which are now frozen at their pre-archival state, since kairos-init stopped being tagged once its source moved in-tree. Left unfixed, every release from here on would have shown "No changes" for all five components, even as real development kept happening in their monorepo paths.

## What changed

- kairos-init, kairos-agent, immucore, kairos-sdk and kcrypt-discovery-challenger are now diffed by path within this repo itself (same two refs as the "Kairos changes" section), not against a separate repo or a frozen version pin.
- provider-kairos and edgevpn (still real external/go.mod dependencies) are now read from this repo's own kairos-init/Makefile and root go.mod post-migration, falling back to the archived kairos-init repo only for a ref that pre-dates the migration, needed for the one release that straddles it (the next one).
- Real drift caught along the way: kairos-init's Makefile pinned EDGEVPN_VERSION at v0.35.4 while the resolved go.mod dependency was already v0.35.3. go.mod is now authoritative post-migration; the Makefile value is used only as the pre-migration fallback, where it was the only place that version ever lived (it was never in kairos-init's go.mod).

## Testing

Verified directly against the real repo: version resolution for both the post-migration and pre-migration-fallback code paths, and path-based commit attribution against the real 2026-08-19/21 migration commit (correctly attributed, and correctly returned nothing for an unrelated path). The full v4.2.0..master range is too large to run end-to-end in a reasonable time from here; recommend a workflow_dispatch dry run against a recent tag pair before the next real release depends on this.

Refs #4242, #4243. A separate issue explains the underlying problem for anyone who hits it from a different angle.
title: fix: make kairos-diff.sh aware of the monorepo migration

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4316

## The bug

A GitHub release exists the moment its tag is pushed, but the assets attached to it can take minutes to finish uploading. Every release-asset download on the kairos-init binary path had the same budget:

```
--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 2
```

About ten seconds. The instance in the issue took **3m40s** from "release published" to "assets uploaded". A version bump landing inside that window gets a 404 from a URL that is perfectly valid a few minutes later.

It is easy to misread, and the issue explains why: the failing target names the component just bumped, only a `Makefile` change busts the buildx cache that otherwise serves the download layer, and every URL returns 200 by the time anyone goes to check.

## Where it still lives

The report points at `kairos-init/Makefile`. Since the monorepo migration that file is no longer on the build path: nothing in `.github/`, `scripts/` or the root `Makefile` invokes it, and the four components it downloads (`kairos-agent`, `immucore`, `kcrypt-discovery-challenger`, `provider-kairos`) are built in tree now. The live path is `scripts/prepare-kairos-init-binaries.sh`, called from `Makefile:224`, which downloads exactly one external dependency: edgevpn.

Both are fixed here. The Makefile is still usable for local runs and reads the same `kairos-init/EDGEVPN_VERSION` pin, so leaving it with the ten-second budget would just be a trap for whoever greps for `--retry 5` next.

## The change

- One `CURL_RETRY` / one `fetch()` per file instead of the flags repeated on each call site.
- Budget is `--retry 30 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --retry-max-time 300`. Bounded at five minutes, which covers the observed window with margin.
- **Download to a temp file instead of piping into tar.** curl retries the whole request, so on a mid-transfer reset the retried bytes are appended to whatever tar has already consumed and the stream is corrupt. A 404 never hit this, because `-f` writes no body, which is why the existing pipe looked fine.
- On failure both paths print the URL and say the assets may still be uploading, so the next person does not rediscover this from scratch.

## The tradeoff

A genuinely wrong pin (a typo, a tag that will never exist) now takes up to five minutes to fail instead of ten seconds. That is the cost of covering the upload window, and it is worth it against a spurious red that needs a full rerun and reads as "the bump is wrong". Fix 2 from the issue, waiting on the release rather than on the asset, is not attempted here; for a single external dependency I do not think it earns the machinery, but I am happy to be told otherwise.

## Verification

Ran all four download paths against real releases, in the worktree:

| target | result |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/prepare-kairos-init-binaries.sh` `fetch()` (edgevpn v0.35.5) | tarball extracted, `edgevpn --version` prints `v0.35.5` |
| `make download-edgevpn` | binary extracted |
| `make pkg/bundled/binaries/kairos-agent` | binary extracted |
| `make pkg/bundled/binaries/fips/kairos-agent-fips` | binary extracted |

Failure path, with the budget shortened so it does not take five minutes:

```
$ make download-edgevpn EDGEVPN_VERSION=v9.99.99 \
    CURL_RETRY="--retry 2 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 1 --retry-max-time 5"
Downloading and extracting edgevpn for architecture amd64...
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
Failed to download https://github.com/mudler/edgevpn/releases/download/v9.99.99/edgevpn-v9.99.99-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz
If that release was published in the last few minutes, its assets may still be uploading.
make: *** [Makefile:106: download-edgevpn] Error 1
```

Same shape for the script: retries, then a non-zero exit with the diagnostic. `bash -n` clean.

## Noted, not fixed here

`kairos-init/Makefile` still pins `AGENT_VERSION`, `IMMUCORE_VERSION`, `KCRYPT_DISCOVERY_CHALLENGER_VERSION` and `PROVIDER_KAIROS_VERSION` against four repositories that are archived, so those pins can never move again. That belongs with the rest of the migration cleanup in #4367, not here.

<sub>Opened by `ci-robbot`, an automated agent operated by @mudler. A human maintainer can override anything here.</sub>
title: fix(build): give release-asset downloads a window that covers the upload

author: ci-robbot
body:
Second PR off #4340. The spec calls these out as prerequisites for the grub reorder, not follow-ups, because both are guards that already misfire.

## `52_installer.yaml`: the plain installer starts on an interactive boot

The guard is `grep -q "install-mode" /proc/cmdline`, and the comment right above it says *"and NOT the install-mode-interactive cmdline as we can have both and we dont want to trigger both"*. `install-mode` is a prefix of `install-mode-interactive`, so the substring match fires on both.

What that means on an interactive boot today: the first stage enables `kairos-installer` and `kairos-webui` and masks `getty@tty1`, then the interactive stage has to `systemctl stop kairos-installer` / `systemctl disable kairos-installer` to undo it. It lands on the right service only because that stage comes later in the same file. Reordering the live grub entries, which is the point of #4340, makes that the common path rather than the rare one.

Fixed by matching space-delimited: `grep -qE "(^| )install-mode( |$)"`.

Worth recording: **`grep -w` does not fix this.** `-w` requires non-word characters around the match, and `-` is not a word constituent, so `install-mode` still matches inside `install-mode-interactive`. I checked, in both busybox `sh` and bash.

`nodepair.enable` is left as a substring match on purpose, in case anyone passes it as `nodepair.enable=true`.

## `25_autologin.yaml`: a guard that has never run

```
(grep -qv "interactive-install" /proc/cmdline || grep -qv "install-mode-interactive" /proc/cmdline )
```

`grep -v` succeeds when *any line* fails to match, and `/proc/cmdline` is one line. So each half succeeds whenever the line lacks that one keyword, and OR'd together the condition is true for every cmdline except one carrying **both** keywords. Root autologin has been unconditional on live boots for as long as this has been here.

I removed the guard instead of repairing it, and this is the one judgment call in the PR:

- `52_installer.yaml` masks `getty@tty1` on an interactive boot, so the `tty1` override is already inert there. The guard's original purpose is served.
- The surviving half is the `serial-getty@ttyS0` autologin, and the interactive installer runs on `TTYPath=/dev/tty1`. Turning the guard on for real would mean a serial-console machine booting the interactive entry sees nothing on serial *and* gets no shell. That is worse than what we have.

So the behaviour is unchanged and the file now says so. If you would rather serial consoles stopped autologging into root on a live ISO, that is a separate and deliberate change, and this PR makes it a one-line one.

## Verified

- `go test ./kairos-init/pkg/validation/`: 33 specs, green. The new ones evaluate the real `if` expressions the way yip does (`sh -c`, per `yip/pkg/console.StandardConsole.Run`), against a synthetic `/proc/cmdline` and `/run/cos/live_mode` in a temp dir. Stages are looked up by the service they enable, not by index, so the specs survive the file being reordered.
- Mutation-checked against the old expressions: `starts only the interactive installer on install-mode-interactive` and `autologins when the cmdline carries both interactive keywords` both fail, the other 31 pass. Those two are exactly the cmdlines the old guards got wrong.
- `golangci-lint run ./kairos-init/pkg/validation/...` (v2.13.2, the pin in `.golangci-version`): clean.
- `kairos-init/pkg/bundled` does not build in my environment (`pattern binaries/edgevpn: no matching files found`, the Makefile fetches it), so I could not run that suite. It is untouched by this diff.
title: fix(cloudconfig): make the install-mode guards say what they mean

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4533.

`AddSystemdConfSortKey` walks the whole ESP on UKI install, upgrade and reset, and rewrites every `*.conf` that is not `loader.conf`. When the conf reader failed it logged and carried on with the `nil` map the reader returns, then wrote the sort key into it:

```go
conf, err := sdkutils.SystemdBootConfReader(path)
if err != nil {
	log.Errorf("Error reading conf file to extract values %s: %s", conf, path)
}
...
conf["sort-key"] = sortKey        // panic: assignment to entry in nil map
```

The panic lands after `DeployImage` and after the artifact set has been copied into place, so the ESP is already half rewritten, the deferred remount back to read-only does not run, and immucore's boot-failure reporting has no error to classify.

## The change

Leave an entry we cannot read alone, keep walking, and return the joined errors at the end.

Skipping the file rather than writing it is what the write path forces. The block below the read rebuilds the whole file from the map, so continuing with an empty map would truncate the entry to a bare `sort-key` line and drop `title` and `uki`/`efi`. That entry does not boot. The panic was the only thing stopping that today.

Continuing the walk rather than aborting it matters because all three call sites only warn:

- [`install.go#L182-L185`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/install.go#L182-L185)
- [`upgrade.go#L108-L111`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/upgrade.go#L108-L111)
- [`reset.go#L92-L95`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/d17464a2/agent/pkg/uki/reset.go#L92-L95)

Returning on the first bad file would mean one damaged conf quietly costs every entry the walk had not reached yet its sort key, and the walk is in name order, so a stray `aaa.conf` would take `active`, `passive`, `recovery` and `statereset` with it. This is the one thing here that is a judgement call rather than a straight fix, so it is worth disagreeing with if you read it differently: the alternative is to return immediately and be consistent with `upgradeEfiKeysInLoaderEntries`, which does abort.

The `Errorf` arguments were also swapped: the format is `"...%s: %s"` and the args were `conf, path`, so the first verb got the nil map, the second got the path, and `err` was never printed at all.

## Tests

Three specs in `common_extra_test.go`, replacing the one that pinned the panic as expected behaviour (`It("panics on unreadable conf files")`). All three fail on `master`, two with the panic:

- an unreadable conf is reported by path and cause, and its contents are unchanged afterwards
- a conf with no newline in its first 64 KiB is reported too, which is the `bufio.ErrTooLong` branch of the reader rather than the `os.Open` one, and the shape a `.conf` takes when its contents get replaced by garbage
- an unreadable `aaa.conf` no longer stops `active.conf` from getting `sort-key 0001` with its `title` and `uki` intact

## Verification

```
go build ./agent/...                     ok
go test ./agent/pkg/uki/                 ok
golangci-lint run ./agent/pkg/uki/...    0 issues
```

`./agent/pkg/action/` has one failure, `RenderTemplate ... renders the template with config and state`, which asserts `amd64` and fails identically on unmodified `master` on this machine. Not related to this diff.

The trigger cannot be exercised end to end here: `kairos-agent` runs as root, so the permission-denied path is a test-only shortcut to the same reader failure. On a real machine the reachable causes are `EIO` on the vfat ESP, which is mounted read-only outside these three operations, and the too-long-line branch above. What the fix changes is the failure mode, not how often it fires.
title: fix(uki): report an unreadable loader entry instead of panicking

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4567.

## Root cause

The `Config from cloudconfig` fixture sets:

```yaml
upgrade:
  recovery: true
  system:
    source: oci:busybox
```

Each `It` in that block builds its config with `config.ScanNoLogs(...)` and then
replaces `Runner`, `Fs`, `Mounter`, `CloudInitRunner` and `Logger` with the suite
doubles. It never replaces `ImageExtractor`, so the config keeps the real
`OCIImageExtractor{}`.

`NewUpgradeSpec` ends in `setUpgradeSourceSize` -> `GetSourceSize` ->
`ImageExtractor.GetOCIImageSize("busybox", ...)`, and a failure there is returned,
not tolerated. So the spec is one unauthenticated request to Docker Hub, and the
`Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())` on the next line is really an assertion about
the network. Anonymous Docker Hub pulls are rate limited per source IP, which
explains the batching @mauro-agent saw (9 of 15, then 0 of 20) rather than an even
scatter.

## Evidence

Building the suite at `c26aa279` and refusing all outbound traffic
(`HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1`) turns the flake into a hard, 100% reproducible
failure with the cause in the message:

```
[FAILED] Unexpected error:
    failed initializing spec: failed calculating size: Get "https://index.docker.io/v2/":
    proxyconnect tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
```

Run against the whole package, that is the *only* spec that fails: 191 passed, 1
failed. Nothing else in `agent/pkg/config` reaches the network.

## The change

Give that spec the `FakeImageExtractor` the rest of the suite already uses. Three
lines, test-only.

## Verification

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full suite, network refused | 191 passed, **1 failed** | **192 passed, 0 failed** |
| full suite, network normal | 192 passed | 192 passed |
| focused spec x5, network refused | fails every time | passes every time |
| suite runtime | 8.6s refused / 1.8s normal | 1.8s both |

The runtime column is the same root cause seen from the other side: the spec was
spending seconds waiting on a registry round trip.

## Note on scope

This is the flake in the issue and nothing else. The wider point, that
`config.Scan*` hands back a config carrying a live `OCIImageExtractor` and every
caller has to remember to swap it, is real but is a production-code change and
belongs in its own PR.
title: test(config): keep the upgrade cloud-config spec off the registry

body:
## Summary

- Bumps `github.com/mudler/yip` from `v1.26.0` to `v1.26.1`
- Picks up [mudler/yip#336](https://github.com/mudler/yip/pull/336): Hetzner native metadata API fix

## Why

Hetzner removed all EC2-compatible metadata routes on **2026-08-01** ([changelog](https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2026-08-01-removed-metadata-routes)).

`v1.26.0` still used the old AWS-shared constants pointing at `/latest/meta-data/` — so `Probe()` returned `false`, the Hetzner datasource was never selected, and Kairos nodes booted with no hostname, no SSH keys, and no cloud-config applied.

`v1.26.1` fixes this by fetching `/hetzner/v1/metadata` (the native endpoint), parsing the full YAML response, and preserving SSH key provisioning via the `public-keys` field in that document.

Closes #4374

## Test plan

- [ ] Boot a Kairos node on Hetzner Cloud after this bump and verify cloud-config is applied (hostname set, SSH keys present)

author: ci-robbot
body:
Refs #4196. This is the agent half; the server half is kairos-io/AuroraBoot#768.

## What changed

`os.Hostname()` was read exactly once, when building the registration payload, and no hostname was ever sent again.

Registration is also the one payload the agent stops sending. `Register()` returns early whenever credentials are already on disk:

```go
if creds, err := c.loadCredentials(); err == nil {
    c.credentials = creds
    c.logger.Infof("loaded existing credentials for node %s", creds.NodeID)
    return nil
}
```

So after first boot, no hostname reaches the server at all. That is the whole of #4196: a cloud-config that templates the name

```yaml
hostname: kairos-{{ trunc 4 .MachineID }}
```

can lose the race with phone-home registration, so the node registers as the image default and the AuroraBoot UI shows `kairos` for the rest of its life.

`HeartbeatData` gains `Hostname` and `sendHeartbeat` re-reads it per tick.

## Where the read lives

New `gatherHostname()` in `netinfo.go`, next to `gatherAddresses`, not in `sysinfo.go`. The two existing gatherers already draw the line this change depends on, and their comments say it out loud:

- `sysinfo.go`: *"Results are cached since system info doesn't change between heartbeats."*
- `netinfo.go`: *"Unlike gatherSystemInfo it is NOT cached: addresses change (DHCP, NIC churn) and must be re-read on every heartbeat."*

The hostname is in the second group, and caching it is exactly the bug being fixed, so the doc comment says so rather than leaving the next person to rediscover it.

## Empty, not a placeholder, on failure

A failed read reports `""`. The server treats a missing hostname as "nothing to report" and preserves what it already has, so an empty string is what keeps a transient read failure from blanking a good record. `"unknown"` would overwrite it with garbage.

`Register()` now goes through the same helper. Identical behaviour, one seam instead of two call sites.

## Verification

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./agent/internal/...
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/agent        0.097s
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/agent/hooks  0.021s
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/bus          0.006s
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/phonehome    2.301s
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/agent/internal/webui        0.170s

$ CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run --timeout=10m ./agent/internal/phonehome/...
0 issues.                       # v2.13.2, matching .golangci-version

$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet ./agent/...   # clean
$ gofmt -l agent/internal/phonehome/ # only uninstall_test.go, already dirty on master
$ git diff --check                   # clean
```

Two new specs, using a `hostnameFn` seam (`SetHostnameFunc` in `export_test.go`, following the existing `SetUninstallRunners`) and the mock server already in `client_test.go`, which captures every `HeartbeatData` it receives:

- a rename between two ticks shows up on the second one, so both names appear in the captured sequence;
- a read error reports an empty hostname on every heartbeat.

Both were checked against the mutation each is meant to catch:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| drop `Hostname` from `sendHeartbeat` | `should report the current hostname on every heartbeat` |
| wrap `gatherHostname` in a `sync.Once` (the original bug shape) | both specs |
| return `"unknown"` instead of `""` on error | `should report an empty hostname rather than a bogus one when it cannot be read` |

## Ordering

Either PR can land first. An older server ignores an extra JSON field, and the server half guards on non-empty, so an agent without this change preserves the stored hostname rather than blanking it.

Not boot-tested. This is a one-field addition to an existing periodic report, with the read itself covered by the seam above, so I did not think an ISO build was warranted. Say so if you would rather see one.
title: fix(agent): report the current hostname on every heartbeat

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4561

## The problem

`provider-decentralized-k8s` aborted on `master` in
[run 34251428760](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34251428760):

```
VM Aborted.
stderr: Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
qemu-system-x86_64: failed to initialize kvm: Permission denied
```

The `Enable KVM group perms` step in the same job was green. It runs under
`bash -e`, so `setfacl` did apply. `Permission denied`, not `No such file or
directory`, so the node existed throughout. The ACL was set and then lost:

```
17:38:26.7  Setting up qemu-system-common
17:38:27.2  Setting up libvirt-daemon-system
17:38:30.8  apt finishes, setfacl runs, exits 0
17:38:32.0  step ends green
17:38:45.0  Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
```

Installing the qemu/libvirt stack triggers udev. `udevadm trigger` is
asynchronous: it queues the events and returns, and udevd applies the packaged
`/dev/kvm` ownership (`root:kvm`, `0660`) whenever it reaches them. Nothing in
the step waited for that queue, so `setfacl` and udevd raced, and the ACL lost.

Only `provider-decentralized-k8s` runs on a GitHub-hosted runner
([`reusable-qemu-test.yaml:133`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/master/.github/workflows/reusable-qemu-test.yaml#L133)),
so it is the only cell that installs libvirt and qemu from scratch on every
run, and the only one that can open this window. On the self-hosted `fast`
label `apt-get install` is a no-op and nothing triggers udev.

## The change

```
  sudo apt-get install -y libvirt-clients ... ovmf curl
+ echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
+ sudo udevadm control --reload-rules || true
+ sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm || true
+ sudo udevadm settle || true
- sudo setfacl -m u:runner:rwx /dev/kvm
+ sudo setfacl -m u:runner:rwx /dev/kvm || true
+ test -w /dev/kvm
```

A rule in `/etc/udev/rules.d/` outranks the packaged one, so the mode holds
however late udevd gets to the event. `udevadm settle` closes the window the
postinst triggers leave open.

`setfacl` stays as a fallback for a runner where `udevadm` is not usable,
which is why the udev commands and the ACL are all `|| true`. The step's
verdict now comes from `test -w /dev/kvm` instead, which is the condition that
actually matters, and it fails in two seconds rather than letting the suite die
minutes later on a spec that has nothing to do with permissions.

The same step in `_uki-test.yaml` gets the same treatment. It runs on the
self-hosted `kvm` label where this does not currently bite, but the step is a
copy of the same code and the new check passes there for the same reason it
passes today.

## Verification

Both files parse (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`), and the generated shell block is clean
under `bash -n`. The race itself only reproduces on a GitHub-hosted runner
doing a cold libvirt install, so CI on this PR is the test.

This is distinct from #4557 and its PR #4558, which are about the panic
swallowing the logs. This one is about why the VM aborted in the first place.
title: fix(ci): keep /dev/kvm writable across the udev re-trigger

author: ci-robbot
body:
First step of the plan in #4340, which @mudler gave the go-ahead on.

## Why

The web UI has to move out of `agent/internal/webui` and into `installer/` before the interactive installer can become the live CD default. Go's internal rule blocks that move today: `webui.go` reads the `webui.disable` and `webui.listen_address` knobs through `agent/internal/agent.LoadConfig`, and `agent/internal/...` is not importable from `installer/`.

## What

`BrandingText`, `WebUI`, `Config` and `LoadConfig` move from `agent/internal/agent/config.go` into a new `sdk/branding`, together with the `/etc/kairos/branding` file lookup that lived in `agent/internal/kairos`.

That lookup was already duplicated: `installer/internal/tui/branding.go` was a copy of `agent/internal/kairos/branding.go`, byte for byte apart from the doc comments. Both copies are gone, and the four TUI call sites use `branding.File` / `branding.DefaultTitleInteractiveInstaller`.

Two renames, because `branding.BrandingText` and `branding.BrandingFile` stutter: `BrandingText` is now `branding.Text`, `BrandingFile` is now `branding.File`. The `Branding` field name on `Config` is unchanged, so `agentConfig.Branding.Reset` still reads the same at every call site.

The spec said `sdk/types/config`. That package already has a `Config` for the install spec, so a second unrelated `config.Config` would have been worse than a small package of its own.

## No behaviour change

The YAML tags, the default path (`/etc/kairos/agent.yaml`), the branding directory, the fallback order and the "a missing file is not an error" contract are all as they were. The four separate `if cfg.Branding.X == ""` blocks became one loop over the same four pairs.

## Verified

- `go build ./agent/... ./installer/... ./sdk/...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run` (v2.13.2, the pin in `.golangci-version`): clean.
- `go test ./installer/... ./agent/internal/...`: all green, including the webui suite.
- `go list -deps ./agent/internal/webui | grep internal/agent` is now empty. That is the point of the change.
- `LoadConfig` had no tests before. It has 9 specs now, against a temp branding dir rather than `/etc`, via an unexported `loadConfig(dir, paths...)` so the exported signature stays as it was. Mutation-checked: neutralising the "only fill an empty field" guard fails the fallback spec with `from the file` where `from the config` is expected.

Next, as separate PRs: the web UI into `installer/` behind one mux, and the two guard bugs in `52_installer.yaml` / `25_autologin.yaml` that have to land before the grub reorder.
title: refactor(branding): move the branding config into the sdk

author: mauro-agent
body:
## What

Adds a native Go fuzz test for `sdk/collector.DeepMerge` -- the function every `#cloud-config` source is merged through at boot -- for the Fuzzing item on OpenSSF Scorecard (currently 0/10 for kairos). The fuzz test found three distinct panics, all fixed here:

1. A nested map value produced by the `json.Unmarshal` fallback in `parseReaders` (a plain `map[string]interface{}`) fails a direct type assertion to the named `ConfigValues` type. `yaml.Unmarshal` happens to recreate `ConfigValues` at every nesting level, so this only shows up on the JSON path.
2. A source that decodes to an empty document (`nil` `ConfigValues`) panics writing into that nil map during a merge.
3. Two sources that both explicitly set the same key to `null` panic in `reflect.Type.Kind()` on a nil `Type`.

Any two merged config sources can hit one of these, so a crafted or malformed `#cloud-config` is a denial-of-service against a node's boot path today.

## How

- `asConfigValues` normalizes a map value into `ConfigValues` before merging, instead of a bare type assertion.
- `deepMergeMaps` allocates a map if handed `nil`.
- `DeepMerge` returns early whenever `a` is `nil`, regardless of `b`, instead of only when `b` is non-nil.

## Testing

- `go test ./sdk/collector/...` (ginkgo suite) passes, including three new regression cases.
- `go test ./sdk/collector/... -fuzz FuzzDeepMerge -fuzztime 30s`: ~390k executions, no crashes, after the fix (crashed within seconds before it).

## Scope

One of several fixes from an OpenSSF Scorecard fuzzing follow-up.

---

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MK9cEkL2f2kuHiGkxsnhx5

author: mauro-agent
body:
## What's broken

Debian/Ubuntu's `grub-efi-riscv64-bin` package (added by [kairos-init#398](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos-init/pull/398)) ships its prebuilt EFI binary under a `monolithic/` subdirectory:

```
/usr/lib/grub/riscv64-efi/monolithic/grubriscv64.efi
```

AuroraBoot's riscv64 search list (`getEfiGrubFilesForArch` in `pkg/ops/iso.go`) looks one level up:

```go
"/usr/lib/grub/riscv64-efi/grubriscv64.efi",
```

No symlink bridges the two, so AuroraBoot's search of the rootfs comes up empty and it silently falls back to whatever `grubriscv64.efi` happens to exist on the *build host* instead of the one this image actually installed. Observed live building a Kairos Ubuntu 24.04 riscv64 image in [mauromorales/homelab](https://github.com/mauromorales/homelab): the build host's own file was the only reason the resulting ISO booted at all, which is not something to depend on.

## Fix

A new workaround stage, right next to the existing "Link grub-editenv to grub2-editenv" one it mirrors: check for the monolithic binary, symlink it to the path AuroraBoot expects, no-op if the link already exists. `OnlyIfOs: "Ubuntu.*|Debian.*"`, `OnlyIfArch: "riscv64"`.

This keeps riscv64 self-contained the same way amd64/arm64 already are -- the rootfs kairos-init builds carries its own bootloader, nothing borrowed from whatever happens to be on the machine running AuroraBoot.

## Verification

`gofmt -l` clean. `go build`/`go vet` on `./kairos-init/pkg/stages/...` with `GOARCH=riscv64` (the only arch this stage touches) hits an unrelated pre-existing failure in `pkg/bundled`'s embed pattern (`binaries/kairos` vs. the Makefile's `kairos-installer` output) -- same failure with or without this change, confirmed by reverting it and re-running. Structurally verified against the existing `schema.Stage` fields already used identically elsewhere in this same file.

Co-developed-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
title: fix(riscv64): symlink Debian/Ubuntu's monolithic grubriscv64.efi to the path AuroraBoot expects

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4299.

## The bug

`BuildEvent` downloads k0s with the upstream installer script, moves the binary
to `/usr/bin` and then hand-writes the units in
`provider/internal/services/k0s.go`, because the relocated binary and the
Dockerfile build context both defeat the installer's own service handling.

`k0s install controller` is the only place upstream that turns
`spec.install.systemUsers` into real accounts
([`cmd/install/controller.go`](https://github.com/k0sproject/k0s/blob/main/cmd/install/controller.go)
calls `install.EnsureControllerUsers`). Skipping it skips them, so the image
ships without `etcd`, `konnectivity-server`, `kube-apiserver` and
`kube-scheduler`.

k0s starts regardless, warns that its configured users do not exist, and runs
kine, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler as root with
root-owned key material. Exactly what @bdegeeter reported on RHEL 9.8.

## The fix

Create the missing accounts next to the units, matching what
`k0s install controller` would have done:

| | |
|---|---|
| accounts | `etcd`, `konnectivity-server`, `kube-apiserver`, `kube-scheduler` |
| home | `/var/lib/k0s` (`constant.DataDirDefault`) |
| shell | `nologin`, or `false` where that is absent |
| home directory | not created |
| existing accounts | left alone |

The five components upstream names collapse to four accounts because
`KineUser` is defined as `kube-apiserver`, "apiserver needs to be able to read
the kine unix socket". Upstream `getControllerUserNames` sorts and compacts for
the same reason; the list here is already in that order and a spec pins it.

Failures fail the build rather than being logged and ignored. A silent root
fallback is the bug being fixed, so the quiet path is the one worth closing.

### Three tools, not one

Upstream tries `useradd`, then Debian's `adduser`. That is not enough here.
Alpine is a supported family and its base package set
(`kairos-init/pkg/values/packagemaps.go`) contains neither `shadow` nor
`adduser`; the only applet of that name comes from busybox, and it takes short
options and rejects the long ones the other two want. Sending
`--disabled-password --gecos ...` there would fail every Alpine image build.
So `adduser` is checked for being a busybox symlink and given `-h -s -S -D -H`
instead.

## Why build time

`/etc` is an ephemeral tmpfs overlay (`RW_PATHS: "/var /etc /srv"`) and
`/etc/passwd` is not among `PERSISTENT_STATE_PATHS`, so an account created at
runtime would not survive a reboot. Baking it into the image gives every node
running that image the same account, for the life of the image.

One consequence worth naming: `/var/lib/k0s` *is* a persistent state path,
while the UID `useradd --system` picks is fixed per image build. If a later
image build allocates a different UID, the persisted k0s data keeps the old
ownership. Pinning the UIDs would close that, but it risks colliding with
distro packages across six families, and upstream k0s does not pin either. Left
out deliberately; happy to follow up if you want it.

## Testing

13 specs, over an injected lookup/PATH/symlink/exec environment, in a new
`Services Suite`.

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./provider/internal/services/...
Ran 13 of 13 Specs in 0.001 seconds
SUCCESS! -- 13 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 0 Skipped

$ CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run --timeout=12m ./provider/...   # v2.13.2, from .golangci-version
0 issues.
```

Each spec was checked against a mutation of the code it covers, so none of them
is decorative:

| mutation | specs that go red |
|---|---|
| stop skipping accounts that already exist | 2 |
| `isBusybox` always false | 1 |
| hoist the shell lookup out of the loop | 1 |
| drop `--system` from `useradd` | 2 |
| return on the first failure instead of joining | 1 |

Not verified on our end: a real image build. The k0s provider path needs a
`kairos-init` build with `--provider k0s`, which I cannot run here. The account
list, the flags and the home directory are all checked against k0s `main`
(`pkg/install/users_linux.go`, `pkg/constant/constant.go`,
`pkg/apis/k0s/v1beta1/system.go`), not against a running controller.

The worker units are written unconditionally today and stay that way; these
accounts are controller-only upstream but cost nothing on a worker, and the
build cannot know which role the node will take.
title: fix(provider): create the k0s system users at build time

author: thev1ndu
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Follow-up to #4281. That PR added the *ephemeral* per-PR ISO size delta; this one adds the *durable* "track sizes over time" half of #3816, ported from the hadron `size-history.sh` pattern.

On every merge to `master`, a new `size-history` job records the size of each built ISO into a CSV on an orphan `size-history` branch and regenerates a Markdown table and an SVG chart (one independently scaled panel per ISO) from it, so trends survive the log / step-summary purging the per-PR report is subject to.

- `scripts/iso-size-history.sh` holds the `record` / `render` / `all` logic so it runs and is testable outside CI.
- The CSV is long-format (one row per merge+artifact), and artifacts are paired by a **version-stripped canonical key**, so a changing set of ISOs and the per-build release suffix in artifact names both pair correctly over time.
- Release tags are looked up from the API and annotated onto their merge row (never a separate row).
- The publish step is `continue-on-error` so a history hiccup never fails the build; pushes rebase-and-retry so close merges don't clobber each other.

Opened as a draft for early review of the approach while #4281 lands.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Closes #3816
title: :chart_with_upwards_trend: ci: track ISO sizes over time on merge to master

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4557.

## The bug

`tests/tests_suite_test.go` passes a `types.OnFailure` callback to peg that calls Ginkgo's `Fail()`. peg calls that callback from a goroutine it starts itself, in `pkg/machine.monitor`:

```go
go func() {
	...
	if !p.IsAlive() {
		code, err := p.ExitCode()
		if err != nil || code != "0" {
			f(p)     // our callback
		}
```

`Fail()` works by panicking, and Ginkgo can only rescue that panic in goroutines it owns. So every VM abort takes the whole suite down with an unrecovered panic rather than failing the spec. Ginkgo's own panic text names the fix.

Last seen on master in [run 34251428760](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/actions/runs/34251428760) (`provider-decentralized-k8s`), where a runner without `/dev/kvm` produced:

```
stderr: Could not access KVM kernel module: Permission denied
...
panic: Your Test Panicked
	/home/runner/work/kairos/kairos/tests/tests_suite_test.go:453
created by github.com/spectrocloud/peg/pkg/machine.monitor in goroutine 37
```

and, at the end of the job:

```
##[warning]No files were found with the provided path: tests/**/logs/*. No artifacts will be uploaded.
```

That empty artifact is the real cost. All 20 spec files call `gatherLogs(vm)` from an `AfterEach` guarded by `CurrentSpecReport().Failed()`, and a panic skips every one of them. For the whole VM-abort class of failure, including real product crashes rather than just this infra case, we get no report, no serial log, no `dmesg`, no `kairos-agent logs` tarball.

## Verification

`tests/` is a separate Go module and is not covered by `make test` (`go test ./...` from the repo root), so a regression test added here would never run in CI. Instead I reproduced the failure and the fix against peg's real code path, on a box with no qemu and no KVM, using `types.WithProcessName` to point the machine at `/bin/false` and the `OnFailure` closure copied verbatim from this file:

```go
m, _ := machine.New(
	types.QEMUEngine,
	types.WithProcessName("/bin/false"),
	types.WithStateDir(stateDir),
	types.WithSSHPort("42424"),
	types.OnFailure(onFailure),
)
m.Create(context.Background())
Eventually(func() string { out, _ := m.Command("echo ping"); return out }, 30*time.Second, 5*time.Second).Should(Equal("ping\n"))
```

Before, byte-for-byte the handler on master:

```
Will run 1 of 1 specs

VM Aborted.
Exit status: 1
panic: Your Test Panicked
	Fail(fmt.Sprintf("\nVM Aborted....
	  However, if you make an assertion in a goroutine, Ginkgo can't capture the
	  panic.
```

No `AFTEREACH-RAN`, no summary, no report.

After, the same handler with this patch applied:

```
VM Aborted.
Exit status: 1
AFTEREACH-RAN: this is where gatherLogs() lives
------------------------------
• [FAILED] [30.006 seconds]
a VM whose qemu dies on startup [It] reports the abort

  [FAILED]
  VM Aborted.
  ...
Summarizing 1 Failure:
  [FAIL] a VM whose qemu dies on startup [It] reports the abort
Ran 1 of 1 Specs in 30.007 seconds
FAIL! -- 0 Passed | 1 Failed
```

`go vet ./...` and `go test -c` on the `tests` module are both clean.

## One trade-off, deliberately not fixed here

`GinkgoRecover` marks the spec failed but does not interrupt the goroutine running it. In the repro above the spec still sat out the full 30 seconds of its `Eventually`. In the real suite that wait is `vm.EventuallyConnects(1200)`, so a VM that never boots will now take 20 minutes to end the run where the panic used to kill it in seconds. The trade is 20 minutes of runner time on a rare failure against having logs for every VM abort, which seems clearly worth it, but it is a real cost and worth saying out loud.

Short-circuiting that wait is a separate change and a larger one: `EventuallyConnects` is peg's own method, so cutting it short means routing the 20 call sites through a local helper that also watches the machine. The seam already exists, since peg's `monitor` returns a context that is cancelled when the process exits and `startVM()` already returns it. Happy to do that in a follow-up if you want it.
title: fix(tests): recover the VM-abort failure instead of panicking the suite

author: itxaka-agent
body:
Three places in this tree downloaded something and then ran or extracted it
without ever checking what came back. All three now verify a sha256 first,
through one new shared `sdk/verify` package instead of per-site checksum code.

- `kairos-init/pkg/stages/steps_install.go` -- `DownloadAndExtract` takes a
  `checksumsURL` and verifies the tarball against the `*-checksums.txt` sibling
  goreleaser publishes in the same GitHub release. Checked live that
  kairos-agent, immucore and mudler/edgevpn all publish it today. Covers both
  binary loops and the opt-in `.init_versions.yaml` override path.
- `provider/internal/provider/buildEvent.go` -- k3s and k0s used to share one
  unverified `curl | sh`-shaped path. Split them: k3s now goes through
  `downloadK3sInstaller`, which verifies get.k3s.io's script against
  `install.sh.sha256sum` from k3s-io/k3s (added in k3s-io/k3s#8312 for exactly
  this purpose; the two are byte-identical today).
- `provider/internal/role/p2p/kubevip.go` -- `KubeVIP.ManifestURL` turned out to
  be an arbitrary operator-supplied URL from the provider's own cloud-config,
  not a fixed upstream release URL (the default path uses a bundled local asset
  and never hits the network at all). Nothing for Kairos to pin, so there is a
  new optional `manifest_sha256` for the operator to pin it themselves; when set
  the download goes through `downloadVerifiedManifest` (temp file then rename,
  same pattern as `sdk/utils/image.ExtractRawExtension`), when unset behaviour is
  exactly as before so existing configs keep working.

get.k0s.sh is no longer run on this path at all. The earlier version of
this PR left it alone behind a `TODO(supply-chain)` -- k0sproject/get is a
bare GitHub Pages index.html with no checksum or signature published
anywhere, so there was nothing to hook into -- but `c5abd82e` took the
script out of the loop instead of leaving it unverified.
`downloadVerifiedK0sBinary` in `provider/internal/provider/buildEvent.go`
resolves the k0s version, fetches k0sproject/k0s's own `sha256sums.txt`
for that release, and pulls the binary directly from the GitHub release,
verified against that digest. Same shape as the k3s path, and it needs
nothing new from upstream to work.

`sdk/verify` is small on purpose: `VerifiedDownload(url, want SHA256Sum)` fails
closed on a malformed digest, network error, non-2xx status or digest mismatch;
`FetchChecksums(url)` is the plain unverified fetch of the checksums listing
itself, the one thing that cannot verify itself; `ChecksumFromSumsFile` parses
goreleaser-style listings case-insensitively. No retry logic -- callers needing
backoff wrap it with avast/retry-go, and this deliberately stays out of the way
of the in-flight retry consolidation elsewhere in `sdk/`.

`VerifiedDownload` never cleared `destination` before starting, which only
bites once a caller passes a fixed path instead of a temp file --
`k0sBinaryDest` is `/usr/bin/k0s`. With a stale file left there by an
earlier run, `grab` took it for a partial transfer and issued an HTTP
Range request against a full-file URL: either the verified output came
back quietly wrong, or on error the stale file stayed exactly where it
was, which the function's own doc comment promises it will not do. Caught
in review. `destination` is now cleared before the download attempt and
again on the error path, covered by
`TestVerifiedDownload_StaleDestinationIsReplaced` and
`TestVerifiedDownload_PartialDownloadRemovedOnError`.

Covered by new tests in `sdk/verify`, `kairos-init/pkg/stages`,
`provider/internal/provider` and `provider/internal/role/p2p`, all against local
httptest servers, no real network calls. Note for reviewers: `sdk/collector` has
4 failing specs on this branch, and they fail identically on unmodified
upstream/master (confirmed with `git stash` before touching anything) -- not from
this change, don't go chasing it.

Signed-off-by: itxaka-agent <itxaka-agent@users.noreply.github.com>
title: fix: verify sha256 on unverified download-and-run paths

author: ci-robbot
body:
Partial fix for #4257.

The reported symptom does not reproduce on `master`: `size: 300000` reaches the partitioner intact through the real decode path, and the 1.4 TiB the reporter saw came from `data_partition` being treated as `Size == 0` on v2.27.5, which kairos-agent#1305 already dealt with. Details and the arithmetic are in the issue.

What is still wrong is the tail reservation. The backup GPT header and partition array sit in the last 33 sectors of a 512-byte disk, so a partition running to the end of the disk has to give them back. `kairosPartsToDiskfsGPTParts` took them off the last *requested* partition unconditionally, whichever sector it ended on:

```
data_partition: size = 733986304 bytes, want 734003200 (short by 16896)
```

That is a 1 TiB disk holding 1.3 GiB of partitions, so the last one ends with the best part of a terabyte to spare and still loses 33 sectors, and its end sector stops being 2048-aligned.

The fix computes the end from the requested size and hands the tail back only when the partition actually crosses it. Overshooting by more than the tail is a layout that does not fit and `validateGPTPartitionsFit` still rejects it, so sizes that add up to exactly the disk keep working with the last partition ending on the last usable sector, as before.

Tests: the two new specs and `TestLastFixedPartitionKeepsItsRequestedSize` fail against the pre-patch function and pass after; `TestPartitionsFillingTheWholeDiskStillFit` passes both ways and pins the behaviour the unconditional reserve existed for. The existing spec that asserted the old shave is rewritten, and a companion one covers the partition that does reach the tail.

`go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test ./sdk/... ./agent/pkg/partitioner/ ./agent/pkg/config/ ./agent/pkg/implementations/...` are green locally except `sdk/sysext`, which wants a docker socket this box does not have.

The second commit is a typo fix (`mapstrcuture` -> `mapstructure` on `Partition.FS`, `Partition.Flags`, `schema.Partition.FS`). No behaviour change, since mapstructure falls back to case-insensitive field-name matching when it finds no tag. Drop it if you would rather keep this to one thing.
title: fix(partitioner): reserve the GPT tail only from a partition that reaches it

author: ci-robbot
body:
Fixes #4535

## The bug

On a node that has never installed an extension, the **first** `kairos-agent sysext install` always fails, and only the second one works:

```
$ rm -rf /var/lib/kairos
$ kairos-agent sysext install "http://.../hello.sysext.raw"
ERR failed installing system extension error="failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: mkdir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: file exists"
$ kairos-agent sysext install "http://.../hello.sysext.raw"
INF System extension http://.../hello.sysext.raw installed
```

`sysext list` on the same clean node fails identically.

Found while QA-ing #4482 on a booted VM. It is not from that PR, it reproduces on `master`.

## Root cause

`sysextDir` and `confExtDir` carry a trailing slash, and with no `--active`/`--passive`/`--recovery`/`--common` flag `dirFromBootState` hands the bare constant to `vfs.MkdirAll`, which is not trailing-slash safe:

```go
// twpayne/go-vfs/v5 mkdirall.go
err := fileSystem.Mkdir(path, perm)          // ENOENT, parent missing
case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
    parentDir := filepath.Dir(path)          // strips the slash -> the SAME dir
    MkdirAll(fileSystem, parentDir, perm)    // the recursion creates the leaf
    return fileSystem.Mkdir(path, perm)      // creates it again -> EEXIST, returned raw
```

It only fires when a **parent** is missing too. That is exactly why the existing `should create the target dir if it does not exist` spec does not catch it: it removes only `/var/lib/kairos/extensions` and leaves `/var/lib/kairos`, so the first `Mkdir` succeeds and the recursive branch never runs. And the suite's `BeforeEach` pre-creates `/var/lib/kairos/extensions`, so no spec has ever seen a genuinely clean node.

## The fix

Two parts, because either alone is fragile:

1. Drop the trailing slash from `sysextDir`, `confExtDir`, `sysextRunDir` and `confExtRunDir`, and join the boot-state suffixes with an explicit `/`.
2. Route the three `vfs.MkdirAll` call sites (`getDirExtensions`, `EnableExtension`, `InstallExtension`) through one `ensureDir` helper that runs `filepath.Clean` first, so the invariant does not depend on how the constants happen to be written.

`ensureDir` keeps the existing `Stat`-then-create shape rather than calling `MkdirAll` unconditionally. That is deliberate: dropping the guard would make the read-only-FS specs fail, because `ReadOnlyFS.Mkdir` returns `EPERM` on a directory that already exists and `MkdirAll` passes that straight through.

The run dirs never went through `MkdirAll`, only `filepath.Join`, so cleaning them changes nothing at runtime. They are in the diff for consistency.

## Verification

Four new specs, in a context whose `BeforeEach` removes `/var/lib/kairos` entirely: first sysext install, first confext install, first install followed by `enable --active`, and `list` on a node with nothing installed.

All four fail on `master`:

```
Summarizing 4 Failures:
  [FAIL] ... creates the sysext dir on the first install [sysext]
  [FAIL] ... creates the confext dir on the first install [sysext]
  [FAIL] ... creates the boot-state dir on the first install [sysext]
  [FAIL] ... lists no extensions rather than failing [sysext]
```

with the same error the VM produced:

```
failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/extensions/: mkdir /tmp/go-vfs-vfst.../var/lib/kairos/extensions: file exists
failed to create target dir /var/lib/kairos/confexts/:   mkdir /tmp/go-vfs-vfst.../var/lib/kairos/confexts: file exists
```

All four pass with the fix, and the full package suite is clean:

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./agent/pkg/action/ -count=1
Ran 216 of 216 Specs -- 215 Passed | 1 Failed
```

The one failure is `RenderTemplate action test / renders the template with config and state`, which fails identically on pristine `master` (212 of 212, 211 passed, same single failure). It is unrelated to this change.

Three existing expectations moved from `Destination: "/var/lib/kairos/extensions/"` to `"/var/lib/kairos/extensions"`, tracking the constant.

`gofmt` and `go vet` are clean on the package.

## Note for #4482

Once this lands, the bundled-extension path in #4482 works on a fresh node. Today that PR's abort-before-upgrade correctly refuses to upgrade when a bundled extension fails to install, which turns this bug into a node that gets neither the extension nor the OS upgrade.
title: fix(sysext): create the extensions dir on the first install

author: ci-robbot
body:
Closes #1697. Part 2 of 2 that @mudler asked for; the boot-time half is #4457, which is independent of this one.

## What was actually imported

`github.com/containerd/containerd v1.7.34` was in `go.mod` for **one function call**:

| Site | What it used |
|---|---|
| [`immucore/pkg/op/operation.go:45`](https://github.com/kairos-io/kairos/blob/73f1d10c/immucore/pkg/op/operation.go#L45) | `mount.All([]mount.Mount{m.MountOption}, m.Target)`, the only call into the library |
| `immucore/pkg/op/mount.go:39`, `pkg/op/fs.go:44,54,78,115` | `mount.Mount` purely as a struct carrying `{Type, Source, Options}` |
| `immucore/internal/utils/mounts.go:117` | `MountToFstab(mount.Mount)`, turning that struct into an fstab line |

Nothing else in the monorepo imported containerd v1. So a container runtime was in the dependency tree for a mount syscall and an option parser.

## The replacement

`immucore/internal/mount`, 129 lines, only what immucore reaches:

- **Option string to flags/data split.** The same table containerd used, so `rw`, `ro`, `bind`, `suid`, `dev`, `exec`, `async` become flags and `size=`, `lowerdir=`, `upperdir=`, `workdir=` fall through to the data argument.
- **The read-only bind two-step.** `mount(2)` ignores `MS_RDONLY` when `MS_BIND` is set, so `bind,ro` comes up **writable** unless a second `MS_REMOUNT` call applies it. No caller passes both today (`MountBind` passes only `bind`, and the `ro` mounts in `MountCustomMountsDagStep` are block devices), but a custom mount from cloud-config can, and losing that silently is how you ship a writable mount that says `ro` in fstab.
- **The page-size check** on the data string.

### One deliberate difference from containerd

containerd's table gave `"defaults"` a zero flag and then tested `f.flag != 0`, so `"defaults"` fell through to the *data* string:

```go
		if f, exists := flags[o]; exists && f.flag != 0 {
```

Any filesystem that validates its mount options rejects that. Here `defaults` is a real no-op flag, so a custom mount configured with `defaults` works instead of failing with `EINVAL`.

### What is not ported, and why none of it is reachable

| Left out | Why |
|---|---|
| loop device setup (`loop`, `direct-io`) | immucore sets up its loop device with `losetup -f` in `steps.go:71`, never through a mount option |
| `mount.fuse` / `mount.fuse3` helper binaries | the fstype comes from cloud-config or `DiskFSType`, neither of which produces `fuse.*` |
| overlay `lowerdir` compaction over one page | `MountWithBaseOverlay` builds exactly one `lowerdir` |
| `UnmountAll`, FUSE-aware unmount | immucore unmounts through its own `syscall.Unmount` wrapper |
| `CL_UNPRIVILEGED` flag preservation | that path is for user namespaces; immucore is PID 1 in the initramfs |
| propagation options (`shared`, `rslave`, ...) | not in containerd's table either, so behaviour is unchanged. They need their own `mount(2)` call, and `chroot.go` already does that directly |

`remount` with empty data now always issues the syscall, where containerd skipped the initial call. No caller in immucore passes `remount` through these options.

## Testing

`immucore/internal/mount/mount_test.go` uses a seam on the syscall to assert what reaches the kernel:

- flags and data split correctly for the option set immucore really passes
- clearing options undo setters, last one wins (`ro,rw` vs `rw,ro`)
- `defaults` sets no flag and does not reach the data string
- a read-only bind issues two syscalls, the second with `MS_REMOUNT|MS_RDONLY` on the target
- a writable bind issues one
- the syscall error is wrapped and names both source and target, which the retry loop in `pkg/op` logs
- oversized data is rejected before the syscall runs
- `All` mounts every entry and stops at the first failure

```
$ CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./immucore/...
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/internal/mount
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/internal/utils
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/cmd
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/op
ok  github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/immucore/pkg/state
```

`go build` over the repo is unchanged apart from the pre-existing `kairos-init` embed of `binaries/edgevpn`, which needs the downloaded artifacts. The boot tests in CI are what really exercise this: every mount immucore performs goes through the new code.

## Note on #1697

The issue also carries @pataha's 10 to 15 second mount stall. That is **not** fixed by this PR, and I do not want closing this to bury it. The containerd wrapper was a thin shim over `mount(2)`, so removing it buys no time. The time is in `MountOPWithFstab`, and it splits into three:

1. the one second wait before the first attempt, fixed in #4457
2. `DiskFSType` forks `blkid` twice per attempt and `Fsck` forks again from the prepare callback
3. `Sync()`, a full `syscall.Sync()` that flushes every mounted filesystem, runs twice per mount

Happy to take 2 and 3 in a third PR if wanted.
title: refactor(immucore): drop the containerd mount dependency

author: ci-robbot
body:
The `scan shipped bundle` release gate is red on every open PR that triggers
it (#4483, #4554, #4555). It is not any of those diffs.

## Root cause

[GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj) was
published on **2026-09-08** and covers:

```
google.golang.org/grpc  >= 1.83.0, < 1.83.2   patched: 1.83.2
```

`go.mod` pinned **v1.83.1**, so the advisory landed on a version the repo was
already shipping. Nothing had to change here for the gate to go red, which is
why it looks like an unrelated PR broke it.

Two sibling advisories are already clear at v1.83.1 and are not the cause:

| advisory | published | vulnerable | patched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GHSA-qc2q-p7wx-3px3 | 2026-09-08 | `<= 1.83.0` | 1.83.1 |
| GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc | 2026-09-01 | `<= 1.83.0` | 1.83.1 |

grpc reaches the shipped bundle through `provider-kairos`, which pulls it via
`kube-vip` and `gobgp`:

```
$ go mod why google.golang.org/grpc
github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/provider/internal/provider/config
github.com/kube-vip/kube-vip/pkg/kubevip
github.com/osrg/gobgp/v4/api
google.golang.org/grpc
```

`provider-kairos` is one of the binaries `make binaries` puts in
`kairos-init/pkg/bundled/binaries`, so the finding is in something Kairos
publishes and the gate is right to block it.

## The change

`go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.83.2` plus `go mod tidy`. Indirect-only
patch bump.

`go mod tidy` also drops six stale `go.sum` lines (`go-containerregistry`
v0.22.0, `moby/moby/api` v1.55.0, `moby/moby/client` v0.5.1). That drift is
**pre-existing**, not from this bump: running tidy on an unmodified `master`
removes the same six lines. Happy to drop them from this PR if you would
rather keep it to two lines.

## Verification

- `go build ./provider/... ./agent/... ./sdk/...` passes.
- `go vet ./provider/internal/provider/config/...` passes.
- The only `go build ./...` failure is the pre-existing
  `pattern binaries/edgevpn: no matching files found` embed error, which needs
  `make binaries` first and reproduces identically on unmodified `master`.

I could not run osv-scanner end to end to confirm the green: `api.osv.dev` is
blocked from this box, so the scan extracts packages and then cannot resolve
advisories. The version-range match above is from GitHub's advisory API, so
the conclusion rests on the published range rather than on a local clean run.

Refs #3985.
title: fix(deps): bump grpc to v1.83.2 for GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj

author: itxaka-agent
body:
The absorption of kairos-io/kairos-init into this monorepo replaced the build
pipeline but never deleted the old `kairos-init/Makefile`. It still describes
the pre-monorepo world: download pinned releases of kairos-agent, immucore,
kcrypt-discovery-challenger and provider-kairos from their own repos, then bake
those versions into `version-info.yaml`. Today `kairos-init-embed` in the root
Makefile calls `scripts/prepare-kairos-init-binaries.sh`, which takes the
freshly built `kairos` multi-call binary, `kairos-installer` and
`provider-kairos` from `dist/`, reports them as `in-tree`, and only fetches
edgevpn as a real external pin.

Why it is safe to delete:

- Nothing references it -- not the root Makefile, not `.github/workflows/*`, not
  any script, not `kairos-init/Dockerfile`. The only mention left in the repo was
  a stale comment, fixed here
- It is already broken. `pkg/bundled/bundled.go` embeds `binaries/kairos`,
  `binaries/provider-kairos`, `binaries/kairos-installer`, `binaries/edgevpn`
  and `binaries/version-info.yaml`; the Makefile's `download` target produces
  none of the first one and fetches paths that are no longer embedded. `make all`
  in `kairos-init/` cannot produce a buildable binary today
- Its pins (v2.31.4 / v0.20.4 / v0.13.4 / v2.16.4) are frozen at the last
  releases of repos that are now archived
- `test`, `test-coverage`, `lint` and `lint-fix` duplicate the root Makefile's
  `test` and `lint-go` for the same package

Out of scope on purpose: kairos-init's runtime `VersionOverrides` mechanism
(`pkg/config/config.go`, `GetInstallKairosBinaries`/`GetInstallProviderBinaries`
in `pkg/stages/steps_install.go`) stays as-is -- dropping
`/etc/kairos/.init_versions.yaml` to pull a different released binary is a live
opt-in feature and has nothing to do with the dead build-time Makefile.
`scripts/kairos-diff.sh` also still references the old per-component repo slugs,
but that is deliberate: it diffs release notes across the pre/post-absorption
boundary. edgevpn stays external, it is genuinely still its own upstream project.

Signed-off-by: itxaka-agent <itxaka-agent@users.noreply.github.com>
